children.translated_text: Book 1: <s>Sādhāraṇa</s> (General Topics), the First Section. Lesson 1: <s>Śāstra-saṃgraha</s> (Summary of the Treatise), the First Chapter. Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 1.

children.text:
1.1.1 dharmārtha-kāmebhyo namaḥ.
1.1.2 śāstre prakṛtatvāt((1)).
1.1.3 tatsamayāvabodhakebhyaś ca ācāryebhyaḥ. iti.
1.1.4 tat-saṃbandhāt. iti.
1.1.5 prajāpatir hi prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā tāsāṃ sthiti-nibandhanaṃ trivargasya sādhanam adhyāyānāṃ śatasahasreṇāgre provāca.
1.1.6 tasyaikadeśikaṃ manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo dharmādhikārikaṃ pṛthak cakāra.
1.1.7 bṛhaspatir arthādhikārikam.
1.1.8 mahādevānucaraś ca nandī sahasreṇādhyāyānāṃ pṛthak kāma-sūtraṃ provāca.
1.1.9 tad eva tu pañcabhir adhyāya-śatair auddālikiḥ śvetaketuḥ saṃcikṣepa.
1.1.10 tad eva tu punar adhy:ardhenādhyāyaśatena [1]sādhāraṇa-[2]sāṃprayogika-[3]kanyā-saṃprayuktaka-[ 4]bhāryādhikārika-[5]pāradārika-[6]vaiśika-[7]aupaniṣadikaiḥ saptabhir adhikaraṇair bābhravyaḥ pāñcālaḥ saṃcikṣepa.
1.1.11 tasya ṣaṣṭaṃ vaiśikam adhikaraṇaṃ pāṭaliputrakāṇāṃ gaṇikānāṃ niyogād dattakaḥ pṛthak cakāra.
1.1.12 tat-prasaṅgāc cārāyaṇaḥ sādhāraṇam adhikaraṇaṃ provāca. suvarṇanābhaḥ sāṃprayogikam. ghoṭakamukhaḥ kanyā-saṃprayuktakam. gonardīyo bhāryādhikārikam. goṇikāputraḥ pāradārikam. kucumāra aupaniṣadikam iti.
1.1.13 evaṃ bahubhir ācāryais tac chāstraṃ khaṇḍaśaḥ praṇītam utsanna-kalpam abhūt.
1.1.14 tatra dattakādibhiḥ praṇītānāṃ śāstrāvayavānām ekadeśatvāt mahad iti ca bābhravīyasya dur:ādhyeyatvāt saṃkṣipya sarvam artham alpena granthena kāmasūtram idaṃ praṇītam.
1.1.15 tasyāyaṃ prakaraṇādhikaraṇa-samuddeśaḥ
1.1.16 śāstra-saṃgrahaḥ. trivarga-pratipattiḥ. vidyāsamuddeśaḥ. nāgaraka-vṛttam. nāyaka-sahāya-dūtī-karmavimarśaḥ. iti sādhāraṇaṃ prathamādhikaraṇam adhyāyaḥ pañca prakaraṇāni pañca.
1.1.17 pramāṇa-kālā-bhāvebhyo ratāvasthāpanam. prīti-viśeṣāḥ. āliṅgana-vicārāḥ. cumbana-vikalpāḥ..nakharadana-jātayaḥ. daśana-cchedya-vidhayaḥ. deśyā upacārāḥ saṃveśana-prakārāḥ citra-ratāni prahaṇa-yogaḥ tad-yuktāś ca sītkṛtopakramāḥ puruṣāyitam puruṣopasṛptāni aupariṣṭakam ratārambhāvasānikam rata-viśeṣāḥ praṇaya-kalahaḥ iti sāṃprayogikaṃ dvitīyam adhikaraṇam. adhyayā daśa prakaraṇāni saptadaśa.
1.1.18 varaṇa-vidhānam sambandha-nirṇayaḥ kanyā-visrambhaṇam bālāyāḥ upakramāḥ iṅgitākāra-sūcanam eka-puruṣābhiyogaḥ prayojyasyopāvartaṇam abhiyogataś ca kanyāyāḥ pratipattiḥ vivāha-yogaḥ iti kanyā-saṃprayuktakaṃ tṛtīyādhikaraṇam. adhyāyāḥ pañca prakaraṇāni nava
1.1.19 ekacāriṇī-vṛttam pravāsacāryā sapatnīṣu jyeṣṭhā-vṛttam kaniṣṭhā-vṛttam punarbhū-vṛttam durbhagā-vṛttam āntaḥpurikam puruṣasya bahvīṣu pratipattiḥ iti bhāryādhikārikaṃ caturtham adhikaraṇam adhyāyau dvau prakaraṇāny aṣṭau
1.1.20 strī-puruṣa-śīlāvasthāpanam vyāvarttana-kāraṇāni strīṣu siddhāḥ puruṣāḥ a:yatna-sādhyā yoṣitaḥ paricaya-kāraṇāni abhiyogāḥ bhāva-parīkṣā dūtī-karmāṇi īśvarakāmitam antaḥpurikaṃ dāra-rakṣitakam iti pāradārikaṃ pañcamam adhikaraṇam adhyāyāḥ ṣaṭ prakaraṇāni daśa((2))
1.1.21 gamya-cintā gamana-kāraṇāni upāvartana-vidhiḥ kāntānuvartanam arthāgamopāyāḥ virakta-liṅgāni virakta-pratipattiḥ niṣkāsana-prakārāḥ viśīrṇa-pratisaṃdhānam.lābhaviśeṣaḥ arthānarthānubandha-saṃśaya-vicāraḥ veśyā-viśeṣāś ca iti vaiśikaṃ ṣaṣṭam adhikaraṇam adhyāyaḥ ṣaṭ prakaraṇāni dvādaśa.
1.1.22 subhagaṃ-karaṇam vaśī-karaṇam vṛṣyāś ca yogāḥ naṣṭa-rāga-pratyānayanam vṛddhi-vidhayaḥ citrāś ca yogāḥ ity aupaniṣadikaṃ saptamam adhikaraṇam adhyāyau dvau prakaraṇāni ṣaṭ.
1.1.23 evaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśad adhyāyāḥ catuḥśaṣṭiḥ prakaraṇāni((3)) adhikaraṇāni sapta sa:pādaṃ śloka-sahasram iti śāstrasya saṃgrahaḥ.
1.1.24v saṃkṣepam imam uktvāsya vistāro 'taḥ pravakṣyate. iṣṭaṃ hi viduṣāṃ loke samāsa-vyāsa-bhāṣaṇam..
children.translated_text: 1.1.1 Salutation to <s>Dharma</s> (virtue), <s>Artha</s> (wealth), and <s>Kāma</s> (pleasure). 1.1.2 Because [<s>Kāma</s>] is the primary subject of this treatise. 1.1.3 And to the teachers who impart the knowledge of its conventions. Thus. 1.1.4 Because of its connection [with all three aims]. Thus. 1.1.5 For <s>Prajāpati</s>, having created beings, first proclaimed the means for achieving the three aims of life (<s>trivarga</s>) — which form the basis for their sustenance — in a hundred thousand chapters. 1.1.6 <s>Manu Svāyaṃbhuva</s> separately extracted from that the portion relating to <s>Dharma</s>. 1.1.7 <s>Bṛhaspati</s> [extracted] the portion relating to <s>Artha</s>. 1.1.8 And <s>Nandī</s>, the attendant of <s>Mahādeva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), separately proclaimed the <s>Kāmasūtra</s> in a thousand chapters. 1.1.9 <s>Śvetaketu</s>, the son of <s>Uddālaka</s>, abridged that same [work] into five hundred chapters. 1.1.10 And that same [work] was further abridged by <s>Bābhravya</s> of <s>Pāñcāla</s> into one hundred and fifty chapters, comprising seven sections: [1] <s>Sādhāraṇa</s> (General), [2] <s>Sāṃprayogika</s> (On Sexual Union), [3] <s>Kanyā-saṃprayuktaka</s> (On Acquiring a Maiden), [4] <s>Bhāryādhikārika</s> (On the Conduct of Wives), [5] <s>Pāradārika</s> (On Other Men's Wives), [6] <s>Vaiśika</s> (On Courtesans), and [7] <s>Aupaniṣadika</s> (On Secret Practices). 1.1.11 <s>Dattaka</s> separately extracted the sixth section on courtesans, at the request of the courtesans of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. 1.1.12 In that connection, <s>Cārāyaṇa</s> expounded the general section; <s>Suvarṇanābha</s>, the section on sexual union; <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>, the section on acquiring a maiden; <s>Gonardīya</s>, the section on the conduct of wives; <s>Goṇikāputra</s>, the section on other men's wives; <s>Kucumāra</s>, the section on secret practices. Thus. 1.1.13 In this way, the treatise, composed piecemeal by many teachers, became nearly lost. 1.1.14 Since the works composed by <s>Dattaka</s> and others constituted only portions of the treatise, and since the [work] of <s>Bābhravya</s>, being extensive, was difficult to study — this <s>Kāmasūtra</s> has been composed, condensing the entire subject matter in a concise text. 1.1.15 Here is the enumeration of its sections and chapters: 1.1.16 Summary of the Treatise; Attainment of the Three Aims of Life; Enumeration of the Arts; The Life of a Man-about-Town; Deliberation on Helpers, Friends, and Female Messengers of the Lover. Thus, the first section, <s>Sādhāraṇa</s> (General Topics): five chapters, five sections. 1.1.17 Classification of Types of Union by Size, Duration, and Temperament; Varieties of Affection; Reflections on Embracing; Varieties of Kissing; Types of Nail-Marks; Kinds of Biting; Regional Customs; Modes of Lying Down; Unusual Positions of Union; Striking and the Corresponding Cries of Pain; The Woman Acting the Man's Part; The Man's Approach; <s>Aupariṣṭaka</s> (Oral Union); Beginning and Ending of Lovemaking; Special Types of Union; Lovers' Quarrels. Thus, the second section, <s>Sāṃprayogika</s> (On Sexual Union): ten chapters, seventeen sections. 1.1.18 The Procedure of Selection; Determining Compatibility; Winning the Maiden's Confidence; Approaches to a Young Girl; Interpreting Gestures and Signs; Pursuit by a Single Man; Causing the Agent to Approach; The Maiden's Response to the Pursuit; Marriage Arrangements. Thus, the third section, <s>Kanyā-saṃprayuktaka</s> (On Acquiring a Maiden): five chapters, nine sections. 1.1.19 The Conduct of an Only Wife; Behavior During the Husband's Absence; The Conduct of the Senior Co-wife Among Co-wives; The Conduct of the Junior; The Conduct of a Remarried Woman; The Conduct of an Unfavored Wife; Life in the Inner Apartments; The Husband's Behavior Among Many Wives. Thus, the fourth section, <s>Bhāryādhikārika</s> (On the Conduct of Wives): two chapters, eight sections. 1.1.20 Ascertaining the Characters of Women and Men; Causes of Resistance; Men Who Succeed with Women; Women Easily Won; Reasons for Acquaintance; Methods of Approach; Testing Her Feelings; The Role of the Female Messenger; The Amours of a Ruler; Life in the Inner Apartments; Guarding One's Wives. Thus, the fifth section, <s>Pāradārika</s> (On Other Men's Wives): six chapters, ten sections. 1.1.21 Reflection on Suitable Clients; Reasons for Going [to a Lover]; Ways of Winning Back; Compliance with the Beloved; Means of Acquiring Wealth; Signs of Disaffection; Dealing with the Disaffected; Ways of Dismissal; Reunion After Separation; Special Gains; Weighing Gains, Losses, Consequences, and Doubts; Types of Courtesans. Thus, the sixth section, <s>Vaiśika</s> (On Courtesans): six chapters, twelve sections. 1.1.22 Recipes for Increasing Attractiveness; Subjugation; Aphrodisiac Preparations; Restoring Lost Passion; Methods for Enlargement; Miscellaneous Recipes. Thus, the seventh section, <s>Aupaniṣadika</s> (On Secret Practices): two chapters, six sections. 1.1.23 Thus, thirty-six chapters, sixty-four sections, seven books, and slightly over a thousand verses — this is the summary of the treatise. 1.1.24 Having stated this summary, the detailed exposition will now be set forth. For it is the custom of the learned to discourse both in summary and in detail.

children.text: 1.1c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre sādhāraṇe prathame 'dhikaraṇe śāstra-saṃgrahaḥ prahamo 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of the illustrious <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the first section <s>Sādhāraṇa</s> (General Topics), the first chapter: <s>Śāstra-saṃgraha</s> (Summary of the Treatise).

leçon 2 atha trivarga-pratipatti-nāmako dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ.
section (prakaraṇa) 2 a) anuṣṭhāna
children.translated_text: Lesson 2: <s>Trivarga-pratipattiḥ</s> (The Attainment of the Three Aims of Life), the Second Chapter. Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 2: a) Practice.

children.text:
1.2.1 śatāyur vai puruṣo vibhajya kālam anyonyānubaddhaṃ parasparasyānupaghātakaṃ trivargaṃ seveta.
1.2.2 bālye vidyā-grahaṇādīn arthān.
1.2.3 kāmaṃ ca yauvane.
1.2.4 sthāvire dharmaṃ mokṣaṃ ca.
1.2.5 a:nityatvād āyuṣo yathopapādaṃ vā seveta.
1.2.6 brahmacaryam eva tv ā vidyā-grahaṇāt. b) avabodhaḥ
1.2.7 a:laukikatvād a:dṛṣṭārthatvād a:pravṛttānāṃ ajñādīnāṃ śāstrāt pravartanam lauki[ka]tvād dṛṣṭārthatvāc ca pravṛttebhyaś ca māṃsa-bhakṣaṇādibhyaḥ śāstrād eva nivāraṇaṃ dharmaḥ.
1.2.8 taṃ śruter dharmajña-samavāyāc ca pratipadyeta.
1.2.9 vidyā-bhūmi-hiraṇya-paśu-dhānya-bhāṇḍopaskara-mitrādīnām arjanam arjitasya vivardhanam arthaḥ.
1.2.10 tam adhyakṣa-pracārād vārtā-samaya-vidbhyo vaṇigbhyaś ceti.
1.2.11 śrotra-tvak-caksur-jihvā-ghrāṇānām ātma-saṃyuktena manasādhiṣṭhitānāṃ sveṣu sveṣu viṣayeṣv ānukūlyataḥ pravṛttiḥ kāmaḥ.
1.2.12 sparśa-viśeṣa-viṣayāt tv asyābhimānika-sukhānuviddhā phalavaty artha-pratītiḥ prādhānyāt kāmaḥ.
1.2.13 taṃ kāma-sūtrān nāgarika-jana-samavāyāc ca pratipadyeta.
1.2.14 eṣāṃ samavāye pūrvaḥ pūrvo garīyān.
1.2.15 arthaś ca rājñaḥ. tan-mūlatvāl loka-yātrāyāḥ. veśyāyāś ca iti trivarga-pratipattiḥ((4)). c) saṃpratipattiḥ
1.2.16 dharmasyā:laukikatvāt tad-abhidāyakaṃ śāstraṃ yuktam. upāya-pūrvakatvād artha-siddheḥ. upāya-pratipattiḥ śāstrāt.
1.2.17 tiryag-yoniṣv api tu svayaṃ pravṛttatvāt kāmasya nityatvāc ca na śāstreṇa kṛtyam astīty ācāryāḥ.
1.2.18 saṃprayoga-parādhīnatvāt strī-puṃsayor upāyam apekṣate.
1.2.19 sā copāya-pratipattiḥ kāma-sūtrād iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
1.2.20 tiryag-yoniṣu punar an:āvṛtatvāt śtrī-jāteś ca ṛtau yāvad arthaṃ pravṛtter a:buddhi-pūrvakatvāc ca pravṛttīnām an:upāyaḥ pratyayaḥ.
1.2.21 na dharmāṃś caret. eṣyat-phalatvāt. saṃśayikatvāc ca.
1.2.22 ko hy a:bāliśo hasta-gataṃ para-gataṃ kuryāt.
1.2.23 varam adya kapotaḥ śvo mayūrāt.
1.2.24 varaṃ sāṃśayikān niṣkād a:sāṃśayikaḥ kārṣāpaṇaḥ. iti laukāyatikāḥ..1.2.25 śāstrasyān:abhiśaṅkatvād abhicārānuvyāhārayoś ca kva cit phala-darśanān nakṣatra-candra- sūrya-tārā-graha-cakrasya lokārthaṃ buddhi-pūrvakam iva pravṛtter darśanād varṇāśramācāra-sthiti-lakṣaṇatvāc ca lokayātrāyā hasta-gatasya ca bījasya bhaviṣyataḥ sasyārthe tyāga-darśanāc cared dharmān iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
1.2.26 nārthāṃś caret. prayatnato 'pi hy ete 'nuṣṭhīyamānā naiva kadā cit syuḥ an:anuṣṭhīyamānā api yadṛcchayā bhaveyuḥ.
1.2.27 tat sarvaṃ kāla-kāritam iti.
1.2.28 kāla eva hi puruṣān arthānarthayor jaya-parājayayoḥ sukha-duḥkhayoś ca sthāpayati.
1.2.29 kālena balir indraḥ kṛtaḥ. kālena vyaparopitaḥ. kāla eva punar apy enaṃ karteti kālakāraṇikāḥ.
1.2.30 puruṣa-kāra-pūrvakatvāt sarva-pravṛttīnām upāyaḥ pratyayaḥ.
1.2.31 a:vaśyaṃ-bhāvino 'py arthasyopāya-pūrvakatvād eva. na niṣkarmaṇo bhadram astīti vātsyāyanaḥ.
1.2.32 na kāmāṃś caret. dharmārthayoḥ pradhānayor evam anyeṣāṃ ca satāṃ pratyanīkatvāt. anarthajana-saṃsargam asad-vyavasāyam aśaucam an:āyatiṃ caite puruṣasya janayanti.
1.2.33 tathā pramādaṃ lāghavam a:pratyayam a:grāhyatāṃ ca.
1.2.34 bahavaś ca kāma-vaśa-gāḥ sa:gaṇā eva vinaṣṭāḥ śrūyante.
1.2.35 yathā dāṇḍakyo nāma bhojaḥ kāmād brāhmaṇa-kanyām abhimanyamānaḥ sa:bandhu-rāṣṭro vinanāśa((5)).
1.2.36 devarājaś ca_ahalyām ati-balaś ca kīcako draupadīṃ rāvaṇaś ca sītām apare cānye ca bahavo dṛśyante kāma-vaśa-gā vinaṣṭā ity arthacintakāḥ.
1.2.37 śarīra-sthiti-hetutvād āhāra-sa:dharmāṇo hi kāmāḥ. phala-bhūtāś ca dharmārthayoḥ.
1.2.38 boddhavyaṃ tu doṣeṣv iva. na hi bhikṣukāḥ santīti sthālyo nādhiśrīyante. na hi mṛgāḥ santīti yavā nopyanta iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
1.2.39 bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ
1.2.39v evam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca dharmaṃ copācaran naraḥ. ihāmutra ca niḥśalyam atyantaṃ sukham aśnute..
1.2.40v1 kiṃ syāt paratrety āśaṅkā kārye yasmin na jāyate. na cārtha-ghnaṃ sukhaṃ ceti śiṣṭās tatra vyavasthitāḥ..
1.2.40v2 trivarga-sādhakaṃ yat syād dvayor ekasya vā punaḥ. kāryaṃ tad api kurvīta na tv ekārthaṃ dvi-bādhakam..
children.translated_text: 1.2.1 A man, whose lifespan is a hundred years, should divide his time and pursue the three aims (<s>trivarga</s>) — which are interconnected with one another and do not obstruct each other. 1.2.2 In childhood, pursuits such as the acquisition of knowledge. 1.2.3 And <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) in youth. 1.2.4 In old age, <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). 1.2.5 Or, because of the uncertainty of lifespan, one should pursue them as occasions arise. 1.2.6 But celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) should be observed until the completion of education. b) Understanding: 1.2.7 <s>Dharma</s> is: because of its supra-worldly nature and its having unseen results, the setting in motion of those who are not [yet] engaged — the ignorant and others — through scripture (<s>śāstra</s>); and because of its worldly nature and having visible results, the restraint through scripture from those [activities] already being practiced, such as eating meat, and so forth. 1.2.8 One should understand that [<s>dharma</s>] from revelation (<s>śruti</s>) and from association with those who know <s>dharma</s>. 1.2.9 <s>Artha</s> (material prosperity) is the acquisition of knowledge, land, gold, cattle, grain, vessels, furnishings, friends, and the like, and the augmentation of what has been acquired. 1.2.10 One should learn that from the practice of superintendents and from merchants versed in the conventions of commerce. 1.2.11 <s>Kāma</s> (pleasure) is the favorable engagement of the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose — directed by the mind conjoined with the self — each in their respective objects. 1.2.12 But primarily, <s>kāma</s> is the fruitful apprehension of an object, pervaded by the self-regarding pleasure arising from the particular domain of touch. 1.2.13 One should understand that from the <s>Kāmasūtra</s> and from association with urbane people (<s>nāgarika</s>). 1.2.14 When these [three aims] coincide, the earlier one takes precedence over the later. 1.2.15 But for a king, <s>artha</s> [takes precedence], because it is the foundation of worldly life. And for a courtesan (<s>veśyā</s>), [<s>artha</s> also takes precedence]. This is the doctrine of the three aims. c) Objections and responses: 1.2.16 Because <s>dharma</s> is supra-worldly, scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) that teaches it is appropriate. Because the accomplishment of <s>artha</s> requires prior methods (<s>upāya</s>), the understanding of methods comes from scripture. 1.2.17 But the teachers say: since <s>kāma</s> is self-arising even among animals, and since it is eternal, there is no need for a scripture [regarding it]. 1.2.18 [<s>Vātsyāyana</s> replies:] because the sexual union of men and women depends on each other, it requires method. 1.2.19 And that understanding of method comes from the <s>Kāmasūtra</s> — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 1.2.20 Among animals, furthermore, because the female sex is unrestricted, and because engagement [in mating] extends only as far as needed during the mating season, and because their activities are not preceded by intelligence — the notion [of kāma among them] is without method. 1.2.21 'One should not pursue <s>dharma</s>, because its fruit comes [only] in the future and because it is doubtful.' 1.2.22 For what person who is not foolish would take what is in hand and give it to another? 1.2.23 'Better a pigeon today than a peacock tomorrow.' 1.2.24 'Better a certain copper coin (<s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>) than a doubtful gold coin (<s>niṣka</s>)' — so say the <s>Lokāyatikas</s> (materialists). 1.2.25 Because of the trustworthiness of scripture, and because in certain cases the results of imprecation (<s>abhicāra</s>) and benediction are seen; because the movement of the circle of stars, moon, sun, planets, and constellations appears to proceed for the sake of the world as if with intelligent purpose; because the course of the world is characterized by the established conduct of the four classes and stages of life; and because one sees the giving up of seed already in hand for the sake of future harvest — one should pursue <s>dharma</s>: so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 1.2.26 'One should not pursue <s>artha</s>. For even when these [means] are practiced with effort, they may never succeed; and even without practice, they may come about by chance.' 1.2.27 'All that is brought about by time (<s>kāla</s>).' 1.2.28 'For it is time alone that places men in prosperity and adversity, victory and defeat, happiness and suffering.' 1.2.29 'By time, <s>Bali</s> was made <s>Indra</s>; by time, he was overthrown; time itself will make him [<s>Indra</s>] again' — so say the fatalists (<s>kālakāraṇikas</s>). 1.2.30 Because all activities are preceded by human effort (<s>puruṣakāra</s>), method is the proper basis. 1.2.31 Even for what must inevitably happen, it is precisely because it requires prior method [that effort is needed]. There is no good fortune for the inactive — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 1.2.32 'One should not pursue <s>kāma</s> — because it is opposed to <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, which are the primary [aims], and to the conduct of other good people. These [pleasures] bring upon a man association with unworthy people, evil enterprise, impurity, and lack of future [good].' 1.2.33 'Likewise, heedlessness, frivolity, untrustworthiness, and unacceptability.' 1.2.34 'And many who were enslaved by desire have been heard to have perished along with their retinue.' 1.2.35 'For example, the <s>Bhoja</s> king named <s>Dāṇḍakya</s>, desiring a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> girl out of lust, perished together with his family and kingdom.' 1.2.36 '<s>Devendra</s> (Indra) [with] <s>Ahalyā</s>, the mighty <s>Kīcaka</s> [with] <s>Draupadī</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> [with] <s>Sītā</s>, and many others are seen to have perished, enslaved by desire' — so say the proponents of <s>artha</s>. 1.2.37 [<s>Vātsyāyana</s> replies:] pleasures (<s>kāma</s>) are of the same nature as food, being the cause of the body's sustenance, and they are the fruit of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>. 1.2.38 But one should be aware of their dangers. For one does not refrain from cooking rice because beggars exist, nor does one refrain from sowing barley because deer exist — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 1.2.39 And here there are verses: 1.2.39v Thus, a man who pursues <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>dharma</s> enjoys supreme and painless happiness, both here and in the hereafter. 1.2.40v1 In any action where the doubt 'What might happen in the next world?' does not arise, and which is not destructive of wealth and is pleasant — in that, the wise are established. 1.2.40v2 Whatever accomplishes all three aims, or two, or even one, that should be done — but not what accomplishes one aim while obstructing the other two.

children.text: 1.2c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre sādhāraṇe prathame 'dhikaraṇe trivarga-pratipattir dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ.((6))
children.translated_text: 1.2c Thus, in the venerable <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the General (<s>Sādhāraṇa</s>) section, the First Book, the chapter on the Attainment of the Three Aims (<s>Trivarga-pratipatti</s>) is the second chapter.

children.text:
leçon 3 atha vidyāsamuddeśa-prakaraṇa-nāmakaḥ tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
section (prakaraṇa) 3
children.translated_text: Lesson 3: Now, the third chapter, called the Section on the Enumeration of Knowledge (<s>Vidyāsamuddeśa-prakaraṇa</s>). Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 3

children.text:
1.3.1 dharmārthāṅgavidyā-kālān an:uparodhayan kāma-sūtraṃ tad-aṅga-vidyāś ca puruṣo 'dhīyīta.
1.3.2 prāg yauvanāt strī. prattā ca patyur abhiprāyāt.
1.3.3 yoṣitāṃ śāstra-grahaṇasyābhāvād an:arthakam iha śāstre strī-śāsanam ity ācāryāḥ.
1.3.4 prayoga-grahaṇaṃ tv āsām. prayogasya ca śāstra-pūrvakatvād iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
1.3.5 tan na kevalam ihaiva. sarvatra hi loke kati cid eva śāstra-jñāḥ. sarva-jana-viṣayaś ca prayogaḥ.
1.3.6 prayogasya ca dūrastham api śāstram eva hetuḥ.
1.3.7 asti vyākaraṇam ity avaiyākaraṇā api yājñikā ūhaṃ kratuṣu prayuñjate.
1.3.8 asti jyautiṣam iti puṇyāheṣu karma kurvate.
1.3.9 tathāśvārohā gajārohāś cāśvān gajāṃś cān:adhigata-śāstrā api vinayante.
1.3.10 tathāsti rājeti dūrasthā api janapadā na maryādām ativartante tadvad etat.
1.3.11 santy api khalu śāstra-prahata-buddhayo gaṇikā rāja-putryo mahāmātra-duhitaraś ca.
1.3.12 tasmād vaiśvāsikāj janād rahasi prayogāñ chāstram ekadeśaṃ vā strī gṛhṇīyāt.
1.3.13 abhyāsa-prayojyāṃś ca cātuḥṣaṣṭikān yogān kanyā rahasy ekākiny abhyaset.
1.3.14 ācāryās tu kanyānāṃ pravṛtta-puruṣa-saṃprayogā saha:saṃpravṛddhā dhātreyikā. tathā:bhūtā vā nir:atyaya-saṃbhāṣaṇā sakhī. savayāś ca mātṛ-śvasā. visrabdhā tat-sthānīyā vṛddha-dāsī. pūrva-saṃsṛṣṭā vā bhikṣukī. svasā ca viśvāsa-prayogāt.
1.3.15 gītam (1), vādyam (2), nṛtyam (3), ālekhyam (4), viśeṣakacchedyam (5), taṇḍula-kusuma-vali- vikārāḥ (6), puṣpāstaraṇam (7), daśana-vasanāgarāgaḥ (8), maṇi-bhūmikā-karma (9), śayana-racanam (10), udaka-vādyam (11), udakāghātaḥ (), citrāś ca yogāḥ (13), mālya-grathana- vikalpāḥ (14), śekharakāpīḍa-yojanam (15), nepathya-prayogāḥ (16), karṇa-pattra- bhaṅgāḥ (17), gandha-yuktiḥ (18), bhūṣaṇa-yojanam (19), aindrajālāḥ (20), kaucumārāś ca (21), hasta-lāghavam (22), vicitra-śāka-yūṣa-bhakṣya-vikāra-kriyā (23),.pānakarasarāgāsava-yojanam (24), sūcīvāna-karmāṇi (25), sūtrakrīḍā (26), vīṇā-ḍamaruka-vādyāni (27), prahelikā (28), pratimālā (29), durvācaka-yogāḥ (30), pustaka-vācanam (31), nāṭakākhyāyikā-darśanam (32), kāvya-samasyāpūraṇam (33), paṭṭikāvāna-vetra-vikalpāḥ (34),takṣa-karmāṇi (35), takṣaṇam (36), vāstu-vidyā (37), rūpya-parīkṣā (38), dhātu-vādaḥ (39), maṇi-rāgākara-jñānam (40), vṛkṣāyurveda-yogāḥ (41), meṣa-kukkuṭa-lāvaka-yuddha-vidhiḥ (42), śuka-sārikā-pralāpanam (43), utsādane saṃvāhane keśamardane ca kauśalam (44),akṣara-muṣtikākathanam
(45), mlecchita-vikalpāḥ (46), deśa-bhāṣā-vijñānam (47), puṣpa-śakaṭikā (48), nimitta-jñānam (49), yantra-mātṛkā (50), dhāraṇa-mātṛkā (51), sampāṭhyam (52), mānasī kāvya-kriyā (53), abhidhānakośaḥ (54), chando-jñānam (55), kriyā-kalpaḥ (56), chalitaka-yogāḥ (57), vastragopanāni (58), dyūta-viśeṣaḥ (59), ākarṣa-krīḍā (60), bāla-krīḍanakāni (61), vainayikīnām (62), vaijayikīnām (63), vyāyāmikīnāṃ ca (64) vidyānāṃ jñānam iti catuḥ-ṣaṣṭir aṅga-vidyā. kāmasūtrāvayavinyaḥ.
1.3.16 pāñcālikī ca catuḥṣaṣṭir aparā. tasyāḥ prayogān anvavetya sāṃprayogike vakṣyāmaḥ. kāmasya tad-ātmakatvāt.
1.3.17v ābhir abhyucchritā veśyā śīla-rūpa-guṇānvitā. labhate gaṇikā-śabdaṃ sthānaṃ ca jana-saṃsadi..
1.3.18v pūjitā sā sadā rājñā guṇavadbhiś ca saṃstutā. prārthanīyābhigamyā ca lakṣya-bhūtā ca jāyate..
1.3.19v yoga-jñā rāja-putrī ca mahāmātra-sutā tathā. sahasrāntaḥ-puram api sva-vaśe kurute patim..
1.3.20v tathā pati-viyoge ca vyasanaṃ dāruṇaṃ gatā. deśāntare 'pi vidyābhiḥ sā sukhenaiva jīvati..
1.3.21v naraḥ kalāsu kuśalo vācālaś cāṭu-kārakaḥ. a:saṃstuto 'pi nārīṇāṃ cittam āśv eva vindati..
1.3.22v kalānāṃ grahaṇād eva saubhāgyam upajāyate. deśa-kālau tv apekṣyāsāṃ prayogaḥ saṃbhaven na vā..
children.translated_text:
1.3.1 A man should study the <s>Kāmasūtra</s> and its subsidiary arts without conflicting with [the proper] times for [studying] <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and their subsidiary disciplines.
1.3.2 A woman [should study] before the onset of youth. After marriage, with her husband's consent.
1.3.3 The teachers [say] that the instruction of women in this <s>śāstra</s> is purposeless, since women have no capacity for grasping treatises.
1.3.4 But <s>Vātsyāyana</s> [says] that women do grasp the practice, and practice is preceded by the treatise.
1.3.5 This is not limited to this [subject] alone. Everywhere in the world, only a few are knowers of treatises, yet practice is within the domain of all people.
1.3.6 And the treatise alone is the cause of practice, even when remote.
1.3.7 [For example,] 'There is grammar' — even non-grammarians who are ritualists employ modification (<s>ūha</s>) in sacrifices.
1.3.8 'There is astronomy' — [thus] they perform rites on auspicious days.
1.3.9 Similarly, horse-riders and elephant-riders train horses and elephants even without having studied the treatise.
1.3.10 Similarly, 'there is a king' — [thus] even people in distant provinces do not transgress the established boundaries. So too in this case.
1.3.11 Indeed, there are courtesans (<s>gaṇikās</s>), princesses, and daughters of high ministers whose intellects are sharpened by treatises.
1.3.12 Therefore, a woman should learn the treatise — or at least a part of it — in private, from a trustworthy person, through practice.
1.3.13 And a maiden should practice in secret, alone, the sixty-four arts that are applicable through practice.
1.3.14 As for the teachers of maidens: a foster-sister who has already had sexual experience with men and has grown up together with her; or a female friend of similar nature with whom conversation is without danger; or a maternal aunt of the same age; or a trusted old female servant who can take her place; or a mendicant woman with whom she has had prior contact; or a sister, through the trust established by practice.
1.3.15 The sixty-four subsidiary arts, which are components of the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>, are: (1) singing, (2) playing musical instruments, (3) dancing, (4) painting, (5) cutting <s>viśeṣaka</s> (decorative leaf patterns), (6) making designs with rice and flowers on the ground, (7) arranging flower-beds, (8) coloring the teeth, garments, and body, (9) inlaying floors with gems, (10) arranging beds, (11) producing music with water, (12) splashing water, (13) various artistic techniques, (14) making various kinds of garlands, (15) arranging chaplets and diadems, (16) costume and theatrical make-up, (17) making ear-ornaments, (18) blending perfumes, (19) arranging jewelry, (20) conjuring tricks, (21) <s>Kaucumāra</s> arts (magic and sorcery), (22) sleight of hand, (23) preparing various kinds of vegetables, soups, and dishes, (24) preparing drinks, colored beverages, and spirits, (25) needlework, (26) string games, (27) playing the <s>vīṇā</s> and <s>ḍamaruka</s> (drum), (28) riddles, (29) verse-capping games, (30) tongue-twisters, (31) reading books aloud, (32) viewing plays and stories, (33) completing verse-puzzles, (34) weaving mats, baskets, and cane-work, (35) carpentry, (36) woodwork, (37) architecture, (38) testing silver and gems, (39) metallurgy, (40) knowledge of gems, colors, and mines, (41) horticultural arts (<s>vṛkṣāyurveda</s>), (42) rules for ram, cock, and quail fights, (43) training parrots and mynahs to speak, (44) skill in shampooing, massage, and hair-dressing, (45) communicating by coded letters and signs, (46) speaking in code (<s>mlecchita</s> ciphers), (47) knowledge of regional languages, (48) making flower-carriages, (49) reading omens, (50) mechanical arts, (51) arts of memory, (52) group recitation, (53) mental composition of poetry, (54) lexicography, (55) knowledge of meters, (56) poetic figures, (57) arts of deception, (58) concealment of garments, (59) various gambling games, (60) dice games, (61) children's games, (62-64) knowledge of the sciences of etiquette, victory, and physical exercise.
1.3.16 There is also another set of sixty-four [arts] pertaining to <s>Pāñcālika</s> (erotic postures). We shall describe their practices in the section on sexual union, since <s>kāma</s> (love) is essentially constituted by them.
1.3.17 A courtesan elevated by these [arts], endowed with good character, beauty, and virtues, obtains the title of <s>gaṇikā</s> (chief courtesan) and a place of honor in the assembly of people.
1.3.18 She is always honored by the king, praised by men of virtue, sought after and approached, and becomes a focal point [of society].
1.3.19 Similarly, a princess or a high minister's daughter who knows these arts brings even a husband with a thousand women in his inner chambers under her control.
1.3.20 And even when separated from her husband or fallen into dire calamity, even in a foreign land, she lives happily through these arts.
1.3.21 A man skilled in the arts, eloquent and charming in speech, quickly wins the hearts of women, even if previously unknown to them.
1.3.22 From the very mastery of the arts, good fortune arises. However, their application may or may not be possible depending on the place and time.

children.text: 1.3c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre sādhāraṇe prathame 'dhikaraṇe vidyā-samuddeśaḥ tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, entitled 'The Enumeration of the Arts' (<s>Vidyāsamuddeśa</s>), in the first book called 'General' (<s>Sādhāraṇa</s>) of the <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of the illustrious <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text:
leçon 4 nāgaraka-vṛtta-nāmakaḥ caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ
section (prakaraṇa) 4
children.translated_text: Chapter Four, entitled 'The Conduct of the Man-about-Town' (<s>Nāgarakavṛtta</s>), Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 4.

children.text:
1.4.1 gṛhīta-vidyaḥ pratigraha-jaya-kraya-nirveśādhigatair arthair anvayāgatair ubhayair vā gārhasthyam adhigamya nāgaraka-vṛttaṃ varteta.
1.4.2 nagare pattane kharvaṭe mahati vā saj-janāśraye sthānam. yātrā-vaśād vā.
1.4.3 tatra bhavanam āsannodakaṃ vṛkṣa-vāṭikavad vibhakta-karma-kakṣaṃ dvi-vāsa-gṛhaṃ kārayet.
1.4.4 bāhye ca vāsa-gṛhe su:ślakṣṇam ubhayopadhānaṃ madhye vinataṃ śuklottara-cchadaṃ śayanīyaṃ syāt. pratiśayyikā ca. tasya śiro-bhāge kūrca-sthānaṃ vedikā ca. tatra rātri-śeṣam anulepanaṃ mālyaṃ siktha-karaṇḍakaṃ saugandhika-puṭikā mātuluṅga-tvacas tāmbūlāni ca syuḥ. bhūmau patadgrahaḥ. nāga-dantāvasaktā vīṇā. citra-phalakam. vartikāsamudgakaḥ. yaḥ kaś cit pustakaḥ. kuraṇṭaka-mālāś ca. nātidūre bhūmau vṛttāstaraṇaṃ samastakam. ākarṣa-phalakaṃ dyūta-phalakaṃ ca. tasya bahiḥ krīḍā-śakuni- pañjarāṇi. ekānte ca takṣa-takṣaña-sthānam anyāsāṃ ca krīḍānām. sv:āstīrṇā preṅkhadolā vṛkṣa-vāṭikāyāṃ sa:pracchāyā. sthaṇḍila-pīṭhikā ca sa:kusumeti bhavana-nyāsaḥ.
1.4.5 sa prātar utthāya kṛta-niyata-kṛtyaḥ gṛhīta-danta-dhāvanaḥ mātrayānulepanaṃ dhūpaṃ srajam iti ca gṛhītvā dattvā sikthakam alaktakaṃ ca dṛṣṭvādarśe mukhm gṛhīta-mukha-vāsa- tāmbūlaḥ kāryāṇy anutiṣṭhet.
1.4.6 nityaṃ snānam. dvitīyakam utsādanam. tṛtīyakaḥ phenakaḥ. caturthakam āyuṣyam. pañcamakaṃ daśamakaṃ vā pratyāyuṣyam ity a:hīnam. sātatyāc ca saṃvṛta-kakṣāsvedāpanodaḥ.
1.4.7 pūrvāhṇāparāhṇayor bhojanam. sāyaṃ cārāyaṇasya.
1.4.8 bhojanānataraṃ śuka-sārikā-pralāpana-vyāpārāḥ. lāvaka-kukkuṭa-meṣa-yuddhāni tās tāś ca kalā-krīḍāḥ. pīṭhamarda-viṭa-vidūṣakāyattā vyāpārāḥ. divā-śayyā ca.
1.4.9 gṛhīta-prasādhanasyāparāhṇe goṣṭhī-vihārāḥ.
1.4.10 pradoṣe ca saṃgītakāni. tad-ante ca prasādhite vāsa-gṛhe saṃcārita-surabhi-dhūpe sa:sahāyasya śayyāyām abhisārikāṇāṃ pratīkṣaṇam.
1.4.11 dūtīnāṃ preṣaṇam svayaṃ vā gamanam.
1.4.12 āgatānāṃ ca manoharair ālāpair upacāraiś ca sa:sahāyasyopakramāḥ..1.4.13 varṣa-pramṛṣṭa-nepathyānāṃ dur:dinābhisārikāṇām svayam eva punar-maṇḍanam mitra-janena vā paricaraṇam ity āhorātrikam.
1.4.14 ghaṭā-nibandhanam goṣṭhī-samavāyaḥ samāpānakam udyāna-gamanam samasyāḥ krīḍāś ca pravartayet.
1.4.15 pakṣasya māsasya vā prajñāte 'hani sarasvatyā bhavane niyktānāṃ nityaṃ samājaḥ.
1.4.16 kuśīlavāś cāgantavaḥ prekṣaṇakam eṣāṃ dadyuḥ. dvitīye 'hani tebhyaḥ pūjā niyataṃ labheran. tato yathā-śraddham eṣāṃ darśanam utsargo vā. vyasanotsaveṣu caiṣāṃ parsparasyaika-kāryatā.
1.4.17 āgantūnāṃ ca kṛta-samavāyānāṃ pūjanam abhyupattiś ca.
1.4.17c ity gaṇa-dharmaḥ.
1.4.18 etena taṃ taṃ devatā-viśeṣam uddiśya saṃbhāvita-sthitayo ghaṭā vyākhyātāḥ.
1.4.19 veśyā-bhavane sabhāyām anyatamasyodvasite vā samāna-vidyā-buddhi-śīla-vitta-vayasāṃ saha veśyābhir anurūpair ālāpair āsana-bandho goṣṭhī.
1.4.20 tatra caiśāṃ kāvya-samasyā kalā-samasyā vā.
1.4.21 tasyām ujjvalā loka-kāntāḥ pūjyāḥ. prīti-samānāś cāhāritaḥ.
1.4.22 paraspara-bhavaneṣu cāpānakāni.
1.4.23 tatra madhu-maireya-surān vividha-lavaṇa-phala-harita-śāka-tikta-kaṭukāmlopadaṃśān veśyāḥ pāyayeyur anupibeyuś ca.
1.4.24 etenodyāna-gamanaṃ vyākhyātam.
1.4.25 pūrvāhṇa eva sv:alaṃkṛtās turagādhirūḍhā veśyābhiḥ saha paricārakānugatā gaccheyuḥ. daivasikīṃ ca yātrāṃ tatrānubhūya kukkuṭa-yuddha-dyūtaiḥ prekṣābhir anukūlaiś ca ceṣṭitaiḥ kālaṃ gamayitvā aparāhṇe gṛhīta-tad-upabhoga-cihnās tathaiva pratyāvrajeyuḥ.
1.4.26 etena racitodgrāhodakānāṃ grīṣme jala-krīḍā-gamanaṃ vyākhyātam.
1.4.27 yakṣa-rātriḥ. kaumudī-jāgaraḥ. su:vasantakaḥ.
1.4.28 saha-kāra-bhañjikā, abhyūṣakhādikā bisakhādikā nava-pattrikā udaka-kṣveḍikā pāñcālānuyānam ekaśālmalī kadamba-yuddhāni tās tāś ca māhimānyo deśyāś ca krīḍā janebhyo viśiṣṭam ācareyuḥ. iti saṃbhūya-krīḍāḥ.
1.4.29 ekacāriṇaś ca vibhava-sāmarthyāt.
1.4.30 gaṇikāyā nāyikāyāś ca sakhībhir nāgarakaiś ca saha caritam etena vyākhyātam.
1.4.31 a:vibhavas tu śarīra-mātro mallikā-phenaka-kaṣāya-mātra-paricchadaḥ pūjyād deśād āgataḥ kalāsu vicakṣaṇas tad-upadeśena goṣṭhyāṃ veśocite ca vṛtte sādhayed ātmānam iti pīṭha-mardaḥ.
1.4.32 bhukta-vibhavas tu guṇavān sa:kalatro veśe goṣṭhyāṃ ca bahu-matas tad-upajīvī ca viṭaḥ.
1.4.33 eka-deśa-vidyas tu krīḍanako viśvāsyaś ca vidūṣakaḥ. vaihāsiko vā.
1.4.34 ete veśyānāṃ nāgarakāṇāṃ ca mantriṇaḥ saṃdhi-vigraha-niyuktāḥ.
1.4.35 tair bhikṣukyaḥ kalā-vidagdhā muṇḍā vṛṣalyo vṛddha-gaṇikāś ca vyākhyātāḥ.
1.4.36 grāma-vāsī ca sa:jātān vicakṣaṇān kautūhalikān protsāhya nāgaraka-janasya vṛttaṃ varṇayañ śradhāṃś ca janayaṃs tad evānukurvīta. goṣṭhīś ca pravartayet. saṃgatyā janam anurañjayet. karmasu ca sāhāyyena cānugṛhṇīyāt. upakārayec ca.
1.4.36c iti nāgaraka-vṛttam.
1.4.37v nātyantaṃ saṃskṛtenaiva nātyantaṃ deśa-bhāṣayā. kathāṃ goṣṭhīṣu kathayaṃl loke bahu-mato bhavet..
1.4.38v yā goṣṭhī loka-vidviṣṭā yā ca svaira-visarpiṇī. para-hiṃsātmikā yā ca na tām avatared budhaḥ..
1.4.39v loka-cittānuvartinyā krīḍā-mātraika-kāryayā. goṣṭhyā saha-caran vidvāṃl loke siddhiṃ niyacchati..
children.translated_text: 1.4.1 Having completed his education, having obtained wealth through gifts, victories, purchases, or employment, or through ancestral inheritance, or both, having entered the householder's stage (<s>gārhasthya</s>), he should follow the lifestyle of a <s>nāgaraka</s> (man-about-town). 1.4.2 His dwelling should be in a city, a large town, a market-town, or a great settlement frequented by good people. Or wherever his travels take him. 1.4.3 There he should have a house built near water, with a garden of trees, having distinct work-areas, and with two living rooms. 1.4.4 In the outer living room, there should be a bed that is well-polished, with pillows on both sides, dipping in the middle, with a white coverlet. And a couch beside it. At the head of it, a stand for cosmetics and a shelf. On these should be the ointments [remaining] from the night, garlands, a box of beeswax, a case of fragrant substances, citron-peel, and <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel leaves). On the ground, a spittoon. A <s>vīṇā</s> hung on an elephant-tusk peg. A painting-board. A case of paint-brushes. Whatever books. And wreaths of <s>kurañṭaka</s> flowers. Not too far away on the ground, a round mat with a cushion. A board for drawing and a dice-board. Outside that, cages for pet birds. In a separate place, a workshop for woodwork and other recreations. In the tree-garden, a well-spread swing with shade. And an earthen bench with flowers — thus is the arrangement of the house. 1.4.5 He should rise in the morning; having completed his regular duties, having cleaned his teeth, having applied a moderate amount of ointment, incense, and garland, having applied beeswax and lac, having looked at his face in a mirror, having taken mouth-freshener and betel, he should attend to his business. 1.4.6 Daily bathing. Every other day, body-massage (<s>utsādana</s>). Every third day, foam-soap (<s>phenaka</s>). Every fourth day, shaving (<s>āyuṣya</s>). Every fifth or tenth day, the full grooming treatment (<s>pratyāyuṣya</s>) — without omission. And regularly, removal of armpit perspiration and body odor. 1.4.7 Meals in the forenoon and afternoon. In the evening, <s>cārāyaṇa</s> (evening entertainment). 1.4.8 After meals, activities such as teaching parrots and <s>sārikā</s> (mynahs) to talk. Quail, cock, and ram fights, and various arts and games. Activities dependent on the <s>pīṭhamarda</s>, <s>viṭa</s>, and <s>vidūṣaka</s>. And a midday nap. 1.4.9 In the afternoon, after dressing, entertainment at social gatherings (<s>goṣṭhī</s>). 1.4.10 At dusk, musical concerts. After that, in the adorned living-room with fragrant incense burning, together with companions, waiting on the bed for women who have come for their assignation (<s>abhisārikā</s>). 1.4.11 Sending of female messengers, or going oneself. 1.4.12 And for those who have come, approaches together with companions, with charming conversation and courtesies. 1.4.13 For women who have come in bad weather with their finery dampened by rain, he should himself re-adorn them, or have his circle of friends attend to them — thus is the daily-and-nightly [routine]. 1.4.14 He should arrange water-pot festivals (<s>ghaṭā-nibandhana</s>), social gatherings (<s>goṣṭhī-samavāya</s>), drinking parties (<s>samāpānaka</s>), garden excursions (<s>udyāna-gamana</s>), verse-completion games (<s>samasyā</s>), and recreations. 1.4.15 On a known day of the fortnight or month, there should be a regular assembly at the temple of <s>Sarasvatī</s> of those appointed [for the purpose]. 1.4.16 Visiting performers should give performances for these [assemblies]. On the second day, they should receive their due honor. Thereafter, attendance or dismissal should be according to one's inclination. In times of misfortune and celebration, they should show mutual solidarity. 1.4.17 Guests who have been introduced should be honored and welcomed. Thus is the law of the assembly (<s>gaṇa-dharma</s>). 1.4.18 By this, the water-pot festivals (<s>ghaṭā</s>), established in honor of various deities, are explained. 1.4.19 At a <s>gaṇikā</s>'s (courtesan's) house, in an assembly-hall, or at the dwelling of any one [of the group], those of equal learning, intellect, character, wealth, and age should hold a social gathering (<s>goṣṭhī</s>) together with courtesans, with fitting conversation and seating. 1.4.20 There, they should engage in poetic verse-completion games or artistic challenges. 1.4.21 Those who are brilliant and universally charming should be honored. And those equal in affection should be treated generously. 1.4.22 Drinking parties should be held at each other's houses. 1.4.23 There, the courtesans should serve and drink honey-wine, <s>maireya</s> (a fermented liquor), <s>surā</s> (spirits), with various salty, fruity, fresh-vegetable, bitter, pungent, and sour accompaniments. 1.4.24 By this, garden excursions are also explained. 1.4.25 In the forenoon itself, well-adorned, mounted on horses, accompanied by courtesans and attendants, they should go. Having spent the day's entertainment there, and having passed the time with cock-fights, gambling, shows, and suitable pastimes, in the afternoon, bearing the marks of those enjoyments, they should return in the same manner. 1.4.26 By this, water-sports in summer at places with arranged fountains are explained. 1.4.27 The <s>Yakṣa</s>-night. The <s>Kaumudī</s> (moonlight) vigil. The <s>Suvasantaka</s> (spring) festival. 1.4.28 The mango-breaking (<s>sahakāra-bhañjikā</s>), roasted-grain-eating, lotus-stalk-eating, new-leaf festival, water-splashing, the <s>Pāñcāla</s> procession, the lone-silk-cotton-tree [game], <s>kadamba</s> battles, and various other regional festivals and games — these they should celebrate in a manner superior to the common people. Thus are the group entertainments (<s>saṃbhūya-krīḍā</s>). 1.4.29 And [some entertainments] are for one going alone, according to one's means and ability. 1.4.30 By this, the conduct of a <s>gaṇikā</s> (courtesan) and a <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine/leading lady) together with their female friends and <s>nāgarakas</s> is explained. 1.4.31 Now, one who is without wealth, having only his body, possessing only <s>mallikā</s>-jasmine oil, foam-soap, and astringent as his equipment, having come from a respectable place, skilled in the arts, should establish himself in social gatherings and in conduct befitting the courtesan's world through his expertise — such is the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (parasite/companion). 1.4.32 One who has enjoyed wealth, possesses virtues, has a wife, and is respected in the courtesan's world and in social gatherings, and who lives by that — such is the <s>viṭa</s> (wit/bon vivant). 1.4.33 One who knows only a part [of the arts], who is a jester and trustworthy — such is the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (buffoon). Or a professional comedian. 1.4.34 These are the ministers of courtesans and <s>nāgarakas</s>, appointed for alliances and disputes. 1.4.35 Through them, female mendicants (<s>bhikṣukī</s>), women skilled in the arts, shaven-headed women, low-caste women, and retired courtesans are enlisted. 1.4.36 And a village-dweller, having encouraged those of his own community who are discerning and curious, describing the lifestyle of city people and inspiring their trust, should imitate that very [lifestyle]. He should organize social gatherings. He should charm people through friendliness. He should help with their work and through assistance. And he should render service. Thus is the lifestyle of the <s>nāgaraka</s>. 1.4.37 (verse) One who, in social gatherings, tells stories neither entirely in Sanskrit nor entirely in the regional language, becomes highly regarded in society. 1.4.38 (verse) A gathering that is hated by people, one that spreads uncontrolled, or one whose nature is harming others — the wise person should not enter such a gathering. 1.4.39 (verse) The learned one who, following the inclinations of people, with recreation as the sole purpose, participates in social gatherings, achieves success in society.

children.text: 1.4c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre sādhāraṇe prathame 'dhikaraṇe nāgaraka-vṛttaṃ caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the first book (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) called 'General' (<s>Sādhāraṇa</s>), the fourth chapter [is] on the Lifestyle of the <s>Nāgaraka</s> (Man-about-town).

children.translated_text: Chapter 5: Now [begins] the fifth chapter, named 'Deliberation on the Conduct of the Hero's Companions and Messengers' (<s>Nāyaka-sahāya-dūta-karma-vimarśa</s>). Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 5.

children.text:
1.5.1 kāmaś caturṣu varṇeṣu sa:varṇataḥ śāstrataś cān:anya-pūrvāyāṃ prayujyamānaḥ putrīyo yaśasyo laukikaś ca bhavati.
1.5.2 tad-viparīta uttama-varnāsu paraparigṛhītāsu ca. pratiṣiddho 'vara-varṇāsv a:niravasitāsu. veśyāsu punarbhūṣu ca na śiṣṭo na pratiṣiddhaḥ. sukhārthatvāt.
1.5.3 tatra nāyikās tisraḥ kanyā punarbhūr veśyā ca. iti.
1.5.4 anya-kāraṇa-vaśāt para-parigṛhītāpi pākṣikī caturthīti goṇikāputraḥ.
1.5.5 sa yadā manyate svairiṇīyam..1.5.6 anyato 'pi bahuśo vyavasita-cāritrā tasyāṃ veśyāyām iva gamanam uttama-varṇinyām api na dharma-pīḍāṃ kariṣyati punarbhūr iyam.
1.5.7 anyapūrvāvaruddhā nātra śaṅkāsti.
1.5.8 patiṃ vā mahāntam īśvaram asmad-a:mitra-saṃsṛṣṭam iyam avagṛhya prabhutvena carati. sā mayā saṃsṛṣṭā snehād enaṃ vyāvartayiṣyati.
1.5.9 vi:rasaṃ vā mayi śaktam apakartu-kāmaṃ ca prakṛtim āpādayiṣyati.
1.5.10 tayā vā mitrī-kṛtena mitra-kāryam a:mitra-pratīghātam anyad vā duṣ:pratipādakaṃ kāryaṃ sādhayiṣyāmi.
1.5.11 saṃsṛṣṭo vānayā hatvāsyāḥ patim asmad-bhāvyaṃ tad-aiśvaryam evam adhigamiṣyāmi.
1.5.12 nir:atyayaṃ vāsyā gamanam arthānubaddham. ahaṃ ca niḥ:sāratvāt kṣīṇa-vṛtty-upāyaḥ. so 'ham anenopāyena tad-dhanam atimahad a:kṛcchrād adhigamiṣyāmi.
1.5.13 marma-jñā vā mayi dṛḍham abhikāmā sā mām an:icchantaṃ doṣa-vikhyāpanena dūṣayiṣyati.
1.5.14 a:sad-bhūtaṃ vā doṣaṃ śraddheyaṃ duṣ:parihāraṃ mayi kṣepsyati yena me vināśaḥ syāt.
1.5.15 āyatimantaṃ vā vaśyaṃ patiṃ matto vibhidya dviṣataḥ saṃgrāhayiṣyati.
1.5.16 svayaṃ vā taiḥ saha saṃsṛjyeta. mad-avarodhānāṃ vā dūṣayitā patir asyās tad asyāham api dārān eva dūṣayan pratikariṣyāmi.
1.5.17 rāja-niyogāc cāntar:vartinaṃ śatruṃ vāsya nirhaniṣyāmi.
1.5.18 yām anyāṃ kāmayiṣye sāsyā vaśagā. tām anena saṃkrameṇādhigamiṣyāmi.
1.5.19 kanyām a:labhyāṃ vātmādhīnām artha-rūpavatīṃ mayi saṃkrāmayiṣyati.
1.5.20 mamā:mitro vāsyāḥ patyā sahaikī:bhāvam upagatas tam anayā rasena yojayiṣyāmīty evam:ādibhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ para-striyam api prakurvīta.
1.5.21 iti sāhasikyaṃ na kevalaṃ rāgād eva.
1.5.21c iti para-parigraha-gamaṇa-kāraṇāni.
1.5.22 etair eva kāraṇair mahā-mātra-saṃbaddhā rāja-saṃbaddhā vā tatraika-deśa-cāriṇī kā cid anyā vā kārya-saṃpādinī vidhavā pañcamīti cārāyaṇaḥ.
1.5.23 saiva pravrajitā ṣaṣṭhīti suvarṇanābhaḥ.
1.5.24 gaṇikāyā duhitā paricārikā vān:anya-pūrvā saptamīti ghoṭakamukhaḥ.
1.5.25 utkrānta-bāla-bhāvā kula-yuvatir upacārānyatvād aṣṭamīti gonardīyaḥ.
1.5.26 kāryāntarā:bhāvād etāsām api pūrvāsv evopalakṣaṇam tasmāc catasra eva nāyikā iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
1.5.27 bhinnatvāt tṛtīya-prakṛtiḥ pañcamīty eke.
1.5.28 eka eva tu sārvalaukiko nāyakaḥ. pracchannas tu dvitīyaḥ. viśeṣālābhāt. uttamādhama-madhyamatāṃ tu guṇa-guṇato vidyāt. tāṃs tūbhayor api guṇā:guṇān vaiśike vakṣyāmaḥ.
1.5.29 a:gamyās tv evaitāḥ kuṣṭhiny unmattā patitā bhinna-rahasyā prakāśa-prārthinī gata-prāya- yauvanātiśvetātikṛṣṇā dur:gandhā saṃbandhinī sakhī pravrajitā saṃbandhi-sakhi-śrotriya- rāja-dārāś ca.
1.5.30 dṛṣṭa-pañca-puruṣā nā:gamyā kā cid astīti bābhravīyāḥ.
1.5.31 saṃbandhi-sakhi-śrotriya-rāja-dāra-varjam iti goṇikāputraḥ.
1.5.32 saha-pāṃsu-krīḍitam upakāra-saṃbaddhaṃ samāna-śīla-vyasanaṃ sahādhyāyinaṃ yaś cāsya marmaṇi rahasyāni ca vidyāt yasya cāyaṃ vidyād vā dhātr-apatyaṃ saha-saṃvṛddhaṃ mitram.
1.5.33 pitṛ-paitāmaham a:visaṃvādakam a:dṛṣṭa-vaikṛtaṃ vaśyaṃ dhruvam a:lobha-śīlam a:parihāryam a:mantra-visrāvīti mitra-saṃpat.
1.5.34 rajaka-nāpita-mālākāra-gāndhika-saurika-bhikṣuka-gopālaka-tāmbūlika-sauvarṇika-pīṭhamarda- viṭa-vidūṣakādayo mitrāṇi. tad-yoṣin mitrāś ca nāgarakāḥ syur iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
1.5.35 yad ubhayoḥ sādhāraṇam ubhayatrodāraṃ viśeṣato nāyikāyāḥ su:visrabdhaṃ tatra dūta-karma.
1.5.36 paṭutā dhāṣṭryam iṅgitākāra-jñatā pratāraṇa-kāla-jñatā viṣahya-buddhitvaṃ laghvī pratipattiḥ sopāyā ca
1.5.36c iti dūta-guṇāḥ.
1.5.37 bhavati cātra ślokaḥ.
1.5.37v ātmavān mitravān yukto bhāvajño deśa-kāla-vit. a:labhyām apy a:yatnena striyaṃ saṃsādhayen naraḥ..
children.translated_text: 1.5.1 <s>Kāma</s> (pleasure), practiced among the four <s>varṇas</s> (classes) with one of the same class, in accordance with the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), and with a woman not previously [married to] another, results in offspring, fame, and social standing. 1.5.2 The opposite [applies] with women of a higher class and those who are married to another — [it is] forbidden. With women of a lower class and those who are unattached, [it is] neither commended nor forbidden, [with] courtesans and remarried women, because its purpose is pleasure. 1.5.3 In this regard, the <s>nāyikās</s> (heroines) are three: a maiden, a remarried woman, and a courtesan. Thus. 1.5.4 A woman married to another may also be a fourth, circumstantial type, [approached] due to some other reason — so says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>. 1.5.5 [This applies] when he considers her a woman of loose conduct. 1.5.6 One who is known to have given herself to many others — approach to such a one, even if of a higher class, will not cause harm to <s>dharma</s>, as with a courtesan; she is like a remarried woman. 1.5.7 One who has been previously [married] and then taken into seclusion — there is no doubt here. 1.5.8 [Or he thinks:] 'This woman controls her husband, who is powerful, a ruler, allied with my enemy, through her dominance. She, once connected with me, will out of affection turn him away.' 1.5.9 'Or she will bring back to a favorable disposition one who is hostile to me, capable of doing me harm, and displeased.' 1.5.10 'Or through a king befriended by her, I shall accomplish a friend's task, the repulsion of an enemy, or some other difficult undertaking.' 1.5.11 'Or, connected with her, having killed her husband, I shall obtain his sovereignty, which should rightfully be mine.' 1.5.12 'Or the approach to her is without danger and connected with wealth. I am impoverished and lacking means of livelihood. By this means, I shall obtain that very great wealth without difficulty.' 1.5.13 'Or she, knowing my vulnerabilities and firmly desiring me, will, if I am unwilling, ruin me by publicizing my faults.' 1.5.14 'Or she will cast upon me a false but credible and hard-to-refute fault, by which I shall be destroyed.' 1.5.15 'Or she will separate her husband, who is tractable and has future promise, from me and join him with my enemies.' 1.5.16 'Or she herself will consort with them. Or her husband will corrupt the women of my household — I shall retaliate by likewise corrupting his wives.' 1.5.17 'Or by the king's command, I shall destroy his enemy who dwells within [the kingdom].' 1.5.18 'The other woman whom I desire is under her control. Through this connection, I shall reach her.' 1.5.19 'Or she will transfer to me a maiden — otherwise unobtainable, under her own authority, possessed of wealth and beauty.' 1.5.20 'Or my enemy has become united with her husband — through her, I shall administer poison to him.' For such and similar reasons, one may approach even another man's wife. 1.5.21 Thus, such boldness [is] not merely from passion alone. 1.5.21c Thus, the reasons for approaching another's wife. 1.5.22 By these very reasons, a woman connected with a high minister or a king, or one who frequents a particular place, or any other woman who accomplishes one's purpose, or a widow, is a fifth [type] — so says <s>Cārāyaṇa</s>. 1.5.23 That same woman, when she has become an ascetic, is a sixth — so says <s>Suvarṇanābha</s>. 1.5.24 The daughter of a courtesan or a female attendant, not previously [married to] another, is a seventh — so says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>. 1.5.25 A young woman of good family who has passed beyond childhood, because of the difference in her manners [from a maiden], is an eighth — so says <s>Gonardīya</s>. 1.5.26 Since there is no distinct category apart from the previous ones for lack of separate purposes, there are only four types of <s>nāyikā</s> — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 1.5.27 Some say a person of the third nature (<s>tṛtīya-prakṛti</s>) is a fifth. 1.5.28 There is indeed only one universal <s>nāyaka</s> (hero/lover); a second is the covert one — because of the lack of distinctive features. One should know the superior, inferior, and middling types by their respective qualities. We shall discuss their qualities and defects in the section on courtesans. 1.5.29 But these women are not to be approached: one afflicted with leprosy, one who is insane, one who has fallen [from caste], one whose secrets are known, one who openly solicits, one whose youth is nearly past, one who is excessively pale, one who is excessively dark, one who has a bad odor, a relative, a female friend, a female ascetic, and the wives of a relative, a friend, a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or a king. 1.5.30 'There is no woman who is not to be approached, provided she has been known by five men' — so say the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>. 1.5.31 'Except the wives of a relative, a friend, a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or a king' — so says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>. 1.5.32 A friend is one who has been a childhood playmate, one bound by reciprocal favors, one of the same temperament and habits, a fellow student, one who knows his vulnerabilities and secrets and whose [secrets] he knows, a foster-sibling, or one who has grown up together. 1.5.33 The qualities of a [good] friend are: hereditary from father and grandfather, trustworthy, never showing change of disposition, tractable, steadfast, not greedy by nature, not to be abandoned, and not a betrayer of counsel. 1.5.34 Washermen, barbers, garland-makers, perfumers, liquor-sellers, mendicants, cowherds, betel-sellers, goldsmiths, <s>pīṭhamardas</s> (companions), <s>viṭas</s> (parasites), <s>vidūṣakas</s> (jesters), and others — along with their women — should be friends of the man-about-town, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 1.5.35 What is common to both [parties], noble on both sides, and especially what is fully trusted by the <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) — therein lies the work of a messenger. 1.5.36 Cleverness, boldness, knowledge of gestures and signs, knowledge of the right moment for deception, resilience of mind, quick understanding, and resourcefulness — 1.5.36c these are the qualities of a [female] messenger. 1.5.37 And here there is a verse: 1.5.37 A man who is self-possessed, has friends, is resourceful, understands feelings, and knows place and time — even a woman who is difficult to obtain, he can win without effort.

children.text:
2.1.1 śaśo vṛṣo 'śva iti liṅgato nāyaka-viśeṣāḥ. nāyikā punar mṛgī baḍavā hastinī ceti.
2.1.2 tatra sa:dṛśa-saṃprayoge sama-ratāni trīṇi.
2.1.3 viparyayeṇa vi:ṣamāṇi ṣaṭ. vi:ṣameṣv api puruṣādhikyaṃ ced an:antara-saṃprayoge dve ucca-rate. vyavahitam ekam ucca-tara-ratam. viparyaye punar dve nīca-rate. vyavahitam ekaṃ nīca-tara-rataṃ ca. teṣu samāni śreṣṭhāni. tara-śabdāṅkite dve kaniṣṭhe. śeṣāṇi madhyamāni.
2.1.4 sāmye 'py uccāṅkaṃ nīcāṅkāj jyāyaḥ. iti pramāṇato nava-ratāni.
2.1.5 yasya saṃprayoga-kāle prītir udāsīnā vīryam alpaṃ kṣatāni ca na sahate sa manda-vegaḥ.
2.1.6 tad-viparyayau madhyama-caṇḍa-vegau bhavataḥ. tathā nāyikāpi.
2.1.7 tatrāpi pramāṇavad eva nava-ratāni.
2.1.8 tadvat kālato 'pi śīghra-madhya-cira-kālā nāyakāḥ.
2.1.9 tatra striyāṃ vivādaḥ.
2.1.10 na strī puruṣavad eva bhāvam adhigacchati.
2.1.11 sātatyāt tv asyāḥ puruṣeṇa kaṇḍūtir apanudyate.
2.1.12 sā punar ābhimānikena sukhena saṃsṛṣṭā rasāntaraṃ janayati tasmin sukha-buddhir asyāḥ.
2.1.13 puruṣa-pratīteś cān:abhijñatvāt kathaṃ te sukham iti praṣṭum a:śakyatvāt.
2.1.14 katham etad upalabhyata iti cet puruṣo hi ratim adhigamya svecchayā viramati na striyam apekṣate na tv evaṃ strīty auddālikaḥ.
2.1.15 tatraitat syāt cira-vege nāyake striyo 'nurajyante śīghra-vegasya bhāvam an:āsādyāvasāne 'bhyasūyinyo bhavanti. tat sarvaṃ bhāva-prāpter a:prāpteś ca lakṣaṇam.
2.1.16 tac ca na. kaṇḍūti-pratīkāro 'pi hi dīrgha-kālaṃ priya iti. etad upapadyata eva. tasmāt saṃdigdhatvād a:lakṣaṇam iti.
2.1.17v saṃyoge yoṣitaḥ puṃsā kaṇḍūtir apanudyate. tac cābhimāna-saṃsṛṣṭaṃ sukham ity abhidhīyate..
2.1.18 sātatyād yuvatir ārambhāt prabhṛti bhāvam adhigacchati. puruṣaḥ punar anta eva. etad upapannataram. na hy a:satyāṃ bhāva-prāptau garbha-saṃbhava iti bābhravīyāḥ.
2.1.19 tatrāpi tāv evāśaṅkā-parihārau bhūyaḥ.
2.1.20 tatraitat syāt ṇ sātatyena rasa-prāptāv ārambha-kāle madhyastha-cittatā nāti:sahiṣṇutā ca. tataḥ krameṇādhiko rāga-yogaḥ śarīre nir:apekṣatvam ante ca virāmābhīpsety etad upapannam iti.
2.1.21 tac ca na. sāmānye 'pi bhrānti-saṃskāre kulāla-cakrasya bhramarakasya vā bhrāntāv eva vartamānasya prārambhe manda-vegatā tataś ca krameṇa pūraṇaṃ vegasyety upapadyate. dhātu-kṣayāc ca virāmābhīpseti. tasmād an:ākṣepaḥ.
2.1.22v suratānte sukhaṃ puṃsāṃ strīṇāṃ tu satataṃ sukham. dhātu-kṣaya-nimittā ca virāmecchopajāyate..
2.1.23 tasmāt puruṣavad eva yoṣito 'pi rasa-vyaktir draṣṭavyā.
2.1.24 kathaṃ hi samānāyām evākṛtāv ekārtham abhiprapannayoḥ kārya-vailakṣaṇyaṃ syāt.
2.1.25 upāya-vailakṣaṇyād abhimāna-vailakṣaṇyāc ca.
2.1.26 katham upāya-vailakṣaṇyaṃ tu sargāt. kartā hi puruṣo 'dhikaraṇaṃ yuvatiḥ. anyathā hi kartā kriyāṃ pratipadyate 'nyathā cādhāraḥ. tasmāc copāya-vailakṣaṇyāt sargād abhimāna-vailakṣaṇyam api bhavati. abhiyoktāham iti puruṣo 'nurajyate. abhiyuktāham aneneti yuvatir iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
2.1.27 tatraitat syād upāya-vailakṣaṇyavad eva hi kārya-vailakṣaṇyam api kasmān na syād iti. tac ca na. hetumad upāya-vailakṣaṇyam. tatra kartr-ādhārayor bhinna-lakṣaṇatvād a:hetumat-kārya-vailakṣaṇyam anyāyyaṃ syāt. ākṛter a:bhedād iti.
2.1.28 tatraitat syāt. saṃhatya kārakair eko 'rtho 'bhinirvartyate. pṛthak pṛthak svārtha-sādhakau punar imau tad a:yuktam iti.
2.1.29 tac ca na. yugapad an:ekārtha-siddhir api dṛśyate. yathā meṣayor abhighāte kapitthayor bhede mallayor yuddha iti. na tatra kāraka-bheda iti ced ihāpi na vastu-bheda iti. upāya-vailakṣaṇyaṃ tu sargād iti tad abhihitaṃ purastāt. tenobhayor api sadṛśī sukha-pratipattir iti.
2.1.30v jāter a:bhedād daṃpatyoḥ sa:dṛśam sukham iṣyate. tasmāt tathopacaryā strī yathāgre prāpnuyād ratim...2.1.31 sa:dṛśatvasya siddhatvāt kāla-yogīny api bhāvato 'pi kālataḥ pramāṇavad eva nava ratāni.
2.1.32 raso ratiḥ prītir bhāvo rāgo vegaḥ samāptir iti rati-paryāyāḥ. saṃprayogo rataṃ rahaḥ śayanaṃ mohanaṃ surata-paryāyāḥ.
2.1.33 pramāṇa-kāla-bhāva-jānāṃ saṃprayogānām ekaikasya nava-vidhatvāt teṣāṃ vyatikare surata-saṃkhyā na śakyate kartum. ati:bahutvāt.
2.1.34 teṣu tarkād upacārān prayojayed iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
2.1.35 prathama-rate caṇḍa-vegatā śīghra-kālatā ca puruṣasya tad-viparītam uttareṣu. yoṣitaḥ punar etad eva viparītam. ā dhātu-kṣayāt.
2.1.36 prāk ca strī-dhātu-kṣayāt puruṣa-dhātu-kṣaya iti prāyovādaḥ.
2.1.37v mṛdutvād upamṛdyatvān nisargāc caiva yoṣitaḥ. prāpnuvanty āśu tāḥ prītim ity ācāryā vyavasthitāḥ..
2.1.38v etāvad eva yuktānāṃ vyākhyātaṃ sāmprayogikam. mandānām avabodhārthaṃ vistaro 'taḥ pravakṣyate((7)).
children.translated_text: 2.1.1 The hare (<s>śaśa</s>), the bull (<s>vṛṣa</s>), and the stallion (<s>aśva</s>) — these are the varieties of men classified by the sexual organ. The woman, again, is the deer (<s>mṛgī</s>), the mare (<s>baḍavā</s>), and the elephant-woman (<s>hastinī</s>). 2.1.2 Among these, in a union of equals, there are three equal unions (<s>sama-rata</s>). 2.1.3 By reversal, six unequal ones. Among the unequal, if the man is larger, in an adjacent-grade union there are two 'high' unions (<s>ucca-rata</s>); with a gap of two grades, one 'highest' union (<s>ucca-tara-rata</s>). In the reverse, two 'low' unions (<s>nīca-rata</s>); with a gap, one 'lowest' union (<s>nīca-tara-rata</s>). Among these, the equal unions are best. The two marked with the comparative suffix (-<s>tara</s>) are the worst. The rest are middling. 2.1.4 Even among equal unions, the high-grade is superior to the low-grade. Thus, there are nine types of union according to size (<s>pramāṇa</s>). 2.1.5 He whose desire at the time of union is indifferent, whose vigor is slight, and who does not endure scratches — he is of mild temperament (<s>manda-vega</s>). 2.1.6 The opposite [two] are of moderate (<s>madhyama</s>) and intense (<s>caṇḍa</s>) temperament. Likewise for the woman. 2.1.7 Here too, as with size, there are nine types of union. 2.1.8 Likewise regarding duration: men are of short (<s>śīghra</s>), moderate (<s>madhya</s>), and long (<s>cira</s>) duration. 2.1.9 Regarding the woman, there is a dispute. 2.1.10 'A woman does not experience the same feeling as a man.' 2.1.11 'Rather, through continuous [stimulation], her itching is relieved by the man.' 2.1.12 'That [relief], mixed with a self-regarding pleasure, produces a different kind of experience — in that lies her sense of pleasure.' 2.1.13 'And because she is unacquainted with the man's experience, and because it is impossible to ask "How is your pleasure?"' 2.1.14 'If it is asked how this is known: a man, having attained satisfaction, stops of his own will and does not depend on the woman; but a woman does not [stop thus]' — thus says <s>Auddālika</s>. 2.1.15 In that case, this may be argued: when the man is of long duration, women become attached; failing to reach the feeling with a man of short duration, they are dissatisfied at the end. All that is a sign of attainment or non-attainment of the [same] feeling. 2.1.16 But that is not so. For the remedy for itching too is pleasant when prolonged. This is perfectly reasonable. Therefore, because of its ambiguity, it is not a conclusive sign. 2.1.17 [Verse:] In union, the man relieves the woman's itching; and that, mixed with self-regarding [pleasure], is called happiness. 2.1.18 'From continuous [stimulation], a woman attains the feeling from the very beginning; a man, however, only at the end. This is more reasonable. For without the attainment of the feeling, conception would not occur' — so say the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>. 2.1.19 Here too, those very same objection and response apply once again. 2.1.20 In that case, this may be argued: when, through continuous [stimulation], the feeling is being attained, at the beginning there is indifference of mind and low tolerance; then, gradually, an increased engagement of passion, indifference to the body, and at the end, a desire to stop — this is reasonable. 2.1.21 But that is not so. Even in the analogy of a spinning potter's wheel or a spinning top — being currently in motion — at the beginning there is slow momentum, and then gradually the momentum builds up. This is reasonable. And the desire to stop is due to the depletion of vital fluids (<s>dhātu-kṣaya</s>). Therefore, no objection stands. 2.1.22 [Verse:] For men, pleasure comes at the end of lovemaking; for women, pleasure is continuous. The desire to stop arises from the depletion of vital fluids. 2.1.23 Therefore, the manifestation of feeling in women too should be regarded as the same as in men. 2.1.24 For how could there be a difference in effect between two who, being of the same form, are engaged in the same purpose? 2.1.25 [The difference is] from the difference in the means and the difference in self-conception. 2.1.26 How is the difference in means? By nature (<s>sarga</s>). For the man is the agent and the woman is the locus. The agent engages in the action in one way, and the substrate in another. Therefore, from the difference in means which is by nature, there is also a difference in self-conception. 'I am the pursuer' — thus the man is gratified. 'I am being pursued by him' — thus the woman — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 2.1.27 In that case: just as there is a difference in means, why should there not also be a difference in effect? But that is not so. The difference in means has a cause — namely, the distinct characteristics of agent and locus. But a causeless difference in effect would be unreasonable, since there is no difference in form. 2.1.28 In that case: when agents work together, a single result is produced. But if each of these two separately achieves its own purpose, that would be unjustified. 2.1.29 But that is not so. The simultaneous accomplishment of multiple purposes is also seen — as in the collision of two rams, the splitting of two wood-apples, or the wrestling of two wrestlers. If you say there is no difference in agents in those cases, then here too there is no difference in substance. But the difference in means is by nature — that has been stated before. Therefore, the experience of pleasure is similar for both. 2.1.30 [Verse:] Because there is no difference in species between husband and wife, similar pleasure is accepted. Therefore, the woman should be treated in such a way that she attains pleasure first. 2.1.31 Since similarity has been established, according to temperament and duration as well — just as with size — there are nine types of union. 2.1.32 <s>Rasa</s> (flavor), <s>rati</s> (enjoyment), <s>prīti</s> (delight), <s>bhāva</s> (feeling), <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>vega</s> (impulse), <s>samāpti</s> (completion) — these are synonyms for sexual pleasure. <s>Saṃprayoga</s> (union), <s>rata</s> (enjoyment), <s>rahas</s> (intimacy), <s>śayana</s> (couch), <s>mohana</s> (enchantment) — these are synonyms for sexual intercourse (<s>surata</s>). 2.1.33 Since each of the types of union based on size, duration, and temperament is ninefold, their combination makes it impossible to enumerate the types of intercourse, because of their excessive multiplicity. 2.1.34 Among these, one should apply the appropriate treatments by reasoning — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 2.1.35 In the first union, the man has intense temperament and short duration; the opposite in subsequent ones. For the woman, this is reversed — until the depletion of vital fluids. 2.1.36 And generally, the depletion of the man's vital fluids occurs before the depletion of the woman's. 2.1.37 [Verse:] Because of the softness, the delicateness, and the innate nature of women, they attain pleasure quickly — so the teachers have determined. 2.1.38 [Verse:] This much has been explained regarding sexual union for those who are adept. For the understanding of the less adept, the detailed exposition will now be set forth.

children.text:
2.1.39v abhyāsād abhimānāc ca tathā saṃpratyayād api. viṣayebhyaś ca tantra-jñāḥ prītim āhuś catur-vidhām..
2.1.40v śabdādibhyo bahir:bhūtā yā karmābhyāsa-lakṣaṇā. prītiḥ sābhyāsikī jñeyā mṛgayādiṣu karmasu..
2.1.41v an:abhyasteṣv api purā karmasv a:viṣayātmikā. saṃkalpāj jāyate prītir yā sā syād ābhimānikī..
2.1.42v prakṛter yā tṛtīyasyāḥ striyāś caivopariṣṭake. teṣu teṣu ca vijñeyā cumabanādiṣu karmasu..
2.1.43v nānyo 'yam iti yatra syād anyasmin prīti-kāraṇe. tantra-jñaiḥ kathyate sāpi prītiḥ saṃpratyayātmikā..
2.1.44v pratyakṣā lokataḥ siddhā yā prītir viṣayātmikā. pradhāna-phalavattvāt sā tad-arthāś cetarā api..
2.1.45v prītīr etāḥ parāmṛśya śāstrataḥ śāstra-lakṣaṇāḥ. yo yathā vartate bhāvas taṃ tathaiva prayojayet((8))..
children.translated_text: 2.1.39 [Verse:] The knowers of the science declare that pleasure (<s>prīti</s>) is fourfold: arising from practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>), from self-conception (<s>abhimāna</s>), from conviction (<s>saṃpratyaya</s>), and from sense-objects (<s>viṣaya</s>). 2.1.40 [Verse:] That pleasure which is external to sounds and other [sensory objects], characterized by habitual practice — that is to be known as arising from practice, as in activities like hunting. 2.1.41 [Verse:] Even in activities not previously practiced, having no direct relation to sense-objects, pleasure arises from imagination — that is from self-conception. 2.1.42 [Verse:] Of the third type of nature, and in the woman's acting the man's part (<s>upariṣṭaka</s>), and in those various activities like kissing and so forth — [pleasure arising from conviction] should be known. 2.1.43 [Verse:] Where the thought 'there is no other [cause of pleasure] than this' arises regarding a particular cause of pleasure — that too is declared by the knowers of the science as pleasure arising from conviction. 2.1.44 [Verse:] That pleasure which is perceptible and established among ordinary people, arising from sense-objects — because it yields the chief fruit, it [is primary], and the others are for its sake. 2.1.45 [Verse:] Having examined these pleasures, which are characterized by the treatise, one should apply the appropriate feeling as it occurs.

children.text: 2.1c iti śrīvātyāyanīye kāmasūtre sāṃprayogike dvitīye 'dhikaraṇe pramāṇa-kāla-bhāvebhyo ratāvasthāpanaṃ prīti-viśeṣā iti prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ. āditaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ((9)).
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the second section <s>Sāṃprayogika</s> (On Sexual Union), the chapter on Classification of Types of Union by Size, Duration, and Temperament, and Varieties of Affection — the first chapter. The sixth from the beginning.

children.translated_text: Lesson 2, Second Chapter. Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 8: Discussion of Embraces (<s>āliṅgana-vicāra-prakaraṇam</s>).

children.text:
2.2.1 saṃprayogāṅgaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭir ity ācakṣate. catuḥṣaṣṭi-prakaraṇatvāt.
2.2.2 śāstram evedaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭir ity ācārya-vādaḥ.
2.2.3 kalānāṃ catuḥṣaṣṭitvāt tāsāṃ ca saṃprayogāṅga-bhūtatvāt kalā-samūho vā catuḥṣaṣṭir iti. ṛcāṃ daśatayīnāṃ ca saṃjñitatvāt. ihāpi tad-artha-saṃbandhāt. pañcāla-saṃbandhāc ca bahv-ṛcair eṣā pūjārthaṃ saṃjñā pravartitā ity eke.
2.2.4 āliṅgana-cumbana-nakha-cchedya-daśana-cchedya-saṃveśana-sīt:kṛta-puruṣāyitaupariṣṭakānām āṣṭānām aṣṭadhā vikalpa-bhedād aṣṭāv aṣṭakāś catuḥṣaṣṭir iti bābhravīyāḥ.
2.2.5 vikalpa-vargāṇām aṣṭānāṃ nyūnādikatva-darśanāt prahaṇa-viruta-puruṣopasṛpti-citra-ratādīnām anyeṣām api vargāṇām iha praveśanāt prāyo-vādo 'yam. yathā sapta-parṇo vṛkṣaḥ pañca-varṇo balir iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
2.2.6 tatrā:samāgatayoḥ prīti-liṅga-dyotanārtham āliṅgana-catuṣṭayam. [1] spṛṣṭakam [2] viddhakam [3] udghṛṣṭakam [4] pīḍitakam iti.
2.2.7 sarvatra saṃjñārthenaiva karmātideśaḥ.
2.2.8 saṃmukhāgatāyāṃ prayojyāyām anyāpadeśena gacchato gātreṇa gātrasya sparśanaṃ [1] spṛṣṭakam.
2.2.9 prayojyaṃ sthitam upaviṣṭaṃ vā vi:jane kiṃ cid gṛhṇāti payo-dhareṇa viddhyet. nāyako 'pi tām avapīḍya gṛhṇīyād iti [2] viddhakam.
2.2.10 tad ubhayam an:ati:pravṛtta-saṃbhāṣaṇayoḥ.
2.2.11 tamasi jana-saṃbādhe vi:jane vātha śanakair gacchator nāti:hrasva-kālam udgharṣaṇaṃ paras-parasya gātrāṇām [3] udghṛṣṭakam.
2.2.12 tad eva kuḍya-saṃdeśena stambha-saṃdeśena vā sphuṭakam avapīḍayed iti [4] pīḍitakam.
2.2.13 tad ubhayam avagata-parasparākārayoḥ.
2.2.14 [1] latāveṣṭitakaṃ [2] vṛkṣādhirūḍhakaṃ [3] tila-taṇḍulakaṃ [4] kṣīra-nīrakam iti catvāri saṃprayoga-kāle..2.2.15 lateva śālam āveṣṭayantī cumbanārthaṃ mukham avanamayet. uddhṛtya manda-sītkṛtā tam āśritā vā kiṃcid rāmaṇīyakaṃ paśyet tal [1] latāveṣṭitakam.
2.2.16 caraṇena caraṇam ākramya dvitīyenoru-deśam ākramantī veṣṭayantī vā tat-pṛṣṭha-saktaika- bāhur dvitīyenāṃsam avanamayantī īṣan manda-sītkṛta-kūjitā cumabanārtham evādhiroḍhum icched iti [2] vṛkṣādhirūḍhakam.
2.2.17 tad ubhayam sthita-karma.
2.2.18 śayana-gatāv evoru-vyatyāsaṃ bhuja-vyatyāsaṃ ca sa:saṃgharṣam iva ghanaṃ saṃsvajete tat [3] tila-taṇḍulakam.
2.2.19 rāgāndhāv an:apekṣitātyayau parasparam anuviśata ivotsaṅga-gatāyām abhimukhopaviṣṭāyāṃ śayane veti [4] kṣīra-jalakam.
2.2.20 tad ubhayaṃ rāga-kāle.
2.2.21 ity upagūhana-yogā bābhravīyāḥ.
2.2.22 suvarṇanābhasya tv adhikam ekāṅgopagūhana-catuṣṭayam.
2.2.23 tatroru-saṃdaṃśenaikam ūrum ūrudvayaṃ vā sarvaprāṇaṃ pīḍayed ity ūrūpagūhanam[1].
2.2.24 jaghanena jaghanam avapīḍya prakīryamāṇa-keśa-hastā nakha-daśana-prahaṇana-cumbana- prayojanāya tad upari laṅghayet taj jaghanopagūhanam[2].
2.2.25 stanābhyām uraḥ praviśya tatraiva bhāram āropayed iti stanāliṅganam[3].
2.2.26 mukhe mukham āsajyākṣiṇī akṣṇor lalāṭena lalāṭam āhanyāt sālalāṭikā[4].
2.2.27 saṃvāhanam apy upagūhana-prakāram ity eke manyante. saṃsparśatvāt.
2.2.28 pṛthak-kālatvād bhinna-prayojanatvād a:sādhāraṇatvān neti vātsyāyanaḥ
2.2.29v pṛcchatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ vāpi tathā kathayatām api. upagūha-vidhiṃ kṛtsnaṃ riraṃsā jāyate nṛṇām..
2.2.30v ye 'pi hy a:śāstritāḥ kecit saṃyogā rāga-vardhanāḥ. ādareṇaiva te 'py atra prayojyāḥ sāṃprayogikāḥ..
2.2.31v śāstrāṇāṃ viṣayas tāvad yāvan manda-rasā narāḥ. raticakre-pravṛtte tu naiva śāstram na ca kramaḥ..
children.translated_text: 2.2.1 They say that the sixty-four [arts] are a component of sexual union — because there are sixty-four sections. 2.2.2 The teachers' view is that this very treatise is called 'the sixty-four.' 2.2.3 Because there are sixty-four arts, and because those arts are component parts of union, the collection of arts may be called 'the sixty-four.' And because the hymns of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> are designated in groups of ten, here too, by virtue of that thematic connection, and because of the connection with <s>Pāñcāla</s>, this designation was introduced by the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> for the purpose of veneration — so say some. 2.2.4 [The classification of] the eight — embracing, kissing, scratching, biting, modes of lying down, the hissing sound (<s>sītkṛta</s>), the woman playing the man's part, and <s>aupariṣṭaka</s> (oral union) — each having eightfold subdivisions, makes eight eights, [equaling] sixty-four: so say the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>. 2.2.5 Since the eight groups of subdivisions are seen to have fewer or more [than eight each], and since other groups too — such as striking, cries, the man's approach, and <s>citrarata</s> (unusual positions) — are included here, this [designation of sixty-four] is merely approximate, just as [one speaks of] 'the seven-leaved tree' or 'the five-colored offering' — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 2.2.6 There, for those who have not yet come together, four kinds of embraces serve to indicate the signs of affection: [1] <s>Spṛṣṭaka</s> (the touching), [2] <s>Viddhaka</s> (the piercing), [3] <s>Udghṛṣṭaka</s> (the rubbing), [4] <s>Pīḍitaka</s> (the pressing). 2.2.7 In every case, the prescribed act is transferred [to practice] simply by its designation. 2.2.8 When the desired woman approaches face-to-face and [the man], under some pretext of passing by, touches her body with his body — that is [1] <s>Spṛṣṭaka</s> (the touching). 2.2.9 The desired woman, standing or sitting in a secluded place, reaches for something, and [the man] presses against her with his breast. The hero too should seize and press her — that is [2] <s>Viddhaka</s> (the piercing). 2.2.10 These two [are appropriate] for those who have not yet engaged in intimate conversation. 2.2.11 In the dark, in a crowd of people, or in a secluded place, as they walk slowly together, the rubbing of each other's bodies for a not-too-brief duration — that is [3] <s>Udghṛṣṭaka</s> (the rubbing). 2.2.12 That very same [embrace], when one presses the other firmly against a wall or a pillar — that is [4] <s>Pīḍitaka</s> (the pressing). 2.2.13 These two [are appropriate] for those who have recognized each other's feelings. 2.2.14 Four [embraces] at the time of union: [1] <s>Latāveṣṭitaka</s> (the twining of a creeper), [2] <s>Vṛkṣādhirūḍhaka</s> (climbing a tree), [3] <s>Tila-taṇḍulaka</s> (sesame and rice), [4] <s>Kṣīra-nīraka</s> (milk and water). 2.2.15 Entwining him like a creeper around a <s>śāla</s> tree, she bends down his face for a kiss; or, having lifted herself up, emitting a soft hissing sound, she leans on him and looks at something charming — that is [1] <s>Latāveṣṭitaka</s> (the twining of a creeper). 2.2.16 Stepping on one of his feet with one of hers, and with the other climbing upon or entwining his thigh, one arm clinging to his back, with the other pulling down his shoulder, softly hissing and cooing, she desires to climb upon him as if for a kiss — that is [2] <s>Vṛkṣādhirūḍhaka</s> (climbing a tree). 2.2.17 Both of these are performed while standing. 2.2.18 While lying down, entwining thighs with thighs and arms with arms, they embrace each other tightly as if with friction — that is [3] <s>Tila-taṇḍulaka</s> (sesame and rice). 2.2.19 Blinded by passion, heedless of any harm, they seem to enter into each other — whether she is seated on his lap facing him, or on the bed — that is [4] <s>Kṣīra-jalaka</s> (milk and water). 2.2.20 Both of these [are performed] during the time of passion. 2.2.21 Thus are the varieties of embrace according to the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>. 2.2.22 But according to <s>Suvarṇanābha</s>, there are additionally four single-limb embraces: 2.2.23 There, [1] the thigh-embrace: pressing one thigh, or both thighs, with the clamp of the thighs, with all one's strength. 2.2.24 [2] The hip-embrace: pressing hip against hip, with hair let loose and hands free, she mounts upon him for the purpose of scratching, biting, striking, and kissing. 2.2.25 [3] The breast-embrace: pressing the chest with both breasts and placing her weight there. 2.2.26 [4] <s>Sālalāṭikā</s>: placing mouth upon mouth, eyes upon eyes, and pressing forehead against forehead. 2.2.27 Some consider that massage (<s>saṃvāhana</s>) too is a form of embrace, because it involves bodily contact. 2.2.28 [But it is] not [an embrace], because it occurs at a different time, serves a different purpose, and is not shared [in the same way] — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 2.2.29v [Verse:] Whether asking about, hearing about, or even speaking of the complete method of embracing — desire arises in men. 2.2.30v Even those unions that are not prescribed in the treatise but that increase passion — those too should be carefully employed in the practice of love. 2.2.31v The domain of the treatises extends only so long as the passion of men is mild; but once the wheel of passion has begun to turn, there is neither treatise nor sequence.
