2.3.1 cumbana-nakha-daśana-cchedyānāṃ na paurvāparyam asti. rāga-yogāt prāk saṃyogād eṣāṃ prādhāyena prayogaḥ. prahaṇa-sītkṛtayoś ca saṃprayoge.
2.3.2 sarvaṃ sarvatra. rāgasyān:apekṣitatvāt. iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
2.3.3 tāni prathama-rate nātivyaktāni viśrabdhikāyāṃ vikalpena ca prayuñjīta. tathā-bhūtatvād rāgasya. tataḥ param atitvarayā viśeṣavat samuccayena rāga-saṃdhukṣaṇārtham.
2.3.4 lalāṭālaka-kapola-nayana-vakṣaḥ-stanoṣṭhāntar:mukheṣu cumbanam.
2.3.5 ūru-saṃdhi-bāhu-nābhi-mūlayor lāṭānām.
2.3.6 rāga-vaśād deśa-pravṛtteś ca santi tāni tāni sthānāni na tu sarva-jana-prayojānīti vātsyāyanaḥ.
2.3.7 tad yathā ṇ [1] nimittikaṃ [2] sphuritakaṃ [3] ghaṭṭitakam iti trīṇi kanyā-cumbanāni.
2.3.8 balāt-kāreṇa niyuktā mukham ādhatte na tu viceṣṭata iti [1] nimittakam.
2.3.9 vadane praveśitaṃ cauṣṭhaṃ manāg apatrapāvagrahītum icchantī spandayati svam oṣṭhaṃ nottaram utsahata iti [2] sphuritakam.
2.3.10 īṣat parigṛhya vi:nimīlita-nayanā kareṇa ca tasya nayane avacchādayanti jihvāgreṇa ghaṭṭayatīti [3] ghaṭṭitakam.
2.3.11 samaṃ tiryag udbhrāntam avapīḍitakam iti caturvidham apare.
2.3.12 aṅguli-saṃpuṭena piṇḍī-kṛtya nirdaśanam oṣṭha-puṭenāvapīḍayed ity avapīḍitakaṃ pañcamam api karaṇam.
2.3.13 dyūtaṃ cātra pravartayet.
2.3.14 pūrvam adhara-saṃpādanena jitam idaṃ syāt.
2.3.15 tatra jitā sārdha-ruditaṃ karaṃ vidhunuyāt praṇuded daśet parivartayed balād āhṛtā vivadet punar apy astu paṇa iti brūyāt. tatrāpi jitā dvi-guṇam āyasyaet.
2.3.16 viśrabdhasya pramattasya vādharam avagṛhya daśanāntargatam a:nirgamaṃ kṛtvā hased utkriśet tarjayed valged āhlayet pranartitat-bhrūṇā ca vicala-nayanena mukhena vihasantītāni tāni ca brūyāt. iti cumbana-dyūta-kalahaḥ.
2.3.17 etena nakha-daśana-cchedya-prahaṇana-dyūta-kalahā vyākhyātāḥ.
2.3.18 caṇḍa-vegayor eva tv eṣāṃ prayogaḥ. tat-sātmyāt.
2.3.19 tasyāṃ cumbantyām ayam apy uttaraṃ gṛhṇīyāt. ity uttara-cumbitam..2.3.20 oṣṭha-saṃdaṃśenāvagṛhyāuṣṭha-dvayam api cumbeta. iti saṃpuṭakaṃ striyāḥ puṃso vā:jāta-vyañjanasya.
2.3.21 tasminn itaro 'pi jihvayāsyā daśanān ghaṭṭayet tālu jihvāṃ ceti jihvā-yuddham.
2.3.22 etena balād vadana-radana-grahaṇaṃ dānaṃ ca vyākhyātam.
2.3.23 samaṃ pīḍitam añcitaṃ mṛdu śeṣāṅgeṣu cumbanaṃ sthāna-viśeṣa-yogāt. iti cumbana-viśeṣāḥ.
2.3.24 suptasaya mukham avalokayantyā svābhiprāyeṇa cumbanaṃ rāga-dīpanam.
2.3.25 pramattasya vivadamānasya vānyato 'bhimukhasya suptābhimukhasya vā nidrā-vyāghātārthaṃ calitakam.
2.3.26 cira-rātrāv āgatasya śayana-suptāyāḥ svābhiprāya-cumbanaṃ prātibodhakam.
2.3.27 sāpi tu bhāva-jijñāsārthinī nāyakasyāgamana-kālaṃ saṃlakṣya vyājena suptā syāt.
2.3.28 ādarśe kuḍye salile vā prayojyāyāś chāyā-cumbanam ākāra-pradarśanārtham eva kāryam.
2.3.29 bālasya citra-karmaṇaḥ pratimāyāś ca cumbanaṃ saṃkrāntakam āliṅganaṃ ca.
2.3.30 tathā niśi prekṣaṇake svajana-samāje vā samīpe gatasya prayojyāyā hastāṅguli-cumbanaṃ saṃviṣṭasya vā pādāṅguli-cumbanam.
2.3.31 saṃvāhikāyās tu nāyakam ākārayantyā nidrā-vaśād a:kāmāyā iva tasyorvor vadanasya nidhānam ūru-cumbanaṃ cety ābhiyogikāni.
2.3.32 bhavati cātra ślokaḥ.
2.3.32v kṛte pratikṛtaṃ kuryād tāḍite pratitāḍitam. karaṇena ca tenaiva cumbite praticumbitam..
children.translated_text:
2.3.1 There is no fixed sequence for kissing, nail-marks, biting, and cutting. Due to the force of passion, their application is predominantly before sexual union. Striking and hissing sounds [occur] during intercourse.
2.3.2 Everything [applies] everywhere, because passion is indifferent [to sequence] — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
2.3.3 In the first act of lovemaking, these should not be too pronounced; during intimate familiarity, they should be applied with variation — such is the nature of passion. Thereafter, with great haste, applied distinctively and in combination, for the purpose of kindling passion.
2.3.4 Kissing [is applied] on the forehead, the hair-part, the cheeks, the eyes, the chest, the breasts, the lips, and the interior of the mouth.
2.3.5 [Also] on the junction of the thighs, the arms, and the navel — among the people of <s>Lāṭa</s>.
2.3.6 Due to the force of passion and regional customs, there are various [other] places, but these are not applicable to everyone — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
2.3.7 These are the three maiden's kisses: [1] <s>nimittaka</s> (nominal), [2] <s>sphuritaka</s> (throbbing), [3] <s>ghaṭṭitaka</s> (touching).
2.3.8 When compelled by force, she places her mouth [on his] but does not move — that is [1] <s>nimittaka</s> (nominal).
2.3.9 When the lip placed in her mouth, wishing slightly bashfully to grasp it, she moves her own lip but does not dare [to take] the upper [lip] — that is [2] <s>sphuritaka</s> (throbbing).
2.3.10 When, slightly grasping [the lip], with eyes closed, covering his eyes with her hand, she touches with the tip of her tongue — that is [3] <s>ghaṭṭitaka</s> (touching).
2.3.11 Others [classify kisses as] four kinds: <s>sama</s> (even), <s>tiryak</s> (oblique), <s>udbhrānta</s> (turned up), and <s>avapīḍitaka</s> (pressed).
2.3.12 Gathering [the lip] into a ball with the cup of the fingers and pressing it with the lip — this <s>avapīḍitaka</s> is also a fifth technique.
2.3.13 And here one should initiate a kissing game.
2.3.14 The one who first captures the lower lip wins.
2.3.15 The one defeated there should, half-crying, shake her hand, push away, bite, turn over, and when forcibly seized, quarrel and say 'Let the wager be again.' If defeated there too, she should redouble her efforts.
2.3.16 Seizing the lower lip of the trusting or inattentive one, trapping it between the teeth so it cannot escape, she should laugh, cry out, threaten, leap, be delighted, dance with her eyebrows, and with rolling eyes and laughing face, say this and that — thus is the kissing wager-quarrel.
2.3.17 By this, the wager-quarrels of nail-marks, biting, cutting, and striking are explained.
2.3.18 But the application of these is only for those of fierce and impetuous temperament, due to their compatibility with it.
2.3.19 When she kisses, he too should take the reciprocal [kiss] — thus is the reciprocal kiss (<s>uttara-cumbita</s>).
2.3.20 Grasping with the lip-clasp, one should kiss both lips — this is <s>saṃpuṭaka</s> (clasped kiss), [performed] by a woman or by a man without a beard.
2.3.21 In that [clasped kiss], the other should also touch her teeth, palate, and tongue with his tongue — thus is the tongue-battle (<s>jihvā-yuddha</s>).
2.3.22 By this, the forcible seizing of the face and teeth, and the giving [in return], are explained.
2.3.23 <s>Sama</s> (even), <s>pīḍita</s> (pressed), <s>añcita</s> (arched), and <s>mṛdu</s> (soft) — kissing on the other limbs varies according to the specific location. Thus are the varieties of kissing.
2.3.24 Looking at the face of the sleeping [beloved] and kissing according to one's desire — this kindles passion (<s>rāga-dīpana</s>).
2.3.25 [Kissing] one who is inattentive, quarreling, turned the other way, or lying face-up asleep, for the purpose of disrupting sleep — this is <s>calitaka</s> (stirring).
2.3.26 When he returns late at night and she is sleeping on the bed, kissing according to his desire to awaken her — this is <s>prātibodhaka</s> (awakening).
2.3.27 And she, wishing to ascertain his feelings, observing the time of the lover's arrival, should pretend to be asleep.
2.3.28 Kissing the shadow [of the beloved] in a mirror, on a wall, or in water — this should be done to reveal one's desire.
2.3.29 Kissing a child, a painting, or a statue — this is <s>saṃkrāntaka</s> (transferred), and so too [transferred] embracing.
2.3.30 Similarly, at night during a performance or in a gathering of one's own people, when [the beloved] has come near, kissing the fingers of the beloved's hand, or when lying together, kissing the toes.
2.3.31 And when a masseuse, while making her feelings known to the lover, as if unwilling due to drowsiness, places her face on his thigh and kisses the thigh — these are <s>ābhiyogika</s> (amorous overtures).
2.3.32 And here there is a verse:
2.3.32v When something is done [to one], one should do it in return; when struck, one should strike back; and with the same technique, when kissed, one should kiss back.

children.text:
2.4.1 rāga-vṛddhau saṃgharṣātmakaṃ nakha-vilekhanam.
2.4.2 tasya prathama-samāgame pravāsa-pratyāgamane pravāsa-gamane kruddha-prasannāyāṃ mattāyāṃ ca prayogaḥ. na nityam a:caṇḍa-vegayoḥ.
2.4.3 tathā daśana-cchedyasya sātmya-vaśād vā.
2.4.4 tad [1] ācchuritakam [2] ardha-candro [3] maṇḍalaṃ [4] rekhā [5] vyāghra-nakhaṃ [6] mayūra-padakaṃ [7] śaśa-plutakam [8] utpala-pattrakam iti rūpato 'ṣṭa-vikalpam.
2.4.5 kakṣau stanau galaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ jaghanam ūrū ca sthānāni.
2.4.6 pravṛtta-rati-cakrāṇāṃ na sthānam a:sthānaṃ vā vidyata iti suvarṇanābhaḥ.
2.4.7 tatra savya-hastāni praty:agra-śikharāṇi dvi-tri-śikharāṇi caṇḍa-vegayor nakhāni syuḥ.
2.4.8 anugata-rāji samam ujjvalam a:malinam a:vipāṭitaṃ vivardhiṣṇu mṛdu snigdha-darśanam iti nakha-guṇāḥ.
2.4.9 dīrghāṇi hasta-śobhīny āloke ca yoṣitāṃ citta-grāhīṇi gauḍāṇāṃ nakhāni syuḥ.
2.4.10 hrasvāni karma-sahiṣṇūni vikalpa-yojanāsu ca svecchāpātīni dākṣiṇatyānām.
2.4.11 madhyamāny ubhaya-bhāñji mahārāṣṭrakāṇām iti.
2.4.12 taiḥ su:niyamitair hanu-deśe stanayor adhare vā laghu-karaṇam an:udgata-lekhaṃ sparśa-mātra-jananād romāñca-karam ante saṃnipāta-vardhamāna-śabdam [1] ācchuritakam.
2.4.13 prayojyāyāṃ ca tasyāṅga-saṃvāhane śirasaḥ kaṇḍūyane piṭaka-bhedane vyākulī-karaṇe bhīṣaṇena prayogaḥ.
2.4.14 grīvāyāṃ stana-pṛṣṭhe ca vakro nakha-pada-niveśo [2] ardha-candraḥ.
2.4.15 tāv eva dvau parsa-parābhimukhau maṇḍalam.
2.4.16 nābhi-mūla-kakundara-vaṃkṣaṇeṣu((10)) tasya prayogaḥ.
2.4.17 sarva-sthāneṣu nāti:dīrghā [4] lekhā((11)).
2.4.18 saiva vakrā [5] vyāghra-nakhakam ā stana-mukham.
2.4.19 pañcabhir abhimukhair lekhā cūcukābhimukhī((12)) [6] mayūra-padakam.
2.4.20 tat-saṃprayoga-ślāghāyāḥ stana-cūcuke saṃnikṛṣṭāni pañca-nakha-padāni [7] śaśa-plutakam.
2.4.21 stana-pṛṣṭhe mekhalā-pathe cotpala-pattrākṛtīty [8] utpala-pattrakam.
2.4.22 ūrvoḥ stana-pṛṣṭhe ca pravāsaṃ gacchataḥ smāraṇīyakaṃ saṃhatāś catasras tisro vā lekhāḥ.
2.4.22c iti nakha-karmāṇi.
2.4.23 ākṛti-vikāra-yuktāni cānyāny api kurvīta.
2.4.24 vikalpānām an:antatvād ānantyāc ca kauśala-vidher abhyāsasya ca sarva-gāmitvād rāgātmakatvāc chedyasya prakārān ko 'bhisamīkṣitum arhatīty ācāryāḥ..2.4.25 bhavati hi rāge 'pi citrāpekṣā. vaicitryāc ca parasparaṃ rāgo janayitavyaḥ. vaicakṣaṇya-yuktāś ca gaṇikās tat-kāminaś ca parasparaṃ prārthanīyā bhavanti. dhanur-vedādiṣv api hi śastra-karma-śāstreṣu vaicitryam evāpekṣyate kiṃ punar iheti vātsyāyanaḥ.
2.4.26 na tu para-parigṛhītāsv evaṃ kuryāt. pracchanneṣu pradeśeṣu tāsām anusmaraṇārthaṃ rāga-vardhanāc ca viśeṣān darśayet.
2.4.27v nakha-kṣatāni paśyantyā gūḍha-sthāneṣu yoṣitaḥ. cirotsṛṣṭāpy abhinavā prītir bhavati peśalā((13))..
2.4.28v cirosṛṣṭeṣu rāgeṣu prītir gacchet parābhavam. rāgāyatana-saṃsmāri yadi na syān nakha-kṣatam..
2.4.29v paśyato yuvatiṃ dūrān nakhocchiṣṭa-payodharām. bahu-mānaḥ parasyāpi rāga-yogaś ca jāyate..
2.4.30v puruṣaś ca pradeśeṣu nakha-cihnair vicihnitaḥ. cittaṃ sthiram api prāyaś calayaty eva yoṣitaḥ..
2.4.31v nānyat paṭutaraṃ kiṃ cid asti rāga-vivardhanam. nakha-danta-samutthānāṃ karmaṇāṃ gatayo yathā.
children.translated_text: 2.4.1 When passion increases, nail-scratching, which is of the nature of rubbing, [is employed]. 2.4.2 Its application is: at the first meeting, upon return from a journey, upon departure for a journey, when an angry woman is placated, and when she is intoxicated. Not constantly, and not for those of gentle temperament. 2.4.3 Likewise for biting — or according to habituation. 2.4.4 It is of eight varieties by form: [1] <s>ācchuritaka</s> (sounding), [2] <s>ardha-candra</s> (half-moon), [3] <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle), [4] <s>rekhā</s> (line), [5] <s>vyāghra-nakha</s> (tiger's claw), [6] <s>mayūra-padaka</s> (peacock's foot), [7] <s>śaśa-plutaka</s> (hare's leap), and [8] <s>utpala-pattraka</s> (blue lotus petal). 2.4.5 The armpits, breasts, throat, back, buttocks, and thighs are the locations. 2.4.6 For those engaged in the wheel of passion, there is no proper or improper location — says <s>Suvarṇanābha</s>. 2.4.7 The nails should be of the left hand, with freshly pointed tips, two-pointed or three-pointed, for those of intense temperament. 2.4.8 The qualities of nails are: with even lines, smooth, bright, clean, unbroken, growing well, soft, and pleasant to look at. 2.4.9 The nails of people from <s>Gauḍa</s> (Bengal) should be long, beautifying the hand, and captivating to women's minds. 2.4.10 Those of the <s>Dākṣiṇātyas</s> (Southerners) should be short, capable of withstanding use, and falling freely into various arrangements. 2.4.11 Those of the <s>Mahārāṣṭrakas</s> should be of medium length, combining both qualities. 2.4.12 With well-controlled [nails], a light pressing on the chin, breasts, or lower lip that leaves no visible mark but produces goosebumps from touch alone, with a sound increasing at the climax — [this is] <s>ācchuritaka</s> (sounding). 2.4.13 Its use is also: during body-massage of the beloved, head-scratching, breaking a pimple, agitation, and with an element of playful alarm. 2.4.14 A curved nail-mark impression on the neck and the upper part of the breast is [the] <s>ardha-candra</s> (half-moon). 2.4.15 Two of those facing each other is <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle). 2.4.16 Its application is on the navel, the base of the waist, and the groin. 2.4.17 A not-too-long [mark] in all places is <s>rekhā</s> (line). 2.4.18 That same [line] curved up to the nipple is <s>vyāghra-nakha</s> (tiger's claw). 2.4.19 A line made by five nails directed toward the nipple is <s>mayūra-padaka</s> (peacock's foot). 2.4.20 Five nail-marks placed close together on the breast-nipple, for the purpose of praising the act of union, is <s>śaśa-plutaka</s> (hare's leap). 2.4.21 A mark in the shape of a blue lotus petal on the upper breast and along the girdle-path is <s>utpala-pattraka</s> (blue lotus petal). 2.4.22 Three or four combined lines on the thighs and upper breast serve as a memento for one departing on a journey. 2.4.22c Thus, the nail-marks. 2.4.23 One should also create other [marks] with variations of form. 2.4.24 Since the variations are endless, and since artistic skill knows no limit, and since practice extends to all, and since scratching is by nature passionate — who is competent to enumerate all its forms? — say the teachers. 2.4.25 For even in passion there is regard for variety. And from variety, mutual passion should be generated. Those courtesans who possess such dexterity, and those who desire them, become mutually sought after. For even in archery and other weapon-arts, variety alone is desired — how much more so here! — says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 2.4.26 But one should not do this to married women [of others]. On concealed parts of their bodies, one should show special marks for the purpose of remembrance and for increasing passion. 2.4.27 (verse) When a woman sees nail-marks on hidden parts of her body, even affection long abandoned is renewed, becoming fresh and delicate. 2.4.28 (verse) In passions long relinquished, affection would decline to insignificance, if there were no nail-marks evoking the seat of passion. 2.4.29 (verse) Seeing from afar a young woman with breasts marked by nails, even in another man, great respect and a stirring of passion arise. 2.4.30 (verse) A man marked with nail-signs on [various] parts of his body usually agitates the mind of a woman, even one that is firmly set. 2.4.31 (verse) There is nothing else as potent for increasing passion as the various effects of actions arising from nails and teeth.

children.translated_text: 2.5.1 Excluding the upper lip, the interior of the mouth, and the eye, the locations for biting are the same as for kissing. 2.5.2 The qualities of teeth are: even, with a smooth sheen, receptive to color, of proper proportion, without gaps, with sharp tips. 2.5.3 And the defects are: blunt, with uneven ridges, rough, uneven, smooth, wide, and widely spaced. 2.5.4 The varieties of biting are eight: [1] <s>gūḍhaka</s> (hidden), [2] <s>ucchūnaka</s> (swollen), [3] <s>bindu</s> (point), [4] <s>bindu-mālā</s> (chain of points), [5] <s>pravāla-maṇi</s> (coral jewel), [6] <s>maṇi-mālā</s> (jewel chain), [7] <s>khaṇḍābhraka</s> (broken cloud), and [8] <s>varāha-carvitaka</s> (boar's chewing). 2.5.5 [A mark] not too red, with only a tinge of color, is <s>gūḍhaka</s> (hidden). 2.5.6 That same, through pressing, [becomes] <s>ucchūnaka</s> (swollen). 2.5.7 Both of these, [when applied as] a dot on the middle of the lower lip, [are called <s>bindu</s> (point)]. 2.5.8 <s>Ucchūnaka</s> and <s>pravāla-maṇi</s> [are placed] on the cheek. 2.5.9 Kissing the ear-ornament, and nail and bite marks are the adornments of the left cheek. 2.5.10 The <s>pravāla-maṇi</s> (coral jewel) is achieved through the practiced application of lips and teeth together. 2.5.11 This [technique] applies to all, and to <s>maṇi-mālā</s> (jewel chain) as well. 2.5.12 The <s>bindu</s> (point) is achieved by the pinching of a small area of skin between two teeth. 2.5.13 With all [teeth], [one achieves] the <s>bindu-mālā</s> (chain of points). 2.5.14 Therefore both chains [bindu-mālā and maṇi-mālā apply] to the throat, armpits, and groin. 2.5.15 On the forehead and thighs, [apply] the <s>bindu-mālā</s>. 2.5.16 A circle-like [mark] with uneven, peaked [impressions] is <s>khaṇḍābhraka</s> (broken cloud) — on the upper breast only. 2.5.17 Dense, elongated, numerous tooth-mark lines with reddish intervals are <s>varāha-carvitaka</s> (boar's chewing) — on the upper breast only. 2.5.18 Both of these [last two] are for those of intense temperament. 2.5.18c Thus, the kinds of biting. 2.5.19 On a <s>viśeṣaka</s> (forehead ornament), an ear-ornament, a flower-corsage, a betel leaf, or a <s>tamāla</s> leaf — for the beloved who is approaching — nail-marks, bite-marks, and the like are tokens of courtship.

children.translated_text: 2.5.20 One should also approach women according to the customs of their region. 2.5.21 Women of <s>Madhyadeśa</s> (the central region) are mostly refined, of clean habits, and averse to kissing, nail-marks, bite-marks, and [love-]scratches. 2.5.22 Likewise women of <s>Bāhlīka</s> and <s>Āvanti</s>. 2.5.23 But they are fond of unusual forms of union (<s>citra-rata</s>). 2.5.24 Women of <s>Mālava</s> and <s>Ābhīra</s> are given to embracing, kissing, nail-marks, bite-marks, and sucking, but avoid scratching, and are amenable to striking. 2.5.25 Women dwelling between the <s>Sindhu</s> and the six rivers [of Punjab] are accustomed to <s>aupariṣṭaka</s> (oral union). 2.5.26 Women of <s>Aparānta</s> and <s>Lāṭa</s> are of violent passion but utter only gentle sighs. 2.5.27 Women of <s>Strīrājya</s> (the 'kingdom of women') and <s>Kośala</s> are fond of vigorous striking, of harsh passion indeed, and given to the use of artificial devices. 2.5.28 Women of <s>Āndhra</s> are naturally tender, fond of sexual pleasure, of unclean tastes, and without refinement. 2.5.29 Women of <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s> are passionate for all sixty-four practices, fond of vulgar and harsh words, and in bed are of impetuous approach. 2.5.30 Women of the cities (<s>nāgarikā</s>) are of exactly the same kind but reveal themselves only in private. 2.5.31 Women of <s>Drāviḍa</s>, when being caressed, only slowly and gradually release their passion. 2.5.32 Women of <s>Vānavāsī</s> are of moderate passion, tolerant of everything, concealing their own body, laughing at others' bodies, and avoiding base, vulgar, and harsh [words]. 2.5.33 Women of <s>Gauḍa</s> are soft-spoken, affectionate, and of tender body. 2.5.34 <s>Suvarṇanābha</s> says: natural temperament is stronger than regional custom. Therefore, regional practices [should not be rigidly followed]. 2.5.35 And one should know that over time, customs in dress, manners, and play travel from one region to another. 2.5.36 In embracing and other [practices], the increase of passion [should be gradual] — the earlier [acts] being varied, and the later ones more intense. 2.5.37 (verse) What a man does while being resisted — after that, [she bears] the mark [of it]. Being unable to endure it, she should reciprocate double that same [act]. 2.5.38 (verse) The retaliation for a 'dot' is a 'garland'; for a garland, a 'cloud-fragment' — thus, as if seized by anger, she should provoke quarrels. 2.5.39 (verse) Seizing his hair, she should lift his face and then drink [from his lips]. She should hide herself and bite here and there, aroused by passion. 2.5.40 (verse) Lifting herself to her lover's neck, resting on the surface of his chest, she should apply the 'jewel-garland' [nail-mark] and whatever else has been observed. 2.5.41 (verse) Even by day, in the midst of people, when shown [a mark] by the lover, she should point to the mark she herself made on him and laugh, unnoticed by others. 2.5.42 (verse) As if wrinkling her face, as if reproaching the lover, she should display with seeming jealousy the marks on her own body. 2.5.43 (verse) Through mutual harmony, even between those who are shy, even over a hundred years, their affection does not diminish.

children.translated_text: 2.6.1 A <s>mṛgī</s> (doe-woman), at the time of passion, widening her hips, should lie down and raise herself. 2.6.2 A <s>hastinī</s> (elephant-woman), as if contracting receive the lover with her hips. 2.6.6 And artificial devices are especially [used] in low union. 2.6.7 [1] <s>Utphullaka</s> (the 'blooming'), [2] <s>Vijṛmbhitaka</s> (the 'yawning'), and [3] 2.6.9 There, he should give space. 2.6.10 In a non-low [union], placing both thighs crosswise and receiving [him] — [this is the] <s>vijṛmbhitaka</s> ('yawning'). 2.6.11 Placing the thighs evenly on both sides and positioning the knees on the sides — through practice, [this is] <s>Indrāṇī</s>. 2.6.12 By this, even a high union can be accommodated. 2.6.13 Reception in the <s>saṃpuṭa</s> (casket position) is for low union. 2.6.14 By this, even lower union for the <s>hastinī</s> is [explained]. 2.6.15 [1] <s>Saṃpuṭaka</s> (casket), [2] <s>Pīḍitaka</s> (pressed), [3] <s>Veṣṭitaka</s> (entwined), and [4] <s>Bāḍavaka</s> (mare's position). 2.6.16 Both feet of both [partners] stretched out straight — [this is] <s>saṃpuṭa</s>. 2.6.17 It is twofold: side-casket and supine-casket — according to the action employed. 2.6.18 But lying on the side, the man should lie on the woman's right side — this is universal. 2.6.19 With the same arrangement as the <s>saṃpuṭaka</s>, pressing the 2.10.1 nāgarakaḥ saha mitra-janena paricārakaiś ca kṛta-puṣpopahāre saṃcārita-surabhi-dhūpe raty-āvāse prasādhite vāsa-gṛhe kṛta-snāna-prasādhanāṃ yuktyāpītāṃ striyaṃ sāntvanaiḥ punaḥ pānena copakramet..2.10.2 dakṣiṇataś cāsyā upaveśanam. keśa-haste vastrānte nīvyām ity avalambanam. raty-arthaṃ savyena bāhunānuddhataḥ pariṣvaṅgaḥ.
2.10.3 pūrva-prakaraṇa-saṃbaddhaiḥ parihāsānurāgair vacobhir anuvṛttiḥ. gūḍhāślīlānāṃ ca vastūnāṃ samasyayā paribhāṣaṇam..
2.10.4 sa:nṛttaṃ a:nṛtaṃ vā gītaṃ vāditram. kalāsu saṃkathāḥ. punaḥ pānenopacchandanam.
2.10.5 jātānurāgāyāṃ kusumānulepana-tāmbūla-dānena ca śeṣa-jana-visṛṣṭiḥ. vi:jane ca yathoktair āliṅganādibhir enām uddharṣayet. tato nīvī-viśleṣaṇādi yathoktam upakrameta.
2.10.5 ity ayaṃ ratārambhaḥ.
2.10.6 ratāvasānikaṃ rāgam ativāhyā:saṃstutayor iva sa:vrīḍayoḥ parasparam a:paśyatoḥ pṛthak pṛthag ācāra-bhūmi-gamanam. pratinivṛttya cā:vrīḍāyamānayor ucita-deśopaviṣṭayos tāmbūla-grahaṇam acchī-kṛtaṃ((44)) candanam anyad vānulepanaṃ tasyā gātre svayam eva niveśayet.
2.10.7 savyena bāhunā caināṃ parirabhya caṣaka-hastaḥ((45)) sāntvayan pāyayet. jalānupānaṃ vā khaṇḍaka-khādyakam anyad vā prakṛti-sātmya-yuktam ubhāv apy upayuñjīyātām.
2.10.8 accha-rasaka-yūṣam((46)) amla-yavāgūṃ((47)) bhṛṣṭa-māṃsopadaṃśāni((48)) pānakāni cūta-phalāni((49)) śuṣka-māṃsaṃ mātuluṅga-cukrakāṇi((50)) sa:śarkarāṇi((51)) ca yathā:deśa-sātmyaṃ ca. tatra madhuram idaṃ mṛdu viśadam iti ca vidaśya vidaśya tat tad upahāret.
2.10.9 harmya-tala-sthitayor vā candrikāsevanārtham āsanam. tatrānukūlābhiḥ kathābhir anuvarteta. tad-aṅka-saṃlīnāyāś candramasaṃ paśyantyā nakṣatra-paṅkti-vyaktī: karaṇam. arundhatī-dhruva-saptarṣi-mālā-darśanaṃ ca.
2.10.9c iti ratāvasānikam.
2.10.10 tatraitad bhavati.
2.10.10v avasāne 'pi ca prītir upacārair upaskṛtā. sa:visrambha-kathā-yogai ratiṃ janayate parām..
2.10.11v paraspara-prīti-karair ātma-bhāvānuvartanaiḥ. kṣaṇāt krodha-parāvṛttaiḥ kṣaṇāt prīti-vilokitaiḥ..
2.10.12v hallīsaka-krīḍanakair((52)) gāyanair lāṭa-rāsakaiḥ. rāga-lolārdra-nayanaiś candra-maṇḍala-vīkṣṇaiḥ..
2.10.13v1 ādye saṃdarśane jāte pūrvaṃ ye syur manorathāḥ. punar-viyoge duḥkhaṃ ca tasya sarvasya kīrtanaiḥ..
2.10.13v2 kīrtanānte ca rāgeṇa pariṣvaṅgaiḥ sa:cumbanaiḥ. tais taiś ca bhāvaiḥ saṃyukto yūno rāgo vivardhate..
children.translated_text:
2.10.1 The <s>nāgaraka</s> (man-about-town), together with his circle of friends and attendants, in the love-chamber adorned with floral offerings and permeated with fragrant incense, in the well-appointed living room, should approach the woman who has bathed and adorned herself and has been given drink with skill, with soothing words and further drink.
2.10.2 He should seat her to his right. He should touch her hair, hand, hem of the garment, and girdle. For the purpose of lovemaking, a gentle embrace with the left arm.
2.10.3 He should engage her in conversation with jesting and amorous words related to the previous topics. And he should speak of concealed intimate matters through verse-completion games.
2.10.4 Singing with or without dancing, instrumental music, conversation about the arts, and further enticement with drink.
2.10.5 When her passion has arisen, by offering flowers, ointments, and <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), the remaining people should be dismissed. In private, he should arouse her with embraces and other [caresses] as previously described. Then he should commence with the untying of the girdle and so forth, as described.
2.10.5 Thus is the beginning of lovemaking (<s>ratārambha</s>).
2.10.6 At the conclusion of lovemaking, having passed through the passion, as if strangers to each other, bashful, not looking at one another, they should go separately to the washing area. Returning, no longer embarrassed, having seated themselves in a suitable place, they should take <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel). He should himself apply pure sandalwood or other ointment to her body.
2.10.7 Embracing her with his left arm, with a cup in hand, he should soothe her and make her drink. Or water to drink, sugar confections, or whatever else suits their natural temperament — both should partake.
2.10.8 Clear fruit-juice broth, sour rice-gruel, roasted meat with accompaniments, fruit-drinks, mango fruits, dried meat, citron and tamarind preparations, [things] with sugar — all according to regional custom. Saying 'This is sweet, this is soft, this is clear,' he should offer each thing, tasting each one.
2.10.9 Or, seated on the terrace of the mansion for enjoying the moonlight, he should engage her with pleasant stories. As she reclines in his lap gazing at the moon, he should point out the rows of constellations — showing her <s>Arundhatī</s>, <s>Dhruva</s> (the Pole Star), and the garland of the Seven Sages (<s>Saptarṣi</s>).
2.10.9c Thus is the conclusion of lovemaking (<s>ratāvasānika</s>).
2.10.10 And here there are [verses]:
2.10.10v Even at the conclusion, affection enhanced by courtesies, combined with intimate conversation, generates the highest pleasure.
2.10.11v With acts that please each other, following each other's moods, now turning away in anger for a moment, now glancing with affection the next,
2.10.12v with <s>hallīsaka</s> dances and sport, with singing and <s>Lāṭa</s> circle-dances, with eyes moist and rolling with passion, with gazing at the orb of the moon,
2.10.13v1 recounting the desires that arose at the first meeting, the sorrow of separation and reunion,
2.10.13v2 and at the end of such recounting, with passionate embraces accompanied by kisses, and with those and other expressions of feeling — thus the passion of the young couple grows.

2.10.14 [1]rāgavad [2]āhārya-rāgaṃ [3]kṛtrima-rāgaṃ [4]vyavahita-rāgaṃ [5]poṭā-rataṃ [6]khala-ratam [7]a:yantrita-ratam iti rata-viśeṣāḥ.
2.10.15 saṃdarśanāt prabhṛty ubhayor api pravṛddha-rāgayoḥ prayatna-kṛte samāgame pravāsa-pratyāgamane vā kalaha-viyoga-yoge tad [1]rāgavat.
2.10.16 tatrātmābhiprāyād yāvad-arthaṃ ca pravṛttiḥ.
2.10.17 madhyastha-rāgayor ārabdhaṃ yad anurajyate tad [2]āhārya-rāgam.
2.10.18 tatra cātuḥṣaṣṭikair yogaiḥ sātmyānuviddhaiḥ saṃdhukṣya saṃdhukṣya rāgam pravarteta.
2.10.19 tat kārya-hetor anyatra saktayor vā [3]kṛtrima-rāgam.
2.10.20 tatra samuccayena yogāñ śāstrataḥ paśyet.
2.10.21 puruśas tu hṛdaya-priyām anyāṃ manasi nidhāya vyavaharet. saṃprayogāt prabhṛti ratiṃ yāvat. atas tad [4]vyavahita-rāgam.
2.10.22 nyūnāyāṃ kumbha-dāsyāṃ paricārikāyāṃ vā yāvad-arthaṃ saṃprayogas tat [5]poṭā-ratam(( 54)).
2.10.23 tatropacarān nādriyeta.
2.10.24 tathā veśyāyā grāmīṇena saha yāvad-artham [6]khala-ratam.
2.10.25 grāma-vraja-pratyanta-yoṣidbhiś ca nāgarasya.
2.10.26 utpanna-visrambhayoś ca parasparānukūlyād [7]a:yantrita-ratam.
children.translated_text:
2.10.14 The special types of union (<s>rata-viśeṣāḥ</s>) are: [1] <s>rāgavat</s> (passionate), [2] <s>āhārya-rāga</s> (acquired passion), [3] <s>kṛtrima-rāga</s> (simulated passion), [4] <s>vyavahita-rāga</s> (transferred passion), [5] <s>poṭā-rata</s> (union with a low woman), [6] <s>khala-rata</s> (rustic union), [7] <s>ayantrita-rata</s> (unrestricted union).
2.10.15 When, from the very first sight, both have intensely grown passion, and the meeting is brought about by effort, or upon return from a journey, or upon reunion after a quarrel and separation — that is [1] <s>rāgavat</s> (passionate).
2.10.16 In that, one engages according to one's own desire and as much as needed.
2.10.17 When two of moderate passion begin [union] and become impassioned — that is [2] <s>āhārya-rāga</s> (acquired passion).
2.10.18 In that, one should proceed by kindling and rekindling passion through the techniques of the sixty-four [arts], applied according to one's temperament.
2.10.19 That which is [done] for a particular purpose, or when both are attached elsewhere — that is [3] <s>kṛtrima-rāga</s> (simulated passion).
2.10.20 In that, one should employ the techniques in combination, according to the treatise.
2.10.21 But a man, placing another woman dear to his heart in his mind, should make love [to the present one], from the beginning of union until climax. Thus, that is [4] <s>vyavahita-rāga</s> (transferred passion).
2.10.22 Union with a low-born woman, a water-carrier, or a female attendant, only as much as needed — that is [5] <s>poṭā-rata</s> (union with a low woman).
2.10.23 In that, one should not concern oneself with courtesies.
2.10.24 Similarly, a courtesan's union with a rustic man, only as much as needed — [6] <s>khala-rata</s> (rustic union).
2.10.25 And a <s>nāgaraka</s>'s [union] with women of villages, cattle-camps, and frontier regions [is also khala-rata].
2.10.26 When both have developed trust and act in mutual harmony — [7] <s>ayantrita-rata</s> (unrestricted union).

children.text: 2.10.26c iti ratāni.
children.translated_text: 2.10.26c Thus are the [special] types of union.

2.10.27 vardhamāṇa-praṇayā tu nayikā sapatnī-nāma-grahaṇaṃ tad-āśrayam ālāpaṃ vā gotra-skhalitaṃ vā na marṣayet. nāyaka-vyalīkaṃ ca.
2.10.28 tatra su:bhṛśaḥ kalaho ruditam āyāsaḥ śiro-ruhāṇām avakṣodanaṃ((56)) prahaṇanam āsanāc chayanād vā mahyāṃ patanaṃ mālya-bhūṣaṇāvamokṣo bhūmau śayyā((57)) ca.
2.10.29 tatra yukta-rūpeṇa sāmnā pāda-patanena vā prasanna-manās tām anunayann upakramya śayanam ārohayet..2.10.30 tasya ca vacanam uttareṇa yojayantī vivṛddha-krodhā sa:kaca-graham asyāsyam unnamayya pādena bāhau śirasi vakṣasi pṛṣṭhe vā sakṛd dvis trir hanyāt. dvāra-deśaṃ gacchet. tatropaviśyāśru-karaṇam iti.
2.10.31 ati:kruddhāpi tu na dvāra-deśād bhūyo gacchet. doṣavattvāt. iti dattakaḥ. tatra yuktito 'nun~īyamānā prasādam ākāṅkṣet. prasannāpi tu sa:kaṣāyair((58)) eva vākyair enaṃ tudatīva prasanna-rati-kāṅkṣiṇī nāyakena parirabhyeta.
2.10.32 sva-bhavanasthā tu nimittāt kalahitā tathā:vida-ceṣṭaiva nāyakam abhigacchet.
2.10.33 tatra pīṭhamarda-viṭa-vidūṣakair nāyaka-prayuktair upaśamita-roṣā tair evāninītā taiḥ sahaiva tad-bhavanam adhigacchet. tatra ca vaset.
2.10.33c iti praṇaya-kalahaḥ.
2.10.34 bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ.
2.10.34v evam etāṃ catuḥṣaṣṭiṃ bābhravyeṇa prakīrtitām. prayuñjāno vara-strīṣu siddhiṃ gacchati nāyakaḥ..
2.10.35v bruvann api anya-śāstrāṇi catuḥṣaṣṭi-vivarjitaḥ. vidvat-saṃsadi nāty:arthaṃ kathāsu paripūjyate..
2.10.36v varjito 'py anya-vijñānair etayā yas tv alaṃkṛtaḥ. sa goṣṭhyāṃ nara-nārīṇāṃ kathāsv agraṃ vigāhate((59))..
2.10.37v vidvadbhiḥ pūjitām enāṃ khalair api su:pūjitam. pūjitāṃ gaṇikā-saṅghair nandinīṃ ko na pūjayet..
2.10.38v nandinī su:bhagā siddhā su:bhagaṃ-karaṇīti ca. nārī-priyeti cācāryaiḥ śāstreṣv eṣā nirucyate..
2.10.39v kanyābhiḥ para-yoṣidbhir gaṇikābhiś ca bhāvataḥ. vīkṣyate bahu-mānena catuḥṣaṣṭi-vicakṣaṇaḥ..
children.translated_text:
2.10.27 But a <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) of growing affection should not tolerate the mention of a co-wife's name, conversation referring to her, a slip of the <s>gotra</s> (family name), or the lover's deception.
2.10.28 In that case, there is a fierce quarrel: weeping, distress, tearing of hair, striking, falling from the seat or bed to the ground, casting off garlands and ornaments, and lying on the floor.
2.10.29 There, with appropriately measured conciliatory words or by falling at her feet, he should make her pleased, pacify her, and lead her up onto the bed.
2.10.30 But she, countering his words with retorts, her anger increased, should seize him by the hair, lift up his face, and strike him with her foot once, twice, or thrice on the arm, head, chest, or back. She should go to the doorway, sit there, and weep.
2.10.31 But even in extreme anger, she should not go beyond the doorway — for that is a fault. So says <s>Dattaka</s>. There, being properly conciliated, she should expect reconciliation. Even when placated, she should still prod him with somewhat bitter words, as if desiring the pleasure of reconciled lovemaking, and be embraced by the lover.
2.10.32 But if the quarrel arises at her own dwelling for some reason, she should go to the lover's [house] with the same kinds of gestures.
2.10.33 There, her anger pacified by the <s>pīṭhamarda</s>, <s>viṭa</s>, and <s>vidūṣaka</s> sent by the lover, brought back by them, she should go with them to his house. And there she should stay.
2.10.33c Thus is the lovers' quarrel (<s>praṇaya-kalaha</s>).
2.10.34 And here there are verses:
2.10.34v Thus, the lover who skillfully applies these sixty-four [arts] proclaimed by <s>Bābhravya</s> upon excellent women achieves success.
2.10.35v Even one who discourses on other treatises, if lacking the sixty-four [arts], is not greatly honored in conversations among assemblies of the learned.
2.10.36v But even one lacking other branches of knowledge, if adorned with these [arts], attains the foremost place in discussions among men and women in social gatherings.
2.10.37v Honored by the learned, well-honored even by rogues, honored by the assemblies of courtesans — who would not honor this delightful [science]?
2.10.38v The masters in their treatises call her 'the delightful one,' 'the auspicious one,' 'the perfected one,' 'the one who makes auspicious,' and 'the beloved of women.'
2.10.39v One skilled in the sixty-four [arts] is regarded with great esteem by maidens, by other men's wives, and by courtesans.

children.text:
3.1.1 sa:varnāyām an:anyapūrvāyāṃ śāstrato 'dhigatāyāṃ dharmo 'rthaḥ putrāḥ saṃbandhaḥ pakṣa-vṛddhir an:upaskṛtā((60)) ratiś ca((61)).
3.1.2 tasmāt kanyām abhijanopetāṃ mātā-pitṛmatīṃ tri-varṣāt prabhṛti nyūna-vayasaṃ ślāghyācāre dhanavati pakṣavati kule saṃbandhi-priye saṃbandhibhir ākule prasūtāṃ prabhūta-mātṛ-pitṛ-pakṣāṃ rūpa-śīla-lakṣaṇa-saṃpannām a:nyūnādhikā:vinaṣṭa-danta-nakha- karṇa-keṣākṣi-stanīm a:rogi-prakṛti-śarīrāṃ tathā:vidha eva śrutavāñ śīlayet((62)).
3.1.3 yā gṛhītvā kṛtinam ātmānaṃ manyeta na ca samānair nindyeta tasyāṃ pravṛttir iti ghoṭakamukhaḥ.
3.1.4 tasyā varaṇe mātā-pitarau saṃbandhinaś ca prayateran. mitrāṇi ca gṛhīta-vākyāny ubhaya-saṃbaddhāni.
3.1.5 tāny anyeṣāṃ varayitṝṇāṃ doṣān pratyakṣān āgamikāṃś ca śrāvayeyuḥ. kaulān pauruṣeyān abhiprāya-saṃvardhakāṃś ca nāyaka-guṇān. viśeṣataś ca kanyā-mātur anukūlāṃs tadātvāyati-yuktān darśayeyuḥ.
3.1.6 daiva-cintaka-rūpaś ca śakuna-nimitta-graha-lagna-bala-lakṣaṇa-darśanena nāyakasya bhaviṣyantam artha-saṃyogaṃ kalyāṇam anuvarṇayet.
3.1.7 apare punar asyānyato viśiṣṭena kanyā-lābhena kanyā-mātaram unmādayeyuḥ.
3.1.8 daiva-nimitta-śakunopaśrutīnām ānulomyena kanyāṃ varayed dadyāc ca.
3.1.9 na yadṛcchayā kevala-mānuṣāyeti ghoṭakamukhaḥ.
3.1.10 suptāṃ rudatīṃ niṣkrāntāṃ varaṇe parivarjayet.
3.1.11 a:praśasta-nāmadheyāṃ ca guptāṃ dattāṃ ghonāṃ((63)) pṛṣatām((64)) ṛṣabhāṃ((65)) vinatāṃ vikaṭāṃ((66)) vimuṇḍāṃ((67)) śuci-dūṣitāṃ((68)) sāṃkarikīṃ((69)) rākāṃ((70)) phalinīṃ mitrāṃ svanujāṃ varṣakarīṃ ca varjayet.
3.1.12v nakṣatrākhyāṃ nadī-nāmnīṃ vṛkṣa-nāmnīṃ ca garhitām. la-kāra-rephopāntāṃ ca varaṇe parivarjayet..
3.1.13 yasyāṃ manaś-cakṣor nibandhas tasyām ṛddhiḥ. netarām ādriyeta. ity eke.
3.1.14 tasmāt pradāna-samaye kanyām udāra-veṣāṃ sthāpayeyuḥ. aparāhṇikaṃ ca. nityaṃ prāsādhitāyāḥ sakhībhiḥ saha krīḍā. yajña-vivāhādiṣu jana-saṃdrāveṣu prāyatnikaṃ darśanam. tathotsaveṣu ca. paṇya-sa:dharmatvāt.
3.1.15 varaṇārtham upagatāṃś ca bhadra-darśanān pradakṣiṇa-vācaś ca tat-saṃbandhi-saṅgatān puruṣān maṅgalaiḥ pratigṛhṇīyuḥ.
3.1.16 kanyāṃ caiṣām alaṃkṛtām anyāpadeśena darśayeyuḥ.
3.1.17 daivaṃ parīkṣaṇaṃ cāvadhiṃ sthāpayeyuḥ. ā pradāna-niścayāt.
3.1.18 snānādiṣu niyujyamānā varayitāraḥ sarvaṃ bhaviṣyatīty uktvā na tad-ahar evābhyupagaccheyuḥ.
3.1.19 deśa-pravṛtti-sātmyād vā brāhma-prājāpatyārṣa-daivānām anyatamena vivāhena śāstrataḥ pariṇayet.
children.translated_text: 3.1.1 In a woman of the same <s>varṇa</s> (class), who has not been previously enjoyed by another, obtained according to the <s>śāstra</s> — there is <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, sons, family connection, increase of one's faction, unadulterated affection, and pleasure. 3.1.2 Therefore, a man of learning should court a maiden endowed with good lineage, whose parents are living, who is at least three years younger, born in a praiseworthy, wealthy family with numerous supporters, one dear to its relations and surrounded by kinsmen, with abundant maternal and paternal connections, endowed with beauty, good character, and auspicious marks, with teeth, nails, ears, hair, eyes, and breasts neither deficient nor excessive nor damaged, and having a naturally healthy body. 3.1.3 That woman, having married whom, he would consider himself accomplished and would not be criticized by his equals — toward her one should direct his efforts — so says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>. 3.1.4 In selecting her, the parents and relations should make efforts; and friends who are trusted spokesmen and connected to both sides. 3.1.5 They should make known to the maiden's party the faults — both evident and reported — of other suitors, and the groom's virtues of family, manly qualities, and those that would enhance their purposes. And especially they should show [qualities] favorable to the maiden's mother, suited to both the present and the future. 3.1.6 And one in the guise of an astrologer should praise the groom's future wealth and prosperity by showing omens, portents, planetary positions, auspicious signs, and favorable marks. 3.1.7 Others should excite the maiden's mother by [hinting at] the prospect of obtaining a maiden superior to this one from elsewhere. 3.1.8 One should select and give the maiden in accordance with divine signs, omens, and things overheard. 3.1.9 Not by chance alone, relying merely on human [judgment] — so says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>. 3.1.10 One who is sleeping, weeping, or has left the house should be avoided in the selection. 3.1.11 And one should avoid a maiden with an inauspicious name, or one who is hidden, already given [to another], snub-nosed, spotted, bull-like, stooped, misshapen, bald, of impure conduct, mixed-caste, full-moon[-born], fruit-bearing [name], friend-named, named after a younger sibling, or rain-making [name]. 3.1.12 [Verse:] One named after a <s>nakṣatra</s>, a river, or a tree — which is inauspicious — and one whose name ends in 'la' or 'ra' should be avoided in the selection. 3.1.13 Prosperity lies in the one upon whom the mind's eye is fixed; one should not attach importance to others — so say some. 3.1.14 Therefore, at the time of giving, they should present the maiden in fine attire. And afternoon [visits should be arranged]. There should be daily play with friends while adorned. Deliberate display at gatherings of people such as sacrifices, weddings, and the like — and likewise at festivals — because it is similar to displaying wares. 3.1.15 And they should receive with auspicious rites those men who come for the purpose of selection, who are of good appearance, who speak favorably, and who come accompanied by the groom's relations. 3.1.16 And they should show them the maiden, adorned, under some other pretext. 3.1.17 And they should set a deadline for the divine examination, until the decision of giving. 3.1.18 When the suitors are engaged in bathing and such rites, having said 'everything shall take place,' they should not agree on that very day. 3.1.19 Or according to regional custom and suitability, he should marry her by the <s>śāstra</s> through one of the forms of marriage: <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Ārṣa</s>, or <s>Daiva</s>.

children.text: 3.1.19c iti varaṇavidhānam((71)).
children.translated_text: 3.1.19c Thus, the procedure of selection.

3.1.20 bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ.
3.1.20v samasyādyāḥ saha-krīḍā vivāhāḥ saṅgatāni ca. samānair eva karyāṇi nottamair nāpi vādhamair..
3.1.21v kanyāṃ gṛhītvā varteta preṣyavad yatra nāyakaḥ. taṃ vidyād ucca-saṃbandhaṃ parityaktaṃ manasvibhiḥ..
3.1.22v svāmivad vicared yatra bāndhavaiḥ svaiḥ puras:kṛtaḥ. a:ślāghyo hīna-saṃbandhaḥ so 'pi sadbhir vinindyate..

children.translated_text: 3.1.20 And here there are verses: 3.1.20 [Verse:] Companionship in amusements and such, marriages, and unions should be made only with equals — not with superiors, nor with inferiors. 3.1.21 [Verse:] Where the groom, having taken the maiden, would live like a servant — one should know that as a high-alliance, abandoned by the self-respecting. 3.1.22 [Verse:] Where one would move about like a master, honored by one's own kinsmen — that ignoble low-alliance is also condemned by the virtuous. 3.1.23 [Verse:] Where play is practiced with mutual enjoyment of pleasure, each distinguishing the other — that alliance should be made. 3.1.24 [Verse:] Even having made a high-alliance, one should afterward be conciliatory toward the kinsmen. But one should never make a low-alliance condemned by the virtuous.

section (prakaraṇa)25 kanyā-visrambhaṇa-prakaraṇam..3.2.1 saṃgatayos tri-rātram adhaḥ śayyā brahmacaryaṃ kṣāra-lavaṇa-varjam āhāras tathā saptāhaṃ satūrya-maṅgala-snānaṃ prasādhanaṃ saha-bhojanaṃ ca prekṣā saṃbandhināṃ ca pūjanam. iti sārvavarṇikam.
children.translated_text: Lesson 2, Second Chapter. Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 25: <s>Kanyā-visrambhaṇa-prakaraṇam</s> (Chapter on Winning the Maiden's Confidence). 3.2.1 For the newly married couple, for three nights there should be sleeping on the ground, celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and food free from pungent and salty [substances]; likewise for seven days — bathing with auspicious music, adornment, eating together, attending performances, and honoring the relations. This is the practice for all <s>varṇas</s>.

children.text:
3.2.2 tasminn etāṃ niśi vi:jane mṛdubhir upacārair upakrameta.
3.2.3 tri-rātram a:vacanaṃ hi stambham iva nāyakaṃ paśyantī kanyā nirvidyeta paribhavec ca tṛtīyām iva prakṛtim. iti bābhravīyāḥ.
3.2.4 upakrameta visrambhayec ca na tu brahmacaryam ativarteta. iti vātsyāyānaḥ.
3.2.5 upakramamāṇaś ca na prasahya kiṃ cid ācaret.
3.2.6 kusuma-sa:dharmāṇo hi yoṣitaḥ su:kumāropakramāḥ. tās tv an:adhigata-viśvāsaiḥ prasabham upakramyamāṇaḥ saṃprayoga-dveṣiṇyo bhavanti. tasmāt sāmnaivopacaret.
3.2.7 yuktyāpi tu yataḥ prasaram upalabhet tenaivānu praviśet.
3.2.8 tat-priyeṇāliṅgenācaritena nāti:kālatvāt.
3.2.9 pūrva-kāyeṇa copakramet. viṣahyatvāt.
3.2.10 dīpāloke vigāḍha-yauvanāyāḥ pūrva-saṃstutāyāḥ. bālāyā a:pūrvāyāś cāndhakāre.
3.2.11 aṅgī-kṛta-pariṣvaṅgāyāś ca vadanena tāmbūla-dānam. tad-a:pratipadyamānāṃ ca sāntvanair vākyaiḥ śapathaiḥ pratiyācitaiḥ pāda-patanaiś ca grāhayet. vrīḍā-yuktāpi yoṣid aty:anta-kruddhāpi na pāda-patanam ativartate iti sārvatrikam.
3.2.12 tad-dāna-prasaṅgeṇa mṛdu viśadam a:kāhalam asyāś cumbanam.
3.2.13 tatra siddhām ālāpayet.
3.2.14 tac-chravaṇārthaṃ yat kiṃ cid alpākṣaram abhidheyam a:jānann iva pṛcchet.
3.2.15 tatra niṣ:pratipattim an:udvejayan sāntvanā-yuktaṃ bahuśa eva pṛcchet.
3.2.16 yatrāpi a:vadantīṃ nirbadhnīyāt.
3.2.17 sarvā eva hi kanyāḥ puruṣeṇa prayujyamānaṃ vacanaṃ viṣahante. na tu laghu-miśrām api vācaṃ vadanti. iti ghoṭakamukhaḥ.
3.2.18 nirbadhyamānā tu śiraḥ-kampena prativacanāni yojayet. kalahe tu na śiraḥ kampayet.
3.2.19 icchasi māṃ necchasi vā kiṃ te 'ham rucito na rucito veti pṛṣṭā ciraṃ sthitvā nirbadhyamānā tad-ānukulyena śiraḥ kampayet. prapañcyamānā tu vivadet.
3.2.20 saṃstutā cet sakhīm anukūlām ubhayato 'pi visrabdhāṃ tām antarā kṛtvā kathāṃ yojayet. tasminn adho-mukhī vihaset. tāṃ cāti:vādinīm adhikṣiped vivadec ca. sā tu parihāsārtham idam anayoktam iti cānuktam api brūyāt. tatra tām apanudya prativacanārtham abhyarthyamānā tūṣṇīm āsīta. nirbadhyamānā tu nāham evaṃ bravīmīty a:vyaktākṣaram an:avasitārthaṃ vacanaṃ brūyāt. nāyakaṃ tu vihasantī kadā cit kaṭākṣaiḥ prekṣeta. ity ālāpa-yojanam.
3.2.21 evaṃ jāta-paricayā cā:nirvadantī tat-samīpe yācitaṃ tāmbūlaṃ vilepanaṃ srajaṃ nidadhyāt. uttarīye vāsya nibadhnīyāt.
3.2.22 yathā:yuktām ācchuritakena((73)) stana-mukulayor((74)) upari spṛśet.
3.2.23 vāryamāṇaś ca tvam api māṃ pariṣvajasva tato naivam ācariṣyāmīti sthityā pariṣvañjayet. svaṃ ca hastam ā nābhideśāt prasārya nirvartayet. krameṇa cainām utsaṅgam āropyādhikam adhikam upakramet. a:pratipadyamānāṃ ca bhīṣayet.
3.2.24 ahaṃ khalu tava dantapadāny adhare kariṣyāmi stana-pṛṣṭhe ca nakha-padam. ātmanaś ca svayaṃ kṛtvā tvayā kṛtam iti te sakhī-janasya purataḥ kathayiṣyāmi. sā tvaṃ kim atra vakṣyasīti bāla-vibhīṣikair bāla-pratyāyanaiś ca śanair enāṃ pratārayet.
3.2.25 dvitīyasyāṃ tṛtīyasyāṃ ca rātrau kiṃ cid adhikaṃ visrambhitāṃ hastena yojayet.
3.2.26 sarvāṅgikaṃ cumbanam upakrameta.
3.2.27 ūrvoś copari vinyasta-hastaḥ saṃvāhana-kriyāyāṃ siddhāyāṃ krameṇoru-mūlam api saṃvāhayet. nivārite saṃvāhane ko doṣa ity ākulayed enām. tac ca sthirī:kuryāt. tatra siddhāyā guhya-deśābhimarśanam.
3.2.28 raśana-viyojanaṃ nīvī-visraṃsanaṃ vasana-parivartanam ūru-mūla-saṃvāhanaṃ ca. ete cāsyānyāpadeśāḥ. yukta-yantrāṃ rañjayet. na tv a:kāle vrata-khaṇḍanam.
3.2.29 anuśiṣyāc ca. ātmānurāgaṃ darśayet. manorathāṃś ca pūrva-kālikān anuvarṇayet. āyatyāṃ ca tad-ānukūlyena pravṛttiṃ pratijānīyāt. sa:patnībhyaś ca sādhvasam avacchindyāt. kālena ca krameṇa vimukta-kanyā-bhāvām an:udvejayann upakrameta. iti kanyā-visrambhanam.
3.2.30 bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ.
3.2.30v evaṃ cittānurāgo bālām upāyena prasādhayet. tathāsya sānuraktā ca su:visrabdhā prajāyate..
3.2.31v naty:antam ānulomyena na cāti:prātilomyataḥ. siddhiṃ gacchati kanyāsu tasmān madhyena sādhayet..
3.2.32v ātmanaḥ prīti-jananaṃ yoṣitāṃ māna-vardhanam. kanyā-visrambhaṇaṃ vetti yaḥ sa tāsāṃ priyo bhavet..
3.2.33v ati:lajjānvītety evaṃ yas tu kanyām upekṣate. so 'n:abhiprāya-vedīti paśuvat paribhūyate...3.2.34v sahasā vāpy upakrāntā kanyā-cittam a:vindatā. bhayaṃ vitrāsam udvegaṃ sadyo dveṣaṃ ca gacchati..
3.2.35v sā prīti-yogam a:prāptā tenodvegena dūṣitā. puruṣa-dveṣiṇī vā syād vidviṣṭā vā tato 'nya-gā((75))..
children.translated_text:
(3.2.2) On that night, in a secluded place, he should approach her with gentle attentions.
(3.2.3) For if, during three nights, she sees the bridegroom [remaining] silent like a post, the maiden will become disgusted and despise [him] as though [he were] a eunuch. Thus [say] the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>.
(3.2.4) He should approach [her] and win her confidence, but should not transgress celibacy. Thus [says] <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
(3.2.5) And while approaching, he should not do anything by force.
(3.2.6) For women are like flowers in nature and require a gentle approach. When they are approached forcibly by those who have not gained their trust, they become averse to sexual union. Therefore, one should treat [them] only with conciliation.
(3.2.7) And by strategy, wherever he perceives an opening, he should proceed through that very [means].
(3.2.8) With an embrace that is pleasing to her and familiar, since the time is not yet [ripe for more].
(3.2.9) And he should approach with the upper body, since that is tolerable.
(3.2.10) [This should be done] in lamplight for one who is in full youth and previously acquainted; for a young girl meeting [him] for the first time, in darkness.
(3.2.11) And when she has accepted the embrace, the giving of <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) from [his] mouth. If she does not accept it, he should make her take it through soothing words, oaths, entreaties, and falling at [her] feet. For even a modest woman or one extremely angry does not resist the falling at [her] feet — this is universal.
(3.2.12) On the occasion of giving that [betel], a soft, clear, and noiseless kiss for her.
(3.2.13) Once that [kiss] is accomplished, he should engage her in conversation.
(3.2.14) For the purpose of hearing her [speak], he should ask something brief and simple, as if not knowing [the answer].
(3.2.15) If she gives no reply, he should ask repeatedly with soothing words, without causing her distress.
(3.2.16) And even [if she remains] silent, he should press her.
(3.2.17) For all maidens endure words spoken by a man, but they do not utter even a syllable mixed with lightness. Thus [says] <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>.
(3.2.18) When pressed, she should frame her replies by nodding her head. But in a quarrel, she should not nod her head.
(3.2.19) When asked 'Do you want me or not? Am I pleasing to you or not?' — after remaining [silent] for a long time and being pressed, she should nod her head in agreement. But when pressed further [for details], she should dispute.
(3.2.20) If she is [already] acquainted [with him], she should place between them a friendly confidante trusted by both and conduct conversation [through her]. In that [situation], she should laugh with face downcast. She should reproach the [confidante] when she speaks too much and quarrel [with her]. And [the confidante] should say, as if in jest, what [the maiden] has said and also what she has not said. There, having pushed her [the confidante] away, when pressed for a reply, she should sit in silence. When further pressed, she should say 'I did not say that' — in indistinct syllables and with unfinished meaning.

children.text:
3.3.1 dhana-hīnas tu guṇa-yukto 'pi madhyastha-guṇo hīnāpadeśo vā sadhano vā prātiveśyaḥ mātṛ-pitṛ-bhrātṛṣu ca paratantraḥ bāla-vṛttir ucita-praveśo vā kanyām alabhyatvān na varayet.
3.3.2 bālyāt prabhṛti caināṃ svayam evānurañjayet.
3.3.3 tathā-yuktaś ca mātula-kulānuvartī dakṣiṇapathe bāla eva mātrā pitrā ca viyuktaḥ paribhūta-kalpo dhanotkarṣād a:labhyāṃ mātula-duhitaram anyasmai vā pūrva-dattāṃ sādhayet.
3.3.4 anyām api bāhyāṃ spṛhayet.
3.3.5 bālāyām evaṃ sati dharmādhigame saṃvananaṃ((76)) ślāghyam iti ghoṭakamukhaḥ.
3.3.6 tayā saha puṣpāvacayaṃ grathanaṃ gṛhakaṃ duhitṛkā-krīḍāyojanaṃ bhakta-pāna-karaṇam iti kurvīta. paricayasya vayasaś cānurūpyāt.
3.3.7 ākarṣa-krīḍā paṭṭikā-krīḍā muṣṭi-dyūta-kṣullakādi-dyūtāni madhyamāṅguli-grahaṇaṃ ṣaṭ-pāṣāṇakādīni ca deśyāni tat:sātmyāt tad-apta-dāsa-ceṭibhis tayā ca sahānukrīḍeta.
3.3.8 kṣveditakāni su:nimilita-kām ārabdhikāṃ lavaṇa-vīthikām anila-tāḍitakāṃ godhūma-pañjikām aṅguli-tāḍikāṃ sakhībhir anyāni ca deśyāni.
3.3.9 yāṃ ca viśvāsyām asyāṃ manyeta tayā saha nir:antarāṃ prītiṃ kuryāt. paricayāṃś ca budhyeta.
3.3.10 dhātreyikāṃ cāsyāḥ priya-hitābhyām adhikam upagṛhṇīyāt. sā hi prīyamāṇā viditākārāpy a:pratyādiśantī taṃ tāṃ ca yojayituṃ śaknutyāt. an:abhihitāpi pratyācāryakam.
3.3.11 a:viditākārāpi hi guṇān evānurāgāt prakāśayet. yathā prayojyānurajyeta.
3.3.12 yatra yatra ca kautukaṃ prayojyāyās tad anu praviśya sādhayet.
3.3.13 krīḍanaka-dravyāṇi yāny a:pūrvāṇi yāny anyāsāṃ viralaśo vidyeraṃs tāny asyā a:yatnena saṃpādayet.
3.3.14 tatra kandukam an:eka-bhakti-citram alpa-kālāntaritam anyad anyac ca saṃdarśayet. tathā sūtra-dāru-gavala-gaja-dantamayīr duhitṛkā madhūcchiṣṭa-piṣṭa-mṛnmayīś ca.
3.3.15 bhakta-pākārtham asyā mahānasikasya ca darśanam.
3.3.16 kāṣṭha-meḍhrakayoś ca saṃyuktayoś ca strī-puṃsayor ajaiḍakānāṃ((77)) deva-kula-gṛhakāṇāṃ ca śuka-parabhṛta-madana-sārikā-lāva-kukkuṭa-tiri-piñjarakāṇāṃ ca vicitrākṛti-saṃyuktānāṃ jala-bhājanānāṃ ca yantrikāṇāṃ vīṇikānāṃ paṭolikānām alaktaka-manaḥśilā-haritāla-hiṅgulaka-śyāmavarṇakādīnāṃ tathā candana-kuṅkumayoḥ pūga-phalānāṃ pattrāṇāṃ kāla-yuktānāṃ ca sakti-viṣaye pracchannaṃ dānaṃ prakāśa-dravyāṇāṃ ca prakāśam. yathā ca sarvābhiprāya-saṃvardhakam enaṃ manyeta tathā prayatitavyam.
3.3.18 prachanna-dānasya tu kāraṇam ātmano guru-janād bhayaṃ khyāpayet. deyasya cānyena spṛhaṇīyatvam iti.
3.3.19 vardhamānānurāgaṃ cākhyānake manaḥ kurvatīm anvarthābhiḥ kathābhiś citta-hāriṇībhiś ca rañjayet.
3.3.20 vismayeṣu prasahyamānām indra-jālaiḥ prayogair vismāpayet. kalāsu kautukinīṃ tat-kauśalena gīta-priyāṃ śruti-harair gītaiḥ. āśva-yujyām aṣṭamī-candrake kaumudyām utasaveṣu yātrāyāṃ grahaṇe gṛhācāre vā vicitrair āpīḍaiḥ karṇa-pattra-bhaṅgaiḥ sikthaka-pradhānair vastrāṅgulīyaka-bhūṣaṇa-dānaiś ca. no ced doṣa-karāṇi manyeta.
3.3.21 anya-puruṣa-viśeṣābhijñatayā dhātreyikāsyāḥ puruṣa-pravṛttau cātuḥ-ṣaṣṭikān yogān grāhayet.
3.3.22 tad-grahaṇopadeśena ca prayojyāyāṃ rati-kauśalam ātmanaḥ prakāśayet.
3.3.23 udāra-veṣaś ca svayam an:upahata-darśanaś ca syāt. bhāvaṃ ca kurvatīm iṅgitākāraiḥ sūcayet.
3.3.24 yavatayo hi saṃsṛṣṭam abhīkṣṇa-darśanaṃ ca puruṣaṃ prathamaṃ kāmayante. kāmayamānā api tu nābhiyuñjata iti prāyo:vādaḥ.
children.translated_text: 3.3.1 One who is lacking in wealth, even if possessed of good qualities, or of middling qualities, or of disreputable origin, or possessing wealth but being a neighbor, or dependent on mother, father, and brothers, or of childish conduct, or one who is a regular visitor — such a man, because of being unattainable [to the girl's family], should not seek the maiden [through formal proposal]. 3.3.2 From childhood itself, he should win her affection personally. 3.3.3 One so disposed, following the maternal uncle's family, in the southern region (<s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>), even as a child separated from mother and father, though nearly despised, may through the increase of wealth win the unattainable maternal uncle's daughter, or one previously given to another. 3.3.4 He may also desire another [girl] from outside [the family]. 3.3.5 When [dealing] with a young girl, winning her over through the acquisition of religious merit (<s>dharma</s>) is praiseworthy — so says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>. 3.3.6 He should engage with her in flower-gathering, garland-making, playing house, doll games, and preparing food and drink — as appropriate to their familiarity and age. 3.3.7 Drawing games, strip games, dice-guessing, <s>kṣullaka</s> and other dice games, catching the middle finger, six-stones, and other local games — being accustomed to these, he should play with her along with her trusted servants and maidservants. 3.3.8 <s>Kṣveditaka</s> (whistling games), <s>sunimilita</s> (well-shut eyes), <s>ārabdhikā</s> (the beginning game), <s>lavaṇa-vīthikā</s> (salt-road), <s>anila-tāḍitaka</s> (wind-struck), <s>godhūma-pañjikā</s> (wheat-cage), <s>aṅguli-tāḍikā</s> (finger-striking), and other regional games [he should play] with her friends. 3.3.9 And whichever [friend] of hers he considers trustworthy, with her he should cultivate continuous affection and learn about [the girl's] acquaintances. 3.3.10 He should especially win over her foster-sister (<s>dhātreyikā</s>) through kindness and favors. For she, being pleased, even if she knows his intentions, without opposing, can bring those two together. Even without being explicitly told, she acts as an intermediary. 3.3.11 Even one who does not know his intentions would reveal his qualities out of affection, so that the desired girl may fall in love. 3.3.12 And wherever the desired girl shows curiosity, entering there he should accomplish [his aim]. 3.3.13 Playthings that are novel and rarely seen among other [girls] — these he should procure for her effortlessly. 3.3.14 There, he should show her balls of various colors, one after another at short intervals. Likewise, dolls made of thread, wood, buffalo horn, and ivory, as well as those made of beeswax, flour, and clay. 3.3.15 He should show her and her cook how to prepare food. 3.3.16 [He should give] concealed gifts of wooden rams and coupled male-and-female figures, pairs of goats and sheep, temple-house models, cages for parrots, cuckoos, <s>madana</s> birds, mynas, quails, and roosters, and variously shaped water vessels, mechanical toys, small <s>vīṇās</s>, small boxes, and cosmetics such as <s>alaktaka</s> (lac dye), <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment), <s>hiṅgulaka</s> (cinnabar), and dark pigment, as well as sandalwood and saffron, betel nuts, leaves, and things appropriate to the season — concealed gifts of valuable items, and open [gifts] of open items. And he should strive so that she considers him one who fulfills all her wishes. 3.3.18 As for the reason for concealed gifts: he should make known his own fear of her elders, and that the gift is coveted by others. 3.3.19 And as her affection grows, he should delight her, who turns her mind to stories, with meaningful tales and captivating narratives. 3.3.20 One who is amazed by wonders, he should astonish with feats of magic; one who is curious about the arts, [he should impress] with skill in those arts; one who loves song, with songs that charm the ear. At the <s>Āśvayujī</s> festival, at the eighth-day moonrise, at the <s>Kaumudī</s> celebration, at seasonal festivals, at processions, at eclipses, or at household ceremonies — with varied <s>āpīḍa</s> ornaments, ear decorations, and gifts predominantly of wax, garments, rings, and ornaments — unless he thinks they would cause offense. 3.3.21 Through the foster-sister's acquaintance with other men, he should have her teach [the girl] the sixty-four arts of love. 3.3.22 And through the pretext of teaching those [arts], he should reveal his own skill in lovemaking to the desired girl. 3.3.23 He should be generously dressed and of unblemished appearance. And when she shows signs of affection, he should indicate [his feelings] through gestures and expressions. 3.3.24 For young women first desire a man with whom they have become familiar and whom they see frequently. Yet even when desiring, they do not make an approach — this is the general rule.

children.translated_text: Thus [ends the section on] the approaches to a maiden.

3.3.25 tān iṅgitākārān vakṣyāmaḥ((79))..3.3.26 saṃmukhaṃ taṃ tu na vīkṣate. vīkṣitā vrīḍāṃ darśayati. rucyam ātmano 'ṅgam apadeśena prakāśayati. pramattaṃ pracchannaṃ nāyakam atikrāntaṃ ca vīkṣate.
3.3.27 pṛṣṭā ca kiṃ cit sa:smitam a:vyaktākṣaram an:avasitārtaṃ ca mandaṃ mandam adho-mukhī kathayati. tat-samīpe ciraṃ sthānam abhinandati. dūre sthitā paśyatu mām iti manyamānā parijanaṃ sa:vadana-vikāram ābhāṣate. taṃ deśaṃ na muñcati.
3.3.28 yat kiṃ cid dṛṣṭvā vihasitaṃ karoti. tatra kathām avasthānārtham anubadhnāti. bālasyāṅka-gatasyāliṅganaṃ cumbanaṃ ca karoti. paricārikāyās tilakaṃ ca racayati. parijanān avaṣṭabhya tās tāś ca līlā darśayati.
3.3.29 tan-mitreṣu viśvāsiti. vacanaṃ caiṣāṃ bahu manyate karoti ca. tat-paricārakaiḥ saha prītiṃ saṃkathāṃ dyūtam iti ca karoti. sva-karmasu ca prabhaviṣṇur ivaitān niyuṅkte. teṣu ca nāyaka-saṃkathām anyasya kathayatsv avahitātāṃ śṛṇoti.
3.3.30 dhātreyikā coditā nāyakayodavasitaṃ praviśati. tām antarā kṛtvā tena saha dyūtaṃ krīḍām ālāpaṃ cāyojayitum icchati. an:alaṃkṛtā darśana-pathaṃ pariharati. karṇa-pattram aṅgulīyakaṃ srajaṃ vā tena yācitā sa:dhīram eva gātrād avatārya sakhyā haste dadāti. tena ca dattaṃ nityaṃ dhārayati. anya-vara-saṃkathāsu viṣaṇṇā bhavati. tat-pakṣakaiś ca saha na saṃsṛjyata iti.
3.3.31 bhavataś cātra ślokau.
3.3.31v dṛṣṭvaitān bhāva-saṃyuktān ākārān iṅgitāni ca. kanyāyāḥ saṃprayogārthaṃ tāṃs tān yogān vicintayet..
3.3.32v bāla-krīḍanakair bālā kalābhir yauvane sthitā. vatsalā cāpi saṃgrāhyā viśvāsya-jana-saṃgrahāt((80)).
children.translated_text: 3.3.25 We shall now describe those signs and gestures. 3.3.26 She does not look directly at him. When looked at, she shows modesty. Under some pretext she reveals an attractive part of her body. She looks at the hero secretly when he is inattentive, passing by, or has gone past. 3.3.27 When asked something, she speaks slowly, face downcast, with a slight smile, in unclear syllables and inconclusive meaning. She delights in staying near him for a long time. Standing far away, thinking "let him see me," she addresses her attendants with a change of expression. She does not leave that place. 3.3.28 Upon seeing something, she laughs. She attaches a conversation to it as a reason to stay. She embraces and kisses a child sitting in her lap. She applies a decorative mark (<s>tilaka</s>) to a maidservant. She displays various playful gestures while leaning on her attendants. 3.3.29 She trusts his friends and considers their words important and acts on them. She engages in affection, conversation, and games with his servants. She commands them authoritatively in her own tasks. And when they tell stories about the hero, she listens with rapt attention. 3.3.30 Sent by her foster-sister, she enters the hero's abode. She wishes to arrange, with [the foster-sister] as intermediary, games, pastimes, and conversation with him. When unadorned, she avoids his line of sight. When asked by him for an ear ornament, a ring, or a garland, she deliberately removes it from her body and places it in her friend's hand. She always wears what he has given her. She becomes despondent at talk of other suitors. And she does not associate with those on their side. 3.3.31 And here there are two verses: 3.3.31v [Verse:] Having observed these signs and gestures accompanied by feeling in the maiden, one should devise various strategies for the purpose of union with her. 3.3.32v [Verse:] A young girl should be won over through childhood play; one in the bloom of youth through the arts; and even an affectionate one, through winning the trust of her confidants.

children.text: 3.3c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāma-sūtre kanyā-saṃprayuktake tṛtīye 'dhikaraṇe bākopakramā iṅitākāra-sūcanaṃ tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ.

children.text:
3.4.1 darśiteṅgitākārāṃ kanyām upāyato 'bhiyuñjīta.
3.4.2 dyūte krīḍanakeṣu ca vivadamānaḥ sākāram asyāḥ pāṇim avalambeta.
3.4.3 yathoktaṃ ca spṛṣṭakādikam((81)) āliṅgana-vidhiṃ vidadhyāt.
3.4.4 pattra-cchedya-kriyāyāṃ ca svābhiprāya-sūcakaṃ mithunam asyā darśayet.
3.4.5 evam anyad viralaśo((82)) darśayet.
3.4.6 jala-krīḍāyāṃ tad-dūrato 'psu nimagnaḥ samīpam asyā gatvā spṛṣṭvā caināṃ tatraivonmajjayet.
3.4.7 navapattrikādiṣu ca sa:viśeṣa-bhāva-nivedanam.
3.4.8 ātma-duḥkhasyānirvedena kathanam.
3.4.9 svapnasya ca bhāva-yuktasyānyāpadeśena.
3.4.10 prekṣaṇake sva-jana-samāje vā samīpopaveśanam. tatrānyāpadiṣṭaṃ sparśanam.
3.4.11 apāśrayārthaṃ ca caraṇena caraṇasya pīḍanam.
3.4.12 tataḥ śanakair ekaikām aṅgulim abhispṛśet.
3.4.13 pādāṅuṣṭhena ca nakhāgrāṇi ghaṭṭayet.
3.4.14 tatra siddhaḥ padāt padam adhikam ākāṅkṣet.
3.4.15 kṣānty-arthaṃ ca tad evābhyaset.
3.4.16 pāda-śauce pādāṅguli-saṃdaṃśena tad-aṅguli-pīḍanam.
3.4.17 dravyasya samarpaṇe pratigrahe vā tad-gato vikāraḥ.
3.4.18 ācamanānte codakenāsekaḥ.
3.4.19 vijane tamasi ca dvandvam āsīnaḥ kṣāntiṃ kurvīta. samāna-deśa-śayyāyāṃ ca.
3.4.20 tatra yathārtham an:udvejayato bhāva-nivedanam.
3.4.21 vivikte ca kiṃ cid asti kathayitavyam ity uktvā nirvacanaṃ bhāvaṃ ca tatropalakṣayet. yathā pāradārike vakṣyāmaḥ.
3.4.22 vidita-bhāvas tu vyādhim apadiśyaināṃ vārtā-grahaṇārthaṃ svam udavasitam ānayet.
3.4.23 āgatāyāś ca śiraḥ-pīḍane niyogaḥ. pāṇim avalambya cāśyāḥ sākāraṃ nayanayor lalāṭe ca nidadhyāt.
3.4.24 auśādhāpadeśārthaṃ cāsyāḥ karma vinirdiśet.
3.4.25 idaṃ tvayā kartavyam. na hy etad-ṛte kanyāyā anyena kāryam iti gacchantīṃ punar āgamanānubandham enāṃ visṛjet.
3.4.26 asya ca yogasya trirātraṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ ca prayuktiḥ.
3.4.27 abhīkṣṇa-darśanārtham āgatāyāś ca goṣṭhīṃ vardhayet.
3.4.28 anyābhir api saha viśvāsanārtham adhikam adhikaṃ cābhiyuñjīta. na tu vacā nirvadet.
3.4.29 dūra-gata-bhāvo 'pi hi kanyāsu na nirvedena sidhyātīti ghoṭakamukhaḥ.
3.4.30 yadā tu bahu-siddhāṃ manyeta tadaivopakramet..3.4.31 pradoṣe niśi tamasi ca yoṣito manda-sādhvasāḥ((83)) su:rata-vyavasāyinyo rāgavatyaś ca bhavanti. na tu puruṣaṃ pratyācakṣate. tasmāt tat-kālaṃ prayojayitavyā iti prāyovādaḥ.
3.4.32 eka-puruṣābhiyogānāṃ tv a:saṃbhave gṛhītārthayā dhātreyikayā sakhyā vā tasyām antar:bhūtayā tam artham a:nirvadantyā sahainām aṅkam ānāyayet. tato yathoktam abhiyuñjīta.
3.4.33 svāṃ vā paricārikām ādāv eva sakhītvenāsyāḥ praṇidadhyāt.
3.4.34 yajñe vivāhe yātrāyām utsave vyasane prekṣaṇaka-vyāpṛte((84)) jane tatra tatra ca dṛṣṭeṅgitākārāṃ parīkṣita-bhāvām ekākinīm upakrameta.
3.4.35 na hi dṛṣṭa-bhāvā yoṣito deśe kāle ca prayujyamānā((85)) vyāvartanta iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
children.translated_text:
3.4.1 One should skillfully approach a maiden who has shown her feelings through gestures and signs.
3.4.2 During gambling and games, while disputing, he should meaningfully take hold of her hand.
3.4.3 And as previously described, he should employ the embrace beginning with <s>spṛṣṭaka</s> (touching).
3.4.4 And in the art of leaf-cutting (<s>pattra-cchedya</s>), he should show her a couple that indicates his intention.
3.4.5 Likewise, he should show other [suggestive images] occasionally.
3.4.6 During water-sports, having submerged at a distance in the water, he should go near her, touch her, and emerge right there.
3.4.7 And at the <s>Navapatrikā</s> festival and the like, a declaration of special affection.
3.4.8 Narrating one's own sorrow without discouragement.
3.4.9 And [telling] a dream connected with his feelings, under the pretext of something else.
3.4.10 At a spectacle or a gathering of one's own people, sitting nearby; there, touching under some pretext.
3.4.11 And pressing foot upon foot as if for support.
3.4.12 Then he should slowly touch each finger one by one.
3.4.13 And with the big toe, he should tap the tips of her nails.
3.4.14 Having succeeded there, he should seek to advance step by step.
3.4.15 And for the sake of [gaining her] forbearance, he should practice that very same [approach].
3.4.16 During the washing of feet, pressing her fingers with the toe-clasp — pressing those fingers.
3.4.17 In the giving or receiving of an object, a change in his [demeanor] directed toward her.
3.4.18 At the end of sipping water, sprinkling her with water.
3.4.19 And in a secluded or dark place, sitting as a couple, he should exercise patience. And likewise on a shared sleeping-place.
3.4.20 There, a declaration of feelings that is truthful and not alarming to her.
3.4.21 And in private, having said 'There is something I must tell you,' he should indicate through etymology his feelings there — as we shall describe in the section on other men's wives.
3.4.22 But when her feelings are known, feigning illness, he should have her brought to his own quarters for the purpose of obtaining news.
3.4.23 And when she has arrived, the task is to press her head. Holding her hand, he should meaningfully place it upon her eyes and forehead.
3.4.24 And under the pretext of medicine, he should assign tasks for her.
3.4.25 [He should say:] 'This must be done by you, for this cannot be done by a maiden through anyone else' — and dismissing her as she departs, with a condition for her return.
3.4.26 This procedure should be applied over three nights and three twilight-periods.
3.4.27 And when she comes for the purpose of frequent visits, he should extend the conversation.
3.4.28 He should also engage her through others to build her trust, and he should approach her more and more. But he should not express his feelings verbally.
3.4.29 'For even one whose feelings have gone far does not succeed with maidens through [mere] verbal declaration' — so says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>.
3.4.30 But when he considers her well-won over, only then should he make his advance.
3.4.31 At dusk, in the night, and in the darkness, women are of mild timidity, inclined to the engagement of lovemaking, and become passionate — and they do not refuse a man. Therefore, one should engage her at that time — this is the general rule.
3.4.32 But when the approach of a single man is not possible, he should bring her to his lap through a nurse-companion or female friend who has entered into her confidence and who does not openly discourage that purpose. Then he should approach as described.
3.4.33 Or he should first establish his own maidservant in friendship with her.
3.4.34 At a sacrifice, wedding, festival procession, calamity, spectacle, or when people are busy — wherever she has been observed through gestures and signs and her feelings have been tested — he should approach her when she is alone.
3.4.35 'For women whose feelings have been perceived, when engaged at the right place and time, do not turn away' — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.translated_text: Thus, the approach of a single man.

3.4.36 mandāpadeśā((87)) guṇavaty api kanyā dhana-hīnā kulīnāpi samānair a:yācyamānā mātāpitṛ-viyuktā vā jñāti-kula-vartinī vā prāpta-yauvanā pāṇi-grahaṇaṃ svayam abhīpseta.
3.4.37 sā tu guṇavantaṃ śaktaṃ su:darśanaṃ bāla-prītyābhiyojayet.
3.4.38 yaṃ vā manyeta mātāpitror a:samīkṣayā svayam apy ayam indriya-daurbalyān mayi pravartiṣyata iti priya-hitopacārair abhīkṣṇa-saṃdarśanena ca tam āvarjayet.
3.4.39 mātā caināṃ sakhībhir dhātreyikābhiś ca saha tad-abhimukhīṃ kuryāt.
3.4.40 puṣpa-gandha-tāmbūla-hastāyā vi:jane vi:kāle ca tad-upasthānam. kalā-kauśala-prakāśane vā saṃvāhane śirasaḥ pīḍane caucitya-darśanam. prayojyasya sātmya-yuktāḥ kathā-yogāḥ bālāyām upakrameṣu yathoktam ācaret((88)).
3.4.41 na caivāntarāpi((89)) puruṣaṃ svayam abhiyuñjīta. svayam abhiyoginī hi yuvatiḥ saubhāgyaṃ jahātīty ācāryāḥ.
3.4.42 tat-prayuktānāṃ tv abhiyogānām ānulomyena grahaṇam.
3.4.43 pariṣvaktā((90)) ca na vikṛtiṃ bhajet. ślakṣṇam((91)) ākāram a:jānatīva pratigṛhīyāt. vadana-grahaṇe balāt-kāraḥ.
3.4.44 rati-bhāvanām abhyarthyamānāyāḥ kṛcchrād guhya-saṃsparśanam.
3.4.45 abhyarthitāpi nātivivṛtā svayaṃ syāt. anyatrā:niścaya-kālāt((92)).
3.4.46 yadā tu manyetānurakto mayi na vyāvartayiṣyata iti tadaivainam abhiyuñjānaṃ bāla-bhāva- mokṣāya tvaret.
3.4.47 vimukta-kanyā-bhāvā ca viśvāsyeṣu prakāśayet.
children.translated_text:
3.4.36 A maiden who is virtuous but of meager prospects, or though well-born is not sought by equals, or who is separated from her parents, or who dwells with relatives — having reached maturity, should herself desire marriage.
3.4.37 She should engage, through youthful affection, a man who is virtuous, capable, and handsome.
3.4.38 Or one whom she thinks: 'Even without the deliberation of my parents, he will of his own accord, through the weakness of his senses, turn toward me' — him she should win over through affectionate and pleasing courtesies and through frequent meetings.
3.4.39 And her mother should direct her, together with her friends and nurse-companions, toward that [man].
3.4.40 With flowers, perfumes, and betel in hand, in private and at opportune times, attending upon him; displaying skill in arts; providing massage and head-pressing — showing propriety [in all]. The topics of conversation should be suited to the intended [man]; and in the initial approaches to a young woman, she should conduct herself as described.
3.4.41 But she should never herself directly approach a man, even inwardly; for a young woman who approaches [a man] herself loses her good fortune — so say the teachers.
3.4.42 But she may accept his approaches with compliance.
3.4.43 And when embraced, she should not show agitation; she should accept the gentle gestures as if not knowing [their intent]. When he grasps her face — resistance by force.
3.4.44 When entreated about the act of love, the touching of intimate parts should [come] with difficulty.
3.4.45 Even when entreated, she should not herself be excessively open — except at the time of final consummation.
3.4.46 But when she thinks 'He is attached to me, he will not turn away,' only then should she hasten to allow him who is approaching to remove her maidenly reticence.
3.4.47 And having given up her maidenhood, she should make it known to those she trusts.

children.text: 3.4.47c iti prayojyasyopāvartanam((93)).
children.translated_text: 3.4.47c Thus, the winning over of the intended [maiden].

children.text:
3.4.48 bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ.
3.4.48v kanyābhiyujyamānā tu yaṃ manyetāśrayaṃ sukham. anukūlaṃ ca vaśyaṃ ca tasya kuryāt parigraham..
3.4.49v an:apekṣya guṇān yatra rūpam aucityam eva ca. kurvīta dhana-lobhena patiṃ sāpatnakeṣv api..
3.4.50v tatra yukta-guṇaṃ vaśyaṃ śaktam balavad arthinam. upāyair abhiyuñjānaṃ kanyā na pratilobhayet..
3.4.51v varaṃ vaśyo daridro 'pi nir:guṇo 'py ātma-dhāraṇaḥ. guṇair yukto 'pi na tv evaṃ bahu-sādhāraṇaḥ..
3.4.52v prāyeṇa dhanināṃ dārā bahavo nir:avagrahāḥ. bāhye saty upabhoge 'pi nirvisrambhā bahiḥ-sukhāḥ..
3.4.53v nīco yas tv abhiyuñjīta puruṣaḥ palito 'pi vā. vi:deśa-gati-śīlaś ca na sa saṃyogam arhati..
3.4.54v yadṛcchayābhiyukto yo dambha-dyūtādhiko 'pi. sa:patnīkaś ca sāpatyo na sa saṃyogam arhati..
3.4.55v guṇa-sāmye 'bhiyoktṝṇām eko varayitā varaḥ. tatrābhiyoktari śraiṣṭhyam anurāgātmako hi saḥ((94))..
children.translated_text:
3.4.48 And here there are verses:
3.4.48v A maiden being courted should accept as her own the one whom she considers a comfortable refuge, who is agreeable and controllable.
3.4.49v Where virtues, appearance, and propriety are disregarded — she should not, out of greed for wealth, take a husband [who brings her] among co-wives.
3.4.50v A maiden should not resist one who possesses suitable qualities, is controllable, capable, strongly desirous, and employs proper means.
3.4.51v Better a controllable [husband], even if poor, even if without qualities, [so long as he is] self-sufficient — but never one who, though endowed with qualities, is shared by many.
3.4.52v Generally, the wives of the wealthy, being many and unrestrained, though enjoying external pleasures, are without trust and find their happiness outside [the marriage].
3.4.53v But a man who is low-born, or grey-haired, or habitually travels to foreign lands — he is not worthy of union.
3.4.54v One who approaches by chance, or one given to deceit and gambling, or one who already has a wife and children — he is not worthy of union.
3.4.55v When suitors are equal in qualities, he who is a single suitor is the best choice; for among suitors, the one who approaches first is supreme, for he is possessed of true love.
