Lesson 5: The Fifth Chapter.
Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 31: [Chapter on the Means of Marriage (<s>vivāha-yoga-prakaraṇam</s>)].

children.text:
3.5.1 prācuryeṇa((95)) kanyāyā vivikta-darśanasyālābhe dhātreyikāṃ priya-hitābhyām upagṛhyopasarpet.
3.5.2 sā cainām a:viditā nāma nāyakasya bhūtvā tad-guṇair anurañjayet. tasyāś ca rucyān nāyaka-guṇān bhūyiṣṭham upavarṇayet.
3.5.3 anyeṣāṃ varayitṝṇāṃ doṣān abhiprāya-viruddhān pratipādayet..3.5.4 mātāpitroś ca guṇān:abhijñatāṃ lubdhatāṃ ca capalatāṃ ca bāndhavānām.
3.5.5 yāś cānyā api samāna-jātīyāḥ kanyāḥ śakuntalādyāḥ sva-buddhyā bhartāraṃ prāpya saṃprayuktā modante sma((96)) tāś cāsyā nidarśayet.
3.5.6 mahā-kuleṣu sāpatnakair bādhyamānā vidviṣṭāḥ duḥkhitāḥ parityaktāś ca dṛśyante.
3.5.7 āyatiṃ cāsya varṇayet.
3.5.8 sukham an:upahatam eka-cāritāyāṃ nāyakānurāgaṃ ca varṇayet.
3.5.9 sa:manorathāyāś cāsyā apāyaṃ sādhvasaṃ vrīḍāṃ ca hetubhir avacchindyāt.
3.5.10 dūtī-kalpaṃ ca sakalam ācaret((97)).
3.5.11 tvām a:jānatīm iva nāyako balād grahīṣyatīti tathā su:parigṛhītaṃ syād iti yojayet.
3.5.12 pratipannām abhipretāvakāśa-vartinīṃ nāyakaḥ śrotriyāgārād agnim ānayya kuśān āstīrya yathā-smṛti hutvā ca triḥ parikramet.
3.5.13 tato mātari pitari ca prakāśayet.
3.5.14 agni-sākṣikā hi vivāhā na nivartanta ity ācārya-samayaḥ.
3.5.15 dūṣayitvā caināṃ śanaiḥ sva-jane prakāśayet.
3.5.16 tad-bāndhavāś ca yathā kulasyāghaṃ pariharanto daṇḍa-bhayāc((98)) ca tasmā evaināṃ dadyus tathā yojayet.
3.5.17 an:antaraṃ ca prīty-upagraheṇa rāgeṇa tad-bāndhavān prīṇayed((99)) iti.
3.5.18 gāndharveṇa vivāhena vā ceṣṭeta.
3.5.19 a:pratipadyamānāyām antaś-cāriṇīm anyāṃ kula-pramadāṃ pūrva saṃsṛṣṭāṃ prīyamāṇāṃ copagṛhya tayā saha viṣahyam avakāśam enām anya-kāryāpadeśenānāyayet.
3.5.20 tataḥ śrotriyāgārād agnim iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa((100)).
3.5.21 āsanne ca vivāhe mātaram asyās tad-abhimata-doṣair anuśayaṃ((101)) grāhayet.
3.5.22 tatas tad-anumatena prātiveśyā-bhāvane((102)) niśi nāyakam ānāyya śrotriyāgārād agnim iti sam~ānaṃ pūrveṇa.
3.5.23 bhrātaram asyā vā samāna-vayasaṃ veśyāsu para-strīṣu vā prasaktam a:sukareṇa sāhāyya-dānena priyopagrahaś ca su:dīrgha-kālam anurañjayet. ante ca svābhiprāyaṃ grāhayet.
3.5.24 prāyeṇa hi yuvānaḥ samāna-śīla-vyasana-vayasāṃ vayasyānām arthe jīvitam api tyajanti. tatas tenaivānya-kāryāt tām ānāyayet. viṣahyaṃ sāvakāśam((103)) iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa.
3.5.25 aṣṭamī-candrikādiṣu ca dhātreyikā madanīyam enāṃ pāyayitvā kiṃ cid ātmanaḥ kāryam uddiśya nāyakasya viṣahyaṃ deśam ānayet. tatraināṃ madāt saṃjñām a:pratipadyamānāṃ dūṣayitveti samānaṃ pūrveṇa.
3.5.26 suptāṃ caikacāriṇīṃ dhātreyikāṃ vārayitvā saṃjñām a:pratipadyamānāṃ dūṣayitveti samānaṃ pūrveṇa((104)).
3.5.27 grāmāntaram udyānaṃ vā gacchantīṃ viditvā su:saṃbhṛta-sahāyo nāyakas tadā rakṣiṇo vitrāsya hatvā vā kanyām apaharet((105)).
3.5.27c iti vivāha-yogāḥ.
3.5.28v pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ pradhānaṃ syād vivāho dharmataḥ sthiteḥ. pūrvābhāve tataḥ kāryo yo ya uttara uttaraḥ..
3.5.29v vyūḍhānāṃ hi vivāhānām anurāgaḥ phalaṃ yataḥ. madhyamo 'pi hi sad-yogo gāndharvas tena pūjitaḥ..
3.5.30v sukhatvād a:bahu-kleśād api cāvaraṇād iha. anurāgātmakatvāc ca gāndharvaḥ pravaro mataḥ((106))..
children.translated_text:
3.5.1 When it is not generally possible to see the maiden in private, one should approach through her foster-sister, winning her over with affection and helpfulness.
3.5.2 She, pretending not to know the lover's name, should make the maiden attracted by describing his virtues. And she should describe at length those virtues of the lover that appeal to the maiden's taste.
3.5.3 She should point out the faults of other suitors that are contrary to the maiden's wishes.
3.5.4 And [she should point out] the parents' lack of discernment of [the lover's] virtues, and the greed and fickleness of [the maiden's] relatives.
3.5.5 She should give her examples of other maidens of similar status — such as <s>Śakuntalā</s> and others — who, having chosen a husband by their own judgment, were happily united.
3.5.6 [She should say:] 'Women in great families, oppressed by co-wives, are seen to be hated, miserable, and abandoned.'
3.5.7 And she should describe his future prospects.
3.5.8 She should describe the unimpaired happiness of being an only wife, and the lover's devotion.
3.5.9 And she should dispel with reasons the maiden's apprehension, timidity, and bashfulness regarding her desires.
3.5.10 And she should perform all the functions of a female messenger.
3.5.11 She should arrange it so that [the maiden thinks:] 'The lover will seize you by force, as if you were unknowing' — so that it may be well accomplished.
3.5.12 When the maiden has consented and is present at the desired place, the lover should bring fire from the house of a <s>Śrotriya</s> (learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>), spread <s>kuśa</s> grass, perform oblations according to the <s>smṛti</s> (sacred tradition), and circumambulate [the fire] three times.
3.5.13 Then he should make it known to the mother and father.
3.5.14 For marriages witnessed by fire cannot be reversed — this is the convention of the teachers.
3.5.15 Having deflowered her, he should gradually make it known to her family.
3.5.16 And he should arrange it so that her relatives, in order to avoid disgrace to the family and out of fear of punishment, would give her to him alone.
3.5.17 And immediately thereafter, he should please her relatives with affectionate attentions and devotion.
3.5.18 Or he should strive for a <s>Gāndharva</s> marriage (marriage by mutual consent).
3.5.19 If she does not consent, he should enlist another noble woman of the inner circle who is previously acquainted [with the maiden] and favorably disposed, and through her, on a suitable occasion, bring the maiden under the pretext of some other purpose.
3.5.20 Then, [the procedure] 'bringing fire from the <s>Śrotriya</s>'s house' and so forth is the same as before.
3.5.21 And when the marriage is near, he should cause her mother to feel regret through [pointing out] the faults of the suitor she favors.
3.5.22 Then, with her consent, at a neighbor's house at night, having brought the lover, [the procedure] 'bringing fire from the <s>Śrotriya</s>'s house' and so forth is the same as before.
3.5.23 Or he should win over her brother of the same age — one who is attached to courtesans or other men's wives — by readily helping him and showing him kindness over a very long period. And at the end, he should make his intention known.
3.5.24 For generally, young men will even give up their lives for the sake of friends of similar character, habits, and age. Then, through that [brother], under the pretext of some other matter, he should bring her [to a place where] 'it is suitable and there is opportunity' — the rest is the same as before.
3.5.25 And on occasions such as the eighth-day moonlight [festival], the foster-sister, having given her an intoxicating drink and mentioning some business of her own, should bring her to a suitable place of the lover. There, having deflowered her while she, due to intoxication, does not perceive what is happening — the rest is the same as before.
3.5.26 And [if she is] sleeping alone, having dismissed the foster-sister, having deflowered her while she does not perceive what is happening — the rest is the same as before.
3.5.27 Or, learning that she is going to another village or garden, the lover, well-equipped with companions, should at that time frighten or overpower the guards and carry off the maiden.
3.5.27c Thus are the methods of marriage (<s>vivāha-yogāḥ</s>).
3.5.28v The earlier [forms of] marriage should take precedence by the rule of <s>dharma</s>. In the absence of the earlier [forms], the successively later ones should be resorted to.
3.5.29v Since the fruit of marriages duly performed is mutual love, even a union of the middle type — the <s>Gāndharva</s> [marriage] — is honored for this reason.
3.5.30v Because of its pleasantness, because it involves not much hardship, and because even of its inferior [ritual] status in this world, and because its essence is mutual love — the <s>Gāndharva</s> [marriage] is considered the best.

Lesson 1: The First Chapter.
Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 32: [The Section on the Conduct of an Only Wife (<s>Eka-cāriṇī-vṛtta</s>)].

children.text:
4.1.1 bhāryaikacariṇī gūḍha-viśrambhā((107)) devavat patim ānukulyena varteta.
4.1.2 tan-matena kuṭumba-cintām ātmani saṃniveśayet.
4.1.3 veśma ca śuci su:saṃmṛṣṭa-sthānaṃ viracita-vividha-kusumaṃ ślakṣṇa-bhūmi-talaṃ hṛdya-darśanaṃ((108)) triṣavaṇācarita-bali-karma pūjita-devatāyatanaṃ kuryāt.
4.1.4 na hy ato 'nyad gṛhasthānāṃ citta-grāhakam astīti gonardīyaḥ.
4.1.5 guruṣu bhṛtya-vargeṣu nāyaka-bhaginīṣu((109)) tat-patiṣu ca yathārhaṃ pratipattiḥ((110)).
4.1.6 paripūteṣu ca harita-śāka-vaprān ikṣu-stambāñ jīraka-sarṣapājamoda-śatapuṣpā-tamāla-gulmāṃś ca kārayet((111)).
4.1.7 kubjakāmalaka-mallikā-jātī-kuraṇṭaka-navamālikā-tagara-nandyāvartajapā-gulmān anyāṃś ca bahu-puṣpān bāla-kośīraka-pātālikāṃś ca vṛkṣa-vāṭikāyāṃ ca sthaṇḍilāṇi mano-jñāni kārayet((112)).
4.1.8 madhye kūpaṃ vāpīṃ dīrghikāṃ vā khānayet.
4.1.9 bhikṣukī-śramāṇā-kṣapaṇā-kulaṭā-kuhakekṣaṇikā-mūla-kārikābhir na saṃsṛjyeta.
4.1.10 bhojane ca rucitam idam asmai dveṣyam idaṃ pathyam idam a:pathyam idam iti ca vindyāt.
4.1.11 svaraṃ bahir upaśrutya bhavanam āgacchataḥ kiṃ kṛtyam iti bruvatī sajjā((113)) bhavana-madhye tiṣṭhet.
4.1.12 paricārikam apanudya svayaṃ pādau prakṣālayet.
4.1.13 nāyakasya ca na vimukta-bhūṣaṇaṃ vijane saṃdarśane tiṣṭhet.
4.1.14 ati:vyayam a:sad-vyayaṃ vā kurvāṇaṃ rahasi bodhayet.
4.1.15 āvāhe vivāhe yajñe gamanaṃ sakhībhiḥ saha goṣṭhīṃ devatābhigamanm ity anujñātā kuryāt.
4.1.16 sarva-krīḍāsu ca tad-ānulomyena pravṛttiḥ.
4.1.17 paścāt saṃveśanaṃ pūrvam utthānam an:avabodhanaṃ ca suptasya.
4.1.18 mahānasaṃ ca su:guptaṃ syād darśanīyaṃ ca.
4.1.19 nāyakāpacāreṣu kiṃ cit kaluṣitā nāty:arthaṃ nirvadet.
4.1.20 sādhikṣepa-vacanaṃ tv enaṃ mitra-jana-madhya-stham ekākinaṃ vāpy upālabheta. na ca mūla-kārikā syāt.
4.1.21 na hy ato 'nyad a:pratyaya-kāraṇam astīti gonardīyaḥ.
4.1.22 dur:vyāhṛtaṃ dur:nirīkṣitam anyato mantraṇaṃ dvāra-deśāvasthānaṃ nirīkṣaṇaṃ vā niṣkuṭeṣu((114)) mantraṇaṃ vivikteṣu ciram avasthānam iti varjayet.
4.1.23 sveda-danta-paṅka-dur:gandhāṃś ca budhyeteti virāga-kāraṇam.
4.1.24 bahu-bhūṣaṇaṃ vividha-kusumānulepanaṃ vividhāṅga-rāga-samujjvalaṃ vāsa ity ābhigāmiko veṣaḥ.
4.1.25 pratanu-ślakṣṇālpa-dukūlatā parimitam ābharaṇaṃ su:gandhitā nāty:ulvaṇam((115)) anulepanam. tathā śuklāny anyāni puṣpāṇīti vaihāriko veṣaḥ.
4.1.26 nāyakasya vratam upavāsaṃ ca svayam api karaṇenānuvarteta. vāritāyāṃ ca nāham atra nirbandhanīyeti tad-vacaso nivartanam.
4.1.27 mṛd-vidala-kāṣṭha-carma-loha-bhāṇḍānāṃ ca kāle sam:argha-grahaṇam((116)).
4.1.28 tathā lavaṇa-snehayoś ca gandha-dravya-kaṭuka-bhāṇḍauṣadhānāṃ ca dur:labhānāṃ bhavaneṣu pracchannaṃ nidhānam.
4.1.29 mūlakāluka-pālaṅkī-damanakāmrātakairvāruka-trapu-savārtāka-kūṣmāṇḍālābu-sūraṇa-śukanāsā- svayamguptā-tila-parṇikāgnimantha-laśuna-palāṇḍu-prabhṛtīnāṃ sarvauṣadhīnāṃ ca bīja-grahaṇaṃ kāle vāpaś ca.
4.1.30 svasya ca sārasya parebhyo nākhyānaṃ bhartṛ-mantritasya ca.
4.1.31 samānāś ca striyaḥ kauśalenojjvalatayā pākena mānena tathopacārair atiśayīta.
4.1.32 sāṃvatsarikam āyaṃ saṃkhyāya tad-anurūpaṃ vyayaṃ kuryāt.
4.1.33 bhojanāvaśiṣṭād go-rasād ghṛta-karaṇam tathā tela-guḍayoḥ. karpāsasya ca sūtra-kartanam sūtrasya vānam. śikya-rajju-pāśa-valkala-saṃgrahaṇam. kuṭṭana-kaṇḍanāvekṣaṇam. āma-cāmaṇḍa-tuṣaka-khakuṭy-aṅgārāṇām upayojanam. bhṛtya-vetana- bharaṇa-jñānam. kṛṣi-paśu-pālana-cintā-vāhana-vidhāna-yogāḥ. meṣa-kukkuṭa-lāvaka- śuka-śārikā-parabhṛta-mayūra-vānara-mṛgāṇām avekṣaṇam. daivasikāya-vyaya-piṇḍī- karaṇam iti ca vidyāt.
4.1.34 taj-jaghanyānāṃ ca jīrṇa-vāsasāṃ saṃcayas tair vividha-rāgaiḥ śuddhair vā kṛta-karmaṇāṃ paricārakāṇām anugraho mānārtheṣu ca dānam anyatra vopayogaḥ..4.1.35 surā-kumbhīnām āsava-kumbhīnāṃ ca sthāpanaṃ tad-upayogaḥ kraya-vikrayāv āya-vyāyāvekṣaṇam.
4.1.36 nāyaka-mitrāṇāṃ ca srag-anulepana-tāmbūla-dānaiḥ pūjanaṃ nyāyataḥ.
4.1.37 śvaśrū-svaśura-paricaryā tat-pāratantryam an:uttara-vāditā parimitā:pracaṇḍālāpa-karaṇam an:uccair hāsaḥ tat-priyā:priyeṣu sva-priyā:priyeṣv iva vṛttiḥ.
4.1.38 bhogeṣv an:utsekaḥ.
4.1.39 parijane dākṣiṇyam.
4.1.40 nāyakasyā:nivedya na kasmai cid dānam.
4.1.41 sva-karmasu bhṛtya-jana-niyamanam utsaveṣu cāsya pūjanam.
children.translated_text: 4.1.1 A wife who is devoted to one husband, with deep secret trust, should behave toward her husband with compliance, as toward a god. 4.1.2 According to his wishes, she should take upon herself the care of the household. 4.1.3 She should make the house clean, with well-swept spaces, decorated with various flowers, with smooth floors, pleasing to look at, with offerings performed at the three junctions of the day, and with the family shrine properly worshipped. 4.1.4 For there is nothing else that captures the minds of householders more than this — says <s>Gonardīya</s>. 4.1.5 Toward elders, the household servants, the husband's sisters, and their husbands, she should behave with appropriate respect. 4.1.6 In the kitchen garden, she should have planted: beds of green vegetables, sugarcane stalks, cumin, mustard, celery, dill, and <s>tamāla</s> bushes. 4.1.7 She should have planted in the garden: bushes of <s>kubja</s>, gooseberry, jasmine, <s>jātī</s>, <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>, <s>navamālikā</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>nandyāvarta</s>, <s>japā</s> (hibiscus), and other profusely flowering plants, as well as young <s>kośīraka</s> and <s>pātālikā</s> trees, and she should arrange pleasant ground-plots in the tree-garden. 4.1.8 In the middle, she should have a well, a step-well, or a tank dug. 4.1.9 She should not associate with female mendicants, <s>śramaṇās</s> (ascetics), <s>kṣapaṇās</s> (Jain nuns), loose women, fortune-tellers, or herbalist women. 4.1.10 Regarding food, she should know what he likes, what he dislikes, what is wholesome for him, and what is unwholesome. 4.1.11 Hearing his voice outside as he comes home, saying 'What is to be done?', she should stand ready in the middle of the house. 4.1.12 Dismissing the attendant, she should herself wash his feet. 4.1.13 She should not stand before the husband without her ornaments, or in a deserted place. 4.1.14 If he makes excessive or improper expenditures, she should advise him in private. 4.1.15 Attending weddings, marriage ceremonies, sacrifices, going out, social gatherings, and visits to temples — these she should do only with permission. 4.1.16 And in all recreations, she should follow his inclinations. 4.1.17 She should go to bed after him and rise before him, and not wake him when he is asleep. 4.1.18 The kitchen should be well-concealed yet well-kept. 4.1.19 When the husband misbehaves, she should show slight displeasure but not rebuke him excessively. 4.1.20 But she may reproach him with gentle sarcasm when among friends or when alone — and she should not be a user of magic roots. 4.1.21 For there is nothing else that causes greater loss of trust than that — says <s>Gonardīya</s>. 4.1.22 She should avoid: speaking rudely, looking improperly, whispering to others, standing at the doorway or peering out, whispering in secluded garden nooks, and remaining long in solitary places. 4.1.23 She should be aware that perspiration, dirty teeth, body odor, and foul smells cause aversion. 4.1.24 Abundant jewelry, various flower-ointments, garments bright with various body-colors — this is the dress for lovemaking. 4.1.25 Thin, smooth, scanty fine cloth, limited ornaments, pleasant fragrance without excess, and white flowers — this is the dress for leisure. 4.1.26 She should herself observe her husband's vows and fasts, and if forbidden [from fasting alongside him], she should desist from her insistence at his word. 4.1.27 She should acquire vessels of earth, bark, wood, leather, and metal at the right time and price. 4.1.28 Likewise, salt, oils, fragrant substances, pungent spices, utensils, medicines, and rare items should be stored secretly in the house. 4.1.29 She should collect seeds of radish, potato, spinach, <s>damanaka</s>, wild mango, cucumber, squash, eggplant, pumpkin, gourd, <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant yam), <s>śukanāsā</s>, <s>svayamguptā</s>, <s>tilaparṇikā</s>, <s>agnimantha</s>, garlic, onion, and all medicinal herbs at the proper time, and plant them. 4.1.30 She should not reveal her own affairs to others, nor what her husband has confided. 4.1.31 She should surpass other women of equal standing through her skill, radiance, cooking, propriety, and courtesies. 4.1.32 Having calculated the annual income, she should make expenditures proportionate to it. 4.1.33 She should know: making ghee from leftover milk-products, and oils and molasses; spinning cotton into thread and weaving thread into cloth; collecting cord, rope, bark-fiber, and creeper-rope; supervising husking and pounding; utilizing raw hides, wool, chaff, potsherds, and charcoal; managing servants' wages and maintenance; caring for agriculture, animal-husbandry, vehicle arrangements; looking after sheep, roosters, quails, parrots, mynahs, cuckoos, peacocks, monkeys, and deer; and accounting for daily income and expenditure. 4.1.34 She should collect her husband's worn garments; and through various dyes or cleanly made, these should be given to attendants as rewards or donations for meritorious purposes, or used otherwise. 4.1.35 She should manage the storage and use of liquor and spirit jars, and oversee buying, selling, income, and expenditure. 4.1.36 She should honor the husband's friends with garlands, ointments, and betel in proper fashion. 4.1.37 Service to her mother-in-law and father-in-law, subordination to them, not answering back, measured and restrained speech, not laughing loudly, and treating their likes and dislikes as her own. 4.1.38 No arrogance in enjoyments. 4.1.39 Courtesy toward the household. 4.1.40 Without informing the husband, she should not give anything to anyone. 4.1.41 She should manage the servants in their duties and worship [the husband] during festivals.

children.text: 4.1.41c ity ekacāriṇī-vṛttam((117)).
children.translated_text: 4.1.41c Thus, the conduct of a devoted wife.

children.text: section (prakaraṇa)33 [pravāsa-caryyā-prakaraṇam]
children.translated_text: Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 33: [Chapter on Conduct During the Husband's Absence].

children.text:
4.1.42 pravāse maṅgala-mātrābharaṇā devatopavāsa-parā vārtāyāṃ sthitā gṛhān avekṣeta.
4.1.43 śayyā ca guru-jana-mūle. tad-abhimatā kārya-niṣpattiḥ. nāyakābhimatānāṃ cārthānām arjane pratisaṃskāre ca yatnaḥ.
4.1.44 nitya-naimittikeṣu karmasūcito vyayaḥ. tad-ārabdhānāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ samāpane matiḥ.
4.1.45 jñāti-kulasyān:abhigamanam anyatra vyasanotsavābhyām((118)). tatrāpi nāyaka-parijanādhiṣṭhitāyā nātikālam avasthānam a:parivartita-pravāsa-veṣatā ca.
4.1.46 guru-janānujñātānāṃ karaṇam upavāsānām. paricārakaiḥ śucibhir ājñādhiṣṭhitair anumatena kraya-vikraya-karmaṇā sārasyāpūraṇaṃ tanū-karaṇaṃ ca śaktyā vyayānām.
4.1.47 āgate ca prakṛtisthāyā eva prathamato darśanaṃ daivata-pūjanam upahārāṇāṃ cāharaṇam.
4.1.47c iti pravāsa-caryā((119)).
4.1.48 bhavataś cātra ślokau.
4.1.48v sad-vṛttam((120)) anuvarteta nāyakasya hitaiṣiṇī. kula-yoṣā punarbhūr vā veśyā vāpy ekacāriṇī.. dharmam arthaṃ tathā kāmaṃ labhante sthānam eva ca. niḥ:sapatnaṃ ca bhartāraṃ nāryaḥ sad-vṛttam āśritāḥ..
children.translated_text: 4.1.42 During the husband's absence, wearing only auspicious ornaments, devoted to worship and fasting, occupied with household affairs, she should watch over the house. 4.1.43 She should sleep near the elders. The completion of tasks should be as they desire. She should make efforts in acquiring and maintaining the things dear to the husband. 4.1.44 Expenditures should be as indicated for regular and occasional duties. She should aim to complete the tasks he had begun. 4.1.45 She should not visit the homes of her relatives, except in cases of calamity or festival. Even then, accompanied by the husband's household members, she should not stay too long, and should maintain her appearance as during the absence. 4.1.46 She should observe the fasts permitted by the elders. Through clean servants under her direction, with authorized buying and selling, she should replenish the stores and reduce expenses as far as possible. 4.1.47 And when he returns, she should first present herself in her natural state, then worship the deities and bring offerings. 4.1.47c Thus, the conduct during absence. 4.1.48 And here are two verses: (verse) A wife who desires her husband's welfare should follow good conduct — whether a woman of family, a remarried woman, or even a courtesan acting as a devoted wife. <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s>, and <s>Kāma</s>, as well as standing, and a husband free from rivals — these women who follow good conduct obtain.

children.text: 4.1c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre bhāryādhikārike caturthe 'dhikaraṇe ekacāriṇī-vṛttaṃ pravāsa-cāryā ca prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the fourth section <s>Bhāryādhikārika</s> (On the Conduct of Wives), the first chapter: The Conduct of a Devoted Wife and Behavior During the Husband's Absence.

children.text:
leçon 2 dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ.
section (prakaraṇa)34 [jyeṣṭhādi-vṛtta-prakaraṇam]
children.translated_text: Lesson 2: The Second Chapter. Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 34: [Chapter on the Conduct of the Senior Wife and Others].

children.text:
4.2.1 jāḍya-dauḥśīlya-daurbhāgyebhyaḥ prajān:utpatter ābhīkṣṇyena dārikotpatter nāyaka-cāpalād vā sapatny-adhivedanam.
4.2.2 tad ādita eva bhakti-śīla-vaidagdhya-khyāpanena parijihīrṣet. prajā:nutpattau ca svayam eva sāpatnake codayet.
4.2.3 adhividyamānā ca yāvac chakti-yogād ātmano 'dhikatvena sthitiṃ kārayet.
4.2.4 āgatāṃ caināṃ bhaginīvad īkṣeta. nayaka-viditaṃ ca prādoṣikaṃ vidhimatīva yatnād asyāḥ kārayet. saubhāgyajaṃ vaikṛtam utsekaṃ vāsyā nādriyeta.
4.2.5 bhartari pramādyantīm upekṣeta. yatra manyetārtham iyaṃ svayam api pratipatsyata iti tatrainām ādarata evānuśiṣyāt.
4.2.6 nāyaka-saṃśrave ca rahasi viśeṣān adhikān darśayet.
4.2.7 tad-apatyesv a:viśeṣaḥ. parijana-varge 'dhikānukampā. mitra-varge prītiḥ. ātma-jñātiṣu nāty:ādaraḥ. taj-jñātiṣu cāti:saṃbhramaḥ.
4.2.8 bahvībhis tv adhivinnā a:vyavahitayā saṃsṛjyeta.
4.2.9 yāṃ tu nāyako 'dhikāṃ cikīrṣet tāṃ bhūta-pūrva-subhagayā protsāhya kalahayet.
4.2.10 tataś cānukampeta.
4.2.11 tābhir ekatvenādhikāṃ cikirṣītāṃ svayam a:vivadamānā dur:janī:kuryāt.
4.2.12 nāyakena tu kalahitām enāṃ pakṣapātāvalambanopabṛmhitām āśvāsayet.
4.2.13 kalahaṃ ca vardhayet.
4.2.14 mandaṃ vā kalaham upalabhya svayam eva saṃdhukṣayet.
4.2.15 yadi nāyako 'syām adyāpi sānunaya iti manyeta tadā svayameva sandhau prayateta.
children.translated_text:
4.2.1 The supersession by a co-wife (<s>sapatny-adhivedana</s>) [occurs] due to stupidity, bad character, or misfortune; due to the non-production of offspring; due to the frequent birth of daughters; or due to the fickleness of the husband.
4.2.2 She should try to ward this off from the very beginning by making known her devotion, good character, and cleverness. And in the event of non-production of offspring, she herself should urge [the husband] toward the co-wife.
4.2.3 When being superseded, she should maintain her position as superior to the extent of her abilities.
4.2.4 And she should regard the newly arrived [co-wife] as a sister. With the husband's knowledge, she should diligently perform the evening rituals for her, as if [the co-wife] were observant of propriety. She should not pay attention to the other's arrogance or haughtiness born of being favored.
4.2.5 She should overlook [the co-wife] when the latter is negligent toward the husband. Where she thinks 'she will understand this matter herself,' there she should instruct her with [apparent] regard.
4.2.6 And within the husband's hearing, she should in private reveal her own special and superior [qualities].
4.2.7 Toward the co-wife's children, [she should show] no discrimination. Toward the attendant class, greater compassion. Toward the circle of friends, affection. Toward her own relatives, not excessive regard. Toward the other's relatives, excessive attentiveness.
4.2.8 But when superseded by many [co-wives], she should associate with the one nearest [in rank].
4.2.9 Whichever one the husband wishes to favor more, she should encourage that one — using the formerly favored one — and incite quarrels.
4.2.10 And then she should show compassion.
4.2.11 Without quarreling herself, she should defame the one whom all of them unitedly wish to elevate as the favorite.
4.2.12 But when [a co-wife] has quarreled with the husband, she should console her, being strengthened by taking her side.
4.2.13 And she should intensify the quarrel.
4.2.14 Or, having noticed a mild quarrel, she should herself fan the flames.
4.2.15 If she thinks the husband is still conciliatory toward her [rival], then she herself should make efforts toward reconciliation.

children.text: 4.2.15c iti jyeṣṭhā-vṛttam((121)).
children.translated_text: 4.2.15c Thus [is described] the conduct of the senior wife (<s>jyeṣṭhā-vṛtta</s>).

children.text: section (prakaraṇa)35
children.translated_text: Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 35

children.text:
4.2.16 kaniṣṭhā tu mātṛvat sa:patnīṃ paśyet.
4.2.17 jñāti-dāyam api tasyā a:viditaṃ nopayuñjīta.
4.2.18 ātma-vṛttāntāṃs tad-adhiṣṭhitān kuryāt.
4.2.19 anujñātā patim adhiśayīta.
4.2.20 na vā tasyā vacanam anyasyāḥ kathayet.
4.2.21 tad-apatyāni svebhyo 'dhikāni paśyet..4.2.22 rahasi patim adhikam upacaret.
4.2.23 ātmanaś ca sapatnī-vikāra-jaṃ duḥkhaṃ nācakṣīta.
4.2.24 patyuṣ ca sa:viśeṣakaṃ gūḍhaṃ mānaṃ lipset.
4.2.25 anena khalu pathya-dānena jīvāmīti brūyāt.
4.2.26 tat tu ślāghayā rāgeṇa vā bāhir nācakṣīta.
4.2.27 bhinna-rahasyā hi bhartur avajñāṃ labhate.
4.2.28 jyeṣṭhā-bhayāc ca nigūḍha-saṃmānārthinī syād iti gonardīyaḥ.
4.2.29 dur:bhāgam an:apatyāṃ ca jyeṣṭhām anukampeta nāyakena cānukampayet.
4.2.30 prasahya tv enām ekacāriṇī-vṛttam anutiṣṭhet
children.translated_text:
4.2.16 The junior wife (<s>kaniṣṭhā</s>) should regard the co-wife as a mother.
4.2.17 She should not use even the gifts from her own family without the other's knowledge.
4.2.18 She should conduct her own affairs under the other's authority.
4.2.19 When given permission, she may sleep with the husband.
4.2.20 She should not report the other's words, whether good or bad, to anyone. She would be praised as well-conducted in the house if she bears children. She should regard the senior wife's feet as of greater value than her own head. And with the husband's knowledge, she should serve her.
4.2.21 She should not approach the husband in the other's presence.
4.2.22 The [senior wife's] words spoken in the ear of the husband she should not repeat.
4.2.23 The senior wife's children should be treated with more [affection] than her own.
4.2.24 In private she may serve the husband.
4.2.25 She should not reveal the secrets told by the senior wife to the husband.
4.2.26 The senior wife's friends — she should serve them and make herself agreeable.
4.2.27 And toward the husband's friends and attendants, even more so.
4.2.28 She should be devoted to worship of the gods, festivals, chanting, fasting, and vows.
4.2.29 She should not adorn herself more than the senior wife.
4.2.30 If offended, she should not [respond with] anger, but should approach with tears through the mediation of the senior wife.

children.text: 4.2.30c iti kaniṣṭhā-vṛttam((122)).
children.translated_text: 4.2.30c Thus [is described] the conduct of the junior wife (<s>kaniṣṭhā-vṛtta</s>).

children.text: section (prakaraṇa)36
children.translated_text: Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 36

children.text:
4.2.31 vidhavā tv indriya-daurbalyād āturā bhoginaṃ guṇa-saṃpannaṃ ca yā punar vindet sā punarbhūḥ.
4.2.32 yatas tu svecchayā punar api niṣkramaṇaṃ nir:guṇo 'yam iti tadānyaṃ kāṅkṣed iti bābhravīyāḥ.
4.2.33 saukhyārthinī sā kilānyaṃ punar vindeta.
4.2.34 guṇeṣu sopabhogeṣu sukha-sākalyaṃ tasmāt tato viśeṣa iti gonardīyaḥ.
4.2.35 ātmanaś cittānukūlyād iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
4.2.36 sā bāndhavair nāyakād āpānakodyāna-śraddhā-dāna-mitra-pūjanādi vyaya-sahiṣṇu karma lipseta.
4.2.37 ātmanaḥ sāreṇa vālaṅkāraṃ tadīyam ātmīyaṃ vā bibhṛyāt.
4.2.38 prīti-dāyeṣv a:niyamaḥ.
4.2.39 svecchayā ca gṛhān nirgacchatī prīti-dāyād anyan nāyaka-dattaṃ jīyeta. niṣkāsyamānā tu na kiṃ cid dadyāt.
4.2.40 sā prabhaviṣṇur iva tasya bhavanam āpnuyāt.
4.2.41 kulajāsu tu prītyā varteta.
4.2.42 dākṣiṇyena parijane sarvatra sa:parihāsā mitreṣu pratipattiḥ. kalāsu kauśalam adhikasya ca jñānam.
4.2.43 kalaha-sthāneṣu ca nāyakaṃ svayam upalabheta.
4.2.44 rahasi ca kalayā catuḥṣaṣṭyānuvarteta. sa:patnīnāṃ ca svayam upakuryāt. tāsām apatyeṣv ābhāraṇa-dānam. teṣu svāmivad upacāraḥ. maṇḍanakāni veṣānādareṇa kurvīta. parijane mitravarge cādhikaṃ viśrāṇanam((123)). samājāpānakodyāna-yātrā-vihāra-śīlatā ca.
children.translated_text:
4.2.31 A widow who, afflicted by the weakness of her senses, takes again a man endowed with enjoyments and good qualities — she is a remarried woman (<s>punarbhū</s>).
4.2.32 But since departure at one's own will is possible again, [the marriage to] a worthless man should not be [considered permanent] — she should desire another, according to the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>.
4.2.33 However, a great family [may] not permit this, as it would be contrary to the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), according to <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.
4.2.34 She should, by whatever means available, make the current man into a vessel of good qualities — that is the summary.
4.2.35 Her ornament is continence; and [she should maintain] friendliness with her co-wives.
4.2.36 She should give him the personal property brought from her former husband's house, and make herself well-disposed through pleasant service.
4.2.37 She should display greater skill in the sixty-four arts than the co-wives.
4.2.38 But she should respect the co-wives' children as if they were her own, and her own children even more [should be given] to them.
4.2.39 The husband she should serve privately with additional affection.
4.2.40 The faults born of her former life she should demonstrate to be the result of [his] instructions alone.
4.2.41 She should not excessively reveal her former experience in the arts of love.
4.2.42 In the matters in which the former husband delighted, she should please the current one.
4.2.43 But she should not speak of her affection for the former husband before the current one.
4.2.44 She should make him understand by comparison: 'In such-and-such a manner did the former one act' — in the case of a deficient [husband].

children.text: 4.2.44c iti punarbhūvṛttam((124)).
children.translated_text: 4.2.44c Thus [is described] the conduct of the remarried woman (<s>punarbhū-vṛtta</s>).

children.text: section (prakaraṇa)37
children.translated_text: Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 37

children.text:
4.2.45 durbhagā tu sāpatnaka-pīḍitā yā tāsām adhikam iva patyāv upacaret tām āśrayet. prakāśyāni ca kalā-vijñānāni darśayet. daurbhāgyād rahasyānām a:bhāvaḥ.
4.2.46 nāyakāpatyānāṃ dhātreyikāni kuryāt.
4.2.47 tan-mitrāṇi copagṛhya tair bhaktim ātmanaḥ prakāśayet.
4.2.48 dharma-kṛtyeṣu ca puraś-cāriṇī syād vratopavāsayoś ca.
4.2.49 parijane dākṣiṇyam. na cādhikam ātmānaṃ paśyet.
4.2.50 śayane tat-sātmyenātmano 'nurāga-pratyānayanam.
4.2.51 na copālabheta vāmatāṃ ca na darśayet.
4.2.52 yayā ca kalahitaḥ syāt kāmaṃ tām āvartayet.
4.2.53 yāṃ ca pracchannāṃ kāmayet tām anena saha saṃgamayed gopayec ca.
4.2.54 yathā ca pativratātvam a:śāṭhyaṃ nāyako manyeta tathā pratividadhyāt.
children.translated_text:
4.2.45 An unlucky wife (<s>durbhagā</s>) — one who is afflicted by co-wives — should serve with greater [devotion] toward the husband than those [co-wives], and should take shelter with her. She should publicly display her knowledge of the arts. Due to her misfortune, she has no secrets [worth hiding].
4.2.46 She should serve as nurse to the husband's children. And she should make the husband's friends into her own allies. She should maintain constant devotion to the gods. She should observe the complete [ritual] duty on festive occasions. She should be modest, not haughty, not luxurious, and not quarrelsome with the co-wives.
4.2.47 She should seek a co-wife who is favored by the husband and would be helpful [to her]; or [one who], though favored by the husband, has an unsteady disposition and is susceptible to jealousy.
4.2.48 If the husband is attached to the senior wife, she should create division between them through an intimate companion.
4.2.49 She should be useful to the husband even from a distance.
4.2.50 She should be thoroughly versed in <s>mantras</s> (incantations), in preparations, in roots, and in the gaining of his favor.
4.2.51 She should not openly display anger or grief.
4.2.52 The husband's personal effects she should not disregard, nor approach them at improper times.
4.2.53 She should keep her own person and dwelling clean and well-ordered.
4.2.54 She should exhibit compliance with the husband's wishes.

children.text: 4.2.54c iti durbhagā-vṛttam((125)).
children.translated_text: 4.2.54c Thus [is described] the conduct of the unlucky wife (<s>durbhagā-vṛtta</s>).

children.text: section (prakaraṇa)38
children.translated_text: Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 38

children.text:
4.2.55 antaḥ-purāṇāṃ ca vṛttam eteṣv eva prakaraṇeṣu lakṣayet((126)).
4.2.56 mālyānulepana-vāsāṃśi cāsāṃ kañcukīyā mahattarikā vā rājño nivedayeyur devībhiḥ prahitam iti.
4.2.57 tad ādāya rājā nirmālyam āsāṃ pratiprābhṛtakaṃ dadyāt.
4.2.58 alaṃkṛtaś ca sv:alaṃkṛtāni cāparāhne sarvāṇy antaḥpurāṇy aikadhyena paśyet.
4.2.59 tāsāṃ yathā-kālaṃ yathārhaṃ ca sthāna-mānānuvṛttiḥ sa:parihāsāś ca kathāḥ kuryāt.
4.2.60 tad-an:antaraṃ punarbhuvas tathaiva paśyet.
4.2.61 tatpo veśyā ābhyantarikā nāṭakīyāś ca.
4.2.62 tāsāṃ yathokta-kakṣāṇi sthānāni.
4.2.63 vāsakapālyas tu yasyā vāsako yasyāś cātīto yasyāś ca ṛtus tat-paricārikānugatā divā śayyotthitasya rājñas tābhyāṃ prahitam aṅgulīyakāṅkam anulepanam ṛtuṃ vāsakaṃ ca nivedayeyuḥ.
4.2.64 tatra rājā yad gṛhṇīyāt tasyā vāsakam ājñāpayet.
4.2.65 utsaveṣu ca sarvāsām anurūpeṇa pūjāpānakaṃ ca. saṃgīta-darśaneṣu ca..4.2.66 antaḥ-pura-cāriṇīnāṃ bahir a:niṣkramo bāhyānāṃ cā:praveśaḥ. anyatra vidita-śaucābhyaḥ. a:parikliṣṭaś ca karmayogaḥ.
children.translated_text:
4.2.55 The conduct of women of the inner apartments (<s>antaḥpura</s>) should be discerned from these very sections.
4.2.56 Their garlands, ointments, and garments — the chamberlain (<s>kañcukīyā</s>) or the chief attendant should present [them] to the king, saying 'Sent by the queens.'
4.2.57 Taking those, the king should send [them] back as his used remainder (<s>nirmālya</s>). And a particular mark placed on the garland in the evening — thereby she should know [whose turn it is], they say.
4.2.58 Or alternatively, [the king] should honor the one who comes at the appointed time; or honor the one who has come bearing an auspicious thing at a festival.
4.2.59 In the inner apartments, there is no opportunity for concealment — due to their being guarded and due to the impossibility of knowing the proper time, according to <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.
4.2.60 But there is the case of certain [women] whose passion is aroused by proximity.
4.2.61 [The king's] attendants [include]: water-carriers, female servants, female jesters, and female dwarfs.
4.2.62 And because of being concealed, there is opportunity.
4.2.63 [The woman of the harem should] adorn herself, display her beauty, and express herself through gestures.
4.2.64 Having concealed herself [in the place] where the king is going or returning, she should exhibit her form.
4.2.65 Through the door-keeper she should converse with anyone.
4.2.66 And the conduct previously set forth under the topic of the messenger — that should also be observed here.

children.text: 4.2.66c ity āntaḥpurikam((127)).
children.translated_text: 4.2.66c Thus [is described the conduct] of [women] within the inner apartments (<s>āntaḥpurika</s>).

children.text: section (prakaraṇa)39
children.translated_text: Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 39

children.text:
4.2.67 bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ.
4.2.67v puruṣas tu bahūn darān samāhṛtya samo bhavet. na cāvajnāṃ cared āsu vyālikān na saheta ca..
4.2.68v ekasyāṃ yā rati-krīḍā vaikṛtaṃ vā śarīrajam. visrambhād vāpy upālambhas tam anyāsu na kīrtayet..
4.2.69v na dadyāt prasaraṃ strīṇāṃ sa:patnyāḥ kāraṇe kva cit. tathopālabhamānāṃ ca doṣais tām eva yojayet..
4.2.70v anyāṃ rahasi visrambhair anyāṃ pratyakṣa-pūjanaiḥ. bahu-mānais tathā canyām ity evaṃ rañjayet striyaḥ..
4.2.71v udyāna-gamanair bhogair dānais taj-jñāti-pūjanaiḥ. rahasyaiḥ prīti-yogaiś cety ekaikām anurañjayet..
4.2.72v yuvatiś ca jita-krodhā yathā-śāstra-pravartinī. karoti vaśyaṃ bhartāraṃ sa:patnīś cādhitiṣṭhati((128))..
children.translated_text:
4.2.67 And here there are verses:
4.2.67v A man who has gathered many wives should be impartial. He should not behave with contempt toward them, nor should he tolerate their deceits.
4.2.68v Whatever amorous play or bodily intimacy [he engages in] with one — due to familiarity or through the revelation of [another's] secret — he should not speak of before the others. Nor should he [allow] accusations [among them].
4.2.69v He should treat each one according to her particular disposition. He should honor one by the report of another. Having joined in her festivities, he should show her favor with ornaments, clothing, and respect.
4.2.70v He should not entrust one with [watching over] another's conduct. Nor should he ever reveal the faults of one to another. Thus a man endowed with these [qualities] obtains the love of even a thousand women.

5.1.1 vyākhyāta-kāraṇāḥ para-parigrahopagamāḥ((130)).
5.1.2 teṣu sādhyatvam an:atyayaṃ gamyatvam āyatiṃ vṛttiṃ cādita eva parīkṣeta.
5.1.3 yadā tu sthānāt sthānāntaraṃ kāmaṃ pratipadyamānaṃ paśyet tadātma-śarīropaghāta-trāṇārthaṃ para-parigrahān abhyupagacchet.
5.1.4 daśa tu kāmasya sthānāni.
5.1.5 [1]cakṣuḥ-prītir [2]manaḥ-saṅgaḥ [3]saṃkalpotpattir [4]nidrācchedas [5]tanutā [6]viṣayebhyo vyāvṛttir [7]lajjā-pranāśa [8]unmādo [9]mūrcchā [10]maraṇam iti teṣāṃ liṅgāni.
5.1.6 tatrākṛtito lakṣaṇataś ca yuvatyāḥ śīlaṃ satyaṃ śaucaṃ sādhyatāṃ caṇḍavegatāṃ ca lakṣayed ity ācāryāḥ.
5.1.7 vyabhicārād ākṛti-lakṣaṇa-yogānām iṅgitākārābhyām eva pravṛttir boddhavyā yoṣita iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
5.1.8 yaṃ kiṃ cid ujjvalaṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣtvā strī kāmayate. tathā puruṣo 'pi yoṣitām. apekṣayā tu na pravartate iti goṇikāputraḥ.
5.1.9 tatra striyaṃ prati viśeṣaḥ.
5.1.10 na strī dharmam a:dharmaṃ cāpekṣate kāmayata eva. kāryāpekṣayā tu nābhiyuṅkte.
5.1.11 svabhāvāc ca puruṣeṇābhiyujyamānā cikīrṣanty api vyāvartate.
5.1.12 punaḥ punar abhiyuktā siddhyati.
5.1.13 puruṣas tu dharma-sthitim ārya-samayaṃ cāpekṣya kāmayamāno 'pi vyāvartate.
5.1.14 tathā-buddhiś cābhiyujyamāno 'pi na siddhyati.
5.1.15 niṣ:kāraṇam abhiyuṅkte. abhiyujyāpi punar nābhiyuṅkte. siddhāyāṃ ca mādhyasthyaṃ gacchati.
5.1.16 su:labhām avamanyate. dur:labhām ākaṅkṣata iti prāyovādaḥ((131)).
children.translated_text:
5.1.1 The reasons for approaching other men's wives have been explained.
5.1.2 In such [cases], one should first examine the achievability, the absence of danger, the accessibility, the future [consequences], and the conduct.
5.1.3 But when one sees desire progressing from one stage to the next, one should approach other men's wives for the purpose of protecting one's own body and life from harm.
5.1.4 Now, there are ten stages of desire.
5.1.5 [1] Delight of the eyes, [2] attachment of the mind, [3] arising of intention, [4] loss of sleep, [5] emaciation, [6] turning away from sense-objects, [7] destruction of shame, [8] madness, [9] fainting, [10] death — these are their signs.
5.1.6 Therein, from [a woman's] appearance and characteristics, one should observe a young woman's character, truthfulness, purity, achievability, and intensity of passion — so say the teachers.
5.1.7 Because of the unreliability of the conjunctions of appearance and characteristics, a woman's inclination should be discerned only from her gestures and expressions — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
5.1.8 A woman desires any man she sees who is brilliant. Likewise, a man [desires] women. But out of consideration [for consequences], neither takes action — so says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.
5.1.9 Therein, there is a particular [difference] regarding women.
5.1.10 A woman does not consider <s>dharma</s> or <s>adharma</s>; she simply desires. But out of practical considerations, she does not pursue [the desire].
5.1.11 And by nature, even though willing, when approached by a man, she turns away.
5.1.12 When approached again and again, she yields.
5.1.13 But a man, considering his standing in <s>dharma</s> and the conventions of the noble, turns away even while desiring.
5.1.14 And one who is of such understanding, even when approached, does not yield.
5.1.15 He approaches without reason. Having approached, he withdraws again. And when she has been won over, he becomes indifferent.
5.1.16 He despises the easily available. He desires the difficult to attain — this is the general rule.

children.text:
5.1.17 tatra vyāvartana-kāraṇāni((132)).
5.1.18 patyāv anurāgaḥ.
5.1.19 apatyāpekṣā.
5.1.20 atikrāntavayastvam.
5.1.21 duḥkhābhibhavaḥ.
5.1.22 virahān:upalambhaḥ.
5.1.23 avajñayopamantrayata iti krodhaḥ.
5.1.24 a:pratarkya iti saṃkalpa-varjanam.
5.1.25 gamiṣyatīty an:āyatir anyatra prasakta-matir iti ca.
5.1.26 asaṃvṛtākāra ity udvegaḥ.
5.1.27 mitreṣu nisṛṣta-bhāva iti teṣv apekṣā.
5.1.28 śuṣkābhiyogīty āśaṅkā.
5.1.29 tejasvīti sādhvasam.
5.1.30 caṇḍa-vegaḥ samartho veti bhayaṃ mṛgyāḥ.
5.1.31 nāgarakaḥ kalāsu vicakṣaṇa iti vrīḍā.
5.1.32 sakhitvenopacarita iti ca.
5.1.33 a:deśa-kāla-jña ity asūyā.
5.1.34 paribhava-sthānam ity a:bahu-mānaḥ.
5.1.35 ākārito 'pi nāvabudhyata ity avajñā.
5.1.36 śaso manda-vega iti ca hastinyāḥ.
5.1.37 matto 'sya mā bhūd an:iṣṭam ity anukampā.
5.1.38 ātmani doṣa-darśanān nirvedaḥ.
5.1.39 viditā satī sva-jana-bahiṣ:kṛtā bhaviṣyāmīti bhayam.
5.1.40 palita ity an:ādaraḥ.
5.1.41 patyā prayuktaḥ parīkṣata iti vimarśaḥ.
5.1.42 dharmāpekṣā ceti.
5.1.43 teṣu yadātmani lakṣayet tadādita eva paricchindyāt.
5.1.44 āryatva-yuktāni rāga-vardhanāt.
5.1.45 a:śakti-jāny upāya-pradarśanāt.
5.1.46 bahu-māna-kṛtāny ati:paricayāt.
5.1.47 paribhava-kṛtāny ati:śauṇḍīryād((133)) vaicakṣaṇyāc ca.
5.1.48 tat-paribhava-jāni praṇatyā..
5.1.49 bhaya-yuktāny āśvasanād iti((134)).
children.translated_text:
5.1.17 Therein, the causes of a woman's turning away:
5.1.18 Affection for her husband.
5.1.19 Regard for her offspring.
5.1.20 Having passed the age [of passion].
5.1.21 Being overcome by sorrow.
5.1.22 The inability to bear separation.
5.1.23 Anger — when he approaches with contempt.
5.1.24 Abandonment of intention — [thinking:] 'He is unfathomable.'
5.1.25 'He will go away' — [thus] no confidence in the future; 'his mind is attached elsewhere' — [thus the same].
5.1.26 Anxiety — [thinking:] 'his demeanor is unguarded.'
5.1.27 Regard for friends — [thinking:] 'he confides freely in his friends.'
5.1.28 Suspicion — [thinking:] 'his advances are hollow.'
5.1.29 Intimidation — [thinking:] 'he is fierce.'
5.1.30 The doe-woman's fear — [thinking:] 'he is of intense passion and capable.'
5.1.31 Embarrassment — [thinking:] 'he is a man-about-town, skilled in the arts.'
5.1.32 And [thinking:] 'he treats [me merely] as a friend.'
5.1.33 Contempt — [thinking:] 'he does not know the proper place and time.'
5.1.34 Lack of esteem — [thinking:] 'he is an object of humiliation.'
5.1.35 Disdain — [thinking:] 'even when given signals, he does not understand.'
5.1.36 And [disdain] of the elephant-woman — [thinking:] 'he is timid and of slow passion.'
5.1.37 Pity — [thinking:] 'he is intoxicated — may nothing undesirable befall him.'
5.1.38 Despondency — from seeing faults in oneself.
5.1.39 Fear — [thinking:] 'when [my affair] is discovered, I shall be cast out by my own family.'
5.1.40 Disregard — [thinking:] 'he is grey-haired.'
5.1.41 Doubt — [thinking:] 'he is sent by [my] husband to test [me].'
5.1.42 And consideration of <s>dharma</s>.
5.1.43 Among these, whichever [cause] one recognizes in oneself, that one should address from the very beginning.
5.1.44 Those rooted in nobility — by intensifying passion.
5.1.45 Those born of incapacity — by showing the means [of achieving union].
5.1.46 Those arising from esteem — by excessive familiarity.
5.1.47 Those arising from contempt — by excessive boldness and display of skill.
5.1.48 Those born from his contempt [of her] — by prostration.
5.1.49 Those connected with fear — by reassurance.

children.text: 5.1.50 puruṣās tv amī prāyeṇa siddhāḥ ṇ kāmasūtra-jñaḥ kathākhyāna-kuśalo bālyāt prabhṛti saṃsṛṣṭaḥ pravṛddha-yauvanaḥ krīḍana-karmādināgata-viśvāsaḥ preṣaṇasya kartocita-saṃbhāṣaṇaḥ priyasya kartānyasya bhūta-pūrvo dūto marma-jña uttamayā prārthitaḥ sakhyā pracchannaṃ saṃsṛṣṭaḥ subhagābhikhyātaḥ saha-saṃvṛddhaḥ prātiveśyaḥ kāma-śīlas tathā-bhūtaś ca paricārako dhātreyikā-parigraho nava-varakaḥ prekṣodyāna-tyāga- śīlo vṛṣa iti siddha-pratāpaḥ sāhasikaḥ śūro vidyā-rūpa-guṇopabhogaiḥ patyur atiśayitā mahārha-veṣopacāraś ceti((135)).
children.translated_text: 5.1.50 But these types of men are generally successful [with women]: one who knows the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>; skilled in storytelling; intimate since childhood; strong in the prime of youth; one who has gained trust through play and amusement; an habitual messenger; one who does favors as a matter of course; one who was previously another's lover; a knower of her vulnerabilities; one solicited by an excellent [woman]; a friend [of her husband] who has been intimate in secret; famous for his attractiveness; one who grew up together [with her]; a neighbor; one who is lustful by nature; similarly a servant; a foster-brother's companion; a newly-married young man; a frequenter of spectacles, garden-parties, and festivals; a virile man — [such a one] of well-known prowess; a bold man; a hero; one who surpasses the husband in knowledge, beauty, good qualities, and enjoyments; one whose dress and attire are magnificent.

children.text:
5.1.51 yathātmanaḥ siddhatāṃ paśyed evaṃ yoṣito 'pi.
5.1.52 a:yatna-sādhyā yoṣitas tv imāḥ ṇ abhiyoga-mātra-sādhyāḥ. dvāra-deśāvasthāyinī. prāsādād rāja-mārgāvalokinī. taruṇa-prātiveśya-gṛhe goṣṭhī-yojinī. satata-prekṣiṇī. prekṣitā pārśva-vilokinī. niṣ:kāraṇaṃ sa:patnyādhivinnā. bhartṛ-dveṣiṇī vidviṣṭā ca. parihāra-hīnā. nir:apatyā.
5.1.53 jñāti-kula-nityā. vipannāpatyā. goṣṭhī-yojinī. prīti-yojinī. kuśīlava-bhāryā. mṛta-patikā bālā. daridrā bahūpabhogā. jyeṣṭha-bhāryā bahu-devarakā. bahu-māninī nyūna-bhartṛkā. kauśalābhimāninī bhartur maurkhyeṇodvignā. a:viśeṣatayā lobhena.
5.1.54 kanyā-kāle yatnena vāritā kathaṃ cid a:labdhābhiyuktā ca sā tadānīm. samāna-buddhi-śīla- medhā-pratipatti-sātmyā. prakṛtyā pakṣapātinī. an:aparādhe vimānitā.tulya-rupābhiś cādhaḥ kṛtā. proṣita-patiketi. īrṣyālu-pūti-cokṣa-klība-dīrgha-sūtra-kāpuruṣa-kubja-vāmana- virūpa-maṇikāra-grāmya-dur:gandhi-rogi-vṛddha-bhāryāś ceti.
5.1.55 ślokāv atra bhavataḥ.
5.1.55v icchā svabhāvato jātā kriyayā paribṛṃhitā. buddhyā saṃśodhitodvegā sthirā syād an:apāyinī..
5.1.56v siddhatām ātmano jñātvā liṅgāny unnīya yoṣitām. vyāvṛtti-kāraṇocchedī naro yoṣitsu sidhyati((136))..
children.translated_text:
5.1.51 Just as one recognizes one's own success [with women], so too [should one recognize] that of the woman.
5.1.52 These women, however, are attainable without effort — indeed, achievable by mere approach: one who stands by the doorway; one who looks from a balcony onto the royal highway; one who assembles socially at a young neighbor's house; one who constantly stares; one who, when looked at, glances sideways; one who has been superseded by a co-wife without cause; one who hates her husband, and one who is hated [by him]; one who lacks [familial] protection; one who is childless.
5.1.53 One who constantly frequents her relatives' household; one whose children have died; one who assembles socially; one who arranges friendly [gatherings]; a player's wife; a young widow; a poor woman who loves pleasures greatly; the senior wife with many brothers-in-law; one who is proud [of her qualities] but has an inferior husband; one proud of her skills and vexed by her husband's foolishness; [one attracted] through lack of discrimination and out of greed.
5.1.54 One who, during her girlhood, was carefully restrained, but somehow was not obtained — she who was approached [and rejected] — she [is available] at that time. One whose mind, character, intellect, understanding, and temperament are similar [to one's own]; one who is by nature partial; one humiliated without cause; one placed below [others of] equal beauty. One whose husband is away. There are also two verses here.
5.1.55v Desire, born naturally, nourished by action, purified by intellect of its anxiety, becomes firm and unshakable.
5.1.56v Having recognized one's own potential for success, discerning the signs in women, and removing the causes of their resistance — a man succeeds with women.

children.text: 5.1c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre pāradārike pañcame 'dhikaraṇe strī-puruṣa-śīlāvasthāpanaṃ vyāvartana-kāraṇāni strīṣu siddhāḥ puruṣā a:yatna-sādhyā yoṣitaḥ prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: 5.1c Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the Fifth Book '<s>Pāradārika</s>' (On Other Men's Wives), the first chapter: Determining the Dispositions of Women and Men, Causes of Resistance, Men Who Are Successful with Women, and Women Who Are Attainable Without Effort.

5.2.1 yathā kanyā svayam abhi-yoga-sādhyā na tathā dūtyā. para-striyas tu sūkṣma-bhāvā dūtī-sādhyā na tathātmanety ācāryāḥ.
5.2.2 sarvatra śakti-viṣaye svayaṃ sādhanam upapannatarakaṃ dur:upapādatvāt tasya dūtī-prayoga iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
5.2.3 prathama-sāhasā a:niyantraṇa-saṃbhāṣāś ca svayaṃ pratāryāḥ. tad-viparītāś((137)) ca dūtyeti prāyo-vādaḥ.
5.2.4 svayam abhiyokṣyamāṇas tv ādāv eva paricayaṃ kuryāt.
5.2.5 tasyāḥ svābhāvikaṃ darśanaṃ prāyatnikaṃ ca.
5.2.6 svābhāvikam ātmano bhavana-saṃnikarṣe prāyatnikaṃ mitra-jñāti-mahāmātra-vaidya-bhavana- saṃnikarṣe vivāha-yajñotsava-vyasanodyāna-gamanādiṣu.
5.2.7 darśane cāsyāḥ satataṃ sākāraṃ prekṣaṇaṃ keśa-saṃyamanaṃ nakhācchuraṇam ābharaṇa-prahlādanam adharauṣṭha-vimardanaṃ tās tāś ca līlā vayasyaiḥ saha prekṣamāṇāyās tat-saṃbaddhāḥ parāpadeśinyaś ca kathās tyāgopabhoga-prakāśanaṃ sakhyur utsaṅga-niṣaṇṇasya sāṅa-bhaṅgaṃ jṛmbhaṇam eka-bhrū-kṣepaṇaṃ manda-vākyatā tad-vākya-śravaṇaṃ tām uddiśya bālenānya-janena vā sahānyopadiṣṭā vyarthā kathā tasyāṃ svayaṃ manorathāvedanam anyāpadeśena tām evoddiśya bāla-cumbanam āliṅganaṃ ca jihvayā cāsya tāmbūla-dānaṃ pradeśinyā hanu-deśa-ghaṭṭanaṃ tat tad-yathā- yogaṃ yathāvakāśaṃ ca prayoktavyam.
5.2.8 tasyāś cāṅka-gatasya bālasya lālanaṃ bāla-krīḍanakānāṃ cāsya dānaṃ grahaṇaṃ tena saṃnikṛṣṭatvāt kathā-yojanaṃ tat-saṃbhāṣaṇa-kṣameṇa janena ca prītim āsādya kāryaṃ tad-anubandhaṃ ca gamanāgamanasya yojanaṃ saṃśraye cāsyās tām a:paśyato nāma kāma-sūtra-saṃkathā.
5.2.9 prasṛte tu paricaye tasyā haste nyāsaṃ nikṣepaṃ ca nidadhyāt. tat prati-dinaṃ prati-kṣaṇaṃ caikadeśato gṛhṇīyāt. saugandhikaṃ pūga-phalāni ca.
5.2.10 tām ātmano dāraiḥ saha visrambha-goṣṭhyāṃ viviktāsane ca yojayet.
5.2.11 nitya-darśanārthaṃ viśvāsanārthaṃ ca..5.2.12 suvarṇakāra-maṇikāra-vaikaṭika-nīlī-kusumbha-rañjakādiṣu ca kāmārthinyāṃ sahātmano vaśyaiś caiṣāṃ tat-saṃpādane svayaṃ prayateta.
5.2.13 tad-anuṣṭhāna-niratasya loka-vidito dīrgha-kālaṃ saṃdarśana-yogaḥ.
5.2.14 tasmiṃś cānyeṣām api karmaṇām anusandhānam.
5.2.15 yena karmaṇā dravyeṇa kauśalena cārthinī syāt tasya prayogam utpattim āgamam upāyaṃ vijñānaṃ cātmāyattaṃ darśayet.
5.2.16 pūrva-pravṛtteṣu loka-cariteṣu dravya-guṇa-parīkṣāsu ca tayā tat-parijanena ca saha vivādaḥ.
5.2.17 tatra nirdiṣṭāni paṇitāni teṣv enāṃ prāśnikatvena yojayet.
5.2.18 tayā tu vivadamāno 'ty:antādbhūtamiti brūyād.
children.translated_text: 5.2.1 The teachers say: just as a maiden is achievable through self-approach, she is not so through a go-between; but other men's wives, being of subtle disposition, are achievable through a go-between (<s>dūtī</s>), not so through oneself. 5.2.2 <s>Vātsyāyana</s> says: wherever one has the ability, self-approach is more appropriate, since engaging a go-between is more difficult. 5.2.3 Those who are bold at first contact and unrestricted in conversation should be approached by oneself; those of the opposite nature, through a go-between — this is the general rule. 5.2.4 One who intends to approach personally should first establish familiarity. 5.2.5 Seeing her may be natural or contrived. 5.2.6 Natural [seeing] is near one's own house; contrived is near the house of a friend, relative, minister, or physician, or at weddings, sacrifices, festivals, calamities, garden excursions, and the like. 5.2.7 And upon seeing her, one should constantly gaze at her meaningfully, arrange one's hair, scratch one's nails, jingle one's ornaments, chew one's lower lip, and perform various coquettish acts; while she is looking, together with companions, tell stories related to her and with indirect reference; display one's generosity and capacity for enjoyment; while seated on a friend's lap, stretch one's limbs meaningfully, yawn, raise one eyebrow, speak softly, listen to her words; through a child or another person, ostensibly addressing someone else, engage in pointless conversation actually directed at her; express one's desire for her under another pretext; kiss and embrace a child clearly directed at her; give betel with the tongue to the child's mouth; tap the chin-area with the index finger — all these should be employed as appropriate and as opportunity permits. 5.2.8 And one should fondle a child sitting in her lap, give and take the child's toys; through that proximity, arrange conversation; gain affection through a person capable of speaking with her; and conduct the business of that affair, arranging comings and goings; and in her company, when she cannot see [what he holds], discuss the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>. 5.2.9 When familiarity has progressed, one should place deposits and pledges in her hand. These he should reclaim little by little, daily and at intervals. Also perfumes and betel nuts. 5.2.10 He should introduce her to his own wife for intimate conversation and [seat them] together in private. 5.2.11 For the purpose of regular seeing and gaining trust. 5.2.12 When she desires something from goldsmiths, jewelers, dyers of indigo, safflower, or other coloring agents, he should himself endeavor through his own dependents to procure that for her. 5.2.13 Being devoted to fulfilling her needs, the well-known, long-term acquaintance [continues]. 5.2.14 And in this [association], the pursuit of other tasks as well. 5.2.15 Whatever task, material, or skill she needs — he should show that its application, origin, tradition, method, and knowledge all depend upon himself. 5.2.16 In previously established worldly affairs and in the examination of the qualities of materials, he should engage in disputes with her and her attendants. 5.2.17 In those matters that are pointed out and wagered upon, he should appoint her as the judge. 5.2.18 And while disputing with her, he should say, 'This is most extraordinary!'

children.text: 5.2.18c iti paricaya-kāraṇāni((138)).
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the section on] the means of establishing acquaintance.

children.text:
5.2.19 kṛta-paricayāṃ darśiteṅitākārāṃ kanyām ivopāyato 'bhiyuñjīteti. prāyeṇa tatra sūkṣmā abhiyogāḥ. kanyānām a:saṃprayuktatvāt. itarāsu tān eva sphuṭam upadadhyāt. saṃprayuktatvāt.
5.2.20 saṃdarśitākārāyāṃ nirbhinna-sad-bhāvāyāṃ samupabhoga-vyatikare tadīyāny upayuñjīta.
5.2.21 tatra mahārha-gandham uttarīyaṃ kusumaṃ syād aṅgulīyakaṃ ca. tad-dhastād gṛhīta-tāmbūlayā goṣṭhī-gamanodyatasya keśa-hasta-puṣpa-yācanam.
5.2.22 tatra mahārha-gandhaṃ spṛhaṇīyaṃ sva-nakha-daśana-pada-cihnitaṃ sākāraṃ dadyāt.
5.2.23 adhikair adhikaiś cābhiyogaiḥ sādhvasa-vicchedanam.
5.2.24 krameṇa ca vivikta-deśe gamanam āliṅganaṃ cumbanaṃ tāmbūlasya grāhaṇaṃ dānānte dravyāṇāṃ parivartanaṃ guhya-deśābhimarśanaṃ cety abhiyogāḥ.
5.2.25 yatra caikābhiyuktā na tatrāparām abhiyuñjīta.
5.2.26 tatra yā vṛddhānubhūta-viṣayā priyopagrahaiś ca tām upagṛhṇīyāt.
5.2.27 ślokāv atra bhavataḥ
5.2.27v anyatra dṛṣṭa-saṃcāras tad-bhartā yatra nāyakaḥ. na tatra yoṣitaṃ kāṃ cit suprāpām api laṅghayet..
5.2.28v śaṅkitāṃ rakṣitāṃ bhītāṃ sa:śvaśrūkāṃ ca yoṣitam. na tarkayeta medhāvī jānan pratyayam ātmanaḥ((139))..
children.translated_text: 5.2.19 Having established familiarity, one should approach a woman who has shown signs and gestures with skill, just as with a maiden. Generally the approaches there are subtle — because maidens are inexperienced. With the others, one should apply those same [approaches] explicitly, because they are experienced. 5.2.20 When she has shown her feelings and her true nature is revealed, and there is mutual exchange of enjoyment, one should make use of her belongings. 5.2.21 There, she should receive a costly perfume, an upper garment, a flower, or a ring. And taking betel from his hand, when he is about to depart for a social gathering, she should ask for [flowers from his] hair, hand, or [a] flower. 5.2.22 There, he should give a costly, desirable [perfume] marked with his own nail-marks, tooth-marks, and foot-prints, with meaningful expression. 5.2.23 With increasingly bold approaches, [he should effect] the removal of her timidity. 5.2.24 And gradually — going to a secluded place, embracing, kissing, accepting betel, exchanging gifts at the end of giving, touching the intimate parts — these are the approaches. 5.2.25 Where one has pursued one [woman], one should not pursue another there. 5.2.26 There, one who is older and experienced in matters of pleasure — one should win her over with affectionate gifts. 5.2.27 (verse) Where a [woman's] husband has been seen going elsewhere, the man should not approach any woman there, even if easily attainable. 5.2.28 (verse) A wise man, knowing his own reliability, should not pursue a suspicious, guarded, frightened, or mother-in-law-accompanied woman.

children.text: 5.2c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre pāradārike pañcame 'dhikaraṇe paricaya-kāraṇāny abhiyogāḥ dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the fifth book (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) called 'On Other Men's Wives' (<s>Pāradārika</s>), the second chapter: Means of Establishing Acquaintance and Approaches.

children.text:
5.3.1 abhiyuñjāno yoṣitaḥ pravṛttiṃ parīkṣeta. tayā bhāvaḥ parīkṣito bhavati. abhiyogāṃś ca pratigṛhṇīyāt.
5.3.2 mantram a:vrṇvānāṃ dūtyaināṃ sādhayet.
5.3.3 a:pratigṛhyābhiyogaṃ punar api saṃsṛjyamānāṃ dvidhā-bhūta-mānasāṃ vidyāt. tāṃ krameṇa sādhayet.
5.3.4 a:pratigṛhyābhiyogaṃ sa:viśeṣam alaṃkṛtā ca punar dṛśeta tathaiva tam abhigacchec ca vivikte balād grahaṇīyāṃ vidyāt.
5.3.5 bahūn api viṣahate 'abhiyogān na cireṇāpi prayacchaty ātmānaṃ sā śuṣka-pratigrāhiṇī paricaya-vighaṭana-sādhyā.
5.3.6 manuṣya-jāteś cittā:nityatvāt.
5.3.7 abhiyuktāpi pariharati na ca saṃsṛjyate. na ca pratyācaṣṭe. tasminn ātmani ca gauravābhimānāt. sātiparicayāt kṛcchra-sādhyā. marma-jñayā dūtyā tāṃ sādhayet.
5.3.8 sā ced abhiyujyamānā pāruṣyeṇa pratyādiśaty upekṣyā.
5.3.9 paruṣayitvāpi tu prīti-yojinīṃ sādhayet.
5.3.10 kāraṇāt saṃsparśanaṃ sahate nāvabudhyate nāma dvidhā-bhūta-manasā sātatyena kṣāntyā vā sādhyā.
5.3.11 samīpe śayānāyāḥ supto nāma karam upari vinyaset. sāpi suptevopekṣate. jāgratī tv apanuded bhūyo 'bhiyogākāṅkṣiṇī.
5.3.12 etena pādasyopari pādanyāso vyākhyātaḥ((140)).
5.3.13 tasmin prasṛte bhūyaḥ supta-saṃśleṣaṇam upakramet.
5.3.14 tad a:sahamānām utthitāṃ dvitīye 'hani prakṛti-vartinīm abhiyogārthinīṃ vidyāt. a:dṛśyamānāṃ tu dūtī-sādhyām.
5.3.15 ciram a:dṛṣṭāpi prakṛtisthaiva saṃsṛjyate kṛta-lakṣaṇāṃ tāṃ darśitākārām upakramet..5.3.16 a:nabhiyuktāpy ākārayati. vivikte cātmānaṃ darśayati. sa:vepathu-gadgadaṃ vadati. svinna-kara-caranāṅguliḥ svinna-mukhī ca bhavati. śiraḥ-pīḍane saṃvāhane corvor ātmānaṃ nāyake niyojayati.
5.3.17 āturāsaṃvāhikā caikena hastena saṃvāhayantī dvitīyena bāhunā sparśam āvedayati śleṣayati ca. vismita-bhāvā.
5.3.18 nidrāndhā vā parispṛśyorubhyāṃ bāhubhyām api tiṣṭhati. alikaikadeśam ūrvor upari pātayati. ūru-mūla-saṃvāhane niyuktā na pratilomayati. tatraiva hastam ekam a:vicalaṃ nyasyati. aṅga-saṃdaṃśena ca pīḍitaṃ cirād apanayati.
5.3.19 pratigṛhyaivaṃ nāyakābhiyogān punar dvitīye 'hani saṃvāhanāyopagacchati.
5.3.20 nātyarthaṃ saṃsṛjyate. na ca pariharati.
5.3.21 vivikte bhāvaṃ darśayati niṣkāraṇaṃ cā:gūḍham anyatra prachanna-pradeśāt.
5.3.22 saṃnikṛṣṭa-paricārakopabhogyā sā ced ākāritāpi tathaiva syāt sā marmajñayā dūtyā sādhyā.
5.3.23 vyāvartamānā tu tarkaṇīyā
5.3.23c iti bhāva-parīkṣā((141)).
5.3.24 bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ
5.3.24v ādau paricayaṃ kuryāt tataś ca paribhāṣaṇam. paribhāṣaṇa-saṃmiśraṃ mithaś cākāravedanam..
5.3.25v pratyuttareṇa paśyec ced ākārasya parigraham. tato 'bhiyuñjīta naraḥ striyaṃ vigata-sādhvasaḥ..
5.3.26v ākāreṇātmano bhāvaṃ yā nārī prāk prayojayet. kṣipram evābhiyojyā sā prathame tv eva darśane..
5.3.27v ślakṣṇam ākāritā yā tu darśayet sphuṭam uttaram. sāpi tat-kṣaṇa-siddheti vijñeyā rati-lālasā..
5.3.28v dhīrāyām a:pragalbhāyāṃ parīkṣiṇyāṃ ca yoṣiti. eṣa sūkṣmo vidhiḥ proktāḥ siddhā eva sphuṭaṃ striyaḥ..
children.translated_text: 5.3.1 While making advances, one should observe the woman's disposition. Through that, her feeling is tested; and she should accept the advances. 5.3.2 One who does not reveal her intentions should be won over through a female messenger (<s>dūtī</s>). 5.3.3 If she does not accept the advance yet continues to associate [with him], one should know her as being of divided mind; one should win her over gradually. 5.3.4 If she does not accept the advance yet is seen again especially adorned and approaches him in the same manner in a secluded place, one should know her as one to be taken by force. 5.3.5 One who endures many advances but does not yield herself even after a long time — that dry acceptor (<s>śuṣka-pratigrāhiṇī</s>) — is to be won over by disrupting the acquaintance. 5.3.6 Because of the inconstancy of the human mind. 5.3.7 One who, even when pursued, avoids [him] and does not associate, yet does not refuse — out of a sense of dignity toward him and toward herself — she, being excessively familiar, is difficult to win over. One should win her through a female messenger who knows the vulnerable points. 5.3.8 If, when pursued, she rejects him with harshness, she should be disregarded. 5.3.9 But one who, even after being harsh, initiates affection should be won over. 5.3.10 One who endures touching for some reason and pretends not to notice — she, being of divided mind, is to be won over through persistence or patience. 5.3.11 While she lies nearby, he, pretending to be asleep, should place his hand upon her. She too, as if asleep, ignores it; but if, while awake, she pushes it away, [she is] one desiring further advances. 5.3.12 By this, the placing of one foot upon the other is explained. 5.3.13 When that proceeds further, he should commence the embrace-while-sleeping. 5.3.14 If she does not endure it and rises, but on the following day behaves naturally and appears desirous of advances — one should know [her disposition]. But if she is not seen, she is to be won over through a messenger. 5.3.15 Even if not seen for a long time, she associates in her natural manner; one who has shown signs and displayed her feelings — one should approach her. 5.3.16 Even without being pursued, she signals. In a secluded place, she shows herself. She speaks with trembling and stammering. Her fingers, toes, and face become perspiring. She engages herself for the man in head-pressing and thigh-massaging. 5.3.17 Pretending to be an unskilled masseuse, while massaging with one hand, with the other arm she signals the touch and embraces; with an expression of wonder. 5.3.18 Or blinded by sleep, having touched, she remains with both thighs and arms. She lets a part of her forehead fall upon the thighs. When engaged in massaging the root of the thighs, she does not resist. She places one hand there motionless. And she removes pressure from the gripping of limbs only after a long time. 5.3.19 Having thus accepted the man's advances, on the following day she approaches for massaging again. 5.3.20 She does not associate excessively, but she does not avoid [him] either. 5.3.21 In private, she shows her feeling — without reason and unconcealed — except in a hidden place. 5.3.22 If she, being one whose servants and enjoyments are close at hand, even when signaled, remains the same — she is to be won over through a messenger who knows the vulnerable points. 5.3.23 But one who turns away should be examined carefully. Thus, the testing of feelings. 5.3.24 And here there are verses: 5.3.24 [Verse:] First one should cultivate acquaintance, then conversation; mixed with conversation, the mutual communication of feelings. 5.3.25 [Verse:] If through her response he sees the acceptance of the signs, then the man, free from timidity, should make his advance toward the woman. 5.3.26 [Verse:] A woman who first communicates her own feeling through gestures should be approached quickly — at the very first meeting. 5.3.27 [Verse:] She who, when subtly signaled, shows a clear response in return — she too is to be known as one who succeeds instantly, being eager for love. 5.3.28 [Verse:] With a woman who is reserved, not bold, and to be tested — this subtle method is prescribed. Women who are already won over [show themselves] openly.

children.text: 5.3c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre pāradārike pañcame 'dhikaraṇe bhāva-parīkṣā tṛitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the fifth section <s>Pāradārika</s> (On Other Men's Wives), the chapter on Testing Feelings — the third chapter.
