children.text:
5.4.1 darśiteṅgitākāraṃ tu pravirala-darśanām((142)) a:pūrvāṃ ca dūtyopasarpayet.
5.4.2 saināṃ śīlato 'nupraviśyākhyāna-kapaṭaiḥ subhagaṃ-karaṇa-yogair loka-vṛttāntaiḥ kavi-kathābhiḥ pāradārika-kathābhiś ca tasyāś ca rūpa-vijñāna-dākṣiṇya-śīlānupraśaṃsābhiś ca tāṃ rañjayet.
5.4.3 katham evaṃ-vidhāyās tavāyam itthaṃ-bhūtaḥ patir iti cānuśayaṃ grāhayet.
5.4.4 na tava subhage dāsyam api kartuṃ yukta iti brūyāt.
5.4.5 manda-vegatām īrṣyālutāṃ śaṭhatām a:kṛta-jñatāṃ cāsaṃbhoga-śīlatāṃ kadaryatāṃ capalatām anyāni ca yāni tasmin guptāny asyā abhyāśe sati sad-bhāve 'tiśayena bhāṣeta.
5.4.6 yena ca doṣeṇodvignāṃ lakṣayet tenaivānupraviśet.
5.4.7 yadāsau mṛgī tadā naiva śaśatā-doṣaḥ.
5.4.8 etenaiva baḍava-hastinī-viṣayaś coktaḥ.
5.4.9 nāyikāyā eva tu viśvāsyatām upalabhya dūtītvenopasarpayet prathama-sāhasāyāṃ sūkṣma-bhāvāyāṃ ceti goṇikāputraḥ.
5.4.10 sā nāyakasya caritam anulomatāṃ kāmitāni ca kathayet.
5.4.11 prasṛta-sadbhāvāyāṃ ca yuktyā kārya-śarīram itthaṃ vadet.
5.4.12 śṛṇu vicitram idaṃ subhage tvāṃ kila dṛṣtvāmutrāsāv itthaṃ gotra-putro nāyakaś cittonmādam anubhavati. prakṛtyā su:kumāraḥ kadā cid anyatrāparikliṣṭa-pūrvas tapasvī. tato 'dhunā śakyam anena maraṇam apy anubhavitum iti varṇayet.
5.4.13 tatra siddhā dvitīye 'hani vāci vaktre dṛṣṭyāṃ ca prasādam upalakṣya punar api kathāṃ pravartayet.
5.4.14 śṛṇvatyāṃ cāhalyāvimāraka-śākuntalādīny anyāny api laukikāni ca kathayet tad-yuktāni.
5.4.15 vṛṣatāṃ catuḥṣaṣṭi-vijñatāṃ saubhāgyaṃ ca nāyakasya. ślāghanīyatāṃ cāsya pracchannaṃ saṃprayogaṃ bhūtam a:bhūta-pūrvaṃ vā varṇayet.
5.4.16 ākāraṃ cāsya lakṣayet.
5.4.17 sa:vihasitaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃbhāṣate.
5.4.18 āsane copanimantrayate.
5.4.19 kvāsitaṃ kva śayitaṃ kva bhuktaṃ kva ceṣṭitaṃ kiṃ vā kṛtam iti pṛcchati.
5.4.20 vivikte darśayaty ātmānam.
5.4.21 ākhyānakāni niyuṅkte..5.4.22 cintayantī niḥśvāsīti vijṛmbhate ca.
5.4.23 prīti-dāyaṃ ca dadāti.
5.4.24 iṣṭeṣūtsaveṣu ca smarati.
5.4.25 punar-darśanānubandhaṃ visṛjati.
5.4.26 sādhu-vādinī satī kim idam a:śobhanam abhidhatsa iti kathām anubadhnāti.
5.4.27 nāyakasya śāṭhya-cāpalya-saṃbaddhān doṣān dadāti.
5.4.28 pūrva-pravṛttaṃ ca tat-saṃdarśanaṃ kathābhiyogaṃ ca svayam a:kathayantī tayocyamānam ākāṅkṣati.
5.4.29 nāyaka-manoratheṣu ca kathyamāneṣu sa:paribhavaṃ nāma hasati. na ca nirvadatīti.
5.4.30 dūty enāṃ darśitākārāṃ nāyakābhijñānair upabṛṃhayet.
5.4.31 a:saṃstutāṃ tu guṇa-kathanair anurāga-kathābhiś cāvarjayet.
5.4.32 nāsaṃstutādṛṣṭākārayor dūtyam astīty auddālakiḥ.
5.4.33 a:saṃstutayor api saṃsṛṣṭākārayor astīti bābhravīyāḥ.
5.4.34 saṃstutayor apy a:saṃsṛṣṭākārayor astīti goṇikāputraḥ.
5.4.35 a:saṃstutayor a:dṛṣṭākārayor api dūtī-pratyayād iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
5.4.36 tāsāṃ mano-harāṇy upāyanāni tāmbūlam anulepanaṃ srajam aṅgulīyakaṃ vāso vā tena prahitaṃ darśayet.
5.4.37 teṣu nāyakasya yathārthaṃ nakha-daśana-padāni tāni tāni ca cihnāni syuḥ.
5.4.38 vāsasi ca kuṅkumāṅkam añjaliṃ nidadyāt.
5.4.39 patra-cchedyāni nānābhiprāyākṛtīni darśayet. lekha-pattra-garbhāṇi karṇa-pattrāṇy āpīḍāṃś ca.
5.4.40 teṣu sva-manorathākhyāpanam. pratiprābhṛta-dāne((143)) caināṃ niyojayet.
5.4.41 evaṃ kṛta-paraspara-parigrahayoś ca dūtī-pratyayaḥ samāgamaḥ.
5.4.42 sa tu devatābhigamane yātrāyām udyāna-krīḍāyāṃ jalāvataraṇe vivāhe yajña-vyasanotsaveṣv agny-utpāte caura-vibhrame janapadasya cakrārohaṇe prekṣa-vyāpāreṣu teṣu teṣu ca kāryeṣv iti bābhravīyāḥ.
5.4.43 sakhī-bhikṣukī-kṣapaṇikā-tāpasī-bhavaneṣu sukhopāya iti goṇikāputraḥ.
5.4.44 tasyā eva tu gehe vidita-niṣkrama-praveśe cintitātyaya-pratīkāre praveśanam upapannaṃ niṣkramaṇam a:vijñāta-kālaṃ ca tan nityaṃ sukhopāyaṃ ceti vātsyāyanaḥ.
5.4.45 nisṛṣṭārthā[1] parimitārthā[2] patra-hārī[3] svayaṃdūtī[4] mūḍha-dūtī[5] bhāryā-dūtī[6] mūka-dūtī[7] vāta-dūtī[8] ceti dūtī-viśeṣāḥ.
5.4.46 nāyakasya nāyikāyāś ca yathāmanīṣitam artham upalabhya sva-buddhyā kārya-saṃpādinī nisṛṣṭārthā[1].
5.4.47 sā prāyeṇa saṃstuta-saṃbhāṣaṇayoḥ.
5.4.48 nāyikayā prayuktā a:saṃstuta-saṃbhāṣaṇayor api.
5.4.49 kautukāc cānurūpau yuktāv imau parasparasyety a:saṃstutayor api.
5.4.50 kāryaikadeśam abhiyogaikadeśaṃ copalabhya śeṣaṃ saṃpādayatīti parimitārthā[2].
5.4.51 sā dṛṣṭa-parasparākārayoḥ pravirala-darśanayoḥ.
5.4.52 saṃdeśa-mātraṃ prāpayatīti patra-hārī[3].
5.4.53 sā pragāḍha-sadbhāvayoḥ saṃsṛṣṭayoś ca deśa-kāla-saṃbodhanārtham.
5.4.54 dautyena prahitānyayā svayam eva nāyakam abhigacched ajānatī nāma tena sahopabhogaṃ svāpne vā kathayet. gotra-skhalitaṃ bhāryāṃ cāsya nindet. td-vyapadeśena svayam īrṣyāṃ darśayet. nakha-daśana-cihnitaṃ vā kiṃ cid dadyāt. bhavate 'ham ādau dātuṃ saṃkalpiteti cābhidadhīta. mama bhāryāyā kā ramaṇīyeti vivikte paryanuyuñjīta sā svayaṃ-dūtī[4].
5.4.55 tasya vivikte darśanaṃ pratigrahaś ca.
5.4.56 pratigraha-cchalenānyām abhisaṃdhāyāsyāḥ saṃdeśāśravaṇa-dvāreṇa nāyakaṃ sādhayet tāṃ copahanyāt sāpi svayaṃ-dūtī[4].
5.4.57 etayā nāyako 'py anya-dūtaś ca vyākhyātaḥ.
5.4.58 nāyaka-bhāryāṃ mugdhāṃ viśvāsyāyantraṇayānupraviśya nāyakasya ceṣṭitāni pṛcchet. yogāñ śikṣayet. sākāraṃ maṇḍayet. kopam enāṃ grāhayet. evaṃ ca pratipadyasveti śrāvayet. svayaṃ cāsyāṃ nakha-daśanapadāni nirvartayet. tena dvāreṇa nāyākam ākārayet sā mūḍha-dūtī[5].
5.4.59 tasyās tayaiva pratyuttarāṇi yojayet.
5.4.60 sva-bhāryāṃ vā mūḍhaṃ prayojya tayā saha viśvāsena yojayitvā tayaivākārayet. ātmanaś ca vaicakṣaṇyaṃ prakāśayet. sā bhāryā-dutī[6] tasyās tayaivākāra-grahaṇam.
5.4.61 bālāṃ vā paricārikām a:doṣa-jñām a:duṣṭenopāyena prahiṇuyāt. tatra sraji karṇapattre vā gūḍha-lekha-nidhānaṃ nakha-daśana-padam vā sā mūka-dūtī[7]. tasyās tayaiva pratyuttara-prārthanam.
5.4.62 pūrva-prastutārtha-liṅga-saṃbaddham anya-janā:grahaṇīyaṃ laukikārthaṃ vyarthaṃ vā vacanam udāsīnā yā śrāvayet sā vāta-dūtī[8]. tasyā api tayaiva pratyuttara-prārthanam
5.4.62c iti tāsāṃ viśeṣāḥ..5.4.63 bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ
5.4.63v vidhavekṣaṇikā dāsī bhikṣukī śilpa-kārikā. praviśaty āsu viśvāsaṃ dūtī-kāryaṃ ca vindati..
5.4.64 saṃkṣepeṇa dūtī-karmāṇy āha
5.4.64v vidveṣaṃ grāhayet patyau ramaṇīyāni varṇayet. citrān surata-saṃbhogān anyāsām api darśayet..
5.4.65v nāyakasyānurāgaṃ ca punaś ca rati-kauśalam. prārthanāṃ cādhika-strībhir avaṣṭambhaṃ ca varṇayet..
5.4.66v a:saṃkalpitam apy artham utsṛṣṭaṃ doṣa-kāraṇāt. punar āvartayaty eva dūtī vacana-kauśalāt((144))..
children.translated_text:
5.4.1 But when she has shown gestures and signs, and is rarely seen, and has not been previously acquainted, one should approach her through a female messenger (<s>dūtī</s>).
5.4.2 The [messenger], entering into her confidence through her character, should enchant her with clever tales, beautifying recipes, stories of the world, accounts of poets, stories of other men's wives, and praises of her beauty, knowledge, graciousness, and character.
5.4.3 She should cause her to feel regret [saying:] 'How is it that such a one as you has a husband of such a kind?'
5.4.4 She should say: 'It is not fitting, O beautiful one, for you to be even a servant [of such a man].'
5.4.5 She should speak emphatically about [the husband's] sluggishness, jealousy, dishonesty, ingratitude, aversion to pleasure, miserliness, fickleness, and whatever other faults he hides — in his proximity and when occasion arises.
5.4.6 And whichever fault [the wife] is most distressed by, through that very one she should gain entry.
5.4.7 When she is a <s>mṛgī</s> (doe-woman), there is certainly no fault of the <s>śaśa</s>-type (hare-man).
5.4.8 By this, the case of the <s>baḍavā</s> (mare-woman) and <s>hastinī</s> (elephant-woman) is also explained.
5.4.9 But having first gained the trust of the <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) herself, she should approach as a messenger — in the case of the bold woman and the one of subtle feelings — so says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.
5.4.10 She should speak of the lover's conduct, his agreeableness, and his desires.
5.4.11 And when the woman's true feelings have come forth, she should skillfully speak the substance of the matter thus:
5.4.12 'Listen to this wonderful thing, O beautiful one! Having seen you at such-and-such a place, such-and-such a nobleman (<s>gotra-putra</s>), the lover, is experiencing madness of the mind. He is by nature delicate, never before afflicted [by love] for any other, the poor man. So now it is possible he may even experience death' — thus she should describe.
5.4.13 Having succeeded there, on the second day, observing pleasure in her speech, face, and glance, she should continue the conversation further.
5.4.14 When she listens, she should tell stories of <s>Ahalyā</s>, <s>Avimāraka</s>, <s>Śakuntalā</s>, and others, as well as popular tales appropriate to the situation.
5.4.15 She should describe the lover's virility, his knowledge of the sixty-four [arts], his good fortune, his praiseworthiness, and his secret love affairs, whether real or imagined.
5.4.16 And she should observe her expressions.
5.4.17 She smiles and converses upon seeing [the messenger].
5.4.18 She invites her to sit.
5.4.19 She asks: 'Where did you sit? Where did you sleep? Where did you eat? What did you do? What happened?'
5.4.20 She shows herself in private.
5.4.21 She commissions stories [about the lover].
5.4.22 Thinking [of him], she sighs and yawns.
5.4.23 She gives gifts that bring pleasure.
5.4.24 She remembers [the messenger] at desired festivals.
5.4.25 She dismisses her with an arrangement for another meeting.
5.4.26 Being well-spoken, she binds the conversation [saying]: 'What is this unseemly thing you are proposing?'
5.4.27 She mentions faults connected to the lover's dishonesty and fickleness.
5.4.28 But without herself recounting the previous encounter with him and his conversational advances, she waits for them to be told by the other.
5.4.29 And when the lover's desires are being described, she laughs with a show of contempt — but does not rebuke.
5.4.30 The messenger should reinforce the woman who has shown her feelings with tokens of recognition from the lover.
5.4.31 But one who has not been acquainted should be won over with descriptions of virtues and stories of love.
5.4.32 'There is no messenger-work for those who are unacquainted and whose feelings are unknown' — so says <s>Auddālaki</s>.
5.4.33 'Even for those unacquainted, if their feelings are mutually disclosed, there is [messenger-work]' — so say the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>.
5.4.34 'Even for those acquainted, if their feelings are not mutually disclosed, there is [messenger-work]' — so says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.
5.4.35 'Even for those unacquainted and whose feelings are unknown, [there is messenger-work] through the trustworthiness of the messenger' — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
5.4.36 She should show her charming gifts sent by him — <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), ointments, garlands, a ring, or a garment.
5.4.37 On those should be the lover's nail-marks and tooth-marks and various other signs, made with purpose.
5.4.38 And on the garment, she should place a saffron-marked hand-print.
5.4.39 She should show <s>patra-cchedya</s> (decorative leaf-cuttings) of various shapes conveying different meanings, and ear-ornaments and chaplets containing hidden letters.
5.4.40 On those should be declarations of his desires. And she should encourage her to give reciprocal gifts.
5.4.41 And when both have thus accepted each other, the meeting is arranged through the trustworthiness of the messenger.
5.4.42 That [meeting should take place] at visits to temples, during processions, at garden excursions, at bathing, at marriages, at sacrifices, during calamities and festivals, during fire-emergencies, during alarm caused by thieves, during the march of an army through the country, at entertainments and shows, and at various other occasions — so say the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>.
5.4.43 'At the houses of a female friend, a mendicant woman, a female ascetic, or a female renunciant — [meetings are] easily arranged' — so says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.
5.4.44 'But entry into her own house itself — when the coming and going is known, and when measures against dangers have been thought through — with a suitable entrance and an unobserved time of departure, is always the easiest arrangement' — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
5.4.45 The types of female messengers are: [1] <s>nisṛṣṭārthā</s> (one with full authority), [2] <s>parimitārthā</s> (one with limited authority), [3] <s>patra-hārī</s> (letter-carrier), [4] <s>svayaṃdūtī</s> (self-messenger), [5] <s>mūḍha-dūtī</s> (unwitting messenger), [6] <s>bhāryā-dūtī</s> (wife-messenger), [7] <s>mūka-dūtī</s> (silent messenger), [8] <s>vāta-dūtī</s> (wind-messenger).
5.4.46 One who, having understood the desired purpose of both the lover and the <s>nāyikā</s>, accomplishes the task by her own intelligence — [is the] <s>nisṛṣṭārthā</s> [1] (one with full authority).
5.4.47 She is generally [employed] between those already acquainted and in conversation.
5.4.48 [But] when sent by the <s>nāyikā</s>, even between those not acquainted or in conversation.
5.4.49 And out of curiosity [thinking]: 'These two are suited and matched for each other' — even between those unacquainted.
5.4.50 One who, having ascertained part of the task and part of the approach, accomplishes the rest — [is the] <s>parimitārthā</s> [2] (one with limited authority).
5.4.51 She [is employed] between those whose mutual feelings have been observed and who rarely see each other.
5.4.52 One who merely conveys a message — [is the] <s>patra-hārī</s> [3] (letter-carrier).
5.4.53 She [is employed] between those of deep attachment and who are already intimate, for the purpose of informing about place and time.
5.4.54 When sent on an errand by another, she herself goes to the lover pretending not to know [the purpose] and tells him of her enjoyment with him or [relates] a dream. She makes a slip of the family name, criticizes his wife, and under that pretext shows her own jealousy. Or she gives something marked with nail and tooth marks, and says 'I had intended to give this to you first.' In private, she presses him [asking] 'Which of us, my co-wife or I, is more charming?' — she is the <s>svayaṃdūtī</s> [4] (self-messenger).
5.4.55 [For] her, there is a meeting in private and acceptance of gifts.
5.4.56 One who, under the pretext of accepting gifts, targets another woman, and through the channel of hearing this one's messages, wins over the lover and undermines the other — she too is a <s>svayaṃdūtī</s> [4].
5.4.57 By this, the lover himself [acting] as messenger and another [third party acting as] messenger are also explained.
5.4.58 One who, having gained the trust of the lover's naive wife through closeness, asks about the lover's conduct, teaches her techniques, adorns her suggestively, arouses her anger, instructs her 'respond in this way,' and herself produces nail and tooth marks on her — and through that channel attracts the lover — she is the <s>mūḍha-dūtī</s> [5] (unwitting messenger).
5.4.59 Through that same [wife], she arranges the replies.
5.4.60 Or, having employed one's own naive wife and established trust between her [and the target woman], one attracts [the target] through her and reveals one's own cleverness — she is the <s>bhāryā-dūtī</s> [6] (wife-messenger). Through her, the expression of feelings is received.
5.4.61 Or one should send a young female servant who does not understand faults, by an innocent stratagem. In that case, a hidden letter placed in a garland or an ear-ornament, or a nail-tooth mark — she is the <s>mūka-dūtī</s> [7] (silent messenger). Through her, one should seek replies.
5.4.62 One who, being indifferent, conveys a statement that is connected with signs relevant to a previously arranged matter, but not comprehensible to other people, and that seems either mundane or meaningless — she is the <s>vāta-dūtī</s> [8] (wind-messenger). Through her too, replies should be sought.
5.4.62c Thus are the types [of messengers].
5.4.63 And here there are verses:
5.4.63v A widow, a fortune-teller, a female slave, a mendicant woman, a craftswoman — these quickly gain trust and accomplish the work of a messenger.
5.4.64 In brief, the duties of a messenger:
5.4.64v She should create resentment toward the husband, describe delightful things, show the varied pleasures of lovemaking enjoyed by other women,
5.4.65v and describe the lover's devotion, his skill in pleasure, the desire for him among many women, and his steadfastness.
5.4.66v Even a matter not [yet] decided upon, or one abandoned due to some fault, the messenger, through her skill in speech, brings back again.

children.text: 5.4c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre pāradārike pañcame 'dhikaraṇe dūtī-karmāṇi caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the <s>Pāradārika</s> (Concerning Other Men's Wives) section, the Fifth Book, the chapter on the Functions of Go-Betweens (<s>dūtī-karmāṇi</s>) is the fourth chapter.

children.text:
leçon 5 pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ.
section (prakaraṇa)47 [īśvara-kāmita-prakaraṇam]
5.5.1 na rājñāṃ mahāmātrāṇāṃ vā para-bhavana-praveśo vidyate.mahājanena hi caritam eṣāṃ dṛśyate 'nuvidhīyate ca.
5.5.2 savitāram udyantaṃ trayo lokāḥ paśyanti anūdyante ca. gacchantam api paśyanty anupratiṣṭhante ca.
5.5.3 tasmād a:śakyatvād garhaṇīyatvāc ceti na te vṛthā kiṃ cid ācareyuḥ.
5.5.4 a:vaśyaṃ tv ācaritavye yogān prayuñjīran.
5.5.5 grāmādhipater āyuktakasya halotthavṛtti-putrasya((145)) yūno grāmīṇa-yoṣito vacana-mātra- sādhyāḥ. tāś carṣaṇya((146)) ity ācakṣate viṭāḥ.
5.5.6 tābhiḥ saha viṣṭi-karmasu koṣṭhāgāra-praveśe dravyāṇāṃ niṣkramaṇa-praveśanayor bhavana-pratisaṃskāre kṣetra-karmaṇi karpāsorṇātasī-śaṇa-valkalādāne sūtra-pratigrahe dravyāṇāṃ kraya-vikraya-vinimayeṣu teṣu teṣu ca karmasu prayogaḥ.
5.5.7 tathā vraja-yoṣidbhiḥ gavādhyakṣasya.
5.5.8 vidhavānāthā-pravrajitābhiḥ saha sūtrādhyakṣasya.
5.5.9 marmajñātvād rātrāv aṭane cāṭantībhir nāgarasya.
5.5.10 kraya-vikraye paṇyādhyakṣasya.
5.5.11 aṣṭamī-candrakaumudī-su:vasantakādiṣu pattana-nagara-kharvaṭa-yoṣitām īśvara-bhavane sahāntaḥ:purikābhiḥ prāyeṇa krīḍā.
5.5.12 tatra cāpānakānte nagara-striyo yathā-paricayam antaḥ:purikānāṃ pṛthak pṛthag bhogāvāsakān praviśya kathābhir āsitvā pūjitāḥ pratītāś copapradoṣaṃ niṣkrāmayeyuḥ.
5.5.13 tatra praṇihitā rāja-dāsī prayojyāyāḥ pūrva-saṃsṛṣṭā tāṃ tatra saṃbhāṣeta.
5.5.14 rāmaṇīyaka-darśanena yojayet.
5.5.15 prāg eva sva-bhavana-sthāṃ brūyāt. amuṣyāṃ krīḍāyāṃ tava rāja-bhavana-sthānāni rāmaṇīyakāni darśayiṣyāmīti kāle ca yojayet. bahiḥ:pravāla-kuṭṭimaṃ((147)) te darśayiṣyāmi.
5.5.16 maṇi-bhūmikāṃ vṛkṣa-vāṭikāṃ mṛdvīkā-maṇḍapaṃ((148)) samudra-gṛha-prāsādān gūḍha-bhitti-saṃcārāṃś citra-karmāṇi krīḍā-mṛgān yantrāṇi śakunān vyāghra-siṃha-pañjarādīni ca yāni purastād varṇitāni syuḥ.
5.5.17 ekānte ca tad-gatam īśvarānurāgaṃ śrāvayet.
5.5.18 saṃprayoge cāturyaṃ cābhivarṇayet.
5.5.19 a:mantra-śravaṃ ca pratipannāṃ yojayet.
5.5.20 a:pratipadyamānāṃ svayam eveśvara āgatyopacāraiḥ sāntvitāṃ rañjayitvā saṃbhūya ca sānurāgaṃ visṛjet.
5.5.21 prayojyāyāś ca patyur anugrahocitasya dārān nityam antaḥ:puram aucityāt praveśayet. tatra praṇihitā rāja-dāsīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa.
5.5.22 antaḥ:purikā vā prayojyayā saha sva:ceṭikā-saṃpreṣaṇena prītiṃ kuryāt. prasṛta-prītiṃ ca sāpadeśaṃ darśane niyojayet. praviṣṭāṃ pūjitāṃ pītavatīṃ praṇihitā rāja-dāsīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa.
5.5.23 yasmin vā vijñāne prayojyā vikhyātā syāt tad-darśanārtham antaḥ:purikā sopacāraṃ tām āhvayet. praviṣṭāṃ praṇihitā rāja-dāsīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa.
5.5.24 udbhūtān:arthasya bhītasya vā bhāryāṃ bhikṣukī brūyāt asāv antaḥ:purikā rājani siddhā gṛhīta-vākyā mama vacanaṃ śṛṇoti. sva-bhāvataś ca kṛpā-śīlā tām anenopāyenādhigamiṣyāmi. aham eva te praveśaṃ kārayiṣyāmi. sā ca te bhartur mahāntam an:arthaṃ nivartayiṣyatīti pratipannāṃ dvis trir iti praveśayet. antaḥ:purikā cāsyā a:bhayaṃ dadyāt. a:bhaya-śravaṇāc ca saṃprahṛṣṭāṃ praṇihitā rāja-dāsīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa..5.5.25 etayā vṛtty-arthināṃ mahāmātrābhitaptānāṃ balād vigṛhītānāṃ vyavahāre dur:balānāṃ sva-bhogenā:saṃtuṣṭānāṃ rājani prīti-kāmānāṃ rājya-janeṣu paṅktim icchatāṃ sa-jātair bādhyamānānāṃ sa:jātān bādhitu-kāmānāṃ sūcakānām anyeṣām kārya-vaśināṃ jāyā vyākhyātāḥ.
5.5.26 anyena vā prayojyāṃ saha saṃsṛṣṭāṃ saṃgrāhya dāsyam upanītāṃ krameṇāntaḥ:puraṃ praveśayet.
5.5.27 praṇidhinā cāyatim asyāḥ saṃdūṣya rājani vidviṣṭa iti kalatrāvagrahopāyenainām antaḥ:puraṃ praveśayet. iti pracchanna-yogāḥ((149)). ete rāja-putreṣu prāyeṇa.
5.5.28 na tv evaṃ para-bhavanam īśvaraḥ praviśet.
5.5.29 ābhīraṃ koṭṭa-rājaṃ((150)) para-bhavana-gataṃ bhrātṛ-prayukto rajako jaghāna. kāśi-rājaṃ jayasenam aśvādhyakṣa iti.
5.5.30 prakāśa-kāmitāni tu deśa-pravṛtti-yogāt.
5.5.31 prattā janapada-kanyā daśame 'hani kiṃ cid aupāyanikam upagṛhya praviśanty antaḥ:puram upabhuktā eva visṛjyanta ity āndhrāṇām((151)).
5.5.32 mahāmātreśvarāṇām antaḥ:purāṇi niśi sevārthaṃ rājānam upagacchanti vātsagulmakānām.
5.5.33 rūpavatīr janapada-yoṣitaḥ prīty-apadeśena māsaṃ māsārdhaṃ vātivāsayanty antaḥ:purikā vaidarbhāṇām.
5.5.34 darśanīyāḥ sva-bhāryāḥ prīti-dāyam eva mahāmātra-rājabhyo dadaty aparāntakānām.
5.5.35 rāja-krīḍārthaṃ nagara-striyo janapada-striyaś ca saṅghaśa ekaśaś ca rājakulaṃ praviśanti saurāṣṭrakāṇām iti.
5.5.36 ślokāv atra bhavataḥ
5.5.36v ete cānye ca bahavaḥ prayogāḥ pāradārikāḥ. deśe deśe pravartante rājabhiḥ saṃpravartitāḥ..
5.5.37v na tv evaitān prayuñjīta rājā loka-hite rataḥ. nigṛhītāri-ṣaḍ-vargas tathā vijayate mahīm((152))..
children.translated_text: Lesson 5: The Fifth Chapter. Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 47: [The Chapter on the Desires of Rulers]. 5.5.1 For kings and high officials, there is no entering another's house. For the conduct of great men is seen and imitated by the public. 5.5.2 The three worlds watch the rising sun and follow it; they watch it as it sets and follow it likewise. 5.5.3 Therefore, because of the impossibility [of entering others' houses] and the censure [it would bring], they should not engage in anything without purpose. 5.5.4 But when action must be taken, they should employ [specific] methods. 5.5.5 For the village headman, the revenue officer, or the young son of the ploughman, the village women are attainable by mere word alone. These [women] the libertines call <s>carṣaṇī</s> ("rustic women"). 5.5.6 The opportunity [for union] with them arises during forced labor, during entrance to the granary, during the removal and bringing in of goods, during repairs to dwellings, during field work, during the gathering of cotton, wool, flax, hemp, and bark, during the collection of thread, and during the buying, selling, and exchanging of goods, and in various other tasks. 5.5.7 Likewise, the superintendent of cattle [has opportunity] with the women of the cow-herding settlements. 5.5.8 The superintendent of spinning [has opportunity] with widows, destitute women, and female ascetics. 5.5.9 The city superintendent [has opportunity] with women who roam about at night, because he knows their secrets. 5.5.10 The superintendent of commerce [has opportunity] during buying and selling. 5.5.11 At the <s>Aṣṭamī</s> (eighth-day), <s>Candrakaumudī</s>, <s>Suvasantaka</s>, and other festivals, the women of towns, cities, and hamlets generally have sport with the harem women at the ruler's palace. 5.5.12 There, at the end of the drinking party, the city women, according to their acquaintance, entering the separate pleasure apartments of the harem women, having sat and conversed, honored and trusted, should be sent away at dusk. 5.5.13 There, a royal maidservant who has been planted, having been previously acquainted with the desired woman, should speak with her. 5.5.14 She should engage her by showing her beautiful things. 5.5.15 She should say to her beforehand, while still at her own house: "At such-and-such a festival I shall show you the beautiful sights of the royal palace" — and thus engage her at the right time. "I shall show you the coral-inlaid floor." 5.5.16 The jeweled pavilion, the tree garden, the grape arbor, the ocean-house palaces, the secret passages within the walls, the paintings, the pet animals, the mechanical devices, the birds, the tiger and lion cages, and other such things as have been described before. 5.5.17 And in private, she should let her hear of the ruler's affection directed toward her. 5.5.18 And she should describe his skill in lovemaking. 5.5.19 And when she has consented, she should arrange the meeting without anyone hearing the secret. 5.5.20 If she does not consent, the ruler himself should come, and having soothed her with courtesies and won her over, after being with her, he should send her away with affection. 5.5.21 He should regularly have the wife of the desired woman's husband — one accustomed to receiving royal favor — enter the harem as a matter of propriety. Then the planted royal maidservant [proceeds] as before. 5.5.22 Or a harem woman should cultivate affection with the desired woman through the sending of her own maidservant. Having developed the affection, she should arrange a meeting under some pretext. When she has entered, been honored, and been given drink, the planted royal maidservant [proceeds] as before. 5.5.23 Or, if the desired woman is renowned for some particular knowledge or art, a harem woman should invite her respectfully to see that [art]. When she has entered, the planted royal maidservant [proceeds] as before. 5.5.24 A female mendicant (<s>bhikṣukī</s>) should say to the wife of a man who is ruined or frightened: "Such-and-such a harem woman has influence with the king and heeds his word and listens to mine. She is naturally compassionate. I shall approach her by this means and arrange your admission. She will avert the great calamity [threatening] your husband." Having obtained her consent, she should arrange her admission twice, then thrice. And the harem woman should give her assurance of safety. And when she is delighted at hearing the assurance of safety, the planted royal maidservant [proceeds] as before. 5.5.25 By this same method, the wives of those seeking employment, those oppressed by high officials, those forcibly seized, those weak in litigation, those dissatisfied with their own possessions, those desiring the king's favor, those seeking rank among the royal household, those harassed by their peers, and those wishing to harass their peers — [the wives of] informers and others who are dependent on [royal] affairs — are described [as accessible]. 5.5.26 Or, having won over a woman who has been associated with the desired woman, and having brought her into service, one should gradually introduce her into the harem. 5.5.27 Or, through a spy, having ruined [the desired woman's] husband's future prospects and [making it known that] he has incurred the king's displeasure, one should introduce her into the harem by the stratagem of seizing her as a wife [of a traitor]. These are the covert methods. They are generally [employed] by princes. 5.5.28 But a ruler should not himself enter another's house in this way. 5.5.29 The <s>Ābhīra</s> king <s>Koṭṭarāja</s>, having gone to another's house, was killed by a washerman sent by [the man's] brother. [Similarly], <s>Jayasena</s>, the king of <s>Kāśī</s>, [was killed] by the superintendent of horses. 5.5.30 As for the public practices of desire — these [follow] from the customs of each region. 5.5.31 Among the <s>Āndhra</s>s, maidens given in marriage enter the harem on the tenth day with some small offering, and having been enjoyed, are sent away. 5.5.32 Among the <s>Vātsagulma</s>s, the harems of the great ministers and officials visit the king at night for the purpose of service. 5.5.33 Among the <s>Vaidarbha</s>s, the harem women have beautiful village women stay with them for a month or half a month under the pretext of affection. 5.5.34 Among the <s>Aparāntaka</s>s, [the officials] give their own beautiful wives to the great ministers and kings as a gift of goodwill. 5.5.35 Among the <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>s, the city women and village women enter the royal palace in groups or singly for the king's amusement. 5.5.36 There are two verses here: 5.5.36v [Verse:] These and many other practices concerning other men's wives prevail in different regions, established by kings. 5.5.37v [Verse:] But a king devoted to the welfare of the people should not employ these methods. One who has subdued the six enemies of the senses thus conquers the earth.

children.text: 5.5c iti śrīvātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre pāradārike pañcame 'dhikaraṇe īśvara-kāmitam pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the <s>Pāradārika</s> (Concerning Other Men's Wives) section, the Fifth Book, the chapter on the Desires of Rulers (<s>īśvara-kāmita</s>) is the fifth chapter.

leçon 6 ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ.
section (prakaraṇa)48 [antaḥ:purikā-vṛtta-prakaraṇam]
children.translated_text: Lesson 6: The Sixth Chapter. Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 48: [The Chapter on the Conduct of Harem Women (<s>antaḥpurikā-vṛtta</s>)].

children.text:
5.6.1 nāntaḥ:purāṇāṃ rakṣaṇa-yogāt puruṣa-saṃdarśanaṃ vidyate patyuś caikatvād an:eka-sādhāraṇatvāc cā:tṛptiḥ. tasmāt tāni prayogata eva paras-paraṃ rañjayeyuḥ.
5.6.2 dhātreyikāṃ sakhīṃ dāsīṃ vā puruṣavad alaṃkṛtyākṛti-saṃyuktaiḥ kanda-mūla-phalāvayavair apadravyair vātmābhiprāyaṃ nivartayeyuḥ.
5.6.3 puruṣa-pratimā a:vyakta-liṅgāś cādhiśayīran.
5.6.4 rājānaś ca kṛpā-śīlā vināpi bhāva-yogād āyojitāpadravyā yāvad artham ekayā rātryā bahvībhir api gacchanti. yasyāṃ tu prītir vāsaka ṛtur vā tatrābhiprāyataḥ pravartanta iti prācyopacārāḥ.
5.6.5 strī-yogeṇaiva puruṣāṇām apy a:labdha-vṛttīnāṃ viyoniṣu vijātiṣu strī-pratimāsu kevalopamardanāc cābhiprāya-nivṛttir vyākhyātā.
5.6.6 yoṣāveṣāṃś ca nāgarakān prāyeṇānta:purikāḥ paricārikābhiḥ saha praveśayanti.
5.6.7 teṣām upāvartane dhātreyikāś cābhyantara-saṃsṛṣṭā āyatiṃ darśayantyaḥ prayateran.
5.6.8 sukha-praveśitām apasāra-bhūmiṃ viśalatāṃ veśmanaḥ pramādaṃ rakṣiṇām a:nityatāṃ parijanasya varṇayeyuḥ.
5.6.9 na cā:sad-bhūtenārthena praveśayituṃ janam āvartayeyur doṣāt.
5.6.10 nāgarakas tu su:prāpam apy antaḥ:puram apāya-bhūyiṣṭhatvān na praviśed iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
5.6.11 sāpasāraṃ tu pramada-vanāvagāḍhaṃ vibhakta-dīrgha-kākṣyam alpa-pramatta-rakṣakaṃ proṣita-rājakaṃ kāraṇāni samīkṣya bahuṣa āhūyamāno 'rtha-buddhyā kakṣyā-praveśaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tābhir eva vihitopāyaḥ praviśet.
5.6.12 śakti-viṣaye ca prati:dinaṃ niṣkrāmet.
5.6.13 bahiś ca rakṣibhir anyad eva kāraṇam apadiśya saṃsṛjeta.
5.6.14 antaś:cāriṇyāṃ ca paricārikāyāṃ viditārthāyāṃ saktam ātmānaṃ rūpayet. tad-a:lābhāc ca śokam antaḥ:praveśinībhiś ca dūtī-kalpaṃ sakalam ācaret.
5.6.15 rāja-pranidhīṃś ca budhyeta.
5.6.16 dūtyās tv a:saṃcāre yatra gṛhītākārāyāḥ prayojyāyā darśana-yogas tatrāvasthānam.
5.6.17 tasminn api tu rakṣiṣu paricārikā-vyapadeśaḥ.
5.6.18 cakṣur anubadhnantyām iṅgitākāra-nivedanam..5.6.19 yatra saṃpāto 'syās tatra citra-karmaṇas tad-yuktasya vyarthānāṃ gīta-vastukānāṃ krīḍanakānāṃ kṛta-cihnānām āpīnakānām((153)) aṅgulīyakasya ca nidhānam.
5.6.20 praty:uttaraṃ tayā dattaṃ prapaśyet. tataḥ praveśane yateta.
5.6.21 yatra cāsya niyataṃ gamanam iti vidyāt tatra prachannasya prāg evāvasthānam.
5.6.22 rakṣi-puruṣa-rūpo vā tad-anujñāta-velāyāṃ praviśet.
5.6.23 āstaraṇa-prāvaraṇa-veṣṭitasya vā praveśa-nirhārau.
5.6.24 puṭā:puṭa-yogair vā naṣṭacchāyā-rūpaḥ.
5.6.25 tatrāyaṃ prayogaḥ ṇ nakula-hṛdayaṃ corakatumbī-phalāni sarpākṣīṇi cāntardhūmena pacet. tato 'ñjanena sama-bhāgena peṣayet. anenābhyakta-nayano naṣṭa-cchāyā-rūpaś carati [anyaiṣ ca jala-brahma-kṣema-śiraḥ-praṇītair bāhya-pānakair vā.
5.6.26 rātri-kaumudīṣu ca dīpikā-saṃbādhe suraṅgayā vā.
5.6.27 tatraitad bhavati((154)).
5.6.27v dravyāṇām api nirhāre pānakānāṃ praveśane. āpānakotsavārthe 'pi ceṭikānāṃ ca saṃbhrame..
5.6.27v vyatyāse veśmanāṃ caiva rakṣiṇāṃ ca viparyaye. udyāna-yātrā-gamane yātrātaś ca praveśane..
5.6.27v dīrgha-kālodayāṃ yātrāṃ proṣite cāpi rājani. praveśanaṃ bhavet prāyo yūnāṃ niṣkramaṇaṃ tathā..
5.6.28v parasparasya kāryāṇi jñātvā cāntaḥpurālayāḥ. eka-kāryās tataḥ kuryuḥ śeṣāṇām api bhedanam..
5.6.28v dūṣayitvā tato 'nyonyam eka-kāryārpaṇe sthiraḥ. a:bhedyatāṃ gataḥ sadyo yatheṣṭaṃ phalam aśnute..
5.6.29 tatra rāja-kula-cāriṇya eva lakṣaṇyān puruṣān antaḥ:puraṃ praveśayanti nāti:su:rakṣatvād aparāntikānām.
5.6.30 kṣatriya-saṃjñakair antaḥ:pura-rakṣibhir evārthaṃ sādhayanty ābhīrakāṇām.
5.6.31 preṣyābhiḥ saha tad-veṣān nāgaraka-putrān praveśayanti vātsagulmakānām.
5.6.32 svair eva putrair antaḥ:purāṇi kāma-cārair jananī-varjam upayujyante vaidarbhakānām.
5.6.33 tathā praveśibhir eva jñāti-saṃbandhibhir nānyair upayujyante strairājakānām.
5.6.34 brāhmaṇair mitrair bhṛtyair dāsa-ceṭaiś ca gauḍānām.
5.6.35 parispandāḥ karmakarāś cāntaḥ:pureṣv a:niṣidddhā anye 'pi tad-rūpāś ca saindhavānām.
5.6.36 arthena rakṣiṇam upagṛhya sāhasikāḥ saṃhatāḥ praviśanti haimavatānām.
5.6.37 puṣpa-dāna-niyogān nagara-brāhmaṇā rāja-viditam antaḥ:purāṇi gacchanti. paṭāntaritaś caiṣām ālāpaḥ. tena prasaṅgena vyatikaro bhavati baṅga-aṅga-kaliṅgakānām.
5.6.38 saṃhatya navadaśety ekaikaṃ yuvānaṃ pracchādayanti prācyānām iti. evaṃ para-striyaḥ prakurvīta.
children.translated_text: 5.6.1 Because of the guarding arrangements of the <s>antaḥpura</s> (inner harem), there is no possibility of seeing men; and because the husband is one [shared among] many, there is dissatisfaction. Therefore they should satisfy each other through various methods. 5.6.2 They should dress a foster-sister, friend, or servant-girl as a man and satisfy their desires with artificial devices (<s>apadravya</s>) made from bulbs, roots, and fruit-parts that resemble the form [of the male organ]. 5.6.3 They should also lie upon male effigies with indistinct genitalia. 5.6.4 Kings who are compassionate by nature, even without feelings of desire, equipped with artificial devices, visit many women in one night as needed. But the one for whom they have affection, whose turn (<s>vāsaka</s>) it is, or whose season (<s>ṛtu</s>) it is — with her they act according to inclination. These are the customs of the easterners. 5.6.5 By this very practice with women, the satisfaction of men also who have not attained [full] potency — through non-standard orifices, with other species, with female effigies, and through mere friction — is explained. 5.6.6 And harem women generally introduce <s>nāgarakas</s> (city men) dressed in women's clothing through their attendants. 5.6.7 In summoning them, foster-sisters who are intimate with the interior should make efforts, showing [him] the future [rewards]. 5.6.8 They should describe the easy entrance, the place of escape, the spaciousness of the dwelling, the negligence of the guards, and the inconstancy of the attendants. 5.6.9 But they should not summon a person to enter with false pretenses, because of the danger. 5.6.10 <s>Vātsyāyana</s> says: a <s>nāgaraka</s> should not enter even an easily accessible harem, because dangers predominate. 5.6.11 But [if it is] one with an escape route, situated deep within a pleasure-garden, with long separated enclosures, with few and negligent guards, and with the king away — after considering these factors, being frequently summoned, perceiving the approach to the enclosures with means arranged by them, he may enter. 5.6.12 And if it is within his power, he should exit daily. 5.6.13 Outside, he should associate with the guards, citing some other pretext. 5.6.14 He should feign being attached to a serving-maid who goes within and knows the situation; and [feign] grief at not obtaining her; and with women who enter within, he should conduct the entire go-between procedure. 5.6.15 And he should be aware of the king's spies. 5.6.16 When a go-between cannot circulate, where there is a possibility of seeing the woman who has shown her feelings and is to be approached, there he should station himself. 5.6.17 Even there, if guards are present, the pretext is of an attendant. 5.6.18 When she casts her eyes [upon him], communication through signs and gestures. 5.6.19 Where she passes, he should deposit painted objects, song-compositions, toys, marked cakes (<s>āpīnaka</s>), and a ring appropriate to the [intended message]. 5.6.20 He should look for a reply given by her. Then he should endeavor to enter. 5.6.21 Where he knows she regularly goes, there he should station himself concealed beforehand. 5.6.22 Or in the guise of a guard, he may enter at the time permitted by them. 5.6.23 Or entry and exit [are possible] when wrapped in a bedsheet or coverlet. 5.6.24 Or by the application of magical preparations, becoming invisible. 5.6.25 Here is the procedure: one should cook mongoose-heart, wild gourd fruits, and serpent-eyes in enclosed smoke. Then grind them with an equal portion of collyrium. With this applied to the eyes, one moves about as an invisible shadow. [Or with other external potions prepared by water-<s>brahma-kṣema</s>-masters.] 5.6.26 And during moonlight nights, in the crowd of lamps, or through a tunnel. 5.6.27 (verse) In the removal of goods and the bringing-in of drinks, during drinking festivals and celebrations, and in the bustle of servant-girls; in the exchange of quarters and the changing of guards; during garden excursions and re-entry from journeys; during long-duration festivals and when the king is away — then usually the entry and exit of young men [is possible]. 5.6.28 (verse) Having learned each other's affairs, the harem women, united in one cause, should then effect the breaking [of vigilance] of the rest. Having corrupted [the guards] mutually, firm in dedication to one cause, having become unbreakable, one immediately enjoys the desired fruit. 5.6.29 There, women who frequent the royal household introduce handsome men into the harem — because the women of <s>Aparāntika</s> are not very well guarded. 5.6.30 The women of the <s>Ābhīras</s> accomplish their purpose through the very guards of the harem, known as <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. 5.6.31 The women of <s>Vātsagulma</s> introduce city men's sons disguised as servant-girls. 5.6.32 The women of <s>Vaidarbha</s> are enjoyed by their own sons who roam freely, except their mothers. 5.6.33 Likewise, the women of <s>Strīrājya</s> are enjoyed only by relatives and kin who have entry, not by others. 5.6.34 [The harem women] of the <s>Gauḍas</s> [are enjoyed] by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, friends, servants, and slave-attendants. 5.6.35 Bodyguards and workmen who are not prohibited from [entering] the harem, and others of similar guise — [this is the practice] of the <s>Saindhavas</s>. 5.6.36 Bold men, combining together and bribing the guard with wealth, enter — [this is the practice] of the <s>Haimavatas</s>. 5.6.37 City <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> go to the harem with the king's knowledge, under the commission of flower-offerings. Their conversation [with the women] is from behind a curtain. By that pretext, intercourse takes place — [this is the practice] of the <s>Baṅga</s>, <s>Aṅga</s>, and <s>Kaliṅga</s> peoples. 5.6.38 The easterners, combining nine or ten [women], conceal one young man [among them]. Thus should one deal with other men's wives.

children.text: 5.6.38c ity antaḥ:purikā-vṛttam((155)).
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the section on] the conduct of harem women.

5.6.39 ebhya eva ca kāraṇebhyaḥ sva-dārān rakṣet.
5.6.40 kāmopadhā-śuddhān((156)) rakṣiṇo 'ntaḥ:pure sthāpayed ity ācāryāḥ.
5.6.41 te hi bhayena cārthena cānyaṃ prayojayeyus tasmāt kāma-bhayārthopadhā-śuddhān iti goṇikāputraḥ((157)).
5.6.42 a:droho dharmas tam api bhayāj jahyād ato dharma-bhayopadhā-śuddhān iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
5.6.43 vākyābhidhāyinībhiś ca gūḍhākārābhiḥ pramādabhir ātma-dārān((158)) upadadhyāc chaucā:śauca-parijñānārtham iti bābhravīyāḥ
5.6.44 duṣṭānāṃ yuvatiṣu siddhatvān nā:kasmād a:duṣṭa-dūṣaṇam ācared iti vātsyāyanaḥ((159)).
5.6.45 ati:goṣṭhī nir:aṅkuśatvaṃ bhartuḥ svairatā puruṣaiḥ sahā:niyantraṇatā pravāse 'vasthānaṃ videśe nivāsaḥ sva-vṛtty-upaghātaḥ svairiṇī-saṃsargaḥ patyur īrṣyālutā ceti strīṇāṃ vināśa-kāraṇāni.
5.6.46v saṃdṛśya śāstrato yogān pāradārika-lakṣitān. na yāti cchalanāṃ kaś cid sva-dārān prati śāstravit..
5.6.47v pākṣikatvāt prayogāṇām apāyānāṃ ca darśanāt. dharmārthayoś ca vailomyān nācaret pāradārikam..
5.6.48v tad etad dāra-gupty-artham ārabdhaṃ śreyase nṛṇām. prajānāṃ dūṣaṇāyaiva na vijñeyo 'sya saṃvidhiḥ((160))..
children.translated_text: 5.6.39 For these very reasons, one should guard one's own wives. 5.6.40 The teachers say: one should station guards in the harem who have been tested for purity regarding desire (<s>kāma</s>). 5.6.41 But they, through fear or wealth, might employ another [to enter]. Therefore, [one should use guards] tested for purity regarding desire, fear, and wealth — says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>. 5.6.42 Non-injury is <s>dharma</s>; one might abandon even that through fear. Therefore [guards should be] tested for purity regarding <s>dharma</s>, fear, and wealth — says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 5.6.43 The followers of <s>Bābhravya</s> say: one should test one's own wives' purity or impurity through women who report conversations and have concealed intentions. 5.6.44 <s>Vātsyāyana</s> says: since corrupted [agents] are effective among young women, one should not without cause corrupt the uncorrupted. 5.6.45 Excessive socializing, lack of restraint, the husband's licentiousness, unrestricted association with men, residing abroad, dwelling in a foreign land, destruction of livelihood, association with wanton women, and the husband's jealousy — these are the causes of women's ruin. 5.6.46 (verse) Having observed from the treatise the methods noted for adultery, whoever knows the <s>śāstra</s> does not fall into anyone's tricks regarding his own wives. 5.6.47 (verse) Because of the partiality of these methods, the observation of dangers, and the contravention of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, one should not practice adultery. 5.6.48 (verse) This [teaching] was undertaken for the purpose of guarding wives, for the welfare of men. Its method should not be understood as meant for the corruption of the people.

children.text: 5.6c iti śrivātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre pāradārike pañcame 'dhikaraṇe īśvarkāmitaṃ pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ..livre 6 vaiśikaṃ ṣaṣṭam adhikaraṇam.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the fifth book (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) called 'On Other Men's Wives' (<s>Pāradārika</s>), the fifth chapter: The Conduct of the Sovereign's Favorites. children.translated_text: Lesson 1: The First Chapter. Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 50: [The Section on Deliberation Regarding Companions, Those Who May or May Not Be Approached, and the Reasons for Approaching (<s>Sahāya-gamya-agamya-gamana-kāraṇa-cintā-prakaraṇa</s>)].

children.text:
6.1.1 veśyānāṃ puruṣādhigame ratir vṛttiś ca sargāt.
6.1.2 ratitaḥ pravartanaṃ svābhāvikaṃ kṛtrimam arthārtham.
6.1.3 tad api svābhāvikavad rūpayet.
6.1.4 kāma-parāsu hi puṃsāṃ viśvāsa-yogāt.
6.1.5 a:lubdhatāṃ ca khyāpayet tasya nidarśanārtham.
6.1.6 na cān:upāyenārthān sādhayed āyati-saṃrakṣaṇārtham.
6.1.7 nityam alaṅkāra-yoginī rāja-mārgāvalokinī dṛśyamānā na cātivṛttā tiṣṭhet. paṇya-sa: dharmatvāt.
6.1.8 yair nāyakam āvarjayed anyābhyaś cāvacchindyād ātmanaś cān:arthaṃ pratikuryād arthaṃ ca sādhayen na ca gamyaiḥ paribhūyeta tān sahāyān kuryāt.
6.1.9 te tv ārakṣaka-puruṣā dharmādhikaraṇasthā((161)) daiva-jñā vikrāntāḥ śūrāḥ samāna-vidyāḥ kalā-grāhiṇaḥ pīṭhamarda-vīṭa-vidūṣaka-mālākāra-gāndhika-śauṇḍika-rajaka-nāpita- bhikṣukās teca te ca kārya-yogāt.
6.1.10 kevalārthās tv amī gamyāḥ ṇ sva-tantraḥ pūrve vayasi vartamāno vittavān a:parokṣa-vṛttir adhikaraṇavān a:kṛcchrādhigata-vittaḥ. saṃgharṣavān santatāyaḥ subhaga-mānī ślāghanakaḥ paṇḍakaś((162)) ca puṃ-śabdārthī. samāna-spardhī sva-bhāvatas tyāgī. rājani mahāmātre vā siddho daiva-pramāṇo vittāvamānī gurūṇāṃ śāsanātigaḥ sa:jātānāṃ lakṣya-bhūtaḥ sa:vitta eka-putro liṅgī pracchanna-kāmaḥ śūro vaidyaś ceti.
6.1.11 prīti-yaśo-'rthās tu guṇato 'dhigamyāḥ.
6.1.12 mahā-kulīno vidvān sarva-samaya-jñaḥ kavir ākhyāna-kuśalo vāgmī pragalbho vividha-śilpa- jño vṛddha-darśī sthūla-lakṣo mahotsāho dṛḍha-bhaktir an:asūyakas tyāgī mitra-vatsalo ghaṭā-goṣṭhī-prekṣaṇaka-samāja-samasyā-krīḍana-śīlo nīrujo ':vyaṅga-śarīraḥ prāṇavān a:madya-po vṛṣo maitraḥ strīṇāṃ pranetā lālayitā ca. na cāsāṃ vaśa-gaḥ sva-tantra- vṛttir a:niṣṭhuro 'n:īrṣyālur an:avaśaṅkī ceti nāyaka-guṇāḥ.
6.1.13 nāyikāyāḥ punā rūpa-yauvana-lakṣaṇa-mādhurya-yoginī guṇeṣv anuraktā na tathārtheṣu prīti-saṃyoga-śīlā sthira-matir eka-jātīyā viśeṣārthinī nityam a:kadarya-vṛttir goṣṭhī-kalā-priyā ceti nāyikā-guṇāḥ.
6.1.14 nāyikā punar buddhi-śīlācāra ārjavaṃ kṛta-jñatā dīrgha-dūra-darśitvaṃ a:visaṃvāditā deśa-kāla-jñatā nāgarakatā dainyātihāsa-paiśunya-parivāda-krodha-lobha-stambha-cāpala- varjanaṃ pūrvābhibhāṣitā kāma-sūtra-kauśalaṃ tad-aṅga-vidyāsu ceti sādhāraṇa-guṇāḥ.
6.1.15 guṇa-viparyaye doṣāḥ.
6.1.16 kṣayī rogī kṛmi-śakrd vāyasāsyaḥ priya-kalatraḥ paruṣa-vāk kadaryo nirghṛṇo guru-jana-parityaktaḥ steno dambha-śīlo mūla-karmaṇi prasakto mānāpamānayor an:apekṣī dveṣyair apy artha-hāryo vilajja ity a:gamyāḥ.
6.1.17 rāgo bhayam arthaḥ saṃgharṣo vaira-niryātanaṃ jijñāsā pakṣaḥ khedo dharmo yaśo 'nukampā suhṛd-vākyaṃ hrīḥ priya-sādṛśyaṃ dhanyatā rāgāpanayaḥ sājātyaṃ sāhaveśyaṃ sātatyam āyatiś ca gamana-kāraṇāni bhavantīty ācāryāḥ.
6.1.18 artho 'n:artha-pratīghātaḥ prītiś ceti vātsyāyanaḥ.
6.1.19 arthas tu prītyā na bādhitaḥ. asya prādhānyāt.
6.1.20 bhayādiṣu tu guru-lāghavaṃ parīkṣyam
children.translated_text: 6.1.1 For courtesans (<s>veśyās</s>), the pursuit of men involves both pleasure and livelihood, by nature. 6.1.2 Engagement arising from pleasure is natural; [engagement] that is artificial is for the sake of wealth. 6.1.3 But even that she should make appear natural. 6.1.4 Because men trust [women] who are devoted to pleasure. 6.1.5 And she should make known her lack of greed — as a demonstration [of sincerity]. 6.1.6 And she should not pursue wealth without proper method, for the sake of preserving the future. 6.1.7 Always adorned, she should stand looking out at the royal highway, visible but not past her prime — because it is similar to displaying wares. 6.1.8 She should make those her allies who would attract a lover, cut him off from other [women], counteract any disadvantage to herself, secure wealth, and prevent her from being humiliated by those who frequent her. 6.1.9 These are: guards, officers of the law-court, astrologers, the valiant, heroes, those of similar learning, connoisseurs of the arts, the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (confidant), <s>vīṭa</s> (parasite), <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester), garland-makers, perfumers, liquor-sellers, washermen, barbers, mendicants — and others as the occasion requires. 6.1.10 For wealth alone, these are suitable clients: one who is independent, in the prime of youth, wealthy, of visible means, having authority, whose wealth is easily obtained; competitive, of sustained income, thinking himself handsome, given to boasting, and a eunuch (<s>paṇḍaka</s>) desiring the reputation of a man; one who is a rival [of another man], generous by nature, well-established with the king or a high official, one who takes fate as his authority, contemptuous of wealth, who transgresses the commands of his elders, who is the talk of his peers, one who is wealthy, an only son, who wears religious marks, who conceals his desires, a hero, and a physician. 6.1.11 Those pursued for affection, fame, and wealth should be approached based on their qualities. 6.1.12 Of noble family, learned, knowing all conventions, a poet, skilled in narration, eloquent, bold, proficient in various arts, experienced through age, of generous disposition, of great enterprise, of firm devotion, free from envy, generous, fond of friends, frequenting gatherings, spectacles, assemblies, riddle-contests, and play, healthy, of unblemished body, vigorous, not a drunkard, virile, friendly, a leader of women and a cherisher — yet not under their control, independent in conduct, not cruel, not jealous, and not suspicious — these are the qualities of a [good] lover. 6.1.13 And for the heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>): endowed with beauty, youth, auspicious marks, and sweetness; attached to qualities rather than wealth; inclined toward affectionate union; of firm mind; of one type; aspiring for distinction; always free from miserly conduct; and fond of gatherings and arts — these are the qualities of a heroine. 6.1.14 And the heroine's [further qualities]: intelligence, good character and conduct, straightforwardness, gratitude, foresight, trustworthiness, knowledge of place and time, urbanity, avoidance of dejection, gossip, slander, backbiting, anger, greed, obstinacy, and fickleness; speaking first; skill in the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>; and [proficiency] in its subsidiary arts — these are the general qualities. 6.1.15 The opposites of these qualities are faults. 6.1.16 One who is consumptive, diseased, worm-infested, foul-mouthed, fond of his wife, harsh-spoken, miserly, pitiless, abandoned by his elders, a thief, pretentious, addicted to sorcery, indifferent to honor and dishonor, one whose wealth can be taken even by enemies, and one who is shameless — these are unsuitable clients. 6.1.17 Passion, fear, wealth, rivalry, revenge, curiosity, partisanship, sorrow, dharma, fame, compassion, a friend's words, modesty, resemblance to a beloved, [desire for] fortune, removal of passion, similarity of type, companionship with other courtesans, continuity, and future [gain] — these are the causes of going [to a man], according to the teachers. 6.1.18 Wealth, prevention of loss, and affection — [these three,] says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 6.1.19 But wealth is not overridden by affection, because of its primacy. 6.1.20 In [matters of] fear and so forth, the relative weight and lightness should be examined.

children.text: # 50c iti sahāya-gamyāgamya-[gamana-]kāraṇa-cintā((163)).
children.translated_text: Thus, deliberation on allies, suitable and unsuitable clients, and causes for going [to a man].

children.text: section (prakaraṇa)51
children.translated_text: Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 51

children.text:
6.1.21 upamantritāpi gamyena sahasā na pratijānīyāt. puruṣāṇāṃ su:labhāvamānitvāt.
6.1.22 bhāva-jijñāsārthaṃ paricāraka-mukhān saṃvāhaka-gāyana-vaihāsikān gamye tad-bhaktān vā praṇidadhyāt.
6.1.23 tad-a:bhāve pīṭhamardādīn. tebhyo nāyakasya śaucā:śaucaṃ rāgāparāgau saktā:saktatāṃ dānā:dāne ca vidyāt.
6.1.24 saṃbhāvitena ca saha viṭa-purogāṃ prītiṃ yojayet.
6.1.25 lāvaka-kukkuṭa-meṣa-yuddha-śuka-śārikā-pralāpana-prekṣaṇaka-kalā-vyapadeśena pīṭhamardo nāyakaṃ tasyā udavasitam ānayet.
6.1.26 tāṃ vā tasya.
6.1.27 āgatasya prīti-kautuka-jananaṃ kiṃ cid dravya-jātaṃ svayam idam a:sādhāraṇopabhogyam iti prīti-dāyaṃ dadyāt.
6.1.28 yatra ca ramate tayā goṣṭhyainam upacāraiś ca rañjayet.
6.1.29 gate ca sa:parihāsa-pralāpāṃ sopāyanāṃ paricārikām abhīkṣṇaṃ preṣayet..6.1.30 sa:pīṭhamardāyāś ca kāraṇāpadeśena svayaṃ gamanam
children.translated_text: 6.1.21 Even when invited by a suitable client, she should not agree hastily — because men despise [women] easily obtained. 6.1.22 For the purpose of testing his feelings, she should deploy servants, masseuses, singers, and jesters who serve her, or those devoted to him, as agents. 6.1.23 In their absence, the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (confidant) and others. Through them she should learn the lover's purity or impurity, his passion or indifference, his attachment or detachment, and his generosity or lack thereof. 6.1.24 And with a promising [client], she should establish affection led by the <s>viṭa</s> (parasite). 6.1.25 Under the pretext of watching quail-fights, cock-fights, ram-fights, parrot and <s>śārikā</s> (myna) speaking, spectacles, and arts, the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> should bring the lover to her dwelling. 6.1.26 Or her to his. 6.1.27 Upon his arrival, she should give as a gift something that generates affection and curiosity — something that is for her exclusive enjoyment, saying 'this is my special possession' — a gift that creates affection. 6.1.28 And wherever he takes pleasure, she should delight him with conversation and courtesies. 6.1.29 When he departs, she should frequently send a maid bearing playful chatter and gifts. 6.1.30 And she herself, accompanied by the <s>pīṭhamarda</s>, should visit him under some pretext.

# 51c iti gamyopāvartanam((164)).
6.1.31 bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ.
6.1.31v tāmbūlāni srajaś caiva saṃskṛtaṃ cānulepanam. āgatasyāharet prītyā kalā-goṣṭhīś ca yojayet..
6.1.32v dravyāṇi praṇaye dadyāt kuryāc ca parivartanam. saṃprayogasya cākūtam nijenaiva prayojayet..
6.1.33v prīti-dāyair upanyāsair upacāraiś ca kevalaiḥ. gamyena saha saṃsṛṣṭā rañjayet taṃ tataḥ param((165))..
children.translated_text: Thus, the attracting of the suitable client. 6.1.31 And here there are verses: 6.1.31 [Verse:] Betel, garlands, and prepared unguent — she should bring with affection when he arrives, and engage him in arts and conversation. 6.1.32 [Verse:] She should give gifts at the time of courtship and make exchanges; and the intention of union she should bring about through her own [initiative]. 6.1.33 [Verse:] Through affection-gifts, offerings, and courtesies alone — having associated with the suitable client, she should then enchant him further.

children.text: 6.1c iti śrī vātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre vaiśike ṣaṣṭhe 'dhikaraṇe sahāya-gamyā:gamya-cintā gamana-kāraṇaṃ gamyopāvartanaṃ prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the sixth section <s>Vaiśika</s> (On Courtesans), the chapter on Deliberation on Allies, Suitable and Unsuitable Clients, Causes for Going, and Attracting the Suitable Client — the first chapter.

children.text:
6.2.1 saṃyuktā nāyakena tad-raṇjanārtham ekacāriṇī-vṛttam anutiṣṭhet((166)).
6.2.2 rañjayen na tu sajjeta saktavac ca viceṣṭeteti saṃkṣepoktiḥ.
6.2.3 mātari ca krūra-śīlāyām artha-parāyāṃ cāyattā syāt.
6.2.4 tad-a:bhāve mātṛkāyām.
6.2.5 sā tu gamyena nātiprīyeta.
6.2.6 prasahya ca duhitaram ānayet.
6.2.7 tatra tu nāyikāyāḥ saṃtatam a:ratir nirvedo vrīḍāṃ bhayaṃ ca.
6.2.8 na tv eva śāsanātivṛttiḥ.
6.2.9 vyādhiṃ caikam a:nimittam a:jugupsitam a:cakṣur-grāhyam a:nityaṃ ca khyāpayet.
6.2.10 sati kāraṇe tad-apadeśaṃ ca nāyakān:abhigamanam.
6.2.11 nir:mālyasya tu nāyikā ceṭikāṃ preṣayet tāmbūlasya ca.
6.2.12 vyavāye tad-upacāreṣu vismayaḥ.
6.2.13 catuḥṣaṣṭyāṃ śiṣyatvam.
6.2.14 tad-upadiṣṭānāṃ ca yogānām ābhīkṣṇyenānuyogaḥ.
6.2.15 tat-sātmyād rahasi vṛttiḥ.
6.2.16 manorathānām ākhyānam.
6.2.17 guhyānāṃ vaikṛta-pracchādanam.
6.2.18 śayane parāvṛttasyānupekṣaṇam.
6.2.19 ānulomyaṃ guhya-sparśane.
6.2.20 suptasya cumbanam āliṅganaṃ ca.
6.2.21 prekṣaṇam anya-manaskasya. rāja-mārge ca prāsāda-sthāyās tatra viditāyā vrīḍā śāṭhya-nāśaḥ.
6.2.22 tad-dveṣye dveṣyatā. tat-priye priyatā. tad-ramya ratiḥ. tam anu harṣa-śokau. strīṣu jijñāsā. kopaś cā:dīrgaḥ.
6.2.23 sva-kṛteṣv api nakha-daśana-cihneṣv anyāśaṅkā.
6.2.24 anuragasyā:vacanam.
6.2.25 ākāratas tu darśayet.
6.2.26 mada-svapna-vyādhiṣu tu nirvacanam.
6.2.27 ślāghyānāṃ nāyaka-karmaṇāṃ ca.
6.2.28 tasmin bruvāṇe vākyārtha-grahaṇam. tad avadhārya praśaṃsāviṣaye bhāṣaṇam. tad-vākyasya cottareṇa yojanam. bhaktimāṃś cet.
6.2.29 kathāsv anuvṛttir anyatra sa:patnyāḥ.
6.2.30 niḥśvāse jṛmbhate skhalite patite vā tasya cārtim āśaṃsīta.
6.2.31 kṣuta-vyāhṛta-vismiteṣu jīvety udāharaṇam.
6.2.32 daurmanasye vyādhi-daurhṛdāpadeśaḥ.
6.2.33 guṇataḥ parasyā:kīrtanam.
6.2.34 na nindā samāna-doṣasya.
6.2.35 dattasya dhāraṇam.
6.2.36 vṛthāparādhe tad-vyasane vālaṅkārasyā:grahaṇam a:bhojanaṃ ca.
6.2.37 tad-yuktāś ca vilāpāḥ.
6.2.38 tena saha deśa-mokṣaṃ rocayet rājani niṣkrayaṃ ca.
6.2.39 sāmarthyam āyuṣyas tad-avāptau.
6.2.40 tasyārthādhigame 'bhipreta-siddhau śarīropacaye vā pūrva-saṃbhāṣita iṣṭa-devatopahāraḥ.
6.2.41 nityam alaṅkāra-yogaḥ. parimito 'bhyavahāraḥ..6.2.42 gīte ca nāma-gotrayor grahaṇam. glānyām urasi lalāṭe ca karaṃ kurvīta. tat-sukham upalabhya nidrā-lābhaḥ.
6.2.43 autsaṅge cāsyopaveśanaṃ svapanaṃ ca. gamanaṃ viyoge.
6.2.44 tasmāt putrārthinī syāt. āyuṣo nādhikyam icchet.
6.2.45 etasyā:vijñātam arthaṃ rahasi na brūyāt.
6.2.46 vratam upavāsaṃ cāsya nirvartayet mayi doṣa iti. a:śakye svayam api tad-rūpā syāt.
6.2.47 vivāde tenāpy a:śakyam ity artha-nirdeśaḥ.
6.2.48 tadīyam ātmīyaṃ vā svayam a:viśeṣeṇa paśyet.
6.2.49 tena vinā goṣṭhy-ādīnām a:gamanam iti.
6.2.50 nir:mālya-dhāraṇe ślāghā ucchiṣṭa-bhojane ca.
6.2.51 kula-śīla-śilpa-jāti-vidyā-varṇa-vitta-deśa-mitra-guṇa-vayo-mādhurya-pūjā.
6.2.52 gītādiṣu codanam abhijñasya.
6.2.53 bhaya-śītoṣṇa-varṣāṇy an:apekṣya tad-abhigamanam.
6.2.54 sa eva ca me syād ity aurdhvadehikeṣu vacanam.
6.2.55 tad-iṣṭa-rasa-bhāva-śīlānuvartanam.
6.2.56 mūla-karmābhiśaṅkā.
6.2.57 tad-abhigamane ca jananyā saha nityo vivādaḥ.
6.2.58 balātkāreṇa ca yady anyatra tayā nīyeta tadā viṣam an:aśanaṃ śastraṃ rajjum iti kāmayeta.
6.2.59 pratyāyanaṃ ca praṇidhibhir nāyakasya. svayaṃ vātmano vṛtti-grahaṇam.
6.2.60 na tv evārtheṣu vivādaḥ.
6.2.61 mātrā vinā kiṃ cin na ceṣṭeta.
6.2.62 pravāse śīghrāgamanāya śāpa-dānam.
6.2.63 proṣite mṛjāniyamaś cālaṅkārasya pratiṣedhaḥ. maṅgalaṃ tv apekṣyam. ekaṃ śaṅkha-valayaṃ vā dhārayet.
6.2.64 smaraṇam atītānām. gamanam īkṣaṇikopaśrutīnām. nakṣatra-candra-sūrya-tārābhyaḥ spṛhaṇam.
6.2.65 iṣṭasvapnapradarśane tat-saṅgamo mamāstv iti vacanam.
6.2.66 udvego 'n:iṣṭe sānti-karma ca.
6.2.67 pratyāgate kāma-pūjā.
6.2.68 devatopahārāṇāṃ karaṇam.
6.2.69 sakhībhiḥ pūrṇa-pātrasyāharaṇam.
6.2.70 vāyasa-pūjā ca.
6.2.71 prathama-samāgamān:antaraṃ caitad eva vāyasa-pūjā-varjam.
6.2.72 saktasya cānumaraṇaṃ brūyāt.
6.2.73 nisṛṣṭa-bhāvaḥ samāna-vṛttiḥ prayojana-kārī nir:āśaṅko nir:apekṣo 'rtheṣv iti sakta-lakṣaṇāni.
6.2.74 tad etan nidarśanārthaṃ dattaka-śāsanād uktam. an:uktaṃ ca lokataḥ śīlayet puruṣa-prakṛtitaś ca.
6.2.75 bhavataś cātra ślokau
6.2.75v sūkṣmatvād ati:lobhāc ca prakṛtyājñānatas tathā. kāma-lakṣma tu dur:jānaṃ strīṇāṃ tad-bhāvitair api..
6.2.76v kāmayante virajyante rañjayanti tyajanti ca. karṣayantyo 'pi sarvārthāñ jñāyante naiva yoṣitaḥ((167))..
children.translated_text: 6.2.1 Having been united with a lover, she should follow the conduct of a devoted wife (<s>ekacāriṇī</s>) for the purpose of pleasing him. 6.2.2 She should please him but not become attached; yet she should behave as if attached — this is the summary statement. 6.2.3 She should be under the control of her mother, if the mother is of harsh disposition and devoted to wealth. 6.2.4 In her absence, under a surrogate mother (<s>mātṛkā</s>). 6.2.5 But [the mother] should not be overly fond of the lover. 6.2.6 And she should bring her daughter by force [if necessary]. 6.2.7 There, the courtesan should continuously [display] aversion, weariness, modesty, and fear. 6.2.8 But she should never transgress the [mother's] commands. 6.2.9 She should declare a single illness — one that is without [visible] cause, not repulsive, not perceptible to the eye, and not constant. 6.2.10 When there is a reason, she should cite that as the pretext for not going to the lover. 6.2.11 The courtesan should send a maidservant [to him] with the remnants of her garland and with betel. 6.2.12 [She should show] wonder at his courtesies in lovemaking. 6.2.13 [She should assume] the role of pupil in the sixty-four [arts]. 6.2.14 And the techniques taught by him she should practice with frequency. 6.2.15 Being accustomed to them, she should practice them in private. 6.2.16 [She should engage in] the narration of her desires. 6.2.17 [She should engage in] the concealment of deformities of her private parts. 6.2.18 [She should show] attentiveness to him when he turns away in bed. 6.2.19 Compliance in the touching of intimate parts. 6.2.20 Kissing and embracing him when he is asleep. 6.2.21 Gazing at him when he is absorbed in thought. When standing at the upper story on the royal road and being recognized there — modesty and the abandonment of feigned indifference. 6.2.22 Hatred toward what he hates. Affection for what he loves. Delight in what delights him. Following him in joy and sorrow. Curiosity about [other] women. And anger that is not prolonged. 6.2.23 Even when the nail and tooth marks are her own work, suspicion of another [woman]. 6.2.24 Not speaking of her love. 6.2.25 But showing it through gestures. 6.2.26 In intoxication, sleep, and illness, however, open declaration — 6.2.27 — and of the lover's praiseworthy deeds also. 6.2.28 When he speaks, grasping the meaning of his words. Having understood, speaking on topics of praise. And connecting his statement with a [suitable] reply — if he is devoted. 6.2.29 Continuing his stories — except when [they concern] a co-wife. 6.2.30 When he sighs, yawns, stumbles, or falls, she should express concern for his suffering. 6.2.31 When he sneezes, utters something, or is startled, she should say "Long life!" as an exclamation. 6.2.32 In his low spirits, the pretext of illness or pregnancy cravings. 6.2.33 Not praising another's qualities. 6.2.34 Not blaming one who has the same faults [as her lover]. 6.2.35 Wearing what he has given. 6.2.36 When offended without cause, or in his misfortune — refusing ornaments and food. 6.2.37 And lamentations appropriate to the occasion. 6.2.38 She should suggest with him leaving the place, and a ransom to the king. 6.2.39 [She should say that] her ability, her very life depends on attaining him. 6.2.40 When he acquires wealth, achieves his desires, or gains health — offerings to the deity she had previously invoked. 6.2.41 Constant wearing of ornaments. Moderate eating. 6.2.42 In song, the use of his name and family name. Placing her hand on his chest and forehead when he is weary. Falling asleep upon finding him comfortable. 6.2.43 Sitting in his lap and sleeping there. Going [to him] during separation. 6.2.44 From him she should desire a son. She should not wish for longevity beyond his. 6.2.45 She should not reveal to anyone in private the unspoken purpose of this [conduct]. 6.2.46 She should carry out his vows and fasts [saying] "the fault is mine." If unable, she herself should assume that form. 6.2.47 In a dispute, indicating that even he cannot [resolve it]. 6.2.48 She should look upon what is his and what is hers without distinction. 6.2.49 Without him, not going to assemblies and such. 6.2.50 Taking pride in wearing his discarded garlands and eating his leftovers. 6.2.51 Honoring his family, character, craft, caste, learning, appearance, wealth, homeland, friends, virtues, age, and sweetness. 6.2.52 Urging him [to perform] in song and such arts, if he is skilled. 6.2.53 Going to him regardless of fear, cold, heat, or rain. 6.2.54 [Saying] "May he be mine [in the next life too]" — such statements regarding the afterlife. 6.2.55 Following his preferred tastes, emotions, and disposition. 6.2.56 Suspicion of [his use of] love-magic (<s>mūla-karma</s>). 6.2.57 And constant quarreling with her mother about going to him. 6.2.58 If by force she is taken elsewhere by her [mother], she should desire poison, fasting, a weapon, or a rope. 6.2.59 And assuring the lover through spies. Or obtaining for herself a declaration of his commitment. 6.2.60 But never disputing about money. 6.2.61 Without her mother, she should undertake nothing. 6.2.62 When he is away on a journey, an oath for his swift return. 6.2.63 When he is abroad — [observance of] cleanliness discipline and prohibition of ornaments. But auspicious [signs] are to be observed. She should wear a single conch-shell bracelet. 6.2.64 Remembering past times. Consulting oracles, omens, and astrologers. Longing for the stars, moon, sun, and constellations. 6.2.65 When a favorable dream is shown: "May I be united with him" — such a statement. 6.2.66 Anxiety at an unfavorable [dream], and performing rites of propitiation. 6.2.67 When he returns — love-worship (<s>kāma-pūjā</s>). 6.2.68 Making offerings to the deity. 6.2.69 Having friends bring a full vessel. 6.2.70 And worship of the crow (<s>vāyasa-pūjā</s>). 6.2.71 After the first union, all of this same [conduct] — except the worship of the crow. 6.2.72 And to one who is attached, she should speak of dying together (<s>anumaraṇa</s>). 6.2.73 The signs of an attached [lover]: unreserved in emotion, sharing the same conduct, accomplishing her purposes, free of suspicion, and indifferent to money. 6.2.74 This has been stated from the teaching of <s>Dattaka</s> for the purpose of illustration. What is not stated, she should learn from worldly experience and from the nature of each man. 6.2.75 And here there are two verses: 6.2.75v [Verse:] Because of its subtlety, because of excessive greed, and because of ignorance of [women's] nature, the marks of desire in women are difficult to discern even by those experienced in them. 6.2.76v [Verse:] They desire, they become indifferent, they delight, they abandon — women, even while extracting every resource, are never truly known.

children.text: 6.2c iti śrī vātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre vaiśike ṣaṣṭhe 'dhikaraṇe kāntānuvṛttaṃ dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the <s>Vaiśika</s> (Concerning Courtesans) section, the Sixth Book, the chapter on Conforming to the Lover's Moods (<s>kāntānuvṛtta</s>) is the second chapter.

section (prakaraṇa)53 [arthāgamopāya-prakaraṇam]
children.translated_text: Lesson 3: The Third Chapter. Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 53: [The Chapter on Methods of Acquiring Wealth (<s>arthāgamopāya</s>)].

children.text:
6.3.1 saktād vittādānaṃ svābhāvikam upāyataś ca.
6.3.2 tatra svābhāvikaṃ saṃkalpāt samadhikaṃ vā labhamānā nopāyān prayuñjītety ācāryāḥ.
6.3.3 viditam apy upāyaiḥ pariṣkṛtaṃ dvi-guṇaṃ dāsyatīti vātsyāyanaḥ.
6.3.4 alaṃkāra-bhakṣya-bhojya-peya-mālya-vastra-gandha-dravyādīnāṃ vyavahāriṣu kālikam uddhārārttham artha-pratinayanena.
6.3.5 tat-samakṣaṃ tad-vitta-praśaṃsā.
6.3.6 vrata-vṛkṣārāma-devakula-taḍāgodyānotsava-prīti-dāya-vyapadeśaḥ.
6.3.7 tad-abhigamana-nimitto rakṣibhiś caurair vālaṅkāra-parimoṣaḥ.
6.3.8 dāhāt kuḍya-cchedāt pramādād bhavane cārtha-nāśaḥ.
6.3.9 tathā yācitālaṅkārāṇāṃ nāyakālaṅkārāṇāṃ ca tad-abhigamanārthasya vyayasya praṇidhibhir nivedanam.
6.3.10 tad-artham ṛṇa-grahaṇam. jananyā saha tad-udbhavasya vyayasya vivādaḥ..6.3.11 suhṛt-kāryeṣv an:abhigamanam an:abhihāra-hetoḥ.
6.3.12 taiś ca pūrvam āhṛtā guravo 'bhihārāḥ pūrvam upanītāḥ pūrvaṃ śrāvitāḥ syuḥ.
6.3.13 ucitānāṃ kriyāṇāṃ vicchittiḥ.
6.3.14 nāyakārthaṃ ca śilpiṣu kāryam.
6.3.15 vaidya-mahāmātrayor upakāra-kriyā kārya-hetoḥ.
6.3.16 mitrāṇāṃ copakāriṇāṃ vyasaneṣv abhyupapattiḥ.
6.3.17 gṛha-karma sakhyāḥ putrasyotsañjanam dohado vyādhir mitrasya duḥkhāpanayanam iti.
6.3.18 alaṃkāraika-deśa-vikrayo nāyakasyārthe.
6.3.19 tayā śīlitasya cālaṅkārasya bhāṇḍopaskarasya vā vaṇijo vikrayārthaṃ darśanam.
6.3.20 prati:gaṇikānāṃ ca sadṛśasya bhāṇḍasya vyatikare prativiśiṣṭasya grahaṇam.
6.3.21 pūrvopakārāṇām a:vismaraṇam anukīrtanaṃ ca.
6.3.22 praṇidhibhiḥ prati:gaṇikānāṃ lābhātiśayaṃ śrāvayet.
6.3.23 tāsu nāyaka-samakṣam ātmano 'bhyadhikaṃ lābhaṃ bhūtam a:bhūtaṃ vā vrīḍitā nāma varṇayet.
6.3.24 pūrva-yogināṃ ca lābhātiśayena punaḥ sandhāne yatamānānām āviṣ:kṛtaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ.
6.3.25 tat-spardhināṃ tyāga-yogināṃ nidarśanam.
6.3.26 na punar eṣyatīti bāla-yācitakam.
children.translated_text: 6.3.1 The taking of wealth from an attached [lover] is natural and through stratagems. 6.3.2 Regarding that, if she obtains what is natural — equal to or more than expected — she should not employ stratagems, say the teachers. 6.3.3 Even if known [to him], when refined by stratagems, he will give double — says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 6.3.4 Through transactions with dealers in ornaments, food, eatables, drinks, garlands, garments, fragrant substances, and the like, by returning payment [to her] as a periodic commission for procurement. 6.3.5 In his presence, praising his wealth. 6.3.6 The pretext of vows, tree-gardens, temples, tank-gardens, festivals, and gifts of affection. 6.3.7 On the pretext of visiting him, [claiming] robbery of ornaments by guards or thieves. 6.3.8 Loss of wealth in the house from fire, wall-breaching, or negligence. 6.3.9 Likewise, having agents report the expenses incurred in visiting him — [the cost of] borrowed ornaments and the lover's own ornaments. 6.3.10 Taking on debt for that purpose. Quarreling with her mother about the expenses arising from that. 6.3.11 Not attending friends' affairs because of having no gift to bring. 6.3.12 The valuable gifts previously brought by those [other suitors] should have been previously presented and previously made known [to the current lover]. 6.3.13 Discontinuing customary services. 6.3.14 Commissioning artisans for work on the lover's behalf. 6.3.15 Rendering services to physicians and high officials for the sake of [the lover's] affairs. 6.3.16 Coming to the aid of friends and benefactors in their misfortunes. 6.3.17 Household duties; entrusting her friend's son; pregnancy cravings; illness; removing a friend's sorrow — and so forth. 6.3.18 Selling a portion of ornaments for the lover's sake. 6.3.19 Showing to a merchant, for the purpose of sale, ornaments she had been accustomed to wearing, or household goods. 6.3.20 In exchange for comparable goods of rival courtesans, acquiring something superior. 6.3.21 Not forgetting past favors and recounting them. 6.3.22 Through agents, she should let [him] hear of the excessive gains of rival courtesans. 6.3.23 In the presence of the lover, she should describe — modestly, as it were — her own gains surpassing those [rivals], whether real or fabricated. 6.3.24 An open refusal of former lovers who, boasting of their excessive generosity, attempt to reconnect. 6.3.25 Pointing out examples of generous rivals who have been abandoned [by other courtesans]. 6.3.26 A childish plea: 'He will never come back again.'

children.text: # 53 ity arthāgamopāyāḥ((168)).
children.translated_text: Section 53: Thus, the methods of acquiring wealth.

children.text: section (prakaraṇa)54
children.translated_text: Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 54.

children.text:
6.3.27 vi:raktaṃ ca nityam eva prakṛti-vikriyāto vidyān mukha-varṇāc ca.
6.3.28 ūnam atiriktaṃ vā dadāti.
6.3.29 pratilomaiḥ sambadhyate.
6.3.30 vyapadiśyānyat karoti.
6.3.31 ucitam ācchinatti.
6.3.32 pratijñātaṃ vismarati. anyathā vā yojayati.
6.3.33 sv:pakṣaiḥ saṃjñayā bhāṣate.
6.3.34 mitra-kāryam apadiśyānyatra śete.
6.3.35 pūrva-saṃsṛṣṭāyāś ca parijanena mithaḥ kathayati.
6.3.36 tasya sāra-dravyāṇi prāg avabodhād anyāpadeśena haste kurvīta.
6.3.37 tāni cāsyā hastād uttama-rṇaḥ prasahya gṛhṇīyāt.
6.3.38 vivadamānena saha dharmastheṣu((169)) vyavahared
children.translated_text: 6.3.27 One who is disaffected she should always recognize by the change from his natural disposition and from his facial complexion. 6.3.28 He gives less or more [than expected]. 6.3.29 He associates with adversaries. 6.3.30 He professes one thing and does another. 6.3.31 He cuts off what is customary. 6.3.32 He forgets what was promised, or arranges it differently. 6.3.33 He speaks in code with his own people. 6.3.34 On the pretext of a friend's business, he sleeps elsewhere. 6.3.35 He speaks privately with the attendants of a woman with whom he was previously involved. 6.3.36 She should get his valuable possessions into her hands before he realizes, under some pretext. 6.3.37 And a creditor [of hers] should seize those forcibly from her hands. 6.3.38 She should take [the dispute] with him to the courts of law.

children.text: # 54 iti virakta-pratipattiḥ((170)).
children.translated_text: Section 54: Thus, dealing with a disaffected [lover].

children.text: section (prakaraṇa)55
children.translated_text: Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 55.

children.text:
6.3.39 saktaṃ tu pūrvopakāriṇam apy alpa-phalaṃ vyālīkenānupālayet.
6.3.40 a:sāraṃ tu niṣpratipattikam upāyato 'pavāhayet. anyam avaṣṭabhya.
6.3.41 tad-an:iṣṭa-sevā. ninditābhyāsaḥ. oṣṭha-nirbhogaḥ. pādena bhūmer abhighātaḥ. a:vijñāta-viṣayasya saṃkathā. tad-vijñāteṣv a:vismayaḥ kutsā ca. darpa-vighātaḥ adhikaiḥ saha saṃvāsaḥ. an:apekṣaṇam. samāna-doṣāṇāṃ nindā. rahasi cāvasthānam.
6.3.42 jugupsā. pariṣvaṅge bhujamayyā sūcyā vyavadhānam. stabdhatā gātrāṇām. sakthnor vyatyāsaḥ. nidrā-paratvaṃ ca. śrāntam upalabhya codanā. a:śaktau hāsaḥ. śaktāv an:abhinandanam. divāpi. bhāvam upalabhya mahājanābhigamanam.
6.3.43 vākyeṣu cchala-grahaṇam. a:narmaṇi hāsaḥ. narmaṇi cānyam apadiśya hasati vadati tasmin kaṭākṣeṇa parijanasya prekṣaṇaṃ tāḍanaṃ ca. āhatya cāsya kathām anyāḥ kathāḥ. tad-vyālīkānāṃ vyasanānāṃ cā:parihāryāṇām anukīrtanam. marmaṇāṃ ca ceṭikayopakṣepaṇam.
6.3.44 āgate cā:darśanam. a:yācya-yācanam. ante svayaṃ mokṣaś ceti parigrahakasyeti dattakasya.
6.3.45 bhavataś cātra ślokau
6.3.45v parīkṣya gamyaiḥ saṃyogaḥ saṃyuktasyānurañjanam. raktād arthasya cādānam ante mokṣaś ca vaiśikam..
6.3.46v evam etena kalpena sthitā veśyā parigrahe. nātisandhīyate gamyaiḥ karoty arthāṃś ca puṣkalān((171))..
children.translated_text: 6.3.39 But one who is still attached, even if a former benefactor and of little profit, she should maintain through pretense. 6.3.40 But one who is worthless and indecisive, she should remove by stratagem, relying on another [lover]. 6.3.41 Engaging in what he dislikes; practicing objectionable habits; biting the lips; stamping the ground with the foot; conversation about matters unknown [to him]; showing no amazement and disparaging what he knows; undermining his pride; associating with those superior [to him]; disregarding him; criticizing those with similar faults; and staying alone in private. 6.3.42 Showing disgust; in an embrace, placing an arm as a barrier like a needle; stiffness of limbs; crossing the thighs; excessive sleepiness; when she notices he is tired, urging him on; laughing when he is impotent; showing no pleasure when he is potent; even during the day, when she notices his desire, going out among people. 6.3.43 Seizing upon double meanings in his words; laughing when there is no jest; when there is a jest, pretending it was about someone else, she laughs and speaks, and with a sidelong glance looks at and strikes her attendants. Interrupting his talk with other topics; recounting his pretenses and unavoidable misfortunes; and having a maid-servant bring up his vulnerabilities. 6.3.44 Not appearing when he arrives; asking for things that should not be asked; and finally, dismissing him herself — this applies to a kept lover and to a <s>dattaka</s> (one given in patronage). 6.3.45 And here are two verses on this: (verse) After careful examination, union with suitable lovers; once united, keeping them attached; from the attached one, acquisition of wealth; and finally, release — this is the way of the courtesan. 6.3.46 (verse) Thus, a courtesan established in this manner regarding her patron is not deceived by lovers and acquires abundant wealth.

children.text: 6.3c iti śrī vātsyāyanīye kāmasūtre vaiśike ṣaṣṭhe 'dhikaraṇe 'rthāgamopāyā virakta-liṅgāni virakta-pratipattir niṣkāsana-kramās tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāmasūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, in the sixth section <s>Vaiśika</s> (On Courtesans), the third chapter: Methods of Acquiring Wealth, Signs of Disaffection, Dealing with the Disaffected, and the Procedure of Dismissal.

leçon 4 caturthe 'dhyāyaḥ.
