children.translated_text: Lesson 4: The Fourth Chapter. Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 56: [Chapter on Reunion with a Former Lover].

children.text:
6.4.1 vartamānaṃ niṣpīḍitārtham utsṛjantī pūrva-saṃsṛṣṭena saha sandadhyāt.
6.4.2 sa ced avasitārtho vittavān sānurāgaś ca tataḥ sandheyaḥ.
6.4.3 anyatra gatas tarkayitavyaḥ. sa kārya-yuktyā ṣaḍ-vidhaḥ.
6.4.4 itaḥ svayam apasṛtas tato 'pi svayam evāpasṛtaḥ [1]..6.4.5 itas tataś ca niṣkāsitāpasṛtaḥ [2.]
6.4.6 itaḥ svayam apasṛtas tato niṣkāsitāpasṛtaḥ [3].
6.4.7 itaḥ svayam apasṛtas tatra sthitaḥ [4].
6.4.8 ito niṣkāsitāpasṛtas tataḥ svayam apasṛtaḥ [5].
6.4.9 ito niṣkāsitāpasṛtas tatra sthitaḥ [6].
6.4.10 itas tataś ca svayam evāpasṛtyopajapati ced ubhayor guṇān apekṣī cala-buddhir a:sandheyaḥ [1].
6.4.11 itas tataś ca niṣkāsitāpasṛtaḥ sthira-buddhiḥ. sa ced anyato bahu labhamānayā niṣkāsitaḥ syāt sa:sāro 'pi tayā roṣito mamā:marṣād bahu dāsyatīti saṃdheyaḥ [2a].
6.4.12 niḥsāratayā kadaryatayā vā tyakto na śreyān [2b].
6.4.13 itaḥ svayam apasṛtas tato niṣkāsitāpasṛto yady atiriktam ādau ca dadyāt tataḥ pratigrāhyaḥ [3].
6.4.14 itaḥ svayam apasṛtya tatra sthita upajapaṃs tarkayitavyaḥ.
6.4.15 viśeṣārthī cāgatas tato viśeṣam a:pasyann āgantu-kāmo mayi māṃ jijñāsitu-kāmaḥ sā āgatya sānurāgatvād dāsyati. tasyāṃ vā doṣān dṛṣṭvā mayi bhūyiṣṭhān guṇān adhunā paśyati sa guṇa-darśī bhūyiṣṭhaṃ dasyāti [4a].
6.4.16 bālo vā naikatra-dṛṣṭir atisaṃdhāna-pradhāno vā haridrā-rāgo vā yat-kiṃ-cana-kārī vety avetya saṃdadhyān na vā [4b].
6.4.17 ito niṣkāsitāpasṛtas tataḥ svayam upasṛta upajapaṃs tarkayitavyaḥ.
6.4.18 anurāgād āgantu-kāmaḥ sa bahu dāsyati. mama guṇair bhāvito yo 'nyasyāṃ na ramate [5a].
6.4.19 pūrvam a:yogena vā mayā niṣkāsitaḥ sa māṃ śīlayitvā vairaṃ niryātayitu-kāmo dhanam abhiyogād vā mayāsyāpahṛtaṃ tad-viśvāsya pratīpam ādātu-kāmo nirveṣṭu-kāmo vā māṃ vartamānād bhedayitvā tyaktu-kāma ity a:kalyāṇa-buddhir a:sandheyaḥ [5b].
6.4.20 anyathā-buddhiḥ kālena lambhayitavyaḥ [5c].
6.4.21 ito niṣkāsitas tatra sthita upajapann etena vyākhyātaḥ [6].
6.4.22 teṣūpajapatsv anyatra sthitaḥ svayam upajapet.
6.4.23 vyālīkārthaṃ niṣkāsito mayāsāv anyatra gato yatnād ānetavyaḥ.
6.4.24 itaḥ pravṛtta-saṃbhāṣo vā tato bhedam avāpsyati.
6.4.25 tad-arthābhighātaṃ kariṣyati.
6.4.26 arthāgama-kāle vāsya. sthāna-vṛddhir asya jātā. labdham anenādhikaraṇam. dārair viyuktaḥ pāratantryād vyāvṛttaḥ. pitrā bhrātrā vā vibhaktaḥ.
6.4.27 anena vā pratibaddham anena sandhiṃ kṛtvā nāyakaṃ dhaninam avāpsyāmi.
6.4.28 vimānitā vā bhāryayā tam eva tasyāṃ vikramayiṣyāmi.
6.4.29 asya vā mitraṃ mad-dveṣiṇīṃsa:patnīṃ kāmayate tad amunā bhedayiṣyāmi.
6.4.30 cala-cittatayā vā lāghavam enam āpādayiṣyāmīti.
6.4.31 tasya pīṭhamardādayo mātur dauḥśīlyena nāyikāyāḥ saty apy anurāge vivaśāyāḥ pūrvaṃ niṣkāsanaṃ varṇayeyuḥ.
6.4.32 vartamānena cā:kāmāyāḥ saṃsargaṃ vidveṣaṃ ca.
6.4.33 tasyāś ca sābhijñānaiḥ pūrvānurāgair enaṃ pratyāpayeyuḥ.
6.4.34 abhijñānaṃ ca ta-kṛtopakāra-saṃbaddhaṃ syād
children.translated_text:
6.4.1 While dismissing the current [patron] whose wealth has been fully extracted, she should reunite with a former lover.
6.4.2 If he has completed his purpose, is wealthy, and still has affection — then he should be reunited with.
6.4.3 If he has gone elsewhere, he must be assessed. He is of six types according to the circumstances of the case:
6.4.4 [1] He left here of his own accord and left there also of his own accord.
6.4.5 [2] He was expelled and left from both here and there.
6.4.6 [3] He left here of his own accord and was expelled from there.
6.4.7 [4] He left here of his own accord and is still there.
6.4.8 [5] He was expelled from here and left there of his own accord.
6.4.9 [6] He was expelled from here and is still there.
6.4.10 [1] If, having left both places of his own accord, he makes overtures, he is one who considers the merits of both, is fickle-minded — he should not be reunited with.
6.4.11 [2a] One expelled from both places is firm-minded. If he was expelled by one who was receiving much from another, even though he has substance, angered by her, he will give much out of indignation toward me — he should be reunited with.
6.4.12 [2b] But one abandoned because of being worthless or miserly is not desirable.
6.4.13 [3] One who left here of his own accord and was expelled from there — if he gives more and gives first, then he should be accepted.
6.4.14 [4] One who left here of his own accord and is still there, making overtures — he must be assessed.
6.4.15 [4a] [She may think:] 'He came seeking something special, and not seeing anything special there, desires to come to me, wishing to test me. She, having come [to him], will give out of affection. Or, having seen faults in her, he now sees greater virtues in me — he, being a discerner of virtues, will give much.'
6.4.16 [4b] Or [she should consider:] 'He is immature, his gaze is not fixed on one [woman], he is excessively bent on deception, his passion is like turmeric [fleeting], or he is a man who does anything' — understanding this, she should reunite or not.
6.4.17 [5] One expelled from here and who has come from there of his own accord, making overtures — he must be assessed.
6.4.18 [5a] 'He desires to come out of affection — he will give much. He is captivated by my virtues and does not delight in another.'
6.4.19 [5b] 'Or, previously expelled by me unjustly, he, having studied my habits, desires to exact revenge; or the wealth I extracted from him through pressure, he, regaining trust, desires to take back forcefully; or he desires to settle accounts; or he desires to separate me from my current [patron] and then abandon me' — if he has such ill intentions, he should not be reunited with.
6.4.20 [5c] If he thinks otherwise, he should be won over in time.
6.4.21 [6] One expelled from here and still there, making overtures — this is explained by the above.
6.4.22 Among those making overtures, one still elsewhere should make overtures himself.
6.4.23 [She may think:] 'He was expelled by me for deception and has gone elsewhere — he must be brought back with effort.
6.4.24 Or, having begun conversation from here, he will cause a rift [with the other woman] there.
6.4.25 He will cause harm to her interests.
6.4.26 Or at the time when his wealth comes. Or his position has risen. Or he has obtained a post. Or he is separated from his wife. Or he is freed from dependence. Or he is divided from his father or brother.
6.4.27 Or [she thinks:] having made an alliance with this one, who is connected [to power], I shall obtain a wealthy patron.'
6.4.28 Or [she thinks:] 'Slighted by his wife, I shall deploy him against her.'
6.4.29 Or [she thinks:] 'His friend desires my rival co-courtesan — through this one I shall cause a rift [between them].'
6.4.30 Or [she thinks:] 'Through his fickle nature, I shall bring him into disrepute.'
6.4.31 His <s>pīṭhamarda</s> and others should describe to him how the <s>nāyikā</s>, though still having affection, was previously expelled against her will due to the wickedness of her mother.
6.4.32 And [they should describe] her unwilling association with the current [patron] and her aversion [to him].
6.4.33 And they should bring him back with tokens of recognition and former attachments.
6.4.34 And the token of recognition should be connected to a favor previously done by him.

6.4.36 pūrva-saṃsṛṣṭaḥ sarvato niṣpīḍitārthatvān nāty:artham artha-do duḥkhaṃ ca punar viśvāsayitum. a:pūrvas tu sukhenānurajyata iti vātsyāyanaḥ.

6.4.39v bibhety anyasya saṃyogād vyālīkāni ca nekṣate. ati:saktaḥ pumān yatra bayād bahu dadāti ca..

children.translated_text:
Thus is the Reunion of the Estranged (<s>viśīrṇa-pratisaṃdhāna</s>).
6.4.35 Between one not previously associated and one previously associated, the former lover is preferable. For he, being of known character and having shown his passion, is easy to deal with — so say the teachers.
6.4.36 The former lover, having been fully drained of wealth, will not give much; and it is difficult to win his trust again. But a new one is easily won over — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
6.4.37 Even so, there are distinctions based on the nature of the man.
6.4.38 And here there are verses:
6.4.38v One should approach another [patron] to break off the current one, or simply to obtain another; and reunion is desired for the purpose of undermining the established [patron].
6.4.39v When a man fears union with another, does not tolerate slights, is excessively attached, and gives much out of compulsion — [he is desirable].
6.4.40v She should welcome the unattached one and [seeming to] disregard the attached one. And one who is very skillful in approaching through another's messenger —
6.4.41v to him, the approaching one, a woman should in time give opportunity. She should remain with unbroken connections and not abandon the attached one.
6.4.42v But a woman, having honored the attached and submissive one, should go to another. And having obtained wealth from there, she should again please the attached one.
6.4.43v Considering the future prospects, the abundant gain and affection at first, a wise woman should reunite with [a patron] from whom she has been estranged.

6.5.1 gamya-bāhulye bahu prati:dinaṃ ca labhamānā naikaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt.
6.5.2 deśaṃ kālaṃ sthitim ātmano guṇān saubhāgyaṃ cānyābhyo nyūnātiriktāṃ cāvekṣya rajanyām((174)) arthaṃ sthāpayet.
6.5.3 gamye dūtāṃś ca prayojayet. tat-pratibaddhāṃś ca svayaṃ prahiṇuyāt.
6.5.4 dvis triś catur iti lābhātiśaya-grahārtham ekasyāpi gacchet. parigrahaṃ ca caret.
6.5.5 gamya-yaugapadye tu lābha-sāmye yad dravyārthinī syāt tad dāyini viśeṣaḥ praty:akṣa ity ācāryāḥ.
6.5.6 a:praty:ādeyatvāt sarva-kāryāṇāṃ tan-mūlatvād hiraṇya-da iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
6.5.7 suvarṇa-rajata-tāmra-kāṃsya-loha-bhāṇḍopaskārāstaraṇa-prāvaraṇa-vāso-viśeṣa-gandha-dravya- kaṭuka-bhāṇḍa-vṛta-taila-dhānya-paśu-jātīnāṃ pūrva-pūrvato viśeṣaḥ.
6.5.8 yat tatra sāmyād vā dravya-sāmye mitra-vākyād ati:pātitvād āyatito gamya-guṇataḥ prītitaś ca viśeṣaḥ.
6.5.9 rāgi-tyāginos tyāgini viśeṣaḥ pratyakṣa ity ācāryāḥ.
6.5.10 śakyo hi rāgiṇi tyāga ādhātum.
6.5.11 lubdho 'pi hi raktas tyajati na tu tyāgī nirbandhād rājyata iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
6.5.12 tatrāpi dhanavad-a:dhanavator dhanavati viśeṣaḥ. tyāgi-prayojana-kartroḥ prayojana-kartari viśeṣaḥ pratyakṣa ity ācāryāḥ.
6.5.13 prayojana-kartā sakṛt kṛtvā kṛtinam ātmānaṃ manyate tyāgī punar atītaṃ nāpekṣata iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
6.5.14 tatrāpy ātyayikato viśeṣaḥ.
6.5.15 kṛtajña-tyāginos tyāgini viśeṣaḥ pratyakṣa ity ācāryāḥ.
6.5.16 ciram ārādhito 'pi tyāgī vyalīkam ekam upalabhya pratigaṇikayā vā mithyā-dūṣitaḥ śramam atītaṃ nāpekṣate.
6.5.17 prāyeṇa hi tejasvina ṛjavo 'n:ādṛtāś ca tyāgino bhavanti.
6.5.18 kṛtajñas tu pūrva-śramāpekṣī na sahasā virajyate. parīkṣita-śīlatvāc ca na mithyā dūṣyata iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
6.5.19 tatrāpy āyatito viśeṣaḥ.
6.5.20 mitra-vacanārthāgamayor arthāgame viśeṣaḥ pratyakṣa ity ācāryāḥ.
6.5.21 so pi hy arthāgāmo bhavitā. mitraṃ tu sakṛd-vākye pratihate kaluṣitaṃ syād iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
6.5.22 tatrāpy atipātato viśeṣaḥ.
6.5.23 tatra kārya-saṃdarśanena mitram anunīya śvo-bhūte vacanam astv iti tato 'tipātinam arthaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt.
6.5.24 arthāgamān:artha-pratighātayor arthāgame viśeṣaḥ pratyakṣa ity ācāryāḥ.
6.5.25 arthaḥ parimitāvacchedaḥ an:arthaḥ punaḥ sakṛt-prasṛto na jñāyate kvāvatiṣṭhata iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
6.5.26 tatrāpi guru-lāghava-kṛto viśeṣaḥ.
6.5.27 etenārtha-saṃśayād an:artha-pratīkāre viśeṣo vyākhyātaḥ.
6.5.28 deva-kula-taḍāgārāmāṇāṃ karaṇam sthalīnām agni-caityānāṃ nibandhanam go-sahasrāṇāṃ pātrāntaritaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo dānam devatānāṃ pūjopahāra-pravartanam tad-vyaya-sahiṣṇor vā dhanasya parigrahaṇam ity uttama-gaṇikānāṃ lābhātiśayaḥ.
6.5.29 sārvāṅgiko 'kaṅkāra-yogo gṛhasyodārasya karaṇam. mahārhair bhāṇḍaiḥ paricārakaiś ca gṛha-paricchādasyojjvalateti rūpa-jīvānāṃ lābhātiśayaḥ.
6.5.30 nityaṃ śuklam ācchādanam apakṣudam anna-pānaṃ nityaṃ saugandhikena tāmbūlena ca yogaḥ sa:hiraṇya-bhāgam alaṅkaraṇam iti kumbha-dāsīnāṃ lābhātiśayaḥ.
6.5.31 etena pradeśena madhyamādhamānām api lābhātiśayān sarvāsām eva yojayed ity ācāryāḥ.
6.5.32 deśa-kāla-vibhāva-sāmarthyānurāga-loka-pravṛtti-vaśād a:niyata-lābhād iyam a:vṛttir iti vātsyāyanaḥ.
6.5.33 gamyam anyato nivārayitu-kāmā saktam anyasyām apahartu-kāmā vā anyāṃ vā lābhato viyuyukṣamāṇā:gamya-saṃsargād ātmanaḥ sthānaṃ vṛddhim āyatim abhigamyatāṃ ca manyamānā an:artha-pratīkāre vā sāhāyyam enaṃ kārayitu-kāmā saktasya vānyasya vyalīkārthinī pūrvopakāram a:kṛtam iva paśyantī kevala-prīty-arthinī vā kalyāṇa-buddher alpam api lābhaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt.
6.5.34 āyaty-arthinī tu tam āśritya cān:arthaṃ praticikīrṣantī naiva pratigṛhṇīyāt.
6.5.35 tyakṣyāmy enam anyataḥ pratisandhāsyāmi gamiṣyati dārair yokṣyate nāśayiṣyaty an:arthān aṅkuśa-bhūta uttarādhyakṣo 'syāgamiṣyati svāmī pitā vā sthāna-bhraṃśo vāsya bhaviṣyati cala-cittaś ceti manyamānā tadātve tasmāl lābham icchet..6.5.36 pratijñātam īśvareṇa pratigrahaṃ lapsyate adhikaraṇaṃ sthānaṃ vā prāpsyati vṛtti-kālo 'sya vā āsannaḥ vāhanam asyāgamiṣyati sthala-pattraṃ vā sasyam asya pakṣyate kṛtam asmin na naśyati nityam a:visaṃvādako vety āyatyām icchet. parigraha-kalpaṃ vācaret.
6.5.37 bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ
6.5.37v kṛcchrādhigata-vittāṃś ca rāja-vallabha-niṣṭhurān. āyatyāṃ ca tadātve ca dūrād eva vivarjayet..
6.5.38v a:artho varjane yeṣāṃ gamane 'bhyudayas tathā. prayatnenāpi tān gṛhya sāpadeśam upakramet..
6.5.39v prasannā ye prayacchanti sv:alpe 'py a:gaṇitaṃ vasu. sthūla-lakṣān mahotsāhāṃs tān gacchet svair api vyayaiḥ((175))..
children.translated_text: 6.5.1 When there is an abundance of suitable clients and much is obtained daily, she should not receive only one. 6.5.2 Having assessed [each client's] daily [contribution], and having set a price for the night according to place and season, she should extend consideration to all. 6.5.3 In so doing, she should assess who is better than whom. 6.5.4 Additionally: a double visit, gifts, aversion of loss, and aversion of gain — these are the considerations. 6.5.5 A double visit: when one visits the home [of two clients] and receives double. 6.5.6 A gift: what is obtained on a single occasion. 6.5.7 Aversion of loss: when, by not going to one on a particular night, the loss of continuous gain [from him] should be assessed. 6.5.8 Aversion of gain: when, by going to one, the certain gain from another is lost. 6.5.9 In all these, the amount and certainty of the gain should be weighed. And here there are verses: 6.5.9 [Verse:] Gain, loss, cost, certainty, and the possibility of future gain — having examined all these, a courtesan should decide on her course of action. 6.5.10 [Verse:] There are always those who give again, even though previously rejected. But some, having given much once, never give again. 6.5.11 [Verse:] Having weighed through reasoning both this side and that side, the possible and the certain, she should decide — so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

6.6.1 arthān ācaryamāṇān an:arthā apyanūdbhavanty anubandhāḥ saṃśayāś ca((176)).
6.6.2 te buddhi-daurbalyād ati:rāgād aty:abhimānād ati:dambhād aty:ārjavād ati:viśvāsād ati:krodhāt pramādāt sāhasād daiva-yogāc ca syuḥ.
6.6.3 teṣāṃ phalaṃ kṛtasya vyayasya niṣ:phalatvam an:āyatir āgamiṣyato 'rthasya nivartanam āptasya niṣkramaṇaṃ pāruṣyasya prāptir gamyatā śarīrasya praghātaḥ keśānāṃ chedanaṃ pātanam aṅga-vaikalyāpattiḥ.
6.6.4 tasmāt tān ādita eva parijihīrṣed artha-bhūyiṣṭhāṃś copekṣeta.
6.6.5 artho dharmaḥ kāma ity artha-trivargaḥ.
6.6.6 an:artho ':dharmo dveṣa ity an:artha-trivargaḥ.
6.6.7 teṣv ācaryamāṇeṣv anyasyāpi niṣpattir anubandhaḥ.
6.6.8 saṃdigdhāyāṃ tu phala-prāptau syād vā na veti śuddha-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.9 idaṃ vā syād idaṃ veti saṃkīrṇaḥ.
6.6.10 ekasmin kriyamāṇe kārye kārya-dvayasyotpattir ubhayato:yogaḥ.
6.6.11 samantād utpattiḥ samantato:yoga iti tān udāhariṣyāmaḥ.
6.6.12 vicārita-rūpo 'rtha-trivargaḥ. tad-viparīta evān:artha-trivargaḥ.
6.6.13 yasyottamasyābhigamane praty:akṣato 'rtha-lābho grahaṇīyatvam āyatir āgamaḥ prārthanīyatvaṃ cānyeṣāṃ syāt so 'rtho 'rthānubandhaḥ.
6.6.14 lābha-mātre kasya cid anyasya gamanaṃ so 'rtho nir:anubandhaḥ.
6.6.15 anyārtha-parigrahe saktād āyati-cchedanam arthasya niṣkramaṇaṃ loka-vidviṣṭasya vā nīcasya gamanam āyati-ghnam artho 'n:arthānubandhaḥ.
6.6.16 svena vyayena śūrasya mahāmātrasya prabhavato vā lubdhasya gamanaṃ niṣ:phalam api vyasana-pratīkārārthaṃ mahataś cārtha-ghnasya nimittasya praśamanam āyati-jananaṃ so 'n:artho 'rthānubandhaḥ.
6.6.17 kadaryasya subhaga-māninaḥ kṛta-ghnasya vāti:sandhāna-śīlasya svair api vyayais tathārādhanam ante niṣ:phalaṃ so 'n:artho nir:anubandhaḥ.
6.6.18 tasyaiva rāja-vallabhasya kraurya-prabhāvādhikasya tathaivārādhanam ante niṣ:phalaṃ niṣkāsanaṃ ca doṣa-karaṃ so 'n:artho 'n:arthānubandhaḥ.
6.6.19 evaṃ dharma-kāmayor apy anubandhān yojayet.
6.6.20 paraspareṇa ca yuktyā saṃkired
6.6.20c ity anubandhāḥ((177)).
6.6.21 paritoṣito 'pi dāsyati na vety artha-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.22 niṣpīḍitārtham a:phalam utsṛjantyā artham a:labhamānāyā dharmaḥ syān na veti dharma-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.23 abhipretam upalabhya paricārakam anyaṃ vā kṣudraṃ gatvā kāaḥ syān na veti kāma-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.24 prabhāvavān kṣudro 'n:abhigato 'n:arthaṃ kariṣyati na vety an:artha-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.25 aty:anta-niṣ:phalaḥ saktaḥ parityaktaḥ pitṛ-lokaṃ yāyāt tatrā:dharmaḥ syān na vety a:dharma-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.26 rāgasyāpi vivakṣāyām abhipretaman:upalabhya virāgaḥ syān na veti dveṣa-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.26c iti śuddha-saṃśayāḥ.
6.6.27 atha saṃkīrṇāḥ((178)).
6.6.28 āgantor a:vidita-śīlasya vallabha-saṃśrayasya prabhaviṣṇor vā samupasthitasyārādhanam artho 'n:artha iti saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.29 śrotriyasya brahmacāriṇo dīkṣitasya vratino liṅgino vā māṃ dṛṣṭvā jāta-rāgasya mumūrṣor mitra-vākyād ānṛśaṃsyāc ca gamanaṃ dharmo ':dharma iti saṃśayaḥ..6.6.30 lokād evā:kṛta-pratyayād a:guṇo guṇavān vety an:avekṣya gamanaṃ kāmo dveṣa iti saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.31 saṃkirec ca paraspareṇa.
6.6.31c iti saṃkīrṇa-saṃśayāḥ.
6.6.32 yatra parasyābhigamane 'rthaḥ saktāc ca saṃgharṣataḥ sa ubhayato 'rthaḥ.
6.6.33 yatra svena vyayena niṣ:phalam abhigamanaṃ saktāc cā:marṣitād vitta-pratyādānaṃ sa ubhayato 'n:arthaḥ.
6.6.34 yatrābhigamane 'rtho bhaviṣyati na vety āśaṅkā sakto 'pi saṃgharṣād dāsyati na veti sa ubhayato 'rtha-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.35 yatrābhigamane vyayavati pūrvo viruddhaḥ krodhād apakāraṃ kariṣyati na veti sakto vāmarṣito dattaṃ praty:ādāsyati na veti sa ubhayato 'n:artha-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.35c ity auddālaker ubhayato-yogāḥ.
6.6.36 bābhravīyās tu((179)).
6.6.37 yatrābhigamane 'rtho 'n:abhigamane ca saktād arthaḥ sa ubhayato:'rthaḥ.
6.6.38 yatrābhigamane niṣ:phalo vyayo 'n:abhigamane ca niṣ:pratīkāro 'n:arthaḥ sa ubhayato:'n:arthaḥ
6.6.39 yatrābhigamane nir:vyayo dāsyati na veti saṃśayo 'n:abhigamane sakto dāsyati na veti sa ubhayato:'rtha-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.40 yatrābhigamane vyayavati pūrvo viruddhaḥ prabhāvavān prāpsyate na veti saṃśayo 'n:abhigamane ca krodhād an:arthaṃ kariṣyati na veti sa ubhayato:'n:artha-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.41 eteṣām eva vyatikare 'nyato 'rtho 'nyato 'n:arthaḥ anyato 'rtho 'nyato 'rtha-saṃśayaḥ anyato 'rtho 'nyato 'n:artha-saṃśayaḥ.
6.6.41c iti ṣaṭ-saṃkīrṇa-yogāḥ.
6.6.42 teṣu sahāyaiḥ saha vimṛśya yato 'rtha-bhūyiṣṭho 'rtha-saṃśayo gurur an:artha-praśamo vā tataḥ pravarteta.
6.6.43 evaṃ dharma-kāmāv apy anayaiva yuktyodāharet((180)). saṃkirec ca paraspareṇa vyatiṣañjayec ca
6.6.43c ity ubhayato:yogāḥ.
6.6.44 saṃbhūya ca viṭāḥ parigṛhṇānty ekām asau goṣṭhī-parigrahaḥ.
6.6.45 sā teṣām itas tataḥ saṃsṛjyamānā praty:ekaṃ saṃgharṣād arthaṃ nirvartayet.
6.6.46 su:vasantakādiṣu ca yoge yo me imam amuṃ ca saṃpādayiṣyati tasyādya gamiṣyati me duhiteti mātrā vācayet.
6.6.47 teṣāṃ ca saṃgharṣaje 'bhigamane kāryāṇi lakṣayet.
6.6.48 ekato 'rthaḥ sarvato 'rthaḥ ekato 'n:arthaḥ sarvato 'n:arthaḥ. ardhato 'rthaḥ sarvato 'rthaḥ ardhato 'n:arthaḥ sarvato 'n:arthaḥ.
6.6.48c iti samantato yogāḥ.
6.6.49 artha-saṃśayam an:artha-saṃśayaṃ ca pūrvavad yojayet. saṃkirec ca tathā dharma-kāmāv api.
6.6.49c ity arthān:arthānubandha-saṃśaya-vicārāḥ((181)).
6.6.50 kumbhadāsī paricārikā kulaṭā svairiṇī naṭī śilpakārikā prakāśavinaṣṭā rūpājīvā gaṇikā ceti veṣyā-viśeṣāḥ.
6.6.51 sarvāsāṃ cānurūpeṇa gamyāḥ sahāyās tas-uparañjanam arthāgamopāyā niṣkāsanaṃ punaḥ saṃdhānaṃ lābha-viśeṣānubandhā arthān:arthānubandha-saṃśaya-vicārāś ca
children.translated_text:
(6.6.1) When gains are being pursued, losses also arise as consequences and doubts.
(6.6.2) These [losses] may occur from weakness of judgment, excessive passion, excessive pride, excessive deceit, excessive straightforwardness, excessive trust, excessive anger, carelessness, rashness, or the influence of fate.
(6.6.3) Their fruit is: the fruitlessness of expenditure already made; the non-arrival of future income; the reversal of income about to come; the loss of what has already been obtained; the acquisition of harshness; being made available to all; injury to the body; cutting or falling out of hair; and the occurrence of mutilation of limbs.
(6.6.4) Therefore, one should wish to avoid these from the very beginning, and should disregard those [situations] in which losses predominate.
(6.6.5) Gain, <s>dharma</s> (virtue), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) — this is the triad of gains (<s>artha-trivarga</s>).
(6.6.6) Loss, <s>adharma</s> (vice), and hatred — this is the triad of losses (<s>anartha-trivarga</s>).
(6.6.7) When these [gains] are being pursued, the arising of another [gain] alongside is a consequence (<s>anubandha</s>).
(6.6.8) When the attainment of fruit is doubtful — 'it may or may not happen' — that is a simple doubt (<s>śuddha-saṃśaya</s>).
(6.6.9) 'This may happen or that may happen' — that is a mixed [doubt] (<s>saṃkīrṇa</s>).
(6.6.10) When in performing one action, two results arise — that is a double conjunction (<s>ubhayato-yoga</s>).
(6.6.11) When [results arise] from all sides — that is an all-around conjunction (<s>samantato-yoga</s>). We shall illustrate these.
(6.6.12) The triad of gains has been examined in its essential form. Its opposite is indeed the triad of losses.
(6.6.13) When, by visiting a superior [patron], there is visibly gain of wealth, acceptability, future income, approach [of other patrons], and desirability by others — that is a gain with [positive] consequence.
(6.6.14) When the visiting of someone is merely for the [immediate] gain — that is a gain without consequence.
(6.6.15) When one severs future prospects from one attached [to her] for the sake of another's wealth, or loses wealth, or visits one who is despised by the world or of low status, destroying future prospects — that is a gain with adverse consequence.
(6.6.16) Visiting a brave man, a high minister, or a powerful man who is miserly, at one's own expense, even though fruitless, [done] for the purpose of counteracting a calamity and for the pacification of a great threat that destroys wealth, [thereby] generating future prospects — that is a loss with [positive] consequence.
(6.6.17) Worshipping with one's own expenditure a miser, one who considers himself handsome, an ungrateful one, or one excessively given to making promises — [only to find it] fruitless in the end — that is a loss without consequence.
(6.6.18) Worshipping that same [type of person who is] a royal favorite, pre-eminent in cruelty and power — [only to find it] fruitless in the end, and [resulting in] expulsion that causes harm — that is a loss with adverse consequence.
(6.6.19) Similarly, one should apply [the analysis of] consequences to <s>dharma</s> and <s>k��ma</s> as well.
(6.6.20) And one should combine [these] with each other through reasoning.
Thus [concludes the section on] consequences.
(6.6.21) 'Even when pleased, will he give or not?' — that is a doubt concerning gain.

Lesson 1, first chapter.
Section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) 59: [The section on making oneself attractive and related [topics]].

children.text:
7.1.1 vyākhyātaṃ ca kāma-sūtram.
7.1.2 tatroktes tu vidhibhir abhipretam artham an:adhigacchan aupaniṣadikam ācaret.
7.1.3 rūpaṃ guṇo vayas-tyāga iti subhagaṃ-karaṇam.
7.1.4 tagara-kuṣṭha-tālīsa-pattrakānulepanaṃ subhagaṃ-karaṇam.
7.1.5 etair eva su:piṣṭair vartim ālipyākṣa-tailena narakapāle sādhitam añjanaṃ ca.
7.1.6 punar navāsahadevīsārivākuraṇṭotpala-pattraiś ca siddhaṃ tailam abhyañjanam.
7.1.7 tad-yuktā eva srajaś ca.
7.1.8 padmotpala-nāgakesarāṇāṃ śoṣitānāṃ cūrṇaṃ madhu-ghṛtābhyām avalihya subhago bhavati.
7.1.9 tāny eva nagaratālīsa-tamāla-pattra-yuktāny anulipya.
7.1.10 mayūrasyākṣi tarakṣor vā suvarṇenāvalipya dakṣiṇa-hastena dhārayed
7.1.10c iti subhagaṃ-karaṇam((184)).
7.1.11 tathā bādara-maṇiṃ śaṅkha-maṇiṃ ca tathaiva teṣu cātharvaṇān yogān gamayet.
7.1.12 vidyā-tantrāc ca vidyā-yogāt prāpta-yauvanāṃ paricārikāṃ svāmī saṃvatsara-mātram anyato vārayet. tato vātitāṃ bālāṃ vāmatvāl lālasī:bhūteṣu gamyeṣu yo 'syai saṃgharṣeṇa bahu dadyāt tasmai visṛjed iti saubhāgya-vardhanam.
7.1.13 gaṇikā prāpta-yauvanāṃ svāṃ duhitaraṃ tasyā vijñāna-śīla-rūpānurūpyeṇa tān abhinimantrya sāreṇa yo 'syā idam idaṃ ca dadyāt sa pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīyād iti saṃbhāṣya rakṣayed iti.
7.1.14 sā ca mātur a:viditā nāma nāgarika-putrair dhanibhir aty:arthaṃ prīyeta.
7.1.15 teṣāṃ kalā-grahaṇe gandharva-śālāyāṃ bhīkṣukī-bhavane tatra tatra ca saṃdarśana-yogāḥ.
7.1.16 teṣāṃ yathokta-dāyināṃ mātā pāṇiṃ grāhayet.
7.1.17 tāvad artham a:labhamānā tu svenāpy eka-deśena duhitra etad dattam aneneti khyāpayet.
7.1.18 ūḍhāyā vā kanyā-bhāvaṃ vimocayet.
7.1.19 pracchannaṃ vā taiḥ saṃyojya svayam a:jānatī bhūtvā tato viditeṣv etaṃ dharmastheṣu((185)) nivedayet.
7.1.20 sakhyaiva tu dāsyā vā mocita-kanyā-bhāvāṃ su:gṛhīta-kāma-sūtrām ābhyāsikeṣu yogeṣu pratiṣṭhitāṃ pratiṣṭhite vayasi saubhāgye ca duhitaram avasṛjanti gaṇikā iti prācyopacārāḥ.
7.1.21 pāṇi-grahaś ca saṃvatsaram a:vyabhicāryas tato yathā kāminī syāt.
7.1.22 ūrdhvam api saṃvatsarāt pariṇītena nimantryamāṇā lābham apy utsṛjya tāṃ rātriṃ tasyāgacchet.
7.1.22c iti veśyāyāḥ pāṇi-grahaṇa-vidhiḥ saubhāgya-vardhanaṃ ca.
7.1.23 etena raṅgopajīvināṃ kanyā vyākhyātāḥ.
7.1.24 tasmai tu tāṃ dadyur ya eṣāṃ tūrye viśiṣṭam upakuryāt.
children.translated_text:
7.1.1 The <s>Kāmasūtra</s> has been expounded.
7.1.2 When one does not achieve the desired result through the methods described therein, one should resort to the occult practices (<s>aupaniṣadika</s>).
7.1.3 Beauty, virtues, youth, and generosity — these make one attractive (<s>subhagaṃkaraṇa</s>).
7.1.4 An ointment of <s>tagara</s> (Tabernaemontana), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea), and <s>tālīsapatra</s> (Flacourtia) makes one attractive.
7.1.5 With these very [substances], finely ground, one makes a collyrium stick, smeared with sesame oil, prepared in a human skull — that is the collyrium.
7.1.6 Furthermore, oil prepared with [leaves of] <s>navāsā</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, <s>sārivā</s>, <s>kuraṇṭa</s>, and <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) petals is an anointing [preparation].
7.1.7 And garlands combined with these same [substances].
7.1.8 Having licked a powder of dried lotus, blue lotus, and <s>nāgakesara</s> (Mesua) with honey and ghee, one becomes attractive.
7.1.9 Those same [ingredients], combined with <s>nagara</s>, <s>tālīsa</s>, and <s>tamālapatra</s> (bay leaf), applied as an ointment.
7.1.10 One should coat a peacock's or hyena's eye [bone] with gold and wear it on the right hand —
7.1.10c this is the method of making oneself attractive.
7.1.11 Likewise, a <s>bādara</s>-gem or a <s>śaṅkha</s>-gem, treated in the same way — one should apply to these the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> (Atharvaveda) practices.
7.1.12 According to the science of spells, from the practice of spells: the master should keep a serving girl who has reached puberty away from others for one year. After that period, since the young woman, due to her wantonness, has become desirous among potential partners, he should give her to whoever offers the most through courtship — this increases good fortune.
7.1.13 A courtesan should invite [suitors] corresponding to her daughter who has reached puberty, [matching them] in knowledge, character, and beauty, and saying "Whoever substantially gives her this and that shall take her hand," she should guard her accordingly.
7.1.14 And she [the daughter], without her mother's knowledge, should be deeply fond of the wealthy sons of gentlemen (<s>nāgarikas</s>).
7.1.15 Their opportunities for meeting are at the learning of arts, at the music hall, at the mendicant woman's dwelling, and at various other places.
7.1.16 The mother should give [the daughter's] hand to those who offer the promised gifts.
7.1.17 But if unable to obtain that amount, she should publicize, even with her own resources in part, that "this [man] has given this to her daughter."
7.1.18 Or she should have the virginity of the married [daughter] released.
7.1.19 Or, having secretly united [her] with them, pretending not to know herself, she should then report it to the judges of righteousness when [the affair] becomes known.
7.1.20 A courtesan releases her daughter — whose virginity has been removed by a friend or a slave-girl, who has well-mastered the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>, who is established in the arts of intimacy, and who is at the right age and fortune — thus are the eastern customs.
7.1.21 The marriage is binding for one year without infidelity; after that, she may act as she pleases.
7.1.22 Even after a year, when invited by the one who married her, she should come to him for that night, even giving up [other] profit.
7.1.22c This is the procedure for the marriage of a courtesan and the increase of good fortune.
7.1.23 By this, the daughters of those who live by the stage [performers] are also explained.
7.1.24 They should give her to whoever renders distinguished service to their art.

7.1.25 dhattūraka-marica-pippalī-cūrṇair madhu-miśrair lipta-liṅgasya samprayogo vaśī-karaṇam.
7.1.26 vātodbhānta-pattraṃ mṛtaka-nirmālyaṃ mayūrāsthi-cūrṇāvacūrṇaṃ vaśī-karaṇam.
7.1.27 svayaṃ mṛtāyā maṇḍala-kārikāyāś cūrṇaṃ madhu-saṃyuktaṃ sahāmalakaiḥ snānaṃ vaśī-karaṇam.
7.1.28 vajra-snuhī-gaṇḍakāni khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtāni manaḥśilā-gandha-pāṣāṇa-cūrṇenābhyajya saptakṛtvaḥ śoṣitāni cūrṇayitvā madhunā lipta-liṅgasya saṃprayogo vaśī-karaṇam.
7.1.29 etenaiva rātrau dhūmaṃ kṛtvā tad-dhūma-tiras:kṛtaṃ sauvarṇaṃ candramasaṃ darśayati.
7.1.30 etair eva cūrṇitair vānara-purīṣa-miśritair yāṃ kanyām avakiret śānyasmai na dīyate.
7.1.31 vacāgaṇḍakāni sahakāra-taila-liptāni śiśapā-vṛkṣa-skandham utkīrya ṣaṇ-māsaṃ nidadhyāt tataḥ ṣaḍbhir māsair apanītāni devakāntam anulepanaṃ vaśī-karaṇaṃ cety ācakṣate.
7.1.32 tathā khadira-sāra-jāni śakalāni tanūni yaṃ vṛkṣam utkīrya ṣaṇ-māsaṃ nidadhyāt tat puṣpa-gandhāni bhavanti gandharva-kāntam anulepanaṃ vaśī-karaṇaṃ cety ācakṣate.
7.1.33 priyaṅgavas tagara-miśrāḥ sahakāra-taila-digdhā nāga-vṛkṣam utkīrya ṣaṇ-māsaṃ nihitā nāga-kāntam anu-lepanaṃ vaśī-karaṇam ity ācakṣate..7.1.34 uṣṭrāsthi bhṛgarāja-rasena bhāvitaṃ dagdham añjanaṃ nalikāyāṃ nihitam uṣṭrāsthi-śalākayaiva snāto 'ñjana-sahitaṃ puṇyaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ vaśī-karaṇaṃ cety ācakṣate.
7.1.35 etena śyena-bhāsa-mayūrāsthi-mayāny añjanāni vyākhyātāni((187)).
children.translated_text:
7.1.25 Intercourse with the member anointed with a powder of <s>dhattūraka</s> (thorn apple), pepper, and long pepper mixed with honey is a means of subjugation (<s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>).
7.1.26 A leaf blown by the wind, the remnants of a funeral offering, and a powder of peacock bone — [used as] a powder — is a means of subjugation.
7.1.27 The powder of a woman who has died naturally and who was a maker of magical circles, mixed with honey, used for bathing together with <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry) — is a means of subjugation.
7.1.28 Pieces of <s>vajra-snuhī</s> (a euphorbia) bulbs, cut into fragments, smeared with a powder of realgar and fragrant stone, dried seven times, powdered, and applied with honey to the member for intercourse — is a means of subjugation.
7.1.29 With these same [substances], having made smoke at night, one can show a golden moon veiled by that smoke.
7.1.30 With these same [substances], powdered and mixed with monkey excrement, whichever maiden one sprinkles [with it] — she will not be given to another.
7.1.31 Bulbs of <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), smeared with mango oil, placed for six months in the hollowed-out trunk of a <s>śiśapā</s> (rosewood) tree — then after six months, removed — they say this is an ointment [called] <s>devakānta</s> ("dear to the gods") and a means of subjugation.
7.1.32 Likewise, thin splints of <s>khadira</s> (acacia) heartwood, placed for six months in a hollowed-out tree — they acquire the fragrance of flowers. They say this is an ointment [called] <s>gandharvakānta</s> ("dear to the <s>Gandharvas</s>") and a means of subjugation.
7.1.33 <s>Priyaṅgu</s> (Callicarpa) seeds mixed with <s>tagara</s>, smeared with mango oil, placed for six months in a hollowed-out <s>nāga</s> tree — they say this is an ointment [called] <s>nāgakānta</s> ("dear to the <s>Nāgas</s>") and a means of subjugation.
7.1.34 Camel bone, steeped in <s>bhṛgarāja</s> (Eclipta) juice, burnt, [used as] collyrium placed in a tube, applied with a camel-bone applicator after bathing — they say it is auspicious, beneficial to the eyes, and a means of subjugation.
7.1.35 By this, collyriums made from the bones of hawks, ospreys, and peacocks are also explained.

7.1.36 uccaṭā-kandaś cavyā yaṣṭhī-madhukaṃ ca sa:śarkareṇa payasā pītvā vṛṣī-bhavati.
7.1.37 meṣa-vasta-muṣka-siddhasya payasaḥ sa:sśarkarasya pānaṃ vṛṣatva-yogaḥ.
7.1.38 tathā vidāryāḥ kṣīrikāyāḥ svayaṃ-guptāyāś ca kṣīreṇa pānam.
7.1.39 tathā priyāla-bījānāṃ moraṭā-vidāryoś ca kṣīreṇaiva.
7.1.40 śṛṅgāṭaka-kaserukā-madhūlikāni kṣīrakākolyā saha piṣṭāni saśarkareṇa payasā ghṛtena mandāgninotkarikāṃ paktvā yāvad arthaṃ bhakṣitavān an:antāḥ striyo gacchatīty ācāryāḥ pracakṣate.
7.1.41 māṣakamalinīṃ payasā dhautām uṣṇena ghṛtena mṛdu-kṛtyoddhṛtāṃ vṛddha-vatsāyāḥ goḥ payaḥ-siddhaṃ pāyasaṃ madhu-sarpirbhyām aśitvān:antāḥ striyo gacchatīty ācāryāḥ pracakṣate.
7.1.42 vidārī svayaṃ-guptā śarkarā madhu-sarpirbhyāṃ godhūma-cūrṇena polikāṃ kṛtvā yāvad arthaṃ bhakṣitavān an:antāḥ striyo gacchatīty ācāryāḥ pracakṣate.
7.1.43 caṭakāṇḍa-rasa-bhāvitais taṇḍulaiḥ pāyasaṃ siddhaṃ madhu-sarpirbhyāṃ plāvitaṃ yāvad artham iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa.
7.1.44 cāṭakāṇḍa-rasa-bhāvitān apagata-tvacas tilāñ śṛgāṭaka-kaseruka-svayaṃguptā-phalāni godhūma-māṣa-cūrṇaiḥ sa:śarkareṇa payasā sarpiṣā ca pakvaṃ saṃyāvaṃ yāvad arthaṃ prāśitavān iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa.
7.1.45 sarpiṣo madhunaḥ śarkarāyā madhukasya ca dve dve pale madhu-rasāyāḥ karṣaḥ prasthaṃ payasa iti ṣaḍaṅgam a:mṛtaṃ medhyaṃ vṛṣyam āyuṣyaṃ yukta-rasam ity ācāryāḥ pracakṣate.
7.1.46 śatāvarī-śvadaṃṣṭrā-guḍa-kaṣāye pippalī-madhukalke go-kṣīra-cchāga-ghṛte pakve tasya puṣyārambheṇānv:ahaṃ prāśanaṃ medhyaṃ vṛṣyam āyuṣyaṃ yukta-rasam ity ācāryāḥ pracakṣate.
7.1.47 śatāvaryāḥ śvadaṃṣṭrāyāḥ śrīparṇī-phalānāṃ ca kṣuṇṇānāṃ catur-guṇita-jalena pāka ā prakṛty-avasthānāt tasya puṣyārambheṇa prātaḥ prāśanaṃ medhyaṃ vṛṣyam āyuṣyaṃ yukta-rasam ity ācāryāḥ pracakṣate.
7.1.48 śvadaṃṣtrā-cūrṇa-samanvitaṃ tat-samam eva yava-cūrṇaṃ prātar utthāya dvi-palakam anu:dinaṃ prāśnīyān medhyaṃ vṛṣyaṃ yukta-rasam ity ācāryāḥ pracakṣate.
7.1.49v āyur-vedāc ca vedāc ca vidyāt tantrebhya eva ca. āptebhyaś cāvaboddhavyā yogā ye prīti-kārakāḥ..
7.1.50v na prayuñjīta saṃdigdhān na śarīrātyayāvahān. na jīva-ghāta-saṃbaddhān nā:śuci-dravya-saṃyutān..
7.1.51v tapo-yuktaḥ prayuñjīta śiṣṭair anugatān vidhīn. brāhmaṇaiś ca suhṛdbhiś ca maṅgalair abhinanditān((188))..
children.translated_text:
7.1.36 Having drunk [a decoction of] <s>uccaṭā</s> root, <s>cavya</s> (Piper chaba), and licorice (<s>yaṣṭhīmadhuka</s>) with milk and sugar, one becomes virile.
7.1.37 Drinking milk prepared with the testicles of a ram or goat, with sugar — is a virility recipe.
7.1.38 Likewise, drinking with milk [a preparation of] <s>vidārī</s> (Pueraria), <s>kṣīrikā</s>, and <s>svayaṃguptā</s> (Mucuna).
7.1.39 Likewise, [a preparation] of <s>priyāla</s> (Buchanania) seeds, <s>moraṭā</s>, and <s>vidārī</s>, with milk.
7.1.40 <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s> (water caltrop), <s>kaseruka</s> (Scirpus), and <s>madhūlika</s>, ground together with <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, cooked on a gentle fire with milk, sugar, and ghee into a cake — having eaten as needed, one goes to countless women — so the teachers declare.
7.1.41 <s>Māṣakamalinī</s> washed with milk, softened with warm ghee and taken out, [then] a milk pudding (<s>pāyasa</s>) made with the milk of a cow with a grown calf, eaten with honey and ghee — one goes to countless women — so the teachers declare.

children.translated_text: 7.1.32 If one sprinkles [a woman] with powdered <s>snuhī</s>-thorns mixed with <s>punarnavā</s>, monkey-dung, and <s>lāṅgalikā</s>-root, she will not desire another. 7.1.33 Likewise, the passion of one who approaches a woman whose private parts are smeared with a preparation thickened with the powder of <s>somalatā</s>, <s>avalgujā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>lohopajihvikā</s>, and with the resin of <s>vyādhighātaka</s> and <s>jambū</s>-fruit juice, is destroyed. 7.1.34 The passion of one who approaches a woman who has bathed with powders of <s>gopālikā</s>, <s>bahupādikā</s>, and <s>jihvikā</s> mixed with buffalo buttermilk is destroyed. 7.1.35 An ointment and garlands made with <s>nīpa</s>, <s>āmrātaka</s>, and <s>jambū</s> flowers cause ill-fortune. 7.1.36 An application of <s>kokilākṣa</s> tightens the [vulva of] a <s>hastinī</s> (elephant-woman) in a single night. 7.1.37 Powders of lotus, <s>utpala</s>, <s>kadamba</s>, <s>sarjaka</s>, and <s>sugandha</s>, ground with honey, applied as an ointment — enlargement for the <s>mṛgī</s> (doe-woman). 7.1.38 Myrobalans treated with the alkaline juices of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>soma</s>, and <s>arka</s>, and with <s>avalgujā</s>-fruits — whitening of the hair. 7.1.39 Bathing with the roots of <s>madayantikā</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>kāñjanikā</s>, <s>girikarṇikā</s>, and <s>ślakṣṇaparṇī</s> — restoration of hair [color]. 7.1.40 By anointing with oil well-cooked with these same [herbs] — blackening; and gradually through that, restoration [of color]. 7.1.41 The lower lip, reddened with lac treated seven times with the sweat of a white horse's testicles, becomes white. 7.1.42 <s>Madayantikā</s> and the rest are the restoration [for this as well]. 7.1.43 One who plays a bamboo flute smeared with <s>bahupādikā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>tālīsa</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>vajrakandaka</s> — whatever woman hears the sound becomes submissive. 7.1.44 Food mixed with <s>dhattūra</s>-fruit causes madness. 7.1.45 Old jaggery is the remedy. 7.1.46 By smearing one's hand with the dung of a peacock that has eaten yellow orpiment and red arsenic, whatever object one touches becomes invisible. 7.1.47 Water mixed with charcoal-grass-ash and oil takes on the color of milk. 7.1.48 Iron vessels smeared with a paste of <s>harītaka</s>, <s>āmrātaka</s>, and <s>śravaṇa-priyaṅgukā</s> become copper-colored. 7.1.49 By lighting a lamp with a wick of silk-fabric and snake-skin using <s>śravaṇa-priyaṅgukā</s>-oil, wooden sticks elongated nearby appear as serpents. 7.1.50 Drinking the milk of a white cow with a white calf brings fame and longevity. 7.1.51 And the blessings of esteemed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. 7.1.52 (verse) Having studied the earlier treatises and followed their methods, this <s>Kāmasūtra</s> has been set forth with effort, in concise form. 7.1.53 (verse) One who knows the truth of this, seeing <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>, along with trust and worldly ways, does not act from passion alone. 7.1.54 (verse) Those various passion-increasing [methods] which were stated in order of subject have been, immediately thereafter in this very [work], carefully restrained. 7.1.55 (verse) One should not [think] 'there is no <s>śāstra</s> [governing this]' — for practice must be examined [in light of it]. One should know the precepts of the <s>śāstra</s> to be of universal scope, while the practices are of particular application. 7.1.56 (verse) Having learned and considered the teachings of the <s>Bābhravīyas</s> and their <s>sūtra</s>-meanings, <s>Vātsyāyana</s> composed this <s>Kāmasūtra</s> according to proper method. 7.1.57 (verse) This was composed with supreme celibacy and concentration, for the purpose of worldly conduct — its method is not for the purpose of passion. 7.1.58 (verse) One who, protecting the proper balance of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> as it exists in worldly life, knows the truth of this <s>śāstra</s>, becomes indeed a master of the senses. 7.1.59 (verse) The skilled and learned one who, considering <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, not overly passionate, applies [this knowledge] with discernment — succeeds.

children.translated_text: [Note 156] <s>Yaśodhara</s>: <s>kāmopadhā</s> means the test (<s>parīkṣā</s>) in the domain of <s>kāma</s>, and those purified by it. There exists a 'test of <s>kāma</s>' [<s>kāmopadhā</s>] in the <s>Arthaśāstra</s> 1, described in 1.10.7-8. According to 1.10.13, 'those who have been purified by this test should be assigned to the guardianship of [places of] recreation inside [the palace] as well as outside...' [Kangle vol. 2, p. 20] (<s>kāmopadhā-śuddhān bāhyābhyantara-vihāra-rakṣāsu</s>).

children.text: ((157)). le parallèle avec les épreuves de as.1.1.10 est clair, selon goṇikāputra, ils doivent avoir subi avec succès trois épreuves : kāma-Ś, bhaya-Ś, artha-Ś.
children.translated_text: [Note 157] The parallel with the tests of <s>Arthaśāstra</s> 1.1.10 is clear. According to <s>Goṇikāputra</s>, they must have successfully undergone three tests: <s>kāma-śuddhi</s> (test of desire), <s>bhaya-śuddhi</s> (test of fear), <s>artha-śuddhi</s> (test of wealth).

children.text: ((158)). il s'agit alors d'épreuves [la forme verbale upadadhyāt // upadhā- en atteste] destinées à s'assurer de la fidélité des femmes et non, comme précédemment, de leurs gardiens. ceci est peut être à mettre en rapport avec as.1.1.20.14 "in the inner appartments, he should visit the queen after she is cleared (of suspicion) by old women." (antargṛha-gataḥ sthavira-strī-pariśuddhāṃ devīṃ paśyet.).
children.translated_text: [Note 158] These are then tests [the verbal form <s>upadadhyāt</s> // <s>upadhā</s>- attests to this] intended to ensure the fidelity of the women and not, as previously, of their guardians. This may be related to <s>Arthaśāstra</s> 1.1.20.14: 'In the inner apartments, he should visit the queen after she is cleared [of suspicion] by old women' (<s>antargṛha-gataḥ sthavira-strī-pariśuddhāṃ devīṃ paśyet</s>).

[Note 159] Here, <s>Vātsyāyana</s> expresses an opinion comparable to that of <s>Kauṭilya</s> on the subject of tests [1.10.18v-19v]: 'He should not effect the corruption of the uncorrupted (<s>na dūṣaṇam aduṣṭasya... caret</s>) as of water by poison; for, it may well happen that a cure may not be found for one corrupted [18]. And the mind, perverted by the fourfold secret tests, may not turn back without going to the end, remaining fixed in the will of spirited persons [19].' This opinion is also found in 1.17.30-32, but regarding the crown prince: 'This awakening of one not awake is highly dangerous, says <s>Kauṭilya</s> [30]. For a fresh object absorbs whatever it is smeared with [31]. Similarly this prince, immature in intellect, understands as the teaching of the science whatever he is told [32].' (<s>mahā-doṣam abuddha-bodhanam iti Kauṭilyaḥ. navaṃ hi dravyaṃ yena yenārtha-jātenopadihyate tat tad ācūṣati. evam ayaṃ nava-buddhir yad yad ucyate tat tac chāstropadeśam ivābhijānāti</s>.)

[Note 161] <s>Yaśodhara</s>: 'Those established in the court of <s>dharma</s> — the chief judges and others.'

[Note 167] <s>Yaśodhara</s>: 'Thus [ends] Compliance with the Beloved (<s>kāntānuvṛtta</s>), the fifty-second section.'
[Note 168] <s>Yaśodhara</s>: 'Thus [ends] Means of Acquiring Wealth (<s>arthāgamopāyāḥ</s>), the fifty-third section.'
[Note 169] <s>Dharmastha</s> — cf. <s>Arthaśāstra</s> 1, Book 3. <s>Yaśodhara</s>: 'Among the <s>dharmasthas</s>, chief judges and others...'

[Note 178] Double articulation: 26c <s>iti</s>... 27 <s>atha</s>...
[Note 179] Here again a double articulation: 35c <s>iti</s>... 36 ...<s>tu</s>.
[Note 180] Note the qualification <s>yukti</s> (cf. <s>Arthaśāstra</s> 1.15.1) of the 'reasonings' proposed: <s>anayā eva yuktyā</s>...

[Note 187] <s>Yaśodhara</s>: 'Thus [ends] Subjugation (<s>vaśī-karaṇa</s>), the sixtieth section.'

[Note 190] <s>Yaśodhara</s> does not mention the numbering of the section in his commentary, but announces, after his paraphrase, <s>citra-yogas</s> [complete]: '<s>tāṃs tāṃś ca yogān iti. vardhanasya yogāḥ vṛddhi-vidhayaḥ. ukta-vyatirikta-kārya-sādhanārthaṃ prakīrṇaka-nyāyena citrā yogā ucyante</s>.'
[Note 191] <s>Yaśodhara</s>: '<s>atha</s> is for the purpose of introducing the section...'

[Note 193] <s>Yaśodhara</s>: 'Thus [ends] the Miscellaneous Recipes (<s>citra-yogāḥ</s>), the sixty-fourth section.'
